article.title: A New Life for an Old Market
article.summary_zh: 小镇通过修缮危楼与革新经营，成功让衰落的老集市重获新生。
article.body:
Last spring, David Green, the deputy head of the town council, started a major project to save the old central market. Over the past five years, local business had declined sharply, and the gross sales of the market shops had fallen by forty percent. The ninety-year-old brick hall suffered from serious neglect, with broken glass, dirty walls, and water leaking from the ceiling. Only eight sellers remained in the cold building, and most local shoppers went to modern supermarkets outside town instead. Green completed a preliminary report to test whether a fresh business venture could bring people back to the town center.

When Green first showed his plan to the public, twelve older shop owners gathered outside his office to protest against it. They feared that higher rent and new rules would soon drive them away from their stalls. Green did not hesitate to face the angry crowd. His first instinct was to defend the council, but he chose to be a patient listener instead. He spent two full afternoons hearing their worries and writing down every detail. After these talks, he offered a rational solution: the town would freeze rent for six months and provide free training for every seller.

Next, a building engineer gave an urgent recommendation about the safety of the hall. Workers had to fix several structural problems before shoppers could safely enter the space. The engineer drew a clear illustration of the roof to explain where the heavy wooden beams had become weak with age. Green had to suspend all business inside the hall for four weeks so that the repair team could finish their work without danger. During this break, the council published a clear guide to specify what kinds of goods sellers could offer in the renewed market.

Under the new rules, the market gave priority to farmers who produced fresh, organic vegetables and grains without harmful chemicals. The council made these farm products the sole items that sellers could offer on the ground floor. In addition, the quick installation of modern cooling machines allowed sellers to keep milk, cheese, and meat fresh even in hot summer weather. This healthy mode of selling proved popular with young families in town. It was a logical choice because twenty-five local farms had already agreed to supply fresh food every morning before seven o'clock.

Today, the old brick hall has completed an inspiring transformation. Local commerce has returned to life, and more than forty family businesses now thrive under the bright glass roof. Daily food sales have risen by sixty percent since the market reopened. While morning trade remains steady, the market also holds occasional weekend events, such as cooking classes and art shows, to attract visitors from nearby towns. This great change proves that collective effort can defeat hard times. When town leaders and citizens work toward a common goal, they can rebuild their community with lasting success.

senses.concept_en: When you write something down, you record it on a piece of paper using a pen or pencil.
You use have to when you are saying that something is necessary or required, or must happen. If you do not have to do something, it is not necessary or required.
You can use have to in order to say that you feel certain that something is true or will happen.
You use have to when you are saying that something is necessary or required, or must happen. If you do not have to do something, it is not necessary or required.
You can use have to in order to say that you feel certain that something is true or will happen.
You use in addition when you want to mention another item connected with the subject you are discussing.
You use more than before a number or amount to say that the actual number or amount is even greater.
If something is more than a particular thing, it has greater value or importance than this thing.
You use more than to say that something is true to a greater degree than is necessary or than average.

a.translation:
第一个字母 A; 一个; 第一的
art. [计] 累加器, 加法器, 地址, 振幅, 模拟, 区域, 面积, 汇编, 组件, 异步

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are referring to someone or something for the first time or when people may not know which particular person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （指初次提及或非特指的人或物）一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are referring to any person or thing of a particular type and do not want to be specific.
gloss_zh: （一类人或事物中非特指的）任何一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of an uncount noun when that noun follows an adjective, or when the noun is followed by words that describe it more fully.
gloss_zh: （用于前加形容词或后加修饰语的不可数名词之前）一（种）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of a mass noun when you want to refer to a single type or make of something.
You use a in quantifiers such as a lot ,a little, and a bit.
gloss_zh: （用于表示数量的词组中）许多/少许/一点

senses.concept_en: You use a or an to refer to someone or something as a typical member of a group, class, or type.
gloss_zh: （一类人或事物中典型的）一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of days, months, or festivals when you are referring to one particular instance of that day, month, or festival.
gloss_zh: （用于日子、月份或节日的名称之前以表示特例）一个

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are saying what someone is or what job they have.
You use a or an in front of the names of people as a way of indicating that you do not know them or anything about them and you are saying their name for the first time.
gloss_zh: （用于不为说话人所知的首次提到的人名前）某一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of people when you want to refer to someone else who has the same qualities or character as the person named.
gloss_zh: （用于人名前，表示与该人有相同特性或品质）类似…的一个（或一位）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of a surname when you want to refer to someone who belongs to the family with that surname.
gloss_zh: （用于姓氏前，表示某人属于某姓氏家族）一位姓…的人

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of artists to refer to one individual painting or sculpture created by them.
gloss_zh: （用于艺术家名字前）一幅…的画，一件…的雕塑作品

senses.concept_en: You use a or an instead of the number 'one', especially with words of measurement such as 'hundred', 'hour', and 'metre', and with fractions such as 'half', 'quarter', and 'third'.
gloss_zh: （代替数字one使用，尤用于hundred，hour和metre等表示度量的单词之前以及half, quarter和third等分数之前）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in expressions such as eight hours a day to express a rate or ratio.
gloss_zh: （用于表示比率的短语中）每一

about.translation:
prep. 在...周围, 大约, 有关, 关于
adv. 大约, 四处, 在附近, 周围

senses.concept_en: You use about to introduce who or what something relates to or concerns.
When you mention the things that an activity or institution is about, you are saying what it involves or what its aims are.
You use about after some adjectives to indicate the person or thing that a feeling or state of mind relates to.
If you do something about a problem, you take action in order to solve it.
When you say that there is a particular quality about someone or something, you mean that they have this quality.
gloss_zh: （某人或某事物）具有（某种特性）

senses.concept_en: About is used in front of a number to show that the number is not exact.
If someone or something moves about, they keep moving in different directions.
If you put something about a person or thing, you put it around them.
If someone or something is about, they are present or available.
gloss_zh: 在手头的;现成的;能得到的

senses.concept_en: If you are about to do something, you are going to do it very soon. If something is about to happen, it will happen very soon.

addition.translation:
n. 加法, 增加的人(或物)
[计] 加法
addition.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts gre

senses.concept_en: An addition to something is a thing which is added to it.
The addition of something is the fact that it is added to something else.
Addition is the process of calculating the total of two or more numbers.

derivation.breakdown_zh: add 加 + -ition 名词：加法

after.translation:
prep. 在...之后, 由于
conj. 在...之后
adv. 后来

senses.concept_en: If something happens after a particular date or event, it happens during the period of time that follows that date or event.
If you do one thing after doing another, you do it during the period of time that follows the other thing.

You use after when you are talking about time. For example, if something is going to happen during the day after or the weekend after a particular time, it is going to happen during the following day or during the following weekend.
If you go after someone, you follow or chase them.
If you are after something, you are trying to get it.
If you call, shout, or stare after someone, you call, shout, or stare at them as they move away from you.
gloss_zh: 朝着（正离去之人喊叫或注视）

senses.concept_en: If you do something after someone, you do it for them, because they cannot or will not do it for themselves.
If you tell someone that one place is a particular distance after another, you mean that it is situated beyond the other place and further away from you.
If one thing is written after another thing on a page, it is written following it or underneath it.
You use after in order to give the most important aspect of something when comparing it with another aspect.
To be named after someone means to be given the same name as them.
gloss_zh: 依照，按照（某人的名字命名）

senses.concept_en: After is used when telling the time. If it is, for example, ten after six, the time is ten minutes past six.
The afternoon is the part of each day which begins at lunchtime and ends at about six o'clock.

against.translation: prep. 反对, 对着, 倚靠

senses.concept_en: If one thing is leaning or pressing against another, it is touching it.
If you are against something such as a plan, policy, or system, you think it is wrong, bad, or stupid.
If you compete against someone in a game, you try to beat them.
If you take action against someone or something, you try to harm them.
If you take action against a possible future event, you try to prevent it.
If you do something against someone's wishes, advice, or orders, you do not do what they want you to do or tell you to do.
gloss_zh: 违背，违抗（愿望、劝告或命令）

senses.concept_en: If you do something in order to protect yourself against something unpleasant or harmful, you do something which will make its effects on you less serious if it happens.
If something is against the law or against the rules, there is a law or a rule which says that you must not do it.
If you are moving against a current, tide, or wind, you are moving in the opposite direction to it.
If something happens or is considered against a particular background of events, it is considered in relation to those events, because those events are relevant to it.
If something is measured or valued against something else, it is measured or valued by comparing it with the other thing.
The odds against something happening are the chances or odds that it will not happen.

age.translation:
n. 年龄, 老年, 成年, 寿命, 时代, 时期
v. 变老, 成熟

senses.concept_en: Your age is the number of years that you have lived.
The age of a thing is the number of years since it was made.
Age is the state of being old or the process of becoming older.
When someone ages, or when something ages them, they seem much older and less strong or less alert.
When food or alcohol is aged or when it ages, it is left to get older before being eaten or drunk, so that it develops a better flavour.
An age is a period in history.
You can say an age or ages to mean a very long time.

agree.translation:
vi. 同意, 赞成, 应允, 适合
vt. 承认, 认定, 同意

senses.concept_en: If people agree with each other about something, they have the same opinion about it or say that they have the same opinion.
If you agree to do something, you say that you will do it. If you agree to a proposal, you accept it.
If people agree on something, or in British English if they agree something, they all decide to accept or do something.
If you agree with an action or suggestion, you approve of it.
If one account of an event or one set of figures agrees with another, the two accounts or sets of figures are the same or are consistent with each other.
If some food that you eat does not agree with you, it makes you feel ill.
If a place or experience agrees with you, it makes you feel healthy and happy.

In grammar, if a word agrees with a noun or pronoun, it has a form that is appropriate to the number or gender of the noun or pronoun. For example, in 'He hates it', the singular verb agrees with the singular pronoun 'he'.

all.translation:
a. 所有的, 全部的, 一切的
adv. 全部, 全然
pron. 全部
n. 全部

senses.concept_en: You use all to indicate that you are referring to the whole of a particular group or thing or to everyone or everything of a particular kind.
You use all to refer to the whole of a particular period of time.
You use all to refer to a situation or to life in general.
You use all to emphasize that something is completely true, or happens everywhere or always, or on every occasion.
gloss_zh: （用于强调真实性或普遍性）完全，遍及，一直

senses.concept_en: You use all at the beginning of a clause when you are emphasizing that something is the only thing that is important.
gloss_zh: （用于句首表示强调某事的唯一重要性）一切，全部

senses.concept_en: You use all in expressions such as in all sincerity and in all probability to emphasize that you are being sincere or that something is very likely.
gloss_zh: （表示强调）非常真诚/极有可能

senses.concept_en: You can use all in front of an adjective when you want to emphasize a quality that affects someone or something temporarily.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词前，强调暂时的一种特征）

senses.concept_en: You use all when you are talking about an equal score in a game. For example, if the score is three all, both players or teams have three points.
gloss_zh: （球赛等双方得分相等时）每人，各（如three all为“三平”）

senses.concept_en: All is used in structures such as all the more or all the better to mean even more or even better than before.
gloss_zh: （用于all the more, all the better等结构中）更加，愈加

senses.concept_en: You use all in expressions such as seen it all and done it all to emphasize that someone has had a lot of experience of something.

allow.translation:
vt. 允许, 同意给予, 承认
vi. 容许, 猜想
[计] 允许命令

senses.concept_en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.
If you are allowed something, you are given permission to have it or are given it.
If you allow something to happen, you do not prevent it.
If one thing allows another thing to happen, the first thing creates the opportunity for the second thing to happen.
If you allow a particular length of time or a particular amount of something for a particular purpose, you include it in your planning.
If you allow that something is true, you admit or agree that it is true.

You use already to show that something has happened, or that something had happened before the moment you are referring to. Speakers of British English use already with a verb in a perfect tense, putting it after 'have', 'has', or 'had', or at the end of a clause. Some speakers of American English use already with the simple past tense of the verb instead of a perfect tense.
gloss_zh: 已经（用already时，英国英语中动词用完成时态，美国英语有时则用一般过去时）

senses.concept_en: You use already to show that a situation exists at this present moment or that it exists at an earlier time than expected. You use already after the verb 'be' or an auxiliary verb, or before a verb if there is no auxiliary. When you want add emphasis, you can put already at the beginning of a sentence.
gloss_zh: 早已（用于be动词或助动词之后，或一般动词之前，表示强调时可置于句首）

also.translation: adv. 也, 并且, 同样地

senses.concept_en: You can use also to give more information about a person or thing, or to add another relevant fact.
You can use also to indicate that something you have just said about one person or thing is true of another person or thing.

and.translation:
conj. 和, 与
[计] 与

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two or more words, groups, or clauses.
gloss_zh: （连接两个以上的单词、词组或子句）和，与，同

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two words or phrases that are the same in order to emphasize the degree of something, or to suggest that something continues or increases over a period of time.
gloss_zh: （连接两个相同的单词或短语，以强调某事物的程度、暗示某事继续发生或在一段时间内不断增加）接连，越…越…

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two statements about events when one of the events follows the other.
gloss_zh: （连接两件相继发生的事件）然后，就

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two statements when the second statement continues the point that has been made in the first statement.
gloss_zh: （连接两句话，第二句话的意思是第一句的延伸）则，而

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two clauses when the second clause is a result of the first clause.
gloss_zh: （连接两个从句，表示因果关系）那么，于是

senses.concept_en: You use and to interrupt yourself in order to make a comment on what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （表示停顿，以便对所说的话进行评论）再说，而

senses.concept_en: You use and at the beginning of a sentence to introduce something else that you want to add to what you have just said. Some people think that starting a sentence with and is ungrammatical, but it is now quite common in both spoken and written English.
gloss_zh: （用于句首，引出补充说明）还有，不过

senses.concept_en: You use and to introduce a question which follows logically from what someone has just said.
gloss_zh: （用以引导与某人之谈话有关的问句）那么，还有

senses.concept_en: And is used by broadcasters and people making announcements to change a topic or to start talking about a topic they have just mentioned.
gloss_zh: （广播员等用以转换话题或讨论刚才提及的话题）也

senses.concept_en: You use and to indicate that two numbers are to be added together.
And is used before a fraction that comes after a whole number.
You use and in numbers larger than one hundred, after the words 'hundred' or 'thousand' and before other numbers.
gloss_zh: （用在大于一百的数字中，置于百位或千位之后，十位及个位之前）

angry.translation: a. 生气的, 愤怒的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When you are angry, you feel strong dislike or impatience about something.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An angry wound or rash is red and painful.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe the sky or sea as angry, you mean that it is dark and stormy.
gloss_zh: （天空或海洋）天昏地暗的，狂风暴雨的

art.translation:
n. 艺术, 人文科学, 技术, 巧妙, 诡计, 美术
[计] 实际保持时间, 特许权和资源表, 平均检索时间, 平均运行时间

senses.concept_en: Art consists of paintings, sculpture, and other pictures or objects which are created for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.
Art is the activity or educational subject that consists of creating paintings, sculptures, and other pictures or objects for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.
gloss_zh: （作为活动或教学科目的）美术

senses.concept_en: The arts are activities such as music, painting, literature, cinema, and dance, which people can take part in for enjoyment, or to create works which express serious meanings or ideas of beauty.
gloss_zh: 艺术（活动）（如音乐、绘画、文学、电影、舞蹈等）

senses.concept_en: At a university or college, arts are subjects such as history, literature, or languages in contrast to scientific subjects.
Arts or art is used in the names of theatres or cinemas which show plays or films that are intended to make the audience think deeply about the content, and not simply to entertain them.
gloss_zh: （用于剧院或电影院的名称中）上演艺术作品的，艺术的

senses.concept_en: If you describe an activity as an art, you mean that it requires skill and that people learn to do it by instinct or experience, rather than by learning facts or rules.
Art is an old-fashioned form of the second person singular of the present tense of the verb be.
gloss_zh: （be的现在式单数第二人称形式，过时用法）

as.translation:
adv. 同样地, 例如
prep. 做为, 当作
conj. 当...之时, 以...的方式, 像...一样, 因为
[计] 高级系统, 先进系统, 辅助存储器, 自治系统

senses.concept_en: If something happens as something else happens, it happens at the same time.
gloss_zh: （表示两件事情同时发生）当…的时候，在…的同时

senses.concept_en: You use as when you are indicating what someone or something is or is thought to be, or what function they have.
If you do something as a child or as a teenager, for example, you do it when you are a child or a teenager.
You use as to say how something happens or is done, or to indicate that something happens or is done in the same way as something else.
You use as in expressions like as a result and as a consequence to indicate how two situations or events are related to each other.
You use as to introduce short clauses which comment on the truth of what you are saying.
You can use as to mean 'because' when you are explaining the reason for something.

attract.translation:
vt. 吸引, 诱惑
vi. 有吸引力

senses.concept_en: If something attracts people or animals, it has features that cause them to come to it.

If someone or something attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them. If a particular quality attracts you to a person or thing, it is the reason why you like them.
gloss_zh: 引起…的注意（或兴趣、赞赏等）；诱惑

senses.concept_en: If you are attracted to someone, you are interested in them sexually.
If something attracts support, publicity, or money, it receives support, publicity, or money.
gloss_zh: 吸引，招引（支持、关注或金钱）

senses.concept_en: If one object attracts another object, it causes the second object to move towards it.

If someone or something moves or is moved away from a place, they move or are moved so that they are no longer there. If you are away from a place, you are not in the place where people expect you to be.
If you look or turn away from something, you move your head so that you are no longer looking at it.
If you put or tidy something away, you put it where it should be. If you hide someone or something away, you put them in a place where nobody can see them or find them.
You use away to talk about future events. For example, if an event is a week away, it will happen after a week.
When a sports team plays away, it plays on its opponents' ground.
You can use away to say that something slowly disappears, becomes less significant, or changes so that it is no longer the same.
gloss_zh: （表示慢慢消失、变得不重要或慢慢改变）

senses.concept_en: You use away to show that there has been a change or development from one state or situation to another.
gloss_zh: （表示从一种状态到另一种状态的变化或发展）

senses.concept_en: You can use away to emphasize a continuous or repeated action.
You use away to show that something is removed.

back.translation:
a. 后面的
vt. 使后退, 支持
vi. 倒退, 背靠
adv. 向后地
n. 背部, 后面

senses.concept_en: If you move back, you move in the opposite direction to the one in which you are facing or in which you were moving before.
If you go back somewhere, you return to where you were before.
If someone or something is back in a particular state, they were in that state before and are now in it again.
gloss_zh: 恢复原状；回到原来的状态

senses.concept_en: If you give or put something back, you return it to the person who had it or to the place where it was before you took it. If you get or take something back, you then have it again after not having it for a while.
If you put a clock or watch back, you change the time shown on it so that it shows an earlier time, for example when the time changes to winter time or standard time.
If you write or call back, you write to or telephone someone after they have written to or telephoned you. If you look back at someone, you look at them after they have started looking at you.
You can say that you go or come back to a particular point in a conversation to show that you are mentioning or discussing it again.
If something is or comes back, it is fashionable again after it has been unfashionable for some time.
gloss_zh: 再次流行；再度成为潮流

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is kept or situated back from a place, they are at a distance away from it.
If something is held or tied back, it is held or tied so that it does not hang loosely over something.
If you lie or sit back, you move your body backwards into a relaxed sloping or flat position, with your head and body resting on something.
If you look or shout back at someone or something, you turn to look or shout at them when they are behind you.

You use back in expressions like back in London or back at the house when you are giving an account, to show that you are going to start talking about what happened or was happening in the place you mention.
gloss_zh: （表示描述场所的转换）在曾提到过的地方

senses.concept_en: If you talk about something that happened back in the past or several years back, you are emphasizing that it happened quite a long time ago.
If you think back to something that happened in the past, you remember it or try to remember it.
A person's or animal's back is the part of their body between their head and their legs that is on the opposite side to their chest and stomach.
The back of something is the side or part of it that is towards the rear or farthest from the front. The back of something is normally not used or seen as much as the front.
Back is used to refer to the side or part of something that is towards the rear or farthest from the front.
The back of a chair or sofa is the part that you lean against when you sit on it.
The back of something such as a piece of paper or an envelope is the side which is less important.
The back of a book is the part nearest the end, where you can find the index or the notes, for example.
You can use back in expressions such as round the back and out the back to refer generally to the area behind a house or other building.
gloss_zh: （用于round the back, out the back等表达方式中）房屋（或其他建筑物）后的区域

senses.concept_en: You use back in expressions such as out back to refer to the area behind a house or other building. You also use in back to refer to the rear part of something, especially a car or building.
gloss_zh: （用于out back等表达方式中）房屋（或其他建筑物）后的区域；（用于in back等表达方式中）汽车（或建筑物等）的后部

senses.concept_en: In team games such as football and hockey, a back is a player who is concerned mainly with preventing the other team from scoring goals, rather than scoring goals for their own team.
gloss_zh: （足球、曲棍球等运动中的）后卫

senses.concept_en: In American football, a back is a player who stands behind the front line, runs with the ball and attacks rather than defends.
gloss_zh: （美式橄榄球运动中的）进攻后卫

senses.concept_en: If a building backs onto something, the back of it faces in the direction of that thing or touches the edge of that thing.
When you back a car or other vehicle somewhere or when it backs somewhere, it moves backwards.
If you back a person or a course of action, you support them, for example by voting for them or giving them money.
If you back a particular person, team, or horse in a competition, you predict that they will win, and usually you bet money that they will win.
gloss_zh: 预测…获胜；（通常指）下赌注于

senses.concept_en: If a singer is backed by a band or by other singers, they provide the musical background for the singer.

be.translation:
v. 是, 表示, 在
[计] 后端, 总线允许

senses.concept_en: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs. be going to
gloss_zh: （和现在分词连用构成动词的进行式）

senses.concept_en: You use be with a past participle to form the passive voice.
gloss_zh: （和过去分词连用构成被动语态）

senses.concept_en: You use be with an infinitive to indicate that something is planned to happen, that it will definitely happen, or that it must happen. be about to
gloss_zh: （和不定式连用表示将来的安排或确定会发生的事情）

senses.concept_en: You use be with an infinitive to say or ask what should happen or be done in a particular situation, how it should happen, or who should do it.
gloss_zh: （和不定式连用表示在某种情况下会发生什么事，应该怎样做或应该由谁来做）

senses.concept_en: You use was and were with an infinitive to talk about something that happened later than the time you are discussing, and was not planned or certain at that time.
gloss_zh: （was和were和不定式连用，表示说话时间之后发生的事）

senses.concept_en: You can say that something is to be seen, heard, or found in a particular place to mean that people can see it, hear it, or find it in that place.
gloss_zh: （表示可见到、可听到、可发现等）

senses.concept_en: You use be to introduce more information about the subject, such as its identity, nature, qualities, or position.
gloss_zh: （用于提供与主语相关的信息）

senses.concept_en: You use be, with 'it' as the subject, in clauses where you are describing something or giving your judgment of a situation.
gloss_zh: （以it作主语，用来进行描述或作出判断）

senses.concept_en: You use be with the impersonal pronoun 'there' in expressions like there is and there are to say that something exists or happens.
gloss_zh: （与非人称代词there连用构成there is和there are表示存在或发生）

senses.concept_en: You use be as a link between a subject and a clause and in certain other clause structures, as shown below.
gloss_zh: （表示主语和从句和其他从句结构之间的某种联系）

senses.concept_en: You use be in expressions like the thing is and the point is to introduce a clause in which you make a statement or give your opinion.
gloss_zh: （用在如the thing is和the point is这样的结构中，引导表示陈述或提出观点的从句）

senses.concept_en: You use be in expressions like to be fair ,to be honest, or to be serious to introduce an additional statement or opinion, and to indicate that you are trying to be fair, honest, or serious.
gloss_zh: （用在如to be fair, to be honest或to be serious 这样的结构中表示尽量）

senses.concept_en: The form 'be' is used occasionally instead of the normal forms of the present tense, especially after 'whether'.
gloss_zh: （有时用来代替现在时态中be的几个常规形式，尤用于whether后）

senses.concept_en: If something is, it exists.
senses.register_label: mainly FORMAL or LITERARY 主正式或文

senses.concept_en: To be yourself means to behave in the way that is right and natural for you and your personality.
gloss_zh: 保持真我；按自己的方式行事；显常态

beam.translation:
n. 横梁, 杆, 光线, 容光焕发
vi. 用梁支承, 微笑, 射出光线
vt. 照耀, 感到欣喜
[计] 束
beam.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is beaming, you mean that they have a big smile on their face because they are happy, pleased, or proud about something.
A beam is a line of energy, radiation, or particles sent in a particular direction.
If something beams radio signals or television pictures or they are beamed somewhere, they are sent there by means of electronic equipment.
A beam of light is a line of light that shines from an object such as a lamp.
If something such as the sun or a lamp beams down, it sends light to a place and shines on it.
A beam is a long thick bar of wood, metal, or concrete, especially one used to support the roof of a building.
In gymnastics, the beam is a piece of equipment that consists of a narrow wooden bar on which gymnasts balance and perform movements.
You use because when stating the reason for something.
You use because when stating the explanation for a statement you have just made.

become.translation:
vi. 变成, 变得
vt. 适合

senses.concept_en: If someone or something becomes a particular thing, they start to change and develop into that thing, or start to develop the characteristics mentioned.
If something becomes someone, it makes them look attractive or it seems right for them.

before.translation:
prep. 在...之前
conj. 在...之前
adv. 在前

senses.concept_en: If something happens before a particular date, time, or event, it happens earlier than that date, time, or event
If you do one thing before doing something else, you do it earlier than the other thing.
You use before when you are talking about time. For example, if something happened the day before a particular date or event, it happened during the previous day.
If you do something before someone else can do something, you do it when they have not yet done it.
If someone has done something before, they have done it on a previous occasion. If someone has not done something before, they have never done it.
If there is a period of time or if several things are done before something happens, it takes that amount of time or effort for this thing to happen.
If a particular situation has to happen before something else happens, this situation must happen or exist in order for the other thing to happen.
gloss_zh: （必须先具备某一条件）才能；在…之前（必须具备某一条件）

senses.concept_en: If someone is before something, they are in front of it.
If you tell someone that one place is a certain distance before another, you mean that they will come to the first place first.
If you appear or come before an official person or group, you go there and answer questions.
If something happens before a particular person or group, it is seen by or happens while this person or this group is present.
If you have something such as a journey, a task, or a stage of your life before you, you must do it or live through it in the future.
gloss_zh: 摆在…面前；使面对；使面临

senses.concept_en: When you want to say that one person or thing is more important than another, you can say that they come before the other person or thing.

break.translation:
n. 休息, 中断, 破裂处, 绝交, 破晓, 突变
vt. 打破, 弄破, 弄坏, 破坏, 违反, 打断, 削弱, 放弃
vi. 破碎, 决裂, 破晓, 突变, 变弱, 暂停
n. 分隔符
[计] 分隔符; 中断; DOS内部命令:设定扫描中断按键的时机

senses.concept_en: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.
If you break a part of your body such as your leg, your arm, or your nose, or if a bone breaks, you are injured because a bone cracks or splits.
If a surface, cover, or seal breaks or if something breaks it, a hole or tear is made in it, so that a substance can pass through.
gloss_zh: （使）（表层、盖子或密封）破裂；撕开

senses.concept_en: When a tool or piece of machinery breaks or when you break it, it is damaged and no longer works.
If you break a rule, promise, or agreement, you do something that you should not do according to that rule, promise, or agreement.
gloss_zh: 破坏，违反（规则、承诺或协议）

senses.concept_en: If you break free or loose, you free yourself from something or escape from it.
If someone breaks something, especially a difficult or unpleasant situation that has existed for some time, they end it or change it.
gloss_zh: 结束（困难或不利局面）；打破（僵局）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something breaks a silence, they say something or make a noise after a long period of silence.
If there is a break in the cloud or weather, it changes and there is a short period of sunshine or fine weather.
If you break with a group of people or a traditional way of doing things, or you break your connection with them, you stop being involved with that group or stop doing things in that way.
If you break a habit or if someone breaks you of it, you no longer have that habit.
To break someone means to destroy their determination and courage, their success, or their career.
gloss_zh: 瓦解…的决心；使丧失勇气；毁掉…的前程

senses.concept_en: If someone breaks for a short period of time, they rest or change from what they are doing for a short period.

See also:lunch break;tea break; A break is a short period of time when you have a rest or a change from what you are doing, especially if you are working or if you are in a boring or unpleasant situation.
A break is a short holiday.
If you break your journey somewhere, you stop there for a short time so that you can have a rest.
To break the force of something such as a blow or fall means to weaken its effect, for example by getting in the way of it.
When a piece of news breaks, people hear about it from the newspapers, television, or radio.
gloss_zh: （消息在报纸、电视或电台）发布，传播

senses.concept_en: When you break a piece of bad news to someone, you tell it to them, usually in a kind way.
gloss_zh: （通常以委婉的方式）透露，告知（坏消息）

senses.concept_en: A break is a lucky opportunity that someone gets to achieve something.
See also:record-breaking; If you break a record, you beat the previous record for a particular achievement.
See also:daybreak; When day or dawn breaks, it starts to grow light after the night has ended.
When a wave breaks, it passes its highest point and turns downwards, for example when it reaches the shore.
If you break a secret code, you work out how to understand it.
If someone's voice breaks when they are speaking, it changes its sound, for example because they are sad or afraid.
gloss_zh: （因悲伤或害怕嗓音）突变，变调

senses.concept_en: When a boy's voice breaks, it becomes deeper and sounds more like a man's voice.
If the weather breaks or a storm breaks, it suddenly becomes rainy or stormy after a period of sunshine.
In tennis, if you break your opponent's serve, you win a game in which your opponent is serving.
gloss_zh: （网球比赛中）破，赢得（对手的发球局）

brick.translation:
n. 砖块, 积木
a. 用砖做的
vt. 用砖造, 用砖砌

senses.concept_en: Bricks are rectangular blocks of baked clay used for building walls, which are usually red or brown. Brick is the material made up of these blocks.
If you say that someone is a brick, you mean that they have helped you or supported you when you were in a difficult situation.

bright.translation:
a. 明亮的, 聪明的, 鲜明的, 欢快的
adv. 明亮地, 欢快地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bright colour is strong and noticeable, and not dark.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bright light, object, or place is shining strongly or is full of light.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as bright, you mean that they are quick at learning things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bright idea is clever and original.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone looks or sounds bright, they look or sound cheerful and lively.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If the future is bright, it is likely to be pleasant or successful.
The brights on a car or other vehicle are the headlights when they are switched on fully.
gloss_zh: （汽车或其他车辆）打开的前灯

bring.translation:
vt. 带来, 产生, 促使, 提出
vi. 生产

senses.concept_en: If you bring someone or something with you when you come to a place, they come with you or you have them with you.
If you bring something somewhere, you move it there.
If you bring something that someone wants or needs, you get it for them or carry it to them.
To bring something or someone to a place or position means to cause them to come to the place or move into that position.
If you bring something new to a place or group of people, you introduce it to that place or cause those people to hear or know about it.
To bring someone or something into a particular state or condition means to cause them to be in that state or condition.
If something brings a particular feeling, situation, or quality, it makes people experience it or have it.
If a period of time brings a particular thing, it happens during that time.
If you bring a legal action against someone or bring them to trial, you officially accuse them of doing something illegal.
gloss_zh: （对某人）提起（诉讼）；将（某人）送上（法庭）

senses.concept_en: If a television or radio programme is brought to you by an organization, they make it, broadcast it, or pay for it to be made or broadcast.
gloss_zh: 提供，制作，播出（电视或广播节目）

senses.concept_en: When you are talking, you can say that something brings you to a particular point in order to indicate that you have now reached that point and are going to talk about a new subject.
gloss_zh: 把（某人）带到（或引到）（某话题）

senses.concept_en: If you cannot bring yourself to do something, you cannot do it because you find it too upsetting, embarrassing, or disgusting.
gloss_zh: 强迫（自己）做（令人伤心、窘迫或讨厌的事）

broken.translation:
a. 坏掉的, 打破的, 断掉的
break的过去分词

senses.concept_en: Broken is the past participle of break .
A broken line is not continuous but has gaps or spaces in it.
gloss_zh: （线条）不连贯的，断续的，中断的

senses.concept_en: You can use broken to describe a marriage that has ended in divorce, or a home in which the parents of the family are divorced, when you think this is a sad or bad thing.
If someone talks in broken English, for example, or in broken French, they speak slowly and make a lot of mistakes because they do not know the language very well.

building.translation:
n. 建筑物, 建筑
[法] 营造, 建筑, 建筑物

senses.concept_en: A building is a structure that has a roof and walls, for example a house or a factory.

business.translation:
n. 生意, 事情, 业务, 商业, 商行, 职责
[经] 企业, 商业, 营业
business.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Business is work relating to the production, buying, and selling of goods or services.

Business is used when talking about how many products or services a company is able to sell. If business is good, a lot of products or services are being sold and if business is bad, few of them are being sold.
A business is an organization which produces and sells goods or which provides a service.
gloss_zh: 工商企业；公司；商店；商铺

senses.concept_en: Business is work or some other activity that you do as part of your job and not for pleasure.
You can use business to refer to a particular area of work or activity in which the aim is to make a profit.
You can use business to refer to something that you are doing or concerning yourself with.
gloss_zh: 眼前所做之事；手头的事

senses.concept_en: You can use business to refer to important matters that you have to deal with.
If you say that something is your business, you mean that it concerns you personally and that other people have no right to ask questions about it or disagree with it.
You can use business to refer in a general way to an event, situation, or activity. For example, you can say something is 'a wretched business' or you can refer to 'this assassination business'.
You can use business when describing a task that is unpleasant in some way. For example, if you say that doing something is a costly business, you mean that it costs a lot.
gloss_zh: （令人不快或耗费钱财的）活儿，事情

but.translation:
prep. 除了
conj. 但是
adv. 仅仅

senses.concept_en: You use but to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said, or to introduce something which adds to what you have just said.
You use but when you are about to add something further in a discussion or to change the subject.
You use but after you have made an excuse or apologized for what you are just about to say.
You use but to introduce a reply to someone when you want to indicate surprise, disbelief, refusal, or protest.
gloss_zh: （引出下文，表示惊讶、难以置信、拒绝或抗议）但是，可是

senses.concept_en: But is used to mean 'except'.
But is used to mean 'only'.
You use buts in expressions like 'no buts' and 'ifs and buts' to refer to reasons someone gives for not doing something, especially when you do not think that they are good reasons.

by.translation:
prep. 被, 经, 由, 在...之旁
adv. 经过, 在近处

senses.concept_en: If something is done by a person or thing, that person or thing does it.
If you say that something such as a book, a piece of music, or a painting is by a particular person, you mean that this person wrote it or created it.
gloss_zh: （图书、音乐、绘画等）由…（创作），出自

senses.concept_en: If you do something by a particular means, you do it using that thing.
If you achieve one thing by doing another thing, your action enables you to achieve the first thing.
You use by in phrases such as 'by chance' or 'by accident' to indicate whether or not an event was planned.
gloss_zh: （用于短语中）由于，出于（偶然或意外）

senses.concept_en: If someone is a particular type of person by nature, by profession, or by birth, they are that type of person because of their nature, their profession, or the family they were born into.
gloss_zh: 就（本性、职业或出身）而言

senses.concept_en: If something must be done by law, it happens according to the law. If something is the case by particular standards, it is the case according to the standards.
gloss_zh: 根据，按照（法律或某种标准）

senses.concept_en: If you say what someone means by a particular word or expression, you are saying what they intend the word or expression to refer to.
If you hold someone or something by a particular part of them, you hold that part.
gloss_zh: （用于表示抓住身体某部位或握住物体某部分）

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is by something else is beside it and close to it.
If a person or vehicle goes by you, they move past you without stopping.
If you stop by a place, you visit it for a short time.
If something happens by a particular time, it happens at or before that time.
If you do something by day, you do it during the day. If you do it by night, you do it during the night.
In arithmetic, you use by before the second number in a multiplication or division sum.
You use by to talk about measurements of area. For example, if a room is twenty feet by fourteen feet, it measures twenty feet in one direction and fourteen feet in the other direction.
gloss_zh: 乘（表示长乘宽得出的居室等的面积）

senses.concept_en: If something increases or decreases by a particular amount, that amount is gained or lost.
Things that are made or sold by the million or by the dozen are made or sold in those quantities.
You use by in expressions such as 'minute by minute' and 'drop by drop' to talk about things that happen gradually, not all at once.

can.translation:
vt. 装罐
n. 罐头, 容器
aux. 能, 可以
[计] 作废字符

senses.concept_en: You use can when you are mentioning a quality or fact about something which people may make use of if they want to.
gloss_zh: （表示某事物的特点）能够，可以

senses.concept_en: You use can to indicate that someone has the ability or opportunity to do something.
gloss_zh: （表示有能力或机会）能，会，可以

senses.concept_en: You use cannot to indicate that someone is not able to do something because circumstances make it impossible for them to do it.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句，表示情况不允许）不能，无法

senses.concept_en: You use can to indicate that something is true sometimes or is true in some circumstances.
You use cannot and can't to state that you are certain that something is not the case or will not happen.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句，表示确信某事不真实或不会发生）不可能，不会

senses.concept_en: You use can to indicate that someone is allowed to do something. You use cannot or can't to indicate that someone is not allowed to do something.
You use cannot or can't when you think it is very important that something should not happen or that someone should not do something.
You use can, usually in questions, in order to make suggestions or to offer to do something.
gloss_zh: （通常用于疑问句，表示建议或提议帮忙）能

senses.concept_en: You use can in questions in order to make polite requests. You use can't in questions in order to request strongly that someone does something.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句时,can 表示礼貌的请求，而 can't 表示强烈请求）

senses.concept_en: You use can as a polite way of interrupting someone or of introducing what you are going to say next.
gloss_zh: （用于有礼貌地打断,或引导要说的话）能,可以

senses.concept_en: You use can with verbs such as 'imagine', 'think', and 'believe' in order to emphasize how you feel about a particular situation.
gloss_zh: （与 imagine, think, believe 等动词连用,用来加强语气）能
senses.register_label: INFORMAL or SPOKEN 非正式或口语

senses.concept_en: You use can in questions with 'how' to indicate that you feel strongly about something.
gloss_zh: （与 how 一起用于疑问句,表示感受强烈）能,能够

senses.concept_en: A can is a metal container in which something such as food, drink, or paint is put. The container is usually sealed to keep the contents fresh.
gloss_zh: （盛放食品、饮料或油漆的）罐子，金属罐，听

senses.concept_en: When food or drink is canned, it is put into a metal container and sealed so that it will remain fresh.
The can is the toilet.
If you are canned, you are dismissed from your job.

ceiling.translation:
n. 天花板
[经] 顶点, 顶线, 上限
ceiling.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: A ceiling is the horizontal surface that forms the top part or roof inside a room.
A ceiling on something such as prices or wages is an official upper limit that cannot be broken.
gloss_zh: （官方定的价格、工资等的）上限，最高限额

senses.concept_en: A ceiling is the greatest height at which a particular aircraft can fly safely.

center.translation:
n. 中心, 中心点, 中锋
a. 中央的, 位在正中的
vt. 集中, 定中心
vi. 居中
[计] 居中; 中央

central.translation:
a. 中央的, 重要的
[医] 中央的, 中心的, 中枢的

senses.concept_en: Something that is central is in the middle of a place or area.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A place that is central is easy to reach because it is in the centre of a city, town, or particular area.
gloss_zh: 位于中央地带的;处于中心的;四通八达的

senses.concept_en: A central group or organization makes all the important decisions that are followed throughout a larger organization or a country.
gloss_zh: 中央的;有最高决策权的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: The central person or thing in a particular situation is the most important one.

derivation.breakdown_zh: centre 中心 + -al 形容词后缀：中心的

change.translation:
n. 变化, 找回的零钱, 找头, 更换
vt. 改变, 更换, 兑换

senses.concept_en: See also:sea change; If there is a change in something, it becomes different.
If you say that something is a change or makes a change, you mean that it is enjoyable because it is different from what you are used to.
If you change from one thing to another, you stop using or doing the first one and start using or doing the second.
When something changes or when you change it, it becomes different.
To change something means to replace it with something new or different.
When you change your clothes or change, you take some or all of your clothes off and put on different ones
A change of clothes is an extra set of clothes that you take with you when you go to stay somewhere or to take part in an activity.
When you change a bed or change the sheets, you take off the dirty sheets and put on clean ones.
When you change a baby or change its nappy or diaper, you take off the dirty one and put on a clean one.
When you change buses, trains, or planes or change, you get off one bus, train, or plane and get on to another in order to continue your journey.
gloss_zh: 转乘，换乘（交通工具）;转车;转机

senses.concept_en: When you change gear or change into another gear, you move the gear lever on a car, bicycle, or other vehicle in order to use a different gear.
Your change is the money that you receive when you pay for something with more money than it costs because you do not have exactly the right amount of money.
See also:small change; Change is coins, rather than paper money.
If you have change for larger notes, bills, or coins, you have the same value in smaller notes, bills, or coins, which you can give to someone in exchange.
When you change money, you exchange it for the same amount of money in a different currency, or in smaller notes, bills, or coins.
See also:cottage cheese;cream cheese;goat cheese;macaroni cheese; Cheese is a solid food made from milk. It is usually white or yellow.

chemical.translation:
n. 化学药品
a. 化学的, 化学上用的

senses.concept_en: Chemical means involving or resulting from a reaction between two or more substances, or relating to the substances that something consists of.
gloss_zh: 化学的;化学反应的;用化学方法生成的

senses.concept_en: Chemicals are substances that are used in a chemical process or made by a chemical process.
gloss_zh: 化学品;化合物;化学制品

choice.translation:
n. 选择, 精选品, 选择权
a. 精选的, 挑三拣四的, 上等的
[计] DOS内部命令:在批处理文件中
该命令用于提示用户作出选择, 决定批处理文件的流程
choice.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If there is a choice of things, there are several of them and you can choose the one you want.
Your choice is someone or something that you choose from a range of things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Choice means of very high quality.

choose.translation:
vt. 选择, 宁愿, 欲
vi. 作出选择, 愿意
[计] 选取

senses.concept_en: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.
If you choose to do something, you do it because you want to or because you feel that it is right.

citizen.translation:
n. 市民, 公民
[法] 公民, 国民, 市民

senses.concept_en: Someone who is a citizen of a particular country is legally accepted as belonging to that country.
The citizens of a town or city are the people who live there.

class.translation:
n. 班级, 阶级, 种类, 课
vt. 分类
[计] 类别; 类; 种类; 类程

senses.concept_en: A class is a group of pupils or students who are taught together.
A class is a course of teaching in a particular subject.
If you do something in class, you do it during a lesson in school.
The students in a school or university who finish their course in a particular year are often referred to as the class of that year.
See also:chattering classes;middle class;upper class;working class; Class refers to the division of people in a society into groups according to their social status.
A class of things is a group of them with similar characteristics.
If someone or something is classed as a particular thing, they are regarded as belonging to that group of things.
If you say that someone or something has class, you mean that they are elegant and sophisticated.
If you describe someone or something as a class person or thing, you mean that they are very good.

clear.translation:
a. 清楚的, 明确的, 澄清的
adv. 清晰地
vt. 澄清, 清除障碍
vi. 放晴, 变清澈
n. 空隙
[计] 清除

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is clear is obvious and impossible to be mistaken about.
gloss_zh: 明显的;显然的;明白无误的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are clear about something, you understand it completely.
gloss_zh: 完全了解的;明白的;清楚的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your mind or your way of thinking is clear, you are able to think sensibly and reasonably, and you are not affected by confusion or by a drug such as alcohol.
gloss_zh: （头脑或思路）清楚的，清晰的，清醒的，不糊涂的

senses.concept_en: To clear your mind or your head means to free it from confused thoughts or from the effects of a drug such as alcohol.
A clear substance is one which you can see through and which has no colour, like clean water.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A clear colour is bright and strong.
If a surface, place, or view is clear, it is free of unwanted objects or obstacles.
gloss_zh: （表面）收拾干净的;（地方）畅通的;（视野）无阻碍的

senses.concept_en: When you clear an area or place or clear something from it, you remove things from it that you do not want to be there.
If something or someone clears the way or the path for something to happen, they make it possible.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If it is a clear day or if the sky is clear, there is no mist, rain, or cloud.
When fog or mist clears, it gradually disappears.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Clear eyes look healthy, attractive, and shining.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your skin is clear, it is healthy and free from spots.
If you say that your conscience is clear, you mean you do not think you have done anything wrong.
If something or someone is clear of something else, it is not touching it or is a safe distance away from it.
gloss_zh: 不接触的;远离的;在安全距离以外的

senses.concept_en: If you drive clear to a place, especially a place that is far away, you go all the way there without delays.
If an animal or person clears an object or clears a certain height, they jump over the object, or over something that height, without touching it.
When a bank clears a cheque or when a cheque clears, the bank agrees to pay the sum of money mentioned on it.
If a course of action is cleared, people in authority give permission for it to happen.
If someone is cleared, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or mistake.

cold.translation:
n. 感冒, 寒冷
a. 寒冷的, 冷淡的, 冷静的
adv. 完全地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is cold has a very low temperature or a lower temperature than is normal or acceptable.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If it is cold, or if a place is cold, the temperature of the air is very low.
Cold weather or low temperatures can be referred to as the cold .

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are cold, your body is at an unpleasantly low temperature.
Cold food, such as salad or meat that has been cooked and cooled, is not intended to be eaten hot.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Cold colours or cold light give an impression of coldness.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A cold person does not show much emotion, especially affection, and therefore seems unfriendly and unsympathetic. If someone's voice is cold, they speak in an unfriendly unsympathetic way.
gloss_zh: 冷淡的;冷酷的;不热情的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A cold trail or scent is one which is old and therefore difficult to follow.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is cold when they are trying to guess the answer to a question or puzzle, you mean that they are thinking about it in the wrong way and are going to give a wrong answer.
If you have a cold, you have a mild, very common illness which makes you sneeze a lot and gives you a sore throat or a cough.

collective.translation:
a. 集体的, 聚集的, 共同的
[医] 集体的, 集合的

senses.concept_en: Collective actions, situations, or feelings involve or are shared by every member of a group of people.
A collective amount of something is the total obtained by adding together the amounts that each person or thing in a group has.
The collective term for two or more types of thing is a general word or expression which refers to all of them.
A collective is a business or farm which is run, and often owned, by a group of people who take an equal share of any profits.

derivation.breakdown_zh: collect 收集 + -ive 形容词后缀：集体的

commerce.translation:
n. 商业, 商务, 贸易
[经] 商业, 贸易, 商务

senses.concept_en: See also:chamber of commerce; Commerce is the activities and procedures involved in buying and selling things.

common.translation:
a. 通常的, 共同的, 通俗的, 公共的
[计] 公用块
common.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is common, it is found in large numbers or it happens often.
If something is common to two or more people or groups, it is done, possessed, or used by them all.
When there are more animals or plants of a particular species than there are of related species, then the first species is called common .
Common is used to indicate that someone or something is of the ordinary kind and not special in any way.

Common decency or common courtesy is the decency or courtesy which most people have. You usually talk about this when someone has not shown these characteristics in their behaviour to show your disapproval of them.
You can use common to describe knowledge, an opinion, or a feeling that is shared by people in general.
gloss_zh: （知识等）众所周知的，共有的，共识的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as common, you mean that they show a lack of taste, education, and good manners.
A common is an area of grassy land, usually in or near a village or small town, where the public is allowed to go.
gloss_zh: （通常指村庄、小镇或其附近的）公共草地

senses.concept_en: The Commons is the same as the House of Commons. The members of the House of Commons can also be referred to as the Commons .
gloss_zh: 同 the House of Commons;（亦指）下议员议员们

community.translation:
n. 社区, 公众, 共有, 共同体
[经] 公众, 共有, 社会

senses.concept_en: The community is all the people who live in a particular area or place.
gloss_zh: （同住一地的人所构成的）社区

senses.concept_en: A particular community is a group of people who are similar in some way.
Community is friendship between different people or groups, and a sense of having something in common.
gloss_zh: （不同人士、团体之间的）友谊，伙伴关系

complete.translation:
a. 完全的, 十足的, 完成的
vt. 完成, 完工, 使圆满
complete.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.
You can use complete to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something and not just part of it.
If something is complete, it contains all the parts that it should contain.
To complete a set or group means to provide the last item that is needed to make it a full set or group.
The complete works of a writer are all their books or poems published together in one book or as a set of books.
If something is complete, it has been finished.
If you complete something, you finish doing, making, or producing it.
If you complete something, you do all of it.
If you complete a form or questionnaire, you write the answers or information asked for in it.
You can use complete to emphasize that someone is skilled at all aspects of a particular activity and is therefore the best example of that kind of person.

cooking.translation:
n. 烹饪
[化] 熬炼; 热炼; 蒸煮

cool.translation:
n. 凉爽, 凉爽的空气
a. 凉爽的, 冷淡的, 冷静的
vi. 冷却, 平息
vt. 使冷却, 使平静

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is cool has a temperature which is low but not very low.
gloss_zh: 凉的;凉爽的;温度不高的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If it is cool, or if a place is cool, the temperature of the air is low but not very low.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Clothing that is cool is made of thin material so that you do not become too hot in hot weather.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Cool colours are light colours which give an impression of coolness.
When something cools or when you cool it, it becomes lower in temperature.
When a feeling or emotion cools, or when you cool it, it becomes less powerful.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that a person or their behaviour is cool, you mean that they are calm and unemotional, especially in a difficult situation.
gloss_zh: （人、行为等）冷静的，沉着的，泰然自若的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that a person or their behaviour is cool, you mean that they are unfriendly or not enthusiastic.
gloss_zh: （人、行为等）冷漠的，冷淡的，不友善的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that a person or their behaviour is cool, you mean that they are fashionable and attractive.
gloss_zh: （人、行为等）酷的，时尚的，吸引人的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is cool about something, you mean that they accept it and are not angry or upset about it.
gloss_zh: 坦然接受的;心平气和的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is cool, you think it is very good.
gloss_zh: 非常好的;特别棒的;绝妙的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use cool to emphasize that an amount or figure is very large, especially when it has been obtained easily.
gloss_zh: （尤指轻易得到的数额）巨大的，整整

senses.concept_en: You use could to indicate that someone had the ability to do something. You use could not or couldn't to say that someone was unable to do something
You use could to indicate that something sometimes happened.
You use could have to indicate that something was a possibility in the past, although it did not actually happen.
gloss_zh: 本能够，本可以（表示某事本有可能发生但却并未发生）

senses.concept_en: You use could to indicate that something is possibly true, or that it may possibly happen.
gloss_zh: （表示某事可能属实或可能发生）可能

senses.concept_en: You use could not or couldn't to indicate that it is not possible that something is true.
You use could to talk about a possibility, ability, or opportunity that depends on other conditions.
gloss_zh: （表示可能性、能力或机会）可能

senses.concept_en: You use could when you are saying that one thing or situation resembles another.
You use could, or couldn't in questions, when you are making offers and suggestions.

You use could in questions when you are making a polite request or asking for permission to do something. Speakers sometimes use couldn't instead of 'could' to show that they realize that their request may be refused.
gloss_zh: （用于礼貌地提出请求或征得许可。当说话者意识到可能被拒绝时，可以用 couldn't 代替 could）能，可以

senses.concept_en: People sometimes use structures with if I could or could I as polite ways of interrupting someone or of introducing what they are going to say next.
gloss_zh: （用以礼貌地打断某人或引出将要说的话）请允许我

senses.concept_en: You use could to say emphatically that someone ought to do the thing mentioned, especially when you are annoyed because they have not done it. You use why couldn't in questions to express your surprise or annoyance that someone has not done something.
gloss_zh: （用以强调某人应该做所提及的事情，尤用于当说话者因为其没做该事而生气时）

senses.concept_en: You use could when you are expressing strong feelings about something by saying that you feel as if you want to do the thing mentioned, although you do not do it.
gloss_zh: （表示想要做某事的强烈感情）

senses.concept_en: You use could after 'if' when talking about something that you do not have the ability or opportunity to do, but which you are imagining in order to consider what the likely consequences might be.
gloss_zh: （用在if后以谈论没有能力或机会做但为考虑可能的结果而设想去做的事）

senses.concept_en: You use could not or couldn't with comparatives to emphasize that someone or something has as much as is possible of a particular quality. For example, if you say 'I couldn't be happier', you mean that you are extremely happy.
gloss_zh: （与比较级连用，强调某物或某人具备某种特征的程度）太…，再…不过

senses.concept_en: In speech, you use how could in questions to emphasize that you feel strongly about something bad that has happened.
gloss_zh: 怎么会（用在疑问句中强调对所发生的不愉快之事的感受）

council.translation:
n. 会议, 委员会
[经] 委员会

senses.pos_zh: 可数集合名词；名称名词
senses.concept_en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.
Council houses or flats are owned by the local council, and people pay rent to live in them.
gloss_zh: （房屋或公寓）地方政府出租的

senses.concept_en: Council is used in the names of some organizations.
In some organizations, the council is the group of people that controls or governs it.
A council is a specially organized, formal meeting that is attended by a particular group of people.

crowd.translation:
n. 群众, 一伙人
vt. 拥挤, 挤满, 挤进

senses.concept_en: A crowd is a large group of people who have gathered together, for example to watch or listen to something interesting, or to protest about something.
A particular crowd is a group of friends, or a set of people who share the same interests or job.
gloss_zh: （志趣相投或工作相同的）一伙人，一帮人

senses.concept_en: When people crowd around someone or something, they gather closely together around them.
If people crowd into a place or are crowded into a place, large numbers of them enter it so that it becomes very full.
If a group of people crowd a place, there are so many of them there that it is full.
If people crowd you, they stand very closely around you trying to see or speak to you, so that you feel uncomfortable.

daily.translation:
a. 每日的, 日常的
adv. 每日地, 日常地
n. 日报

senses.concept_en: If something happens daily, it happens every day.
Daily quantities or rates relate to a period of one day.
A daily is a newspaper that is published every day of the week except Sunday.

danger.translation:
n. 危险, 威胁
[法] 危险, 危险物, 危机

senses.concept_en: Danger is the possibility that someone may be harmed or killed.
A danger is something or someone that can hurt or harm you.
gloss_zh: 危险的事物（或人）；危害;威胁

senses.concept_en: If there is a danger that something unpleasant will happen, it is possible that it will happen.
gloss_zh: （不愉快之事发生的）可能性，风险

decline.translation:
n. 衰退, 跌落, 下降
vt. 使降低, 婉谢
vi. 下降, 衰落, 偏斜
decline.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.
If you decline something or decline to do something, you politely refuse to accept it or do it.
If there is a decline in something, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or quality.

defeat.translation:
n. 败北, 失败
vt. 击败, 使落空
defeat.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you defeat someone, you win a victory over them in a battle, game, or contest.
If a proposal or motion in a debate is defeated, more people vote against it than for it.
If a task or a problem defeats you, it is so difficult that you cannot do it or solve it.
To defeat an action or plan means to cause it to fail.
gloss_zh: 挫败（行动或计划）;使落空

senses.concept_en: Defeat is the experience of being beaten in a battle, game, or contest, or of failing to achieve what you wanted to.

defend.translation:
vt. 防护, 辩护, 防卫
[法] 作...的辩护律师, 辩护, 为...答辩

senses.concept_en: If you defend someone or something, you take action in order to protect them.
If you defend someone or something when they have been criticized, you argue in support of them.
When a lawyer defends a person who has been accused of something, the lawyer argues on their behalf in a court of law that the charges are not true.
When a sports player plays in the tournament which they won the previous time it was held, you can say that they are defending their title.

deputy.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A deputy is the second most important person in an organization such as a business or government department. Someone's deputy often acts on their behalf when they are not there.
In some parliaments or law-making bodies, the elected members are called deputies .

detail.translation:
n. 细节, 详情
vt. 详述, 选派
vi. 画详图
[计] 详细数据

senses.concept_en: The details of something are its individual features or elements.
Details about someone or something are facts or pieces of information about them.
A detail is a minor point or aspect of something, as opposed to the central ones.
You can refer to the small features of something which are often not noticed as detail .
A detail of a picture is a part of it that is printed separately and perhaps made bigger, so that smaller features can be clearly seen.
If you detail things, you list them or give information about them.
If someone is detailed to do a task or job, they are officially ordered to do it.

dirty.translation:
a. 肮脏的, 卑鄙的
vt. 弄脏
vi. 变脏

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is dirty, it is marked or covered with stains, spots, or mud, and needs to be cleaned.
To dirty something means to cause it to become dirty.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe an action as dirty, you disapprove of it and consider it unfair, immoral, or dishonest.
gloss_zh: 卑劣的;卑鄙的;不道德的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something such as a joke, a book, or someone's language as dirty, you mean that it refers to sex in a way that some people find offensive.
gloss_zh: （笑话、书籍、话语等）淫秽的，下流的，黄色的

senses.concept_en: Dirty is used before words of criticism to emphasize that you do not approve of someone or something.
gloss_zh: （用于批评之词前作强调）可恶的，可恨的

derivation.breakdown_zh: dirt 污物 + -y 形容词后缀：脏的

do.translation: v. 做, 进行, 完成

senses.concept_en: Do is used to form the negative of main verbs, by putting 'not' after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.
gloss_zh: （在do之后、主动词的原形之前加 not，构成主动词的否定式）

senses.concept_en: Do is used to form questions, by putting the subject after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.
gloss_zh: （将主语置于do和主动词的原形之间，构成疑问句）

senses.concept_en: Do is used in question tags.
You use do when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing 'do', or giving a negative or positive answer to a question.
gloss_zh: （对含有do的陈述句或疑问句作肯定或否定回答）

senses.concept_en: Do is used with a negative to tell someone not to behave in a certain way.
gloss_zh: （用在否定句中，表示不让某人做出某种举动）

senses.concept_en: Do is used to give emphasis to the main verb when there is no other auxiliary.
gloss_zh: （在没有其他助动词时，用来强调主动词）

senses.concept_en: Do is used as a polite way of inviting or trying to persuade someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （用以礼貌性地邀请或说服某人做某事）

senses.concept_en: Do can be used to refer back to another verb group when you are comparing or contrasting two things, or saying that they are the same.
gloss_zh: （在进行对比、比较或说明两组事物相同时，用来代替前面的动词词组）

senses.concept_en: You use do after 'so' and 'nor' to say that the same statement is true for two people or groups.
gloss_zh: （与 so 或 nor 连用，表示两人或两组事物的情况相同）

senses.concept_en: When you do something, you take some action or perform an activity or task. Do is often used instead of a more specific verb, to talk about a common action involving a particular thing. For example you can say 'do your teeth' instead of 'brush your teeth'.
gloss_zh: 做，干，进行（常用于代替某个具体的动词）

senses.concept_en: Do can be used to stand for any verb group, or to refer back to another verb group, including one that was in a previous sentence.
gloss_zh: （用来代替任何动词词组或前一个句子中的动词词组）

senses.concept_en: You can use do in a clause at the beginning of a sentence after words like 'what' and 'all', to give special emphasis to the information that comes at the end of the sentence.
gloss_zh: （用于句首从句中 what，all等词之后，以强调句尾的信息）

senses.concept_en: If you do a particular thing with something, you use it in that particular way.
If you do something about a problem, you take action to try to solve it.
If an action or event does a particular thing, such as harm or good, it has that result or effect.
gloss_zh: 造成，产生（好的或坏的结果或影响）

senses.concept_en: You can use do to talk about the degree to which a person, action, or event affects or improves a particular situation.
You can talk about what someone or something does to a person to mean that they have a very harmful effect on them.
If you ask someone what they do, you want to know what their job or profession is.
If you are doing something, you are busy or active in some way, or have planned an activity for some time in the future.
If you say that someone or something does well or badly, you are talking about how successful or unsuccessful they are.
If a person or organization does a particular service or product, they provide that service or sell that product.
You can use do when referring to the speed or rate that something or someone achieves or is able to achieve.
If you do a subject, author, or book, you study them at school or college.
If you do a particular person, accent, or role, you imitate that person or accent, or act that role.
You can use do to say that you are able or unable to behave in a particular way.
If someone does drugs, they take illegal drugs.
If you say that something will do or will do you, you mean that there is enough of it or that it is of good enough quality to meet your requirements or to satisfy you.
A do is a party, dinner party, or other social event.
gloss_zh: 宴会;社交聚会;社交活动

down.translation:
a. 向下的
adv. 下, 下去, 降下
prep. 往下, 沿着
n. 丘陵, 软毛, 开阔的高地
[计] 向下, 退下命令

senses.concept_en: To go down something such as a slope or a pipe means to go towards the ground or to a lower level.
If you are a particular distance down something, you are that distance below the top or surface of it.
You use down to say that you are looking or facing in a direction that is towards the ground or towards a lower level.
If you put something down, you put it onto a surface.
If you go or look down something such as a road or river, you go or look along it. If you are down a road or river, you are somewhere along it.
If you are travelling to a particular place, you can say that you are going down to that place, especially if you are going towards the south or to a lower level of land.
gloss_zh: （尤指往南方或往地势低的地方）往，朝

senses.concept_en: If you are down a place, you are at that place. If you go down a place, you go to that place. Some people consider this to be non-standard.
If an amount of something goes down, it decreases. If an amount of something is down, it has decreased and is at a lower level than it was.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are feeling down, you are feeling unhappy or depressed.
gloss_zh: 沮丧的;闷闷不乐的;情绪低落的

senses.concept_en: If something is down on paper, it has been written on the paper.
If a piece of equipment, especially a computer system, is down, it is temporarily not working because of a fault.
gloss_zh: （尤指电脑）死机的，发生故障的

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone downs food or a drink, you mean that they eat or drink it.
If something or someone is downed, they fall to the ground because they have been hurt or damaged in some way.
to down tools see
Down consists of the small, soft feathers on young birds. Down is used to make bed-covers and pillows.
See also:downs; Down is very fine hair.

draw.translation:
vi. 拉, 拖, 拔剑
vt. 拖拉, 挨近, 领取, 打成平局, 引导, 抽签决定, 画, 描写, 制订, 草拟, 吸引
n. 拉, 拖, 拔出, 抽签, 平局
[计] 翻牌, 绘图

senses.concept_en: When you draw, or when you draw something, you use a pencil or pen to produce a picture, pattern, or diagram.
When a vehicle draws somewhere, it moves there smoothly and steadily.
If you draw somewhere, you move there slowly.
If you draw something or someone in a particular direction, you move them in that direction, usually by pulling them gently.
When you draw a curtain or blind, you pull it across a window, either to cover or to uncover it.
If someone draws a gun, knife, or other weapon, they pull it out of its container and threaten you with it.
gloss_zh: 拔出，抽出，掏出（枪、刀等武器）

senses.concept_en: If an animal or vehicle draws something such as a cart, carriage, or another vehicle, it pulls it along.
If you draw a deep breath, you breathe in deeply once.
If you draw on a cigarette, you breathe the smoke from it into your mouth or lungs.
To draw something such as water or energy from a particular source means to take it from that source.
If something that hits you or presses part of your body draws blood, it cuts your skin so that it bleeds.
If you draw money out of a bank, building society, or savings account, you get it from the account so that you can use it.
If you draw a salary or a sum of money, you receive a sum of money regularly.
To draw something means to choose it or to be given it, as part of a competition, game, or lottery.
gloss_zh: （在比赛等中）抽（签）;（在摸彩中）抽（奖）

senses.concept_en: A draw is a competition where people pay money for numbered or named tickets, then some of those tickets are chosen, and the owners are given prizes.
To draw something from a particular thing or place means to take or get it from that thing or place.
If you draw a particular conclusion, you decide that that conclusion is true.
If you draw a comparison, parallel, or distinction, you compare or contrast two different ideas, systems, or other things.
gloss_zh: 作（比较或对比）；加以（区别）

senses.concept_en: If you draw someone's attention to something, you make them aware of it or make them think about it.
If someone or something draws a particular reaction, people react to it in that way.
If something such as a film or an event draws a lot of people, it is so interesting or entertaining that a lot of people go to it.
If someone or something draws you, it attracts you very strongly.
gloss_zh: 使倾心;使动心;强烈吸引

senses.concept_en: If someone will not be drawn or refuses to be drawn, they will not reply to questions in the way that you want them to, or will not reveal information or their opinion.
gloss_zh: 使回答;使透露消息;使说出意见

senses.concept_en: In a game or competition, if one person or team draws with another one, or if two people or teams draw, they have the same number of points or goals at the end of the game.

drive.translation:
n. 驾车, 快车道, 推进力, 驱动, 动力, 击球, 驱动器
vt. 开车, 驱使, 推动, 驾驶
vi. 开车, 猛击, 飞跑
[计] 驱动器

senses.concept_en: When you drive somewhere, you operate a car or other vehicle and control its movement and direction.
If you drive someone somewhere, you take them there in a car or other vehicle.
A drive is a journey in a car or other vehicle.
A drive is a wide piece of hard ground, or sometimes a private road, that leads from the road to a person's house.
gloss_zh: （从马路通往住宅的宽阔）车道

senses.concept_en: If something drives a machine, it supplies the power that makes it work.
Drive is the power supplied by the engine to particular wheels in a car or other vehicle to make the vehicle move.
See also:disk drive; You use drive to refer to the mechanical part of a computer which reads the data on disks and tapes, or writes data onto them.
If you drive something such as a nail into something else, you push it in or hammer it in using a lot of effort.
In games such as cricket, golf, or football, if a player drives a ball somewhere, they kick or hit it there with a lot of force.
In golf, a drive is the first stroke a player makes from the tee.
