If the wind, rain, or snow drives in a particular direction, it moves with great force in that direction.
gloss_zh: （风、雨或雪朝某个方向）吹,卷,刮,冲

senses.concept_en: If you drive people or animals somewhere, you make them go to or from that place.
To drive someone into a particular state or situation means to force them into that state or situation.
The desire or feeling that drives a person to do something, especially something extreme, is the desire or feeling that causes them to do it.
gloss_zh: 驱使，迫使（某人做出极端的事情）

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone has drive, you mean they have energy and determination.
A drive is a very strong need or desire in human beings that makes them act in particular ways.
gloss_zh: 强烈欲望;强烈需求;本能需求

senses.concept_en: A drive is a special effort made by a group of people for a particular purpose.
gloss_zh: （为达到某目的而进行的）努力,运动

senses.concept_en: Drive is used in the names of some streets.
If something happens during a period of time or an event, it happens continuously, or happens several times between the beginning and end of that period or event.
If something develops during a period of time, it develops gradually from the beginning to the end of that period.
An event that happens during a period of time happens at some point or moment in that period.
If you make an effort to do something, you try very hard to do it.
If you say that someone did something with effort or with an effort, you mean it was difficult for them to do.
An effort is a particular series of activities that is organized by a group of people in order to achieve something.
gloss_zh: （为达到某一目的的）有组织的行动，一系列活动

senses.concept_en: If you say that something is an effort, you mean that an unusual amount of physical or mental energy is needed to do it.
gloss_zh: 费力的事;困难的事;劳神的事

senses.concept_en: Eight is the number 8.

engineer.translation:
n. 工程师, 工兵
vt. 设计, 监造, 精明地处理, 策划
engineer.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: See also:chemical engineer;civil engineer;electrical engineer;sound engineer; An engineer is a person who uses scientific knowledge to design, construct, and maintain engines and machines or structures such as roads, railways, and bridges.
An engineer is a person who repairs mechanical or electrical devices.
gloss_zh: 机械修理工;电气修理工；技师

senses.concept_en: An engineer is a person who is responsible for maintaining the engine of a ship while it is at sea.
When a vehicle, bridge, or building is engineered, it is planned and constructed using scientific methods.
gloss_zh: 设计制造（车辆、桥梁、建筑物等）

senses.concept_en: If you engineer an event or situation, you arrange for it to happen, in a clever or indirect way.

enter.translation:
vt. 进入, 参加, 开始, 输入, 回车
vi. 进去, 参加
[计] 输入, 回车

senses.concept_en: When you enter a place such as a room or building, you go into it or come into it.
If you enter an organization or institution, you start to work there or become a member of it.
gloss_zh: 加入;成为…的一员；进入…（工作）

senses.concept_en: If something new enters your mind, you suddenly think about it.
gloss_zh: 突然出现（在头脑中）;掠过（脑海）

senses.concept_en: If it does not enter your head to do, think or say something, you do not think of doing that thing although you should have done.
If someone or something enters a particular situation or period of time, they start to be in it or part of it.
gloss_zh: 开始进入…（状况）;迈入…（时期）

senses.concept_en: If you enter a competition, race, or examination, you officially state that you will compete or take part in it.
gloss_zh: 参加，报名参加（比赛或考试）

senses.concept_en: If you enter someone for a race or competition, you officially state that they will compete or take part in it.
If you enter something in a notebook, register, or financial account, you write it down.
To enter information into a computer or database means to record it there, for example by typing it on a keyboard. 【语法信息】：V n into n 【语法信息】：V n
gloss_zh: （向计算机或数据库中）输入，写入

even.translation:
a. 平坦的, 相等的, 连贯的, 均等的, 公平的, 偶数的, 平均的, 平衡的, 恰好的
vt. 使平坦, 使相等
vi. 变平, 成为相等
adv. 甚至, 实际上, 完全, 十分
n. 偶数, 偶校验
[计] 偶数, 偶校验

senses.concept_en: You use even to suggest that what comes just after or just before it in the sentence is rather surprising.
You use even with comparative adjectives and adverbs to emphasize a quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （与形容词、副词的比较级连用）更加，愈发

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An even measurement or rate stays at about the same level.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An even surface is smooth and flat.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If there is an even distribution or division of something, each person, group, or area involved has an equal amount.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An even contest or competition is equally balanced between the two sides who are taking part.
gloss_zh: （比赛、竞争等）平衡的，不相上下的，势均力敌的

senses.concept_en: If you are even with someone, you do not owe them anything, such as money or a favour.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your voice is even, you are speaking in a very controlled way which makes it difficult for people to tell what your feelings are.
An even number can be divided exactly by the number two.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: See also:evens; If there is an even chance that something will happen, it is no more likely that it will happen than it will not happen.
gloss_zh: （成败机会）各半的，对半的，相等的

event.translation:
n. 事件, 结果, 事情的进程, 竞赛项目
[计] 事件

senses.concept_en: An event is something that happens, especially when it is unusual or important. You can use events to describe all the things that are happening in a particular situation.
gloss_zh: 事件;（尤指）特殊事件，重大事件

senses.concept_en: An event is a planned and organized occasion, for example a social gathering or a sports match.
gloss_zh: （社交聚会、体育比赛等有计划、有组织的）活动

senses.concept_en: An event is one of the races or competitions that are part of an organized occasion such as a sports meeting.
You use every to indicate that you are referring to all the members of a group or all the parts of something and not only some of them.
You use every in order to say how often something happens or to indicate that something happens at regular intervals.
You use every in front of a number when you are saying what proportion of people or things something happens to or applies to.
You can use every before some nouns, for example 'sign', 'effort', 'reason', and 'intention' in order to emphasize what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （用于名词前表示强调）充足的，完全的

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone's every whim, wish, or desire will be satisfied, you are emphasizing that everything they want will happen or be provided.
gloss_zh: （幻想、愿望、欲望等）所有的，全部的

senses.concept_en: If you explain something, you give details about it or describe it so that it can be understood.
If you explain something that has happened, you give people reasons for it, especially in an attempt to justify it.

face.translation:
n. 脸, 面容, 正面, 外观
vt. 面对, 朝, 正视, 面临
vi. 朝, 向
[计] 现场可改变的控制元件

senses.concept_en: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.
If your face is happy, sad, or serious, for example, the expression on your face shows that you are happy, sad, or serious.
The face of a cliff, mountain, or building is a vertical surface or side of it.
gloss_zh: 崖面;山侧;（建筑物的）墙面

senses.concept_en: The face of a clock or watch is the surface with the numbers or hands on it, which shows the time.
If you say that the face of an area, institution, or field of activity is changing, you mean its appearance or nature is changing.
gloss_zh: （地区、机构或活动领域的）外观，面貌

senses.concept_en: If you refer to something as the particular face of an activity, belief, or system, you mean that it is one particular aspect of it, in contrast to other aspects.

If you lose face, you do something which makes you appear weak and makes people respect or admire you less. If you do something in order to save face, you do it in order to avoid appearing weak and losing people's respect or admiration.
If someone or something faces a particular thing, person, or direction, they are positioned opposite them or are looking in that direction.
If you face someone or something, you turn so that you are looking at them.
If you have to face a person or group, you have to stand or sit in front of them and talk to them, although it may be difficult and unpleasant.
If you face or are faced with something difficult or unpleasant, or if it faces you, it is going to affect you and you have to deal with it.
If you face the truth or face the facts, you accept that something is true. If you face someone with the truth or with the facts, you try to make them accept that something is true.
gloss_zh: （使）直面，接受，正视（真理或事实等）

senses.concept_en: If you cannot face something, you do not feel able to do it because it seems so difficult or unpleasant.

fall.translation:
n. 落下, 瀑布, 采伐量, 下降, 落差, 降低, 堕落, 秋天
vi. 倒下, 落下, 来临, 失守, 阵亡, 下跌, 减弱, 倾斜, 垮台, 轮到, 变成, 降低
a. 秋天的

senses.concept_en: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downwards onto or towards the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.
If a person or structure that is standing somewhere falls, they move from their upright position, so that they are then lying on the ground.
See also:rainfall;snowfall; When rain or snow falls, it comes down from the sky.
If you fall somewhere, you allow yourself to drop there in a hurried or disorganized way, often because you are very tired.
gloss_zh: （常因疲乏）一头倒下，一下躺倒

senses.concept_en: If something falls, it decreases in amount, value, or strength.
gloss_zh: （数量）减少;（价值）下降;（力量）减弱

senses.concept_en: If a powerful or successful person falls, they suddenly lose their power or position.
If a place falls in a war or election, an enemy army or a different political party takes control of it.
If someone falls in battle, they are killed.

You can use fall to show that someone or something passes into another state. For example, if someone falls ill, they become ill, and if something falls into disrepair, it is then in a state of disrepair.
If you say that something or someone falls into a particular group or category, you mean that they belong in that group or category.
If the responsibility or blame for something falls on someone, they have to take the responsibility or the blame for it.
If silence or a feeling of sadness or tiredness falls on a group of people, they become silent, sad, or tired.
If a celebration or other special event falls on a particular day or date, it happens to be on that day or date.
gloss_zh: （庆典或特别事件）在，适逢（某日）

senses.concept_en: When light or shadow falls on something, it covers it.
If someone's hair or a garment falls in a certain way, it hangs downwards in that way.
If you say that someone's eyes fell on something, you mean they suddenly noticed it.
When night or darkness falls, night begins and it becomes dark.
You can refer to a waterfall as the falls .
Fall is the season between summer and winter when the weather becomes cooler.
In the Christian religion, the Fall was the occasion when Adam and Eve sinned and God made them leave the Garden of Eden.
gloss_zh: 人类堕落（基督教中指亚当、夏娃违反戒律，被上帝逐出伊甸园）

senses.concept_en: In some sports such as judo and wrestling, a fall is the act of throwing or forcing your opponent to the floor.
gloss_zh: （摔跤中）双肩着地;（柔道中）体落

senses.concept_en: In cricket, when a wicket falls, the team who are fielding get one of the batsmen out.
gloss_zh: （板球中，三柱门）失陷（指击球员出局）

family.translation:
n. 家庭, 家人, 族
a. 家庭的

senses.concept_en: A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.
When people talk about a family, they sometimes mean children.
When people talk about their family, they sometimes mean their ancestors.
You can use family to describe things that belong to a particular family.
You can use family to describe things that are designed to be used or enjoyed by both parents and children.
gloss_zh: 全家共用的;全家共享的

senses.concept_en: A family of animals or plants is a group of related species.

farm.translation:
n. 农场, 农田
vt. 耕种
vi. 种田

senses.concept_en: A farm is an area of land, together with the buildings on it, that is used for growing crops or raising animals, usually in order to sell them.
If you farm an area of land, you grow crops or keep animals on it.
A mink farm or a fish farm, for example, is a place where a particular kind of animal or fish is bred and kept in large quantities in order to be sold.

farmer.translation:
n. 农夫, 农场主
[法] 农民, 农场主, 承包者

senses.concept_en: A farmer is a person who owns or manages a farm.

fear.translation:
n. 恐怖, 害怕, 担心
v. 害怕, 恐惧, 为...担心, 敬畏

senses.concept_en: Fear is the unpleasant feeling you have when you think that you are in danger.
If you fear someone or something, you are frightened because you think that they will harm you.
A fear is a thought that something unpleasant might happen or might have happened.
If you fear something unpleasant or undesirable, you are worried that it might happen or might have happened.
If you say that there is a fear that something unpleasant or undesirable will happen, you mean that you think it is possible or likely.
gloss_zh: （坏事发生的）可能性，机会，几率

senses.concept_en: If you fear for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.
If you have fears for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.
If you fear to do something, you are afraid to do it or you do not wish to do it.
You say that you fear that a situation is the case when the situation is unpleasant or undesirable, and when you want to express sympathy, sorrow, or regret about it.

finish.translation:
n. 完成, 结束, 末道漆, 磨光, 完美
vt. 完成, 结束, 用完, 毁掉
vi. 结束
[计] 完成

senses.concept_en: When you finish doing or dealing with something, you do or deal with the last part of it, so that there is no more for you to do or deal with.
When you finish something that you are making or producing, you reach the end of making or producing it, so that it is complete.
When something such as a course, film, or sale finishes, especially at a planned time, it ends.

You say that someone or something finishes a period of time or an event in a particular way to indicate what the final situation was like. You can also say that a period of time or an event finishes in a particular way.
If someone finishes second, for example, in a race or competition, they are in second place at the end of the race or competition.
To finish means to reach the end of saying something.
The finish of something is the end of it or the last part of it.
The finish of a race is the end of it.
See also:finished; If the surface of something that has been made has a particular kind of finish, it has the appearance or texture mentioned.

first.translation:
adv. 首先, 第一, 优先
a. 第一的
num. 第一
n. 开始, 第一

senses.concept_en: The first thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes before all the others of the same kind.
gloss_zh: 最早的;最先的;第一位的

senses.concept_en: If you do something first, you do it before anyone else does, or before you do anything else.
When something happens or is done for the first time, it has never happened or been done before.
An event that is described as a first has never happened before and is important or exciting.
The first you hear of something or the first you know about it is the time when you first become aware of it.
You use first when you are talking about what happens in the early part of an event or experience, in contrast to what happens later.
In order to emphasize your determination not to do a particular thing, you can say that rather than do it, you would do something else first .
gloss_zh: （强调不愿意做某事）宁可，宁愿

senses.concept_en: You use first when you are about to give the first in a series of items.
The first thing, person, or place in a line is the one that is nearest to you or nearest to the front.
gloss_zh: （一列中）离得最近的，最前面的

senses.concept_en: You use first to refer to the best or most important thing or person of a particular kind.
First is used in the title of the job or position of someone who has a higher rank than anyone else with the same basic job title.
gloss_zh: （用于工作或职位的头衔中）最高的

senses.concept_en: In British universities, a first is an honours degree of the highest standard.
gloss_zh: （英国大学的）优等学位，一级荣誉学位

senses.concept_en: Five is the number 5.
See also:high five; Fives is a British ball game in which you hit a small hard ball with a glove or bat against three walls of a court.
gloss_zh: 墙手球（一种英式球类运动，球小而硬，戴手套或用球拍向场地的三面墙上击球）

fix.translation:
vt. 使固定, 修理, 准备, 安装, 凝视, 牢记, 确定, 整理
vi. 固定, 注视, 确定
n. 困境, 方位, 维修, 贿赂

senses.concept_en: If something is fixed somewhere, it is attached there firmly or securely.
If you fix something, for example a date, price, or policy, you decide and say exactly what it will be.
gloss_zh: 确定，决定，选定（日期、价格、政策等）

senses.concept_en: If you fix something for someone, you arrange for it to happen or you organize it for them.
If you fix something which is damaged or which does not work properly, you repair it.
If you fix a problem or a bad situation, you deal with it and make it satisfactory.
See also:quick fix; You can refer to a solution to a problem as a fix .
If you fix your eyes on someone or something or if your eyes fix on them, you look at them with complete attention.
gloss_zh: （目光）专注于，凝视;目不转睛地看

senses.concept_en: If you fix someone with a particular kind of expression, you look at them in that way.
If you fix your attention on someone or something, you think about them with complete attention.
gloss_zh: 将（注意力）集中在;专心考虑

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is fixed in your mind, you remember them well, for example because they are very important, interesting, or unusual.
gloss_zh: 牢记，铭记，镌刻（在头脑中）

senses.concept_en: If someone fixes a gun, camera, or radar on something, they point it at that thing.
gloss_zh: 把（枪、相机、雷达）对准（或瞄准、指向）

senses.concept_en: If you fix the position of something, you find out exactly where it is, usually by using radar or electronic equipment.
gloss_zh: （通常用雷达或电子设备）找到，弄清，确定（确切位置）

senses.concept_en: If you get a fix on someone or something, you have a clear idea or understanding of them.
If you fix some food or a drink for someone, you make it or prepare it for them.
If you fix your hair, clothes, or make-up, you arrange or adjust them so you look neat and tidy, showing you have taken care with your appearance.
gloss_zh: 整理，收拾（头发、衣服或妆容）

senses.concept_en: If you have your teeth fixed, you have treatment from a dentist to make your teeth even, straight, and white.
If someone fixes a race, election, contest, or other event, they make unfair or illegal arrangements or use deception to affect the result.
gloss_zh: 在（比赛、竞选等活动中）作弊，做手脚，操纵

senses.concept_en: If you accuse someone of fixing prices, you accuse them of making unfair arrangements to charge a particular price for something, rather than allowing market forces to decide it.
An injection of an addictive drug such as heroin can be referred to as a fix .
You can use fix to refer to an amount of something which a person gets or wants and which helps them physically or psychologically to survive.
gloss_zh: （维持身体或心理需要所需的）一个剂量，一定数量

senses.concept_en: If you are in a fix, you are in a difficult situation, especially one that you have caused for yourself.
gloss_zh: （尤指由自己引起的）困境，窘境

senses.concept_en: To fix something such as a dye or photographic image means to treat it with chemicals so that it does not lose its colour or disappear.
If you say that you will fix someone, you mean that you will stop their activities permanently.
See also:fixed;fixings; If you say that you are fixing to do something, you mean that you are planning or intending to do it.

floor.translation:
n. 地板, 楼层, 底部, 底价
vt. 铺地板, 打倒
n. 地面, 地板, 基底
[计] 基底

senses.concept_en: The floor of a room is the part of it that you walk on.
A floor of a building is all the rooms that are on a particular level.
The ocean floor is the ground at the bottom of an ocean. The valley floor is the ground at the bottom of a valley.
The place where official debates and discussions are held, especially between members of parliament, is referred to as the floor .
In a debate or discussion, the floor is the people who are listening to the arguments being put forward but who are not among the main speakers.
The floor of a stock exchange is the large open area where trading is done.
The floor in a place such as a club or disco is the area where people dance.
If you are floored by something, you are unable to respond to it because you are so surprised by it.
See also:floored;flooring;dance floor;first floor;ground floor;shop floor; If someone is floored, especially in boxing, they are hit so hard that they fall over.
gloss_zh: （尤指在拳击比赛中）打倒，击倒

food.translation:
n. 食物, 养料
[医] 食物, 食品

senses.concept_en: See also:convenience food;fast food;health food;junk food;wholefood; Food is what people and animals eat.

for.translation:
prep. 为, 因为, 至于
conj. 因为
[计] DOS批处理命令:对一组参数重复执行指定的命令

senses.concept_en: If something is for someone, they are intended to have it or benefit from it.
If you work or do a job for someone, you are employed by them.
If you speak or act for a particular group or organization, you represent them.
If someone does something for you, they do it so that you do not have to do it.
If you feel a particular emotion for someone, you feel it on their behalf.
If you feel a particular emotion for someone or something, they are the object of that emotion, and you feel it when you think about them.
You use for after words such as 'time', 'space', 'money', or 'energy' when you say how much there is or whether there is enough of it in order to be able to do or use a particular thing.
If something is for sale, hire, or use, it is available to be sold, hired, or used.
You use for when you state or explain the purpose of an object, action, or activity.
You use for after nouns expressing reason or cause.
You can use for to introduce a clause which gives the reason why you made the statement in the main clause.
You can use for to introduce the cause of the fact that you have just mentioned.
For is used in conditional sentences, in expressions such as 'if not for' and 'were it not for', to introduce the only thing which prevents the main part of the sentence from being true.
gloss_zh: （用于条件句中）如果不是为了，要不是

senses.concept_en: You use for to say how long something lasts or continues.
You use for to say how far something extends.
If something is bought, sold, or done for a particular amount of money, that amount of money is its price.
If something is planned for a particular time, it is planned to happen then.
If you do something for a particular occasion, you do it on that occasion or to celebrate that occasion.
If you leave for a particular place or if you take a bus, train, plane, or boat for a place, you are going there.
You use for when you make a statement about something in order to say how it affects or relates to someone, or what their attitude to it is.
After some adjective, noun, and verb phrases, you use for to introduce the subject of the action indicated by the following infinitive verb.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词、名词和动词短语后，引出其后动词不定式的主语）

senses.concept_en: You use for when you say that an aspect of something or someone is surprising in relation to other aspects of them.
gloss_zh: 就…而言（表示相对来说不寻常）

senses.concept_en: If you say that you are for a particular activity, you mean that this is what you want or intend to do.
If you say that something is not for you, you mean that you do not enjoy it or that it is not suitable for you.
If it is for you to do something, it is your responsibility or right to do it.
gloss_zh: （表示负有责任或享有权利）由…

senses.concept_en: If you are for something, you agree with it or support it.
You use for after words such as 'argue', 'case', 'evidence', or 'vote' in order to introduce the thing that is being supported or proved.
gloss_zh: （用于 argue, case, evidence, vote 等词后，引出所支持或被证明之事）

senses.concept_en: For is the preposition that is used after some nouns, adjectives, or verbs in order to introduce more information or to indicate what a quality, thing, or action relates to.
gloss_zh: （置于某些名词、形容词或动词后，引出更多信息或与某性质、事物或行为相关的事物）

senses.concept_en: To be named for someone means to be given the same name as them.
You use for with 'every' when you are stating a ratio, to introduce one of the things in the ratio.
gloss_zh: （与 every 连用，引出比率）每…（就有…）

senses.concept_en: You can use for in expressions such as pound for pound or mile for mile when you are making comparisons between the values or qualities of different things.
gloss_zh: （用于比较）每镑对每镑/每英里对每英里

senses.concept_en: If a word or expression has the same meaning as another word or expression, you can say that the first one is another word or expression for the second one.
You use for in a piece of writing when you mention information which will be found somewhere else.
gloss_zh: （引出可在其他地方找到的信息）至于，对于

senses.concept_en: Forty is the number 40.

When you talk about the forties, you are referring to numbers between 40 and 49. For example, if you are in your forties, you are aged between 40 and 49. If the temperature is in the forties, the temperature is between 40 and 49 degrees.
gloss_zh: 四十多，四十几（指从40至49的数字）

senses.concept_en: The forties is the decade between 1940 and 1949.
gloss_zh: 二十世纪四十年代（指从 1940 年至 1949 年）

four.translation:
num. 四, 四个
[机] 四冲程循环

senses.concept_en: Four is the number 4.
In cricket, if a player hits a four, they score four runs by hitting the ball along the ground so that it crosses the boundary at the edge of the playing area.
A four is a narrow racing boat that is rowed by a team of four people.

free.translation:
a. 自由的, 享受政治权力的, 允许的, 免费的, 丰富的
vt. 释放, 解放, 使自由
adv. 自由地, 免费

senses.concept_en: If something is free, you can have it or use it without paying for it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is free is not restricted, controlled, or limited, for example by rules, customs, or other people.
gloss_zh: 自由的;不受约束的;没有限制的

senses.concept_en: If you free someone of something that is unpleasant or restricting, you remove it from them.
Someone who is free is no longer a prisoner or a slave.
gloss_zh: （人身）自由的;不受监禁（或奴役）的

senses.concept_en: To free a prisoner or a slave means to let them go or release them from prison.
If someone or something is free of or free from an unpleasant thing, they do not have it or they are not affected by it.
See also:duty-free;interest-free;tax-free; A sum of money or type of goods that is free of tax or duty is one that you do not have to pay tax on.
To free someone or something means to make them available for a task or function that they were previously not available for.
If you have a free period of time or are free at a particular time, you are not working or occupied then.
gloss_zh: 空闲的;有空的;不上班的;不在忙的

senses.concept_en: If something such as a table or seat is free, it is not being used or occupied by anyone, or is not reserved for anyone to use.
gloss_zh: 不在用的;无人使用的;未被占用的

senses.concept_en: If you get something free or if it gets free, it is no longer trapped by anything or attached to anything.
gloss_zh: 松开的;脱开的;未缚住的;未固定的

senses.concept_en: If you free someone or something, you remove them from the place in which they have been trapped or become fixed.
gloss_zh: 松开;解开;使不再缚住（或固定）

senses.concept_en: When someone is using one hand or arm to hold or move something, their other hand or arm is referred to as their free one.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is free with something such as advice or money, you mean that they give a lot of it, sometimes when it is not wanted.
gloss_zh: 慷慨的;大手大脚的;过分给予的

freeze.translation:
vi. 冻结, 冷冻, 僵硬, 楞住
vt. 使结冰, 使冻住, 使呆住
n. 结冰, 凝固
[计] 冻结

senses.concept_en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.
If you freeze something such as food, you preserve it by storing it at a temperature below freezing point. You can also talk about how well food freezes .
If something such as a pipe or machine freezes, it becomes blocked or stiff with ice or frozen liquid.
gloss_zh: （管子、机器等因液体结冰）冻得堵塞，冻牢

senses.concept_en: When it freezes outside, the temperature falls below freezing point.
If you freeze, you feel extremely cold.
If someone who is moving freezes, they suddenly stop and become completely still and quiet.
If the government or a company freeze things such as prices or wages, they state officially that they will not allow them to increase for a fixed period of time.
If a government freezes a plan or process, they state officially that they will not allow it to continue for a period of time.

See also:freezing;frozen; If someone in authority freezes something such as a bank account, fund, or property, they obtain a legal order which states that it cannot be used or sold for a particular period of time.
gloss_zh: 冻结，查封（银行账户、基金、财产等）

fresh.translation:
a. 新鲜的, 新奇的, 另外的, 淡的, 精神饱满的, 冒失的
adv. 最新地, 刚刚
n. 开始, 泛滥

senses.concept_en: A fresh thing or amount replaces or is added to a previous thing or amount.
gloss_zh: 新的;替代的;另外的;外加的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is fresh has been done, made, or experienced recently.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Fresh food has been picked or produced recently, and has not been preserved, for example by being frozen or put in a tin.
gloss_zh: （食物）新鲜的，非冷冻的,非罐装的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as fresh, you like it because it is new and exciting.
gloss_zh: 新颖的;别致的;有独创性的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as fresh, you mean that it is pleasant, bright, and clean in appearance.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something smells, tastes, or feels fresh, it is clean or cool.
Fresh water is water that is not salty, for example the water from rivers or lakes.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that the weather is fresh, you mean that it is fairly cold and windy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Fresh colours are clear, bright, and fairly light.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has a fresh face or complexion, their skin looks healthy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you feel fresh, you feel full of energy and enthusiasm.
gloss_zh: 精神抖擞的;精力充沛的

senses.concept_en: Fresh paint is not yet dry.
If you are fresh from a particular place or experience, you have just come from that place or you have just had that experience. You can also say that someone is fresh out of a place.

from.translation: prep. 从, 来自, 根据

senses.concept_en: If something comes from a particular person or thing, or if you get something from them, they give it to you or they are the source of it.
Someone who comes from a particular place lives in that place or originally lived there. Something that comes from a particular place was made in that place.
A person from a particular organization works for that organization.
If someone or something moves or is moved from a place, they leave it or are removed, so that they are no longer there.
If you take one thing or person from another, you move that thing or person so that they are no longer with the other or attached to the other.
If you take something from an amount, you reduce the amount by that much.
From is used in expressions such as away from or absent from to say that someone or something is not present in a place where they are usually found.
If you return from a place or an activity, you return after being in that place or doing that activity.
If you are back from a place or activity, you have left it and have returned to your former place.
If you see or hear something from a particular place, you are in that place when you see it or hear it.
If something hangs or sticks out from an object, it is attached to it or held by it.
You can use from when giving distances. For example, if a place is fifty miles from another place, the distance between the two places is fifty miles.
If a road or railway line goes from one place to another, you can travel along it between the two places.
From is used, especially in the expression made from, to say what substance has been used to make something.
You can use from when you are talking about the beginning of a period of time.
You say from one thing to another when you are stating the range of things that are possible, or when saying that the range of things includes everything in a certain category.
If something changes from one thing to another, it stops being the first thing and becomes the second thing.
You use from after some verbs and nouns when mentioning the cause of something.
You use from when you are giving the reason for an opinion.
From is used after verbs with meanings such as 'protect', 'free', 'keep', and 'prevent' to introduce the action that does not happen, or that someone does not want to happen.
gloss_zh: （用于 protect, free, keep, prevent 等动词后）免于

full.translation:
n. 全部, 完整
a. 充满的, 完全的, 丰富的, 完美的, 丰满的, 详尽的
adv. 完全地, 整整, 十分
vt. 把(衣服等)缝得宽松, 漂洗
[计] 完整

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is full, it contains as much of a substance or as many objects as it can.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a place or thing is full of things or people, it contains a large number of them.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone or something is full of a particular feeling or quality, they have a lot of it.
gloss_zh: 充满（某一情感或特质）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You say that a place or vehicle is full when there is no space left in it for any more people or things.
gloss_zh: 满员的;没有空位（或空间）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your hands or arms are full, you are carrying or holding as much as you can carry.
gloss_zh: （手或胳膊）占着的，拿满了的，挂满了的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you feel full, you have eaten or drunk so much that you do not want anything else.
You use full before a noun to indicate that you are referring to all the details, things, or people that it can possibly include.
Full is used to describe a sound, light, or physical force which is being produced with the greatest possible power or intensity.
gloss_zh: （声音、光线、力气等）最大（强度）的

senses.concept_en: You use full to emphasize the completeness, intensity, or extent of something.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A full statement or report contains a lot of information and detail.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone has or leads a full life, you approve of the fact that they are always busy and do a lot of different things.
You use full to emphasize the force or directness with which someone or something is hit or looked at.
You use full to refer to something which gives you all the rights, status, or importance for a particular position or activity, rather than just some of them.
gloss_zh: （所拥有的权利、地位或重要性）完整的，正式的

senses.concept_en: A full flavour is strong and rich.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a part of someone's body as full, you mean that it is rounded and rather large.
gloss_zh: （身体某一部位）丰满的，圆润的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A full skirt or sleeve is wide and has been made from a lot of fabric.
When there is a full moon, the moon appears as a bright, complete circle.

gather.translation:
n. 集合, 聚集
vi. 聚集, 集合, 渐增
vt. 使聚集, 搜集, 积聚

senses.concept_en: If people gather somewhere or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.
If you gather things, you collect them together so that you can use them.
If you gather information or evidence, you collect it, especially over a period of time and after a lot of hard work.
gloss_zh: （尤指经过一段时间的辛苦工作）收集，搜集（情报、证据等）

senses.concept_en: If something gathers speed, momentum, or force, it gradually becomes faster or more powerful.
gloss_zh: 逐渐增加（速度、动力、力量等）

senses.concept_en: When you gather something such as your strength, courage, or thoughts, you make an effort to prepare yourself to do something.
gloss_zh: 集中（精力、思想等）；鼓起（勇气）；振作（精神）

senses.concept_en: You use gather in expressions such as 'I gather' and 'as far as I can gather' to introduce information that you have found out, especially when you have found it out in an indirect way.
gloss_zh: （用于引出已发现的信息，尤其是间接获得的信息）据我所知，据我了解
collocations: as far as I can gather

senses.concept_en: If you gather fabric or cloth, you make a row of very small folds in it by sewing a thread through it and then pulling the thread tight.

give.translation:
n. 弹性, 适应性
vt. 给, 授予, 供给, 产生, 发表, 付出, 献出, 让出
vi. 捐赠, 支持不住, 让步

senses.concept_en: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as 'She smiled'.
gloss_zh: （与表示身体动作的名词连用，表示该动作）

senses.concept_en: You use give to say that a person does something for another person. For example, if you give someone a lift, you take them somewhere in your car.
You use give with nouns that refer to information, opinions, or greetings to indicate that something is communicated. For example, if you give someone some news, you tell it to them.
gloss_zh: （与表示信息、意见、问候等的名词连用）提供，给出，传递，告诉

senses.concept_en: You use give to say how long you think something will last or how much you think something will be.
People use give in expressions such as I don't give a damn to show that they do not care about something.
If someone or something gives you a particular idea or impression, it causes you to have that idea or impression.
gloss_zh: 使产生（某种想法或印象）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something gives you a particular physical or emotional feeling, it makes you experience it.
gloss_zh: 使身体感到…；使产生（某种情绪）

senses.concept_en: If you give a performance or speech, you perform or speak in public.
If you give something thought or attention, you think about it, concentrate on it, or deal with it.
If you give a party or other social event, you organize it.
If you give someone something that you own or have bought, you provide them with it, so that they have it or can use it.
If you give someone something that you are holding or that is near you, you pass it to them, so that they are then holding it.
To give someone or something a particular power or right means to allow them to have it.
If something gives, it collapses or breaks under pressure.
See also:given; You say that you are given to understand or believe that something is the case when you do not want to say how you found out about it, or who told you.

glass.translation:
n. 玻璃, 玻璃杯, 透镜
vt. 装玻璃于, 反射, 反映
vi. 成玻璃状

senses.concept_en: Glass is a hard transparent substance that is used to make things such as windows and bottles.
A glass is a container made from glass, which you can drink from and which does not have a handle.
Glass is used to mean objects made of glass, for example drinking containers and bowls.
Glasses are two lenses in a frame that some people wear in front of their eyes in order to help them see better.

go.translation:
vi. 去, 走, 达到, 运转, 查阅, 消失, 结束, 放弃, 花费, 流传, 趋于, 打算, 剩下
vt. 以...打赌, 对付, 忍受, 出产, 为被捕者出(保释金)
n. 去, 尝试, 进行

senses.concept_en: When you go somewhere, you move or travel there.
When you go, you leave the place where you are.
You use go to say that someone leaves the place where they are and does an activity, often a leisure activity.

When you go to do something, you move to a place in order to do it and you do it. You can also go and do something, and in American English, you can go do something. However, you always say that someone went and did something.
gloss_zh: 去做…（可用go to do, 也可用go and do，美国英语中还可用go do，然而一般说 went and did）

senses.concept_en: If you go to school, work, or church, you attend it regularly as part of your normal life.
When you say where a road or path goes, you are saying where it begins or ends, or what places it is in.
You can use go in expressions such as 'don't go telling everybody', in order to express disapproval of the kind of behaviour you mention, or to tell someone not to behave in that way.
gloss_zh: （用于否定表达中，表示对所提到行为不赞成或不允许某人有这种行为）

senses.concept_en: You can use go with words like 'further' and 'beyond' to show the degree or extent of something.
gloss_zh: （与further,beyond等词连用，表示某事的进展或程度）

senses.concept_en: If you say that a period of time goes quickly or slowly, you mean that it seems to pass quickly or slowly.
If you say where money goes, you are saying what it is spent on.
If you say that something goes to someone, you mean that it is given to them.
If someone goes on television or radio, they take part in a television or radio programme.
gloss_zh: 上，参加（电视或电台节目）

senses.concept_en: If something goes, someone gets rid of it.
If someone goes, they leave their job, usually because they are forced to.
If something goes into something else, it is put in it as one of the parts or elements that form it.
If something goes in a particular place, it fits in that place or should be put there because it is the right size or shape.
If something goes in a particular place, it belongs there or should be put there, because that is where you normally keep it.
If you say that one number goes into another number a particular number of times, you are dividing the second number by the first.
If one of a person's senses, such as their sight or hearing, is going, it is getting weak and they may soon lose it completely.
If something such as a light bulb or a part of an engine is going, it is no longer working properly and will soon need to be replaced.
gloss_zh: （灯泡、引擎等）损坏，报废，无法正常运转

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is going or has gone, you are saying in an indirect way that they are dying or are dead.

You can use go to say that a person or thing changes to another state or condition. For example, if someone goes crazy, they become crazy, and if something goes green, it changes colour and becomes green.
You can use go when indicating whether or not someone wears or has something. For example, if someone goes barefoot, they do not wear any shoes.
You can use go before adjectives beginning with 'un-' to say that something does not happen. For example, if something goes unheard, nobody hears it.
gloss_zh: （用在以un开头的形容词之前表示某事没有发生）

senses.concept_en: You use go to talk about the way something happens. For example, if an event or situation goes well, it is successful.
If a machine or device is going, it is working.
If a bell goes, it makes a noise, usually as a signal for you to do something.
If something goes with something else, or if two things go together, they look or taste nice together.
You use go to introduce something you are quoting. For example, you say the story goes or the argument goes just before you quote all or part of it.
You use go when indicating that something makes or produces a sound. For example, if you say that something goes 'bang', you mean it produces the sound 'bang'.
You can use go instead of 'say' when you are quoting what someone has said or what you think they will say.
gloss_zh: 说（代替say，表示引述他人的话或认为他们要说的话）

senses.concept_en: A go is an attempt at doing something.
If it is your go in a game, it is your turn to do something, for example to play a card or move a piece.

goal.translation:
n. 目标, 终点, 得分, 球门, 守门员
vi. 攻门, 射门得分
goal.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: In games such as football, netball or hockey, the goal is the space into which the players try to get the ball in order to score a point for their team.
gloss_zh: （足球、无板篮球或曲棍球等的）球门

senses.concept_en: In games such as football or hockey, a goal is when a player gets the ball into the goal, or the point that is scored by doing this.
gloss_zh: （足球或曲棍球赛等的）进球，进球得分

senses.concept_en: Something that is your goal is something that you hope to achieve, especially when much time and effort will be needed.

good.translation:
n. 善行, 好处, 利益
a. 好的, 优良的, 上等的, 愉快的, 有益的, 好心的, 慈善的, 虔诚的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Good means pleasant or enjoyable.
gloss_zh: 愉快的；有趣的；令人愉快的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Good means of a high quality, standard, or level.
gloss_zh: 好的；高品质的；高水准的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are good at something, you are skilful and successful at doing it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a piece of news, an action, or an effect as good, you mean that it is likely to result in benefit or success.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A good idea, reason, method, or decision is a sensible or valid one.
gloss_zh: 合情理的；理由充足的；有根据的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that it is good that something should happen or good to do something, you mean it is desirable, acceptable, or right.
gloss_zh: 令人满意的；合适的；正确的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A good estimate or indication of something is an accurate one.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you get a good deal or a good price when you buy or sell something, you receive a lot in exchange for what you give.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is good for a person or organization, it benefits them.
If something is done for the good of a person or organization, it is done in order to benefit them.
If someone or something is no good or is not any good, they are not satisfactory or are of a low standard.
If you say that doing something is no good or does not do any good, you mean that doing it is not of any use or will not bring any success.
Good is what is considered to be right according to moral standards or religious beliefs.
gloss_zh: 善行；美德；合乎道德的行为

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is good is morally correct in their attitudes and behaviour.
gloss_zh: 正直的；高尚的；品行好的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone, especially a child, who is good obeys rules and instructions and behaves in a socially correct way.
gloss_zh: （尤指小孩）乖的，恭顺的，有礼貌的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is good is kind and thoughtful.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is in a good mood is cheerful and pleasant to be with.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If people are good friends, they get on well together and are very close.
A person's good eye, arm, or leg is the one that is healthy and strong, if the other one is injured or weak.
gloss_zh: （身体部位或器官）健全的，强健的

senses.concept_en: You use good to emphasize the great extent or degree of something.

grain.translation:
n. 谷粒, 颗粒, 谷类, 纹理, 本质
v. (使)成谷粒
grain.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A grain of wheat, rice, or other cereal crop is a seed from it.
Grain is a cereal crop, especially wheat or corn, that has been harvested and is used for food or in trade.
A grain of something such as sand or salt is a tiny hard piece of it.
A grain of a quality is a very small amount of it.
The grain of a piece of wood is the direction of its fibres. You can also refer to the pattern of lines on the surface of the wood as the grain.

great.translation:
a. 大的, 非常的, 主要的, 重大的, 崇高的, 伟大的
adv. 顺利地, 得意地
n. 全部, 大人物, 大师

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use great to describe something that is very large. Great is more formal than big .

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Great means large in amount or degree.
gloss_zh: （数量或程度）大的，巨大的，超乎寻常的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use great to describe something that is important, famous, or exciting.
gloss_zh: 重大的；闻名的；令人激动的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe someone who is successful and famous for their actions, knowledge, or skill as great .
gloss_zh: 伟大的；著名的； 卓越的；优秀的

senses.concept_en: The greats in a particular subject or field of activity are the people who have been most successful or famous in it.
The greats of popular modern music are records that have been successful and that continue to be popular.
If you describe someone or something as great, you approve of them or admire them.
gloss_zh: 美妙的；好极了的；了不起的

senses.concept_en: If you feel great, you feel very healthy, energetic, and enthusiastic.
gloss_zh: 十分健康的；精力旺盛的；充满热情的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use great in order to emphasize the size or degree of a characteristic or quality.
You say great in order to emphasize that you are pleased or enthusiastic about something.
You say great in order to emphasize that you are angry or annoyed about something.
gloss_zh: 哼，这倒好（表示气愤、恼火等）

senses.concept_en: See also:greater; Great is used as part of the name of a species of plant or animal when there is another species of the same plant or animal which is smaller and has different characteristics.
gloss_zh: （用于同类动植物中较大者的名称前）大

green.translation:
n. 绿色, 绿色颜料
a. 绿色的, 未成熟的, 新鲜的, 青春的, 无经验的, 脸色发青的

senses.concept_en: Green is the colour of grass or leaves.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A place that is green is covered with grass, plants, and trees and not with houses or factories.
gloss_zh: 长满青草的；绿油油的；碧绿的

senses.concept_en: Green issues and political movements relate to or are concerned with the protection of the environment.
gloss_zh: 环境保护的；主张环境保护的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone or something is green, you mean they harm the environment as little as possible.
gloss_zh: 有利于环境的；环保的；绿色的

senses.concept_en: Greens are members of green political movements.
gloss_zh: 绿党成员（主张环境保护）

senses.concept_en: A green is a smooth, flat area of grass around a hole on a golf course.
A green is an area of land covered with grass, especially in a town or in the middle of a village.
gloss_zh: （尤指城市或村庄中心的）草坪，绿地

senses.concept_en: Green is used in the names of places that contain or used to contain an area of grass.
gloss_zh: （用于有绿地或过去有绿地的地方中）

senses.concept_en: You can refer to the cooked leaves of vegetables such as spinach or cabbage as greens .

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe fruit and vegetables as green when they are unripe and not ready to be eaten.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is green, you mean that they have had very little experience of life or a particular job.
gloss_zh: 缺乏经验的；不成熟的；幼稚的

gross.translation:
n. 总数, 总量
a. 总共的, 未打折扣的, 恶劣的, 粗野的
vt. 总共收入

senses.concept_en: You use gross to describe something unacceptable or unpleasant to a very great amount, degree, or intensity.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone's speech or behaviour is gross, you think it is very rude or unacceptable.
gloss_zh: （言语、行为）极端粗俗的，下流的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as gross, you think it is very unpleasant.
gloss_zh: 令人不快的；让人恶心的；令人厌恶的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as gross, you mean that they are extremely fat and unattractive.
Gross means the total amount of something, especially money, before any has been taken away.
Gross means the total amount of something, after all the relevant amounts have been added together.
Gross means the total weight of something, including its container or wrapping.
If a person or a business grosses a particular amount of money, they earn that amount of money before tax has been taken away.
gloss_zh: （扣除税金前）总共赚得，总收入为

senses.concept_en: A gross is a group of 144 things.

ground.translation:
n. 土地, 战场, 场地, 地面, 范围
a. 土地的, 地面上的
vt. 放在地上, 使搁浅, 打基础, 给...以训练
vi. 搁浅, 落地, 根据, 基于
a. 磨过的
grind的过去式和过去分词

senses.concept_en: The ground is the surface of the earth.
If you say that something takes place on the ground, you mean it takes place on the surface of the earth and not in the air.
The ground is the soil and rock on the earth's surface.
You can refer to land as ground, especially when it has very few buildings or when it is considered to be special in some way.
gloss_zh: （尤指建筑物极少或具有某种特性的）土地

senses.concept_en: You can use ground to refer to an area of land, sea, or air which is used for a particular activity.
A ground is an area of land which is specially designed and made for playing sport or for some other activity. In American English grounds is also used.
gloss_zh: 运动场，…场（美国英语中亦作grounds）

senses.concept_en: The grounds of a large or important building are the garden or area of land which surrounds it.
gloss_zh: （大型或重要建筑周围的）场地，庭院，花园

senses.concept_en: You can use ground to refer to a place or situation in which particular methods or ideas can develop and be successful.
gloss_zh: （适于方法、思想等发展的）地方

senses.concept_en: You can use ground in expressions such as on shaky ground and the same ground to refer to a particular subject, area of experience, or basis for an argument.
Ground is used in expressions such as gain ground ,lose ground, and give ground in order to indicate that someone gets or loses an advantage.
If something is grounds for a feeling or action, it is a reason for it. If you do something on the grounds of a particular thing, that thing is the reason for your action.
If an argument, belief, or opinion is grounded in something, that thing is used to justify it.
gloss_zh: 以…为根据；建立在…基础上

senses.concept_en: If an aircraft or its passengers are grounded, they are made to stay on the ground and are not allowed to take off.
When parents ground a child, they forbid them to go out and enjoy themselves for a period of time, as a punishment.
If a ship or boat is grounded or if it grounds, it touches the bottom of the sea, lake, or river it is on, and is unable to move off.
The ground in an electric plug or piece of electrical equipment is the wire through which electricity passes into the ground and which makes the equipment safe.
Ground meat has been cut into very small pieces in a machine.
Ground is the past tense and past participle of grind .

guide.translation:
n. 引导者, 导游, 指南, 路标
vt. 指导, 支配, 管理, 带领, 操纵
vi. 任向导
[计] 辅助线

senses.concept_en: In Britain, the Guides is an organization for girls which teaches them to become practical and independent. The Guides used to be called the Girl Guides. In the United States, there is a similar organization called the Girl Scouts.
gloss_zh: （英国的）女童子军（美国为Girl Scout）

senses.concept_en: In Britain, a Guide is a girl who is a member of the Guides.

hall.translation: n. 门厅, 走廊, 会堂
hall.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: The hall in a house or flat is the area just inside the front door, into which some of the other rooms open.
A hall in a building is a long passage with doors into rooms on both sides of it.
See also:city hall;town hall; A hall is a large room or building which is used for public events such as concerts, exhibitions, and meetings.
If students live in hall in British English, or in a hall in American English, they live in a university or college building called a hall of residence.
Hall is sometimes used as part of the name of a large house in the country.
gloss_zh: （乡间）大庄园，府第（用于住宅名称中）

senses.concept_en: Hall is sometimes used as part of the name of a large building, especially one where public events or concerts take place
gloss_zh: 厅，会堂，礼堂（尤用于礼堂、音乐厅等名称中）

hard.translation:
a. 坚硬的, 硬的, 难的, 艰苦的, 困难的, 坚固的, 猛烈的, 艰难的, 结实的, 确实的
adv. 坚硬地, 努力地, 辛苦地, 接近地, 猛烈地, 牢固地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is hard is very firm and stiff to touch and is not easily bent, cut, or broken.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is hard is very difficult to do or deal with.
If you work hard doing something, you are very active or work intensely, with a lot of effort.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hard work involves a lot of activity and effort.
If you look, listen, or think hard, you do it carefully and with a great deal of attention.
If you strike or take hold of something hard, you strike or take hold of it with a lot of force.
You can use hard to indicate that something happens intensely and for a long time.
gloss_zh: 强烈地;猛烈的;长时间地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a person or their expression is hard, they show no kindness or sympathy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are hard on someone, you treat them severely or unkindly.
gloss_zh: 苛刻的;严厉的;不友善的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is hard on a person or thing, you mean it affects them in a way that is likely to cause them damage or suffering.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you have a hard life or a hard period of time, your life or that period is difficult and unpleasant for you.
gloss_zh: （生活、一段日子）艰难的，艰苦的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A hard winter or a hard frost is a very cold one.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hard colours or sounds are harsh or bright and unpleasant to see or hear.
gloss_zh: （颜色）刺目的，晃眼的;（声音）刺耳的，难听的

senses.concept_en: Hard evidence or facts are definitely true and do not need to be questioned.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hard water contains a lot of calcium compounds that stop soap making bubbles and sometimes appear as a deposit in kettles and baths.
gloss_zh: （水质）硬的（指含钙化合物较多）

senses.concept_en: Hard drugs are very strong illegal drugs such as heroin or cocaine.
In phonetics, a hard sound is one such as 'c' or 'g' as pronounced in the words 'cat' or 'give', and not as in the words 'cinema' or 'general'.

harmful.translation: a. 有害的, 伤害的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is harmful has a bad effect on something else, especially on a person's health.
gloss_zh: 有害的;（尤指）有损健康的

have.translation:
vt. 有, 怀有, 拿, 进行
aux. 已经

senses.concept_en: You use the forms have and has with a past participle to form the present perfect tense of verbs.
gloss_zh: （have 和 has 与过去分词连用构成动词的现在完成时）

senses.concept_en: You use the form had with a past participle to form the past perfect tense of verbs.
gloss_zh: （had 与过去分词连用构成动词的过去完成时）

senses.concept_en: Have is used in question tags.
You use have when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing 'have', 'has', or 'had', or answering a question.
gloss_zh: （用于对带有 have,has 或 had 的句子作肯定或否定回答）

senses.concept_en: The form having with a past participle can be used to introduce a clause in which you mention an action which had already happened before another action began.
gloss_zh: （having 和过去分词连用，所引导的分句中提到的动作发生在另一个动作开始之前）

senses.concept_en: You can use have followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would be possible to use the same word as a verb. For example, you can say 'I had a look at the photos' instead of 'I looked at the photos.'
gloss_zh: （have 后接名词代替该名词作动词的用法，描述某一动作或事件）
collocations: I had a look at the photos

senses.concept_en: In normal spoken or written English, people use have with a wide range of nouns to talk about actions and events, often instead of a more specific verb. For example people are more likely to say 'we had ice cream' or 'he's had a shock' than 'we ate ice cream', or 'he's suffered a shock'.
gloss_zh: （在英语口语或书面语中，have可以和很多名词连用以代替某个具体的动词，描述某一动作或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use have to say that someone or something owns a particular thing, or when you are mentioning one of their qualities or characteristics.
If you have something to do, you are responsible for doing it or must do it.

You can use have instead of 'there is' to say that something exists or happens. For example, you can say 'you have no alternative' instead of 'there is no alternative', or 'he had a good view from his window' instead of 'there was a good view from his window'.
gloss_zh: （用于代替 there is, 表示某事物存在或发生了某事）
collocations: he had a good view from his window

senses.concept_en: If you have something such as a part of your body in a particular position or state, it is in that position or state.
If you have something done, someone does it for you or you arrange for it to be done.
If someone has something unpleasant happen to them, it happens to them.
If you have someone do something, you persuade, cause, or order them to do it.
If someone has you by a part of your body, they are holding you there and they are trying to hurt you or force you to go somewhere.
gloss_zh: 抓住（某人身体的某部位）

senses.concept_en: If you have something from someone, they give it to you.
If you have an illness or disability, you suffer from it.
If a woman has a baby, she gives birth to it. If she is having a baby, she is pregnant.
You can use have in expressions such as 'I won't have it' or 'I'm not having that', to mean that you will not allow or put up with something.

he.translation:
pron. 他
n. 男孩, 男人, 雄性动物

senses.concept_en: You use he to refer to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, he is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use 'he or she' or 'they'.
gloss_zh: （书面英语中泛指人）他，她（有些人不喜欢这种用法，更倾向于使用 he or she 或 they）

senses.concept_en: In some religions, He is used to refer to God.

head.translation:
n. 头, 头脑, 领袖, 脑袋, 最前的部分
vt. 为首, 朝向, 前进, 用头顶
vi. 朝特定方向行进, (作物)结穗
a. 头的, 在顶端的, 主要的
[计] 磁头; 冲头

senses.concept_en: Your head is the top part of your body, which has your eyes, mouth, and brain in it.
You can use head to refer to your mind and your mental abilities.
The head of a line of people or vehicles is the front of it, or the first person or vehicle in the line.
gloss_zh: （队伍中的）领头位置;队首;排头

senses.concept_en: If someone or something heads a line or procession, they are at the front of it.
If something heads a list or group, it is at the top of it.
The head of something is the highest or top part of it.
The head of something long and thin is the end which is wider than or a different shape from the rest, and which is often considered to be the most important part.
The head of a school is the teacher who is in charge.
The head of a company or organization is the person in charge of it and in charge of the people in it.
gloss_zh: （公司、组织的）负责人，领导人，首脑，长，主任

senses.concept_en: If you head a department, company, or organization, you are the person in charge of it.
The head of an infected spot is its white or yellow centre.
The head on a glass of beer is the layer of small bubbles that form on the top of the beer.
You can use head to say how many animals of a particular type a farmer has. For example, if they have fifty head of cattle, they have fifty cows.
If you have a bad head, you have a headache.
If you toss a coin and it comes down heads, you can see the side of the coin which has a picture of a head on it.
gloss_zh: （硬币的）有人头像的一面，正面

senses.concept_en: If you are heading for a particular place, you are going towards that place. In American English, you can also say that you are headed for a particular place.
gloss_zh: 朝着（某一地点）行进（美国英语中亦作 are headed）

senses.concept_en: If something or someone is heading for a particular result, the situation they are in is developing in a way that makes that result very likely. In American English, you can also say that something or someone is headed for a particular result.
gloss_zh: 很可能要遭受，会招致（美国英语中亦作 is headed for）

senses.concept_en: If a piece of writing is headed a particular title, it has that title written at the beginning of it.
If you head a ball in football, you hit it with your head in order to make it go in a particular direction.

healthy.translation:
a. 健康的, 有益健康的, 卫生的
[医] 健康的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is healthy is well and is not suffering from any illness.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a feature or quality that you have is healthy, it makes you look well or shows that you are well.
gloss_zh: 显示健康的;反映健康的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is healthy is good for your health.
gloss_zh: 有益于健康的;促进健康的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A healthy organization or system is successful.
gloss_zh: （机构或体系）兴旺的，运作良好的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A healthy amount of something is a large amount that shows success.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you have a healthy attitude about something, you show good sense.

derivation.breakdown_zh: health 健康 + -y 形容词后缀：健康的

hear.translation:
vt. 听到, 倾听, 听说, 审理
vi. 听见, 听

senses.concept_en: When you hear a sound, you become aware of it through your ears.
If you hear something such as a lecture or a piece of music, you listen to it.
If you say that you can hear someone saying something, you mean that you are able to imagine hearing it.
When a judge or a court of law hears a case, or evidence in a case, they listen to it officially in order to make a decision about it.
gloss_zh: （法官或法庭）审理（案件），听取（证词）

senses.concept_en: If you hear from someone, you receive a letter or telephone call from them.
In a debate or discussion, if you hear from someone, you listen to them giving their opinion or information.
gloss_zh: （辩论或讨论中）倾听（意见或情况）

senses.concept_en: If you hear some news or information about something, you find out about it by someone telling you, or from the radio or television.
If you have heard of something or someone, you know about them, but not in great detail.

heavy.translation:
a. 重的, 巨大的, 沉重的, 笨重的, 过度的
adv. 沉重地
n. 重物, 严肃角色

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is heavy weighs a lot.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use heavy to ask or talk about how much someone or something weighs.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Heavy means great in amount, degree, or intensity.
gloss_zh: 大量的;重大的;严重的;强烈的;剧烈的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is heavy is solid in appearance or structure, or is made of a thick material.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy substance is thick in texture.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy meal is large in amount and often difficult to digest.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is heavy with things is full of them or loaded with them.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a person's breathing is heavy, it is very loud and deep.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy movement or action is done with a lot of force or pressure.
A heavy machine or piece of military equipment is very large and very powerful.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a period of time or a schedule as heavy, you mean it involves a lot of work.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Heavy work requires a lot of strength or energy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is heavy on another thing, you mean that it uses a lot of that thing or too much of that thing.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Air or weather that is heavy is unpleasantly still, hot, and damp.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person's face as heavy, you mean that it looks sad, tired, or unfriendly.
gloss_zh: （表情）沉痛的，疲惫呆滞的，阴郁的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your heart is heavy, you are sad about something.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A situation that is heavy is serious and difficult to cope with.
A heavy is a large strong man who is employed to protect a person or place, often by using violence.
gloss_zh: （雇作保镖或打手的）彪形大汉

hesitate.translation: vi. 犹豫, 迟疑, 踌躇, 支吾, 停顿

senses.concept_en: If you hesitate, you do not speak or act for a short time, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried about what you are going to say or do.
If you hesitate to do something, you delay doing it or are unwilling to do it, usually because you are not certain it would be right. If you do not hesitate to do something, you do it immediately.

You can use hesitate in expressions such as 'don't hesitate to call me' or 'don't hesitate to contact us' when you are telling someone that they should do something as soon as it needs to be done and should not worry about disturbing other people.
gloss_zh: 尽管给我打电话/ 尽管和我们联系

high.translation:
n. 高度, 高处
a. 高的, 高级的, 主要的, 高尚的, 高原的, 高音的, 昂贵的, 傲慢的
adv. 高度地, 奢侈地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is high extends a long way from the bottom to the top when it is upright. You do not use high to describe people, animals, or plants.
gloss_zh: 高的（不用于形容人或动植物）

senses.concept_en: You use high to talk or ask about how much something upright measures from the bottom to the top.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is high, it is a long way above the ground, above sea level, or above a person or thing.
gloss_zh: （相对地面、海平面、其他人或物）高的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use high to indicate that something is great in amount, degree, or intensity.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a food or other substance is high in a particular ingredient, it contains a large amount of that ingredient.
If something reaches a high of a particular amount or degree, that is the greatest it has ever been.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is a high priority or is high on your list, you mean that you consider it to be one of the most important things you have to do or deal with.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is high in a particular profession or society, or has a high position, has a very important position and has great authority and influence.
You can use high to describe something that is advanced or complex.
If you aim high, you try to obtain or to achieve the best that you can.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has a high reputation, or people have a high opinion of them, people think they are very good in some way, for example at their work.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If the quality or standard of something is high, it is very good indeed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has high principles, they are morally good.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A high sound or voice is close to the top of a particular range of notes.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When a river is high, it contains much more water than usual.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your spirits are high, you feel happy and excited.
If someone is high on drink or drugs, they are affected by the alcoholic drink or drugs they have taken.
gloss_zh: 喝醉了的;（吸毒后）极度兴奋的

senses.concept_en: A high is a feeling or mood of great excitement or happiness.

his.translation:
pron. 他的
[化] 组氨酸

senses.concept_en: You use his to indicate that something belongs or relates to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, his is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use 'his or her' or 'their'.
gloss_zh: （书面英语中泛指人）他的，她的（有些人不喜欢这种说法，更倾向于使用 his or her 或 their）

senses.concept_en: In some religions, His is used to refer to God.

hold.translation:
n. 把握, 把持力, 柄, 控制, 掌握, 监禁
vt. 保存, 握住, 拿住, 占据, 持有, 拥有
vi. 支持, 持续, 有效
n. 保留
[计] 保留

senses.concept_en: When you hold something, you carry or support it, using your hands or your arms.
Hold is used in expressions such as grab hold of ,catch hold of, and get hold of, to indicate that you close your hand tightly around something, for example to stop something moving or falling.
When you hold someone, you put your arms round them, usually because you want to show them how much you like them or because you want to comfort them.
gloss_zh: （通常为表示喜爱或安慰而）拥抱，抱住

senses.concept_en: If you hold someone in a particular position, you use force to keep them in that position and stop them from moving.
A hold is a particular way of keeping someone in a position using your own hands, arms, or legs.
gloss_zh: （使某人不得动弹的）抓住，夹住

senses.concept_en: When you hold a part of your body, you put your hand on or against it, often because it hurts.
When you hold a part of your body in a particular position, you put it into that position and keep it there.
gloss_zh: 使（身体部位）保持（某种姿势）

senses.concept_en: If one thing holds another in a particular position, it keeps it in that position.
If one thing is used to hold another, it is used to store it.
In a ship or aeroplane, a hold is a place where cargo or luggage is stored.
If a place holds something, it keeps it available for reference or for future use.
If something holds a particular amount of something, it can contain that amount.
If you can hold your drink, you are able to drink large quantities of alcohol without becoming ill or getting drunk.
If a vehicle holds the road well, it remains in close contact with the road and can be controlled safely and easily.
Hold is used with words and expressions indicating an opinion or belief, to show that someone has a particular opinion or believes that something is true.
Hold is used with words such as 'fear' or 'mystery' to indicate someone's feelings towards something, as if those feelings were a characteristic of the thing itself.
gloss_zh: 带给人，使人感到（害怕、神秘等）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'office', 'power', and 'responsibility' to indicate that someone has a particular position of power or authority.
gloss_zh: 担任（职务）;掌握（权力）;负有（责任）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'permit', 'degree', or 'ticket' to indicate that someone has a particular document that allows them to do something.
gloss_zh: 持有（许可、票证等）;拥有（学位等）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'party', 'meeting', 'talks', 'election', and 'trial' to indicate that people are organizing a particular activity.
gloss_zh: 举行（聚会、会议、会谈、选举、审判等）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'conversation', 'interview', and 'talks' to indicate that two or more people meet and discuss something.
See also:holding; Hold is used with nouns such as 'shares' and 'stock' to indicate that someone owns a particular proportion of a business.
Hold is used with words such as 'lead' or 'advantage' to indicate that someone is winning or doing well in a contest.
Hold is used with nouns such as 'attention' or 'interest' to indicate that what you do or say keeps someone interested or listening to you.
gloss_zh: 吸引住（注意力）;保持（兴趣）

senses.concept_en: If you hold someone responsible, liable, or accountable for something, you will blame them if anything goes wrong.
If someone holds you in a place, they keep you there as a prisoner and do not allow you to leave.
If people such as an army or a violent crowd hold a place, they control it by using force.
If you have a hold over someone, you have power or control over them, for example because you know something about them you can use to threaten them or because you are in a position of authority.
gloss_zh: （因握有某人把柄或掌握权力而形成的）控制力，支配力

senses.concept_en: If you ask someone to hold, or to hold the line, when you are answering a telephone call, you are asking them to wait for a short time, for example so that you can find the person they want to speak to.
gloss_zh: （接电话时让对方）稍等，不要挂断

senses.concept_en: If you hold telephone calls for someone, you do not allow people who phone to speak to that person, but take messages instead.
gloss_zh: 代接（电话）并向受话人转告通话内容

senses.concept_en: If something holds at a particular value or level, or is held there, it is kept at that value or level.
If you hold a sound or musical note, you continue making it.
If you hold something such as a train, a lift, or an elevator, you delay it.
If an offer or invitation still holds, it is still available for you to accept.
If a good situation holds, it continues and does not get worse or fail.
If an argument or theory holds, it is true or valid, even after close examination.
If part of a structure holds, it does not fall or break although there is a lot of force or pressure on it.
If laws or rules hold, they exist and remain in force.
If you say that you hold to a particular opinion or belief, you are stating firmly that you continue to have that opinion or belief.
If you hold to a promise or to high standards of behaviour, you keep that promise or continue to behave according to those standards.
gloss_zh: 遵守，恪守（承诺或高尚的行为准则）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something holds you to a promise or to high standards of behaviour, they make you keep that promise or those standards.
gloss_zh: 使遵守，使恪守（承诺或高尚的行为准则）

hot.translation:
a. 热的, 热心的, 辣的, 热情的, 激动的, 猛烈的, 紧迫的
adv. 热, 紧迫地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is hot has a high temperature.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hot is used to describe the weather or the air in a room or building when the temperature is high.
gloss_zh: 天气热的;气温高的;炎热的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are hot, you feel as if your body is at an unpleasantly high temperature.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use hot to talk or ask about how high the temperature of something is.
Hot food is intended to be eaten as soon as it is cooked, as opposed to food that you eat when it has cooled or that you do not cook at all.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can say that food is hot when it has a strong, burning taste caused by chillies, pepper, or ginger.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A hot issue or topic is one that is very important at the present time and is receiving a lot of publicity.
gloss_zh: （议题、话题）热门的，受到广泛关注的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hot news is new, recent, and fresh.
gloss_zh: （消息）刚发布的，最新的，新近的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use hot to describe something that is very exciting and that many people want to see, use, obtain, or become involved with.
gloss_zh: 风行的;走红的;炙手可热的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use hot to describe something that no one wants to deal with, often because it has been illegally obtained and is very valuable or famous.
gloss_zh: （常指非法获得的贵重或知名物品）烫手的，难以销赃的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe a situation that is created by a person's behaviour or attitude as hot when it is unpleasant and difficult to deal with.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A hot contest is one that is intense and involves a great deal of activity and determination.
gloss_zh: （比赛）激烈的，双方全力以赴的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a person or team is the hot favourite, people think that they are the one most likely to win a race or competition.
gloss_zh: 被看好的;最有望获胜的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: See also:hot-tempered; Someone who has a hot temper gets angry very quickly and easily.

illustration.translation:
n. 例证, 插图
[化] 插图
