senses.concept_en: An illustration is an example or a story which is used to make a point clear.
An illustration in a book is a picture, design, or diagram.

derivation.breakdown_zh: illustrate 说明 + -ation 名词后缀：插图说明

in.translation:
prep. 在...期间, 在...之内, 处于...之中, 从事于, 按照, 穿着
adv. 进入, 朝里, 在里面, 在屋里
a. 在里面的, 在朝的
n. 执政者, 交情

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is in something else is enclosed by it or surrounded by it. If you put something in a container, you move it so that it is enclosed by the container.
If something happens in a place, it happens there.
If you are in, you are present at your home or place of work.
When someone comes in, they enter a room or building.
If a train, boat, or plane has come in or is in, it has arrived at a station, port, or airport.
When the sea or tide comes in, the sea moves towards the shore rather than away from it.
Something that is in a window, especially a shop window, is just behind the window so that you can see it from outside.
When you see something in a mirror, the mirror shows an image of it.
If you are dressed in a piece of clothing, you are wearing it.
Something that is covered or wrapped in something else has that thing over or round its surface.
If there is something such as a crack or hole in something, there is a crack or hole on its surface.
If something is in a book, film, play, or picture, you can read it or see it there.
gloss_zh: 在（书、电影、戏剧、图片）之中

senses.concept_en: If you are in something such as a play or a race, you are one of the people taking part.
Something that is in a group or collection is a member of it or part of it.
You use in to specify a general subject or field of activity.
If something happens in a particular year, month, or other period of time, it happens during that time.
If something happens in a particular situation, it happens while that situation is going on.
If you do something in a particular period of time, that is how long it takes you to do it.
If something will happen in a particular length of time, it will happen after that length of time.
You use in to indicate roughly how old someone is. For example, if someone is in their fifties, they are between 50 and 59 years old.
You use in to indicate roughly how many people or things do something.
You use in to express a ratio, proportion, or probability.
If something or someone is in a particular state or situation, that is their present state or situation.
You use in to indicate the feeling or desire which someone has when they do something, or which causes them to do it.
gloss_zh: 带着，充满（某种情感或愿望）

senses.concept_en: If a particular quality or ability is in you, you naturally have it.
You use in when saying that someone or something has a particular quality.
You use in to indicate how someone is expressing something.
You use in in expressions such as in a row or in a ball to describe the arrangement or shape of something.
gloss_zh: （表示排列或形状）成一排/呈球形

senses.concept_en: If something is in a particular colour, it has that colour.
You use in to specify which feature or aspect of something you are talking about.
If you say that something is in, or is the in thing, you mean it is fashionable or popular.
gloss_zh: 时髦的;流行的;受欢迎的

senses.concept_en: You use in with a present participle to indicate that when you do something, something else happens as a result.

inside.translation:
n. 内部, 内脏, 内幕
a. 内部的, 秘密的, 户内的
adv. 在里面
prep. 在...之内

senses.concept_en: Something or someone that is inside a place, container, or object is in it or is surrounded by it.
The inside of something is the part or area that its sides surround or contain.
You can say that someone is inside when they are in prison.
On a wide road, the inside lane is the one which is closest to the edge of the road.
gloss_zh: （马路车道）靠近路边的，慢（道）的

senses.concept_en: Inside information is obtained from someone who is involved in a situation and therefore knows a lot about it.
If you are inside an organization, you belong to it.
Your insides are your internal organs, especially your stomach.
If you say that someone has a feeling inside, you mean that they have it but have not expressed it.
If you do something inside a particular time, you do it before the end of that time.

derivation.breakdown_zh: side 侧 + in- 在内：内部

installation.translation:
n. 安装, 装置, 就职
[医] 结构, 装置, 设立

senses.concept_en: See also:install; An installation is a place that contains equipment and machinery which are being used for a particular purpose.

derivation.breakdown_zh: install 安装 + -ation 名词后缀：安装过程

instead.translation: adv. 作为替代, 反而

senses.concept_en: If you do not do something, but do something else instead, you do the second thing and not the first thing, as the result of a choice or a change of behaviour.

instinct.translation:
n. 本能, 直觉
a. 充满着的

senses.concept_en: Instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.
If you have an instinct for something, you are naturally good at it or able to do it.
If it is your instinct to do something, you feel that it is right to do it.
Instinct is a feeling that you have that something is the case, rather than an opinion or idea based on facts.

it.translation:
pron. 它
[计] 信息论, 输入终端, 智能终端, 内捕获

senses.concept_en: You use it to refer to an object, animal, or other thing that has already been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 它（指物体、动物或上文已提及的其他事物）

senses.concept_en: You use it to refer to a child or baby whose sex you do not know or whose sex is not relevant to what you are saying.
You use it to refer in a general way to a situation that you have just described.
You use it before certain nouns, adjectives, and verbs to introduce your feelings or point of view about a situation.
gloss_zh: （用于某些名词、形容词、动词前说明对某情况的感受、观点）

senses.concept_en: You use it in passive clauses which report a situation or event.
gloss_zh: （用于被动句中引出一个情况或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use it with some verbs that need a subject or object, although there is no noun that it refers to.
gloss_zh: （与动词连用,作形式主语或宾语）

senses.concept_en: You use it as the subject of 'be', to say what the time, day, or date is.
gloss_zh: （用作 be动词的主语,指钟点、星期、日期）

senses.concept_en: You use it as the subject of a link verb to describe the weather, the light, or the temperature.
gloss_zh: （用作系动词的主语，描述天气、光线或温度）

senses.concept_en: You use it when you are telling someone who you are, or asking them who they are, especially at the beginning of a phone call. You also use it in statements and questions about the identity of other people.
gloss_zh: （尤用于刚接通电话时询问、告知身份）

senses.concept_en: When you are emphasizing or drawing attention to something, you can put that thing immediately after it and a form of the verb 'be'.
gloss_zh: （与动词 be 连用，强调突出某物）

item.translation:
n. 项目, 条款, 一则, 项
[计] 项

senses.concept_en: See also:collector's item; An item is one of a collection or list of objects.
An item is one of a list of things for someone to do, deal with, or talk about.
An item is a report or article in a newspaper or magazine, or on television or radio.
gloss_zh: 一篇报道（或文章）;（新闻等的）一条,一则

senses.concept_en: If you say that two people are an item, you mean that they are having a romantic or sexual relationship.

keep.translation:
n. 生计, 维持, 保持
vt. 保持, 保存, 遵守, 看守, 整理, 维持, 履行, 经营, 拘留, 记帐
vi. 保持, 继续不断

senses.concept_en: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it.
If you keep or you are kept in a particular position or place, you remain in it.

If you keep off something or keep away from it, you avoid it. If you keep out of something, you avoid getting involved in it. You can also say that you keep someone off ,away from or out of something.
If someone or something keeps you from a particular action, they prevent you from doing it.
If you try to keep from doing something, you try to stop yourself from doing it.
If you keep something from someone, you do not tell them about it.
If you keep doing something, you do it repeatedly or continue to do it.
Keep is used with some nouns to indicate that someone does something for a period of time or continues to do it. For example, if you keep a grip on something, you continue to hold or control it.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词连用，表示持续一段时间或继续做某事）持续，继续（持有或控制）

senses.concept_en: If you keep something, you continue to have it in your possession and do not throw it away, give it away, or sell it.
If you keep something in a particular place, you always have it or store it in that place so that you can use it whenever you need it.
When you keep something such as a promise or an appointment, you do what you said you would do.
If you keep a record of a series of events, you write down details of it so that they can be referred to later.
If you keep yourself or keep someone else, you support yourself or the other person by earning enough money to provide food, clothing, money, and other necessary things.
Someone's keep is the cost of food and other things that they need in their daily life.
If you keep animals, you own them and take care of them.
If you keep a business such as a small shop or hotel, you own it and manage it.
If someone or something keeps you, they delay you and make you late.
If food keeps for a certain length of time, it stays fresh and suitable to eat for that time.
You can say or ask how someone is keeping as a way of saying or asking whether they are well.
gloss_zh: （用于询问健康状况）保持健康

senses.concept_en: A keep is the main tower of a medieval castle, in which people lived.

kind.translation:
n. 种类, 性质, 方式
a. 亲切的, 仁慈的, 和蔼的

senses.concept_en: If you talk about a particular kind of thing, you are talking about one of the types or sorts of that thing.
If you refer to someone's kind, you are referring to all the other people that are like them or that belong to the same class or set.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is kind behaves in a gentle, caring, and helpful way towards other people.
gloss_zh: 慈祥的；体贴的；乐于助人的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use kind in expressions such as please be so kind as to and would you be kind enough to in order to ask someone to do something in a firm but polite way.
gloss_zh: 请…，…可以吗（表示坚定且客气地请求某人做某事）
collocations: please be so kind as to
would you be kind enough to

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is kind emphasizes the good qualities in something, and perhaps makes it appear better than it really is.
gloss_zh: 突出优点的；使胜过实物的

last.translation:
a. 最后的, 末尾的, 最近的
vi. 持续, 支持, 维持
vt. 使维持, 够...用
adv. 最后, 后来
n. 最后, 末尾, 鞋楦头

senses.concept_en: You use last in expressions such as last Friday ,last night, and last year to refer, for example, to the most recent Friday, night, or year.
gloss_zh: （表示最近过去的）刚过去的星期五/昨晚/去年

senses.concept_en: The last event, person, thing, or period of time is the most recent one.
If something last happened on a particular occasion, that is the most recent occasion on which it happened.
The last thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes after all the others of the same kind.
If you do something last, you do it after everyone else does, or after you do everything else.
If you are the last to do or know something, everyone else does or knows it before you.
Last is used to refer to the only thing, person, or part of something that remains.
You use last before numbers to refer to a position that someone has reached in a competition after other competitors have been knocked out.
gloss_zh: （竞赛中）最后留下的，排位在前的

senses.concept_en: You can use last to indicate that something is extremely undesirable or unlikely.
gloss_zh: 最不想要的；最不可能的

senses.concept_en: The last you see of someone or the last you hear of them is the final time that you see them or talk to them.
If an event, situation, or problem lasts for a particular length of time, it continues to exist or happen for that length of time.
gloss_zh: 持续，延续，维持（一段时间）

senses.concept_en: If something lasts for a particular length of time, it continues to be able to be used for that time, for example because there is some of it left or because it is in good enough condition.
gloss_zh: 够用，保持可用状态（一段时间）

senses.concept_en: You can use last in expressions such as last the game ,last the course, and last the week, to indicate that someone manages to take part in an event or situation right to the end, especially when this is very difficult for them.

leader.translation:
n. 领导者, 社论, 指挥, 领袖, 领唱者, 前导字符
[计] 前导字符

senses.concept_en: The leader of a group of people or an organization is the person who is in control of it or in charge of it.
The leader at a particular point in a race or competition is the person who is winning at that point.
gloss_zh: （比赛或竞赛中的）领先者，占先者

senses.concept_en: The leader among a range of products or companies is the one that is most successful.
gloss_zh: （产品或公司中的）首屈一指者，佼佼者

senses.concept_en: The leader of an orchestra is the most senior violin player, who acts as a deputy to the conductor.
The leader of an orchestra is the conductor.
A leader in a newspaper is a piece of writing which gives the editor's opinion on an important news item.
A leader in a newspaper is the most important story in it.

leak.translation:
n. 漏洞, 漏处, 漏出, 泄漏
vi. 漏, 泄漏
vt. 使渗漏
leak.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If a container leaks, there is a hole or crack in it which lets a substance such as liquid or gas escape. You can also say that a container leaks a substance such as liquid or gas.
A leak is a crack, hole, or other gap that a substance such as a liquid or gas can pass through.
If a secret document or piece of information leaks or is leaked, someone lets the public know about it.

life.translation:
n. 生活, 生命, 人生, 世事, 生物, 寿命, 一生, 生命力, 灵魂, 无期徒刑
[医] 生活, 生存, 生命, 寿命

senses.concept_en: Life is the quality which people, animals, and plants have when they are not dead, and which objects and substances do not have.
You can use life to refer to things or groups of things which are alive.
If you refer to someone's life, you mean their state of being alive, especially when there is a risk or danger of them dying.
gloss_zh: （尤指处于危险之中的）生命，性命

senses.concept_en: Someone's life is the period of time during which they are alive.
You can use life to refer to a period of someone's life when they are in a particular situation or job.
You can use life to refer to particular activities which people regularly do during their lives.
You can use life to refer to the events and experiences that happen to people while they are alive.
If you know a lot about life, you have gained many varied experiences, for example by travelling a lot and meeting different kinds of people.
You can use life to refer to the things that people do and experience that are characteristic of a particular place, group, or activity.
gloss_zh: （有关特定地方、团体或活动的）生活

senses.concept_en: A person, place, book, or film that is full of life gives an impression of excitement, energy, or cheerfulness.
A life of a person is a book or film which tells the story of their life.
If someone is sentenced to life, they are sentenced to stay in prison for the rest of their life or for a very long time.
The life of something such as a machine, organization, or project is the period of time that it lasts for.
gloss_zh: （机器等的）使用期，有效期；（组织、项目等的）存在期

senses.concept_en: In art, life refers to the producing of drawings, paintings, or sculptures that represent actual people, objects, or places, rather than images from the artist's imagination.
A listener is a person who listens to the radio or to a particular radio programme.
gloss_zh: （电台广播的）收听者，听众之一

senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as a good listener, you mean that they listen carefully and sympathetically to you when you talk, for example about your problems.

local.translation:
a. 地方性的, 当地的, 局部的, 乡土的, 本地的
n. 当地居民, 本地新闻, 局部
[计] 本地的; 局部

senses.concept_en: Local means existing in or belonging to the area where you live, or to the area that you are talking about.
gloss_zh: 本地的；本地的；地方性的

senses.concept_en: Local government is elected by people in one area of a country and controls aspects such as education, housing, and transport within that area.
Your local is a pub which is near where you live and where you often go for a drink.
gloss_zh: （常去的）邻近小酒馆，本地酒吧

senses.concept_en: A local anaesthetic or condition affects only a small area of your body.

logical.translation:
a. 合乎逻辑的, 合理的
[法] 逻辑的, 符合逻辑的

senses.concept_en: In a logical argument or method of reasoning, each step must be true if the step before it is true.
gloss_zh: 逻辑（上）的；（论证或推理方法）符合逻辑的

senses.concept_en: The logical conclusion or result of a series of facts or events is the only one which can come from it, according to the rules of logic.
gloss_zh: （结论或结果）逻辑上必然的，顺理成章的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is logical seems reasonable or sensible in the circumstances.

machine.translation:
n. 机器, 机械装置, 机构, 自动售货机, 机械般工作的人
vt. 以机器制造

senses.concept_en: A machine is a piece of equipment which uses electricity or an engine in order to do a particular kind of work.
If you machine something, you make it or work on it using a machine.
gloss_zh: 用机器制造;用机器加工

senses.concept_en: You can use machine to refer to a large and well-controlled system or organization.
If you say that someone is a machine, you mean that they are so tired or bored that they do their work without thinking.
gloss_zh: （由于工作过于劳累或乏味）机械般工作的人，做工作不动脑筋的人

major.translation:
n. 主修课, 成年人, 陆军少校
a. 主要的, 较多的, 大部分的, 成年的, 严重的
vi. 主修
[计] 主要, 主要刻度
major.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use major when you want to describe something that is more important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation.
gloss_zh: 较重要的;较重大的;主要的

senses.pos_zh: 可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词
senses.concept_en: A major is an officer who is one rank above captain in the British army or the United States army, air force, or marines.
gloss_zh: （英国）陆军（或海军陆战队）少校;（美国）陆军（或空军、海军陆战队）少校

senses.concept_en: At a university or college in the United States, a student's major is the main subject that they are studying.
gloss_zh: （美国大学中的）主修课程，专业

senses.concept_en: At a university or college in the United States, if a student is, for example, a geology major, geology is the main subject they are studying.
gloss_zh: （美国大学中）主修…的学生，…专业的学生

senses.concept_en: If a student at a university or college in the United States majors in a particular subject, that subject is the main one they study.
In music, a major scale is one in which the third note is two tones higher than the first.
A major is a large or important company.
The majors are groups of professional sports teams that compete against each other, especially in American baseball.
gloss_zh: 职业体育总会;（尤指美国）职业棒球联合总会，职业棒球大联盟

senses.concept_en: A major is an important sporting competition, especially in golf or tennis.
gloss_zh: 大型体育比赛;（尤指高尔夫球或网球）大赛

make.translation:
vt. 制造, 安排, 创造, 构成, 使得, 产生, 造成, 整理, 布置, 引起, 到达, 进行
vi. 开始, 前进, 增大, 被制造, 被处理
n. 制造, 构造, 性情

senses.concept_en: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.
gloss_zh: （与大量名词连用，表示做动作、说某事等）做出，作出

senses.concept_en: You can use make with certain nouns to indicate that someone does something well or badly. For example, if you make a success of something, you do it successfully, and if you make a mess of something, you do it very badly.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词连用）把…做（好），把…搞（糟）

senses.concept_en: If you make as if to do something or make to do something, you behave in a way that makes it seem that you are just about to do it.
gloss_zh: 摆出…的姿态;做出…的样子

senses.concept_en: In cricket, if a player makes a particular number of runs, they score that number of runs. In baseball or American football, if a player makes a particular score, they achieve that score.
gloss_zh: （在板球、棒球、橄榄球比赛中）得（分）

senses.concept_en: If something makes you do something, it causes you to do it.
If you make someone do something, you force them to do it.

You use make to talk about causing someone or something to be a particular thing or to have a particular quality. For example, to make someone a star means to cause them to become a star, and to make someone angry means to cause them to become angry.
gloss_zh: 使成为（某种人或物）;使具有（某种特性）

senses.concept_en: If you say that one thing or person makes another seem, for example, small, stupid, or good, you mean that they cause them to seem small, stupid, or good in comparison, even though they are not.
If you make yourself understood, heard, or known, you succeed in getting people to understand you, hear you, or know that you are there.
gloss_zh: 使自己（被理解、听见、知晓等）

senses.concept_en: If you make someone something, you appoint them to a particular job, role, or position.
If you make something into something else, you change it in some way so that it becomes that other thing.
To make a total or score a particular amount means to increase it to that amount.
gloss_zh: 使（总数）升为;使（分数）达到

senses.concept_en: When someone makes a friend or an enemy, someone becomes their friend or their enemy, often because of a particular thing they have done.
To make something means to produce, construct, or create it.
If someone makes a film or television programme, they are involved in creating or producing it.
gloss_zh: 拍摄（电影）;制作（电视节目）

senses.concept_en: If you make a meal or a drink, you prepare it.
If you make a note or list, you write something down in that form.
If you make rules or laws, you decide what these should be.
If you make money, you get it by working for it, by selling something, or by winning it.
If something makes something else, it is responsible for the success of that thing.
gloss_zh: （某事物）使（其他事物）变得成功

senses.concept_en: The make of something such as a car or radio is the name of the company that made it

You can use make to say that someone or something has the right qualities for a particular task or role. For example, if you say that someone will make a good politician, you mean that they have the right qualities to be a good politician.
If people make a particular pattern such as a line or a circle, they arrange themselves in this way.
You can use make to say what two numbers add up to.
If someone makes a particular team or makes a particular high position, they do so well that they are put in that team or get that position.
gloss_zh: 成为…的一员;加入;谋得（高级职务）

senses.concept_en: If you make a place in or by a particular time, you get there in or by that time, often with some difficulty.
You use make it when saying what you calculate or guess an amount to be.
You use make it when saying what time your watch says it is.

market.translation:
n. 市场, 交易, 集市, 推销地区, 行情, 市面, 销路
vt. 在市场上交易, 使上市, 销售
vi. 在市场上买卖

senses.concept_en: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold, usually outdoors.
The market for a particular type of thing is the number of people who want to buy it, or the area of the world in which it is sold.
gloss_zh: 需求量;市场需求;顾客群;行销地区

senses.concept_en: The market refers to the total amount of a product that is sold each year, especially when you are talking about the competition between the companies who sell that product.
gloss_zh: （尤用于谈论同行业竞争时）年销售量，市场总额

senses.concept_en: If you talk about a market economy, or the market price of something, you are referring to an economic system in which the prices of things depend on how many are available and how many people want to buy them, rather than prices being fixed by governments.
To market a product means to organize its sale, by deciding on its price, where it should be sold, and how it should be advertised.
gloss_zh: 营销;推销；进行市场推广

senses.concept_en: The job market or the labour market refers to the people who are looking for work and the jobs available for them to do.
The stock market is sometimes referred to as the market .

meat.translation:
n. 肉, 餐, 食物
[经] 肉类

senses.concept_en: Meat is flesh taken from a dead animal that people cook and eat.

milk.translation:
n. 奶, 乳状物
vt. 挤乳, 榨取
vi. 产乳

senses.concept_en: Milk is the white liquid produced by cows, goats, and some other animals, which people drink and use to make butter, cheese, and yoghurt.
If someone milks a cow or goat, they get milk from it, using either their hands or a machine.
Milk is the white liquid produced by women to feed their babies.
Liquid products for cleaning your skin or making it softer are sometimes referred to as milks .
gloss_zh: （清洁皮肤或使其柔嫩的）乳液

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone milks something, you mean that they get as much benefit or profit as they can from it, without caring about the effects this has on other people.

mode.translation:
n. 模态, 调式, 样式, 文体, 状态, 方式, 风尚
[计] 方式; DOS外部命令:设定各种设备命令
mode.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A mode of life or behaviour is a particular way of living or behaving.
A mode is a particular style in art, literature, or dress.
On some cameras or electronic devices, the different modes available are the different programs or settings that you can choose when you use them.
gloss_zh: （照相机、电子设备的）模式，状态

modern.translation:
n. 现代人, 有思想的人
a. 现代的, 时髦的

senses.concept_en: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is modern is new and involves the latest ideas or equipment.
gloss_zh: 现代化的;新式的;最新的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: People are sometimes described as modern when they have opinions or ways of behaviour that have not yet been accepted by most people in a society.
Modern is used to describe styles of art, dance, music, and architecture that have developed in recent times, in contrast to classical styles.
gloss_zh: （艺术、舞蹈、音乐、建筑的风格）现代的，近代的

senses.concept_en: A month is one of the twelve periods of time that a year is divided into, for example January or February.
A month is a period of about four weeks.

more.translation:
n. 更多
a. 多的, 程度较大的, 更大的
adv. 多, 更多, 进一步
[计] DOS外部命令:显示满屏后自动暂停, 并显示:"--More--", 按任意键继续

senses.concept_en: You use more to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else. You can use 'a little', 'a lot', 'a bit', 'far', and 'much' in front of more .
gloss_zh: 更多;较多（该词前可使用 a little，a lot，a bit，far和much）

senses.concept_en: You use more to indicate that something or someone has a greater amount of a quality than they used to or than is average or usual.
If you say that something is more one thing than another, you mean that it is like the first thing rather than the second.
gloss_zh: 更像（前者）地;与其说（是）…，倒不如说（是）

senses.concept_en: If you do something more than before or more than someone else, you do it to a greater extent or more often.
You can use more to indicate that something continues to happen for a further period of time.
You use more to indicate that something is repeated. For example, if you do something 'once more', you do it again once.
You use more to refer to an additional thing or amount. You can use 'a little', 'a lot', 'a bit', 'far' and 'much' in front of more .
gloss_zh: 另外的;附加的（该词前可使用 a little，a lot，a bit，far 和 much）

senses.concept_en: You can use more in expressions like 'no more, no less' and 'neither more nor less' to indicate that what you are saying is exactly true or correct.
gloss_zh: （用于 no more，no less, neither more nor less 等短语中，表示所说完全无误）多了的部分

senses.concept_en: You use more in conversations when you want to draw someone's attention to something interesting or important that you are about to say.

morning.translation: n. 早晨, 早上, 初期

senses.concept_en: The morning is the part of each day between the time that people usually wake up and 12 o'clock noon or lunchtime.
gloss_zh: 早晨;上午（从人们通常醒来到中午或午餐前的一段时间）

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a particular time in the morning, you mean a time between 12 o'clock midnight and 12 o'clock noon.
gloss_zh: 凌晨，早晨，上午（从子夜到中午的这段时间）

most.translation:
n. 最多, 最大
a. 大多数的, 几乎全部的, 最多的
adv. 最, 最多, 极其

senses.concept_en: You use most to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.
You use the most to mean a larger amount than anyone or anything else, or the largest amount possible.
You use most to indicate that something is true or happens to a greater degree or extent than anything else.
You use most to indicate that someone or something has a greater amount of a particular quality than most other things of its kind.
If you do something the most, you do it to the greatest extent possible or with the greatest frequency.
gloss_zh: 最大限度地;最频繁地;最多地

senses.concept_en: You use most in conversations when you want to draw someone's attention to something very interesting or important that you are about to say.
gloss_zh: （在谈话中用于引起注意）最…，极其…

senses.concept_en: You use most to emphasize an adjective or adverb.

nearby.translation:
a. 附近的, 近旁的
adv. 在附近, 近旁地
prep. 在...附近

senses.concept_en: If something is nearby, it is only a short distance away.

neglect.translation:
n. 疏忽, 忽略, 漏做
vt. 疏忽, 忽视, 不顾

senses.concept_en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to look after them properly.
If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the amount of attention that they deserve.
If you neglect to do something that you ought to do or neglect your duty, you fail to do it.

new.translation:
a. 新的, 陌生的, 最近的, 不熟悉的
[法] 新发现的, 新的, 重新开始的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is new has been recently created, built, or invented or is in the process of being created, built, or invented.
gloss_zh: 新的;刚出现的;新做的;新建的

senses.concept_en: Something that is new has not been used or owned by anyone.
You use new to describe something which has replaced another thing, for example because you no longer have the old one, or it no longer exists, or it is no longer useful.
New is used to describe something that has only recently been discovered or noticed.
A new day or year is the beginning of the next day or year.
gloss_zh: （一天或一年）新开始的，初始的

senses.concept_en: New is used to describe someone or something that has recently acquired a particular status or position.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are new to a situation or place, or if the situation or place is new to you, you have not previously seen it or had any experience of it.
New potatoes, carrots, or peas are produced early in the season for such vegetables and are usually small with a sweet flavour.
gloss_zh: （土豆、胡萝卜、豆子等）时鲜的，早的

next.translation:
n. 下一个
a. 下一个的, 其次的, 贴近的
adv. 然后, 下次, 次于
[计] 近邻干扰

senses.concept_en: The next period of time, event, person, or thing is the one that comes immediately after the present one or after the previous one.
You use next in expressions such as next Friday ,next day and next year to refer, for example, to the first Friday, day, or year that comes after the present or previous one.
The next place or person is the one that is nearest to you or that is the first one that you come to.
The thing that happens next is the thing that happens immediately after something else.
When you next do something, you do it for the first time since you last did it.
You use next to say that something has more of a particular quality than all other things except one. For example, the thing that is next best is the one that is the best except for one other thing.
Ninety is the number 90.

When you talk about the nineties, you are referring to numbers between 90 and 99. For example, if you are in your nineties, you are aged between 90 and 99. If the temperature is in the nineties, the temperature is between 90 and 99 degrees.
The nineties is the decade between 1990 and 1999.

not.translation:
adv. 不, 非, 未
[计] 非

senses.concept_en: You use not with verbs to form negative statements.
gloss_zh: （与动词连用构成否定句）不，非，没有

senses.concept_en: You use not to form questions to which you expect the answer 'yes'.
gloss_zh: （构成期望得到肯定回答的疑问句）

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in questions which imply that someone should have done something, or to express surprise that something is not the case.
gloss_zh: （通常以 n't 的形式出现在问句中，用于推断某人应已做某事或表示惊讶）

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in question tags after a positive statement.
gloss_zh: （通常用 n't 的形式，用于肯定陈述后的附加疑问句）是吗? 不是吗?

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in polite suggestions.
gloss_zh: （通常以 n't 的形式，表示礼貌的建议）

senses.concept_en: You use not to represent the negative of a word, group, or clause that has just been used.
gloss_zh: （用于表示对刚提及的单词、词组或从句的否定）不，没有

senses.concept_en: You can use not in front of 'all' or 'every' when you want to say something that applies only to some members of the group that you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于 all 或 every 前，表示部分否定）并非，不是

senses.concept_en: If something is not always the case, you mean that sometimes it is the case and sometimes it is not.
You can use not or not even in front of 'a' or 'one' to emphasize that there is none at all of what is being mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于 a 或 one 前加强语气）（一个…）也不，（一个…）也没有

senses.concept_en: You can use not in front of a word referring to a distance, length of time, or other amount to say that the actual distance, time, or amount is less than the one mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于表示距离、时间或其他数量的词前）不到，少于

senses.concept_en: You use not when you are contrasting something that is true with something that is untrue. You use this especially to indicate that people might think that the untrue statement is true.
gloss_zh: （用于对比真实和不真实的情况，尤用于可能使人产生误解的陈述）不是

senses.concept_en: You use not in expressions such as 'not only', 'not just', and 'not simply' to emphasize that something is true, but it is not the whole truth.
gloss_zh: （用于not only，not just, not simply 等短语中，强调某事物的真实性，但不是全部事实）

now.translation:
adv. 现在, 刚才, 目前
n. 现在
a. 现在的
conj. 由于

senses.concept_en: You use now to refer to the present time, often in contrast to a time in the past or the future.
If you do something now, you do it immediately.
You use now or now that to indicate that an event has occurred and as a result something else may or will happen.
You use now to indicate that a particular situation is the result of something that has recently happened.
In stories and accounts of past events, now is used to refer to the particular time that is being written or spoken about.
gloss_zh: （用于讲述故事或过去的事情）这时，这会儿

senses.concept_en: You use now in statements which specify the length of time up to the present that something has lasted.
You say 'Now' or 'Now then' to indicate to the person or people you are with that you want their attention, or that you are about to change the subject.
gloss_zh: （引起听者的注意或改变话题）喂，喏，好

senses.concept_en: Some people say 'Now' when they are thinking of what to say next.
gloss_zh: （用于考虑接下来想说的内容）哦，嗯

senses.concept_en: You use now to give a slight emphasis to a request or command.
gloss_zh: （用于委婉地强调请求或命令）好，行

senses.concept_en: You can say 'Now' to introduce information which is relevant to the part of a story or account that you have reached, and which needs to be known before you can continue.
gloss_zh: （引出与已讲述内容有关的信息及继续讲述之前需要了解的信息）你看，喏

senses.concept_en: You say 'Now' to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said.

occasional.translation:
a. 偶然的, 临时的
[法] 偶然的, 特殊场合的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Occasional means happening sometimes, but not regularly or often.
gloss_zh: 偶尔的；间或的；有时发生的

derivation.breakdown_zh: occasion 场合 + -al 形容词：偶然的

senses.concept_en: You use of to combine two nouns when the first noun identifies the feature of the second noun that you want to talk about.
gloss_zh: （用于连接两个名词，其中前者表示后者的特定方面）

senses.concept_en: You use of to combine two nouns, or a noun and a present participle, when the second noun or present participle defines or gives more information about the first noun.
gloss_zh: （用于连接两个名词或名词与现在分词，其中后者对前者进行界定或补充信息）

senses.concept_en: You use of after nouns referring to actions to specify the person or thing that is affected by the action or that performs the action. For example, 'the kidnapping of the child' refers to an action affecting a child; 'the arrival of the next train' refers to an action performed by a train.
gloss_zh: （用于指称动作的名词后说明该动作的对象或主体）

senses.concept_en: You use of after words and phrases referring to quantities or groups of things to indicate the substance or thing that is being measured.
gloss_zh: （用于指称数量或组群的词和短语后表示计量的对象）

senses.concept_en: You use of after the name of someone or something to introduce the institution or place they belong to or are connected with.
gloss_zh: （用于人或事物的名称后引出其所属或相关的机构或地方）

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun referring to a container to form an expression referring to the container and its contents.
gloss_zh: （用于指称容器的名词后，说明容器及其所含物）

senses.concept_en: You use of after a count noun and before an uncount noun when you want to talk about an individual piece or item.
gloss_zh: （用在可数名词后、不可数名词前表示某一单个物品）

senses.concept_en: You use of to indicate the materials or things that form something.
gloss_zh: （表示材料或成分）由…制成（或组成）的

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun which specifies a particular part of something, to introduce the thing that it is a part of.
gloss_zh: （用于名词后表示其为某事物的一部分）

senses.concept_en: You use of after some verbs to indicate someone or something else involved in the action.
gloss_zh: （用于某些动词后表示动作所涉及的人或事物）关于，由于

senses.concept_en: You use of after some adjectives to indicate the thing that a feeling or quality relates to.
gloss_zh: （用于某些形容词后表示与情感或特性相关的事物）对，为

senses.concept_en: You use of before a word referring to the person who performed an action when saying what you think about the action.
gloss_zh: （用于指称施动者的单词前说明对该动作的看法）出自…，在…一方

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun which describes someone or something, to introduce the person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于描述名词后引出所指的人或事物）

senses.concept_en: If something is more of or less of a particular thing, it is that thing to a greater or smaller degree.
gloss_zh: （表示程度）更大/较小程度上的…

senses.concept_en: You use of to indicate a characteristic or quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （表示某人或某事物具有的特点或特性）

senses.concept_en: You use of after the verb 'be' to indicate a characteristic or quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （用于be动词后表示某人或某事物具有的特点或特性）

senses.concept_en: You use of to specify an amount, value, or age.
You use of after a noun such as 'month' or 'year' to indicate the length of time that some state or activity continues.
gloss_zh: （用于年、月等名词后表示状态或活动的持续时间）

senses.concept_en: You can use of to say what time it is by indicating how many minutes there are before the hour mentioned.
gloss_zh: （表示时间离某一钟点差几分）在…之前

offer.translation:
n. 给予(物), 出价, 提议, 意图, 报价
vt. 提供, 出价, 奉献, 试图, 使出现, 演出
vi. 出现, 献祭, 提议, 求婚
offer.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you offer something to someone, you ask them if they would like to have it or use it.
If you offer to do something, you say that you are willing to do it.
An offer is something that someone says they will give you or do for you.
If you offer someone information, advice, or praise, you give it to them, usually because you feel that they need it or deserve it.
gloss_zh: 提供（信息、建议等）；作出（表扬）

senses.concept_en: If you offer someone something such as love or friendship, you show them that you feel that way towards them.
If people offer prayers, praise, or a sacrifice to God or a god, they speak to or give something to their god.
gloss_zh: （向上帝或神）奉献（祈祷、赞美），祭献（牺牲）

senses.concept_en: If an organization offers something such as a service or product, it provides it.
gloss_zh: （机构等）提供，给予（服务、产品等）

senses.concept_en: An offer in a shop is a specially low price for a specific product or something extra that you get if you buy a certain product.
If you offer a particular amount of money for something, you say that you will pay that much to buy it.
An offer is the amount of money that someone says they will pay to buy something or give to someone because they have harmed them in some way.

office.translation:
n. 办公室, 部, 公职, 职责
[化] 办公室

senses.concept_en: An office is a room or a part of a building where people work sitting at desks.
An office is a department of an organization, especially the government, where people deal with a particular kind of administrative work.
An office is a small building or room where people can go for information, tickets, or a service of some kind.
gloss_zh: （问询、购票或提供服务的）处，所

senses.concept_en: A doctor's or dentist's office is a place where a doctor or dentist sees their patients.
If someone holds office in a government, they have an important job or position of authority.

old.translation:
n. 以前, 往昔
a. 老的, 旧的, 古老的, 年长的, 老练的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.
gloss_zh: 年老的；年纪大的；不年轻的

senses.concept_en: You use old to talk about how many days, weeks, months, or years someone or something has lived or existed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is old has existed for a long time.
gloss_zh: 古老的；长久的；历史悠久的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is old is no longer in good condition because of its age or because it has been used a lot.
You use old to refer to something that is no longer used, that no longer exists, or that has been replaced by something else.
gloss_zh: 旧时的；过去的；从前的；过时的

senses.concept_en: You use old to refer to something that used to belong to you, or to a person or thing that used to have a particular role in your life.
gloss_zh: 原来（属于自己）的；原先（生活中）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An old friend, enemy, or rival is someone who has been your friend, enemy, or rival for a long time.
gloss_zh: （朋友）相识已久的；（敌人）结有宿怨的；（对手）长期竞争的

senses.concept_en: You can use old to express affection when talking to or about someone you know.

on.translation:
prep. 在...之上
adv. ...上去
a. 正起作用的
[计] 打开

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is on a surface or object, the surface or object is immediately below them and is supporting their weight.
If something is on a surface or object, it is stuck to it or attached to it.
If you put, throw, or drop something on a surface, you move it or drop it so that it is then supported by the surface.
You use on to say what part of your body is supporting your weight.
You use on to say that someone or something touches a part of a person's body.
gloss_zh: （表示接触到身体某部位）在…上

senses.concept_en: If someone has a particular expression on their face, their face has that expression.
When you put a piece of clothing on, you place it over part of your body in order to wear it. If you have it on, you are wearing it.
You can say that you have something on you if you are carrying it in your pocket or in a bag.
If someone's eyes are on you, they are looking or staring at you.
If you hurt yourself on something, you accidentally hit a part of your body against it and that thing causes damage to you.
If you are on an area of land, you are there.
If something is situated on a place such as a road or coast, it forms part of it or is by the side of it.
gloss_zh: 是（道路、海岸等）的一部分；在…边上

senses.concept_en: If you get on a bus, train, or plane, you go into it in order to travel somewhere. If you are on it, you are travelling in it.
gloss_zh: 上，乘（公共汽车、火车或飞机）

senses.concept_en: If there is something on a piece of paper, it has been written or printed there.
If something is on a list, it is included in it.
Books, discussions, or ideas on a particular subject are concerned with that subject.
You use on to introduce the method, principle, or system which is used to do something.
gloss_zh: 以，凭，靠（某一方法、原则或系统）

senses.concept_en: If something is done on an instrument or a machine, it is done using that instrument or machine.
gloss_zh: 通过，借助于（某一器械或机器）

senses.concept_en: If information is, for example, on tape or on computer, that is the way that it is stored.
If something is being broadcast, you can say that it is on the radio or television.
When an activity is taking place, you can say that it is on .
You use on in expressions such as 'have a lot on' and 'not have very much on' to indicate how busy someone is.
gloss_zh: （表示某人忙碌程度）忙得很/没什么可忙

senses.concept_en: You use on to introduce an activity that someone is doing, particularly travelling.
gloss_zh: （引出所进行的活动，特别是旅行）处于…情况中，在从事…中

senses.concept_en: When something such as a machine or an electric light is on, it is functioning or in use. When you switch it on, it starts functioning.
gloss_zh: （机器、电灯等）开着，工作着，使用中

senses.concept_en: If you are on a committee or council, you are a member of it.
You can indicate when something happens by saying that it happens on a particular day or date.
gloss_zh: 在（某一日子或日期）（发生）

senses.concept_en: You use on when mentioning an event that was followed by another one.
You use on to say that someone is continuing to do something.
If you say that someone goes on at you, you mean that they continually criticize you, complain to you, or ask you to do something.
You use on in expressions such as from now on and from then on to indicate that something starts to happen at the time mentioned and continues to happen afterwards.
You often use on after the adverbs 'early', 'late', 'far', and their comparative forms, especially at the beginning or end of a sentence, or before a preposition.
gloss_zh: （常用在副词early，late，far及其比较级之后，尤置于句首、句尾或介词之前）

senses.concept_en: Someone who is on a drug takes it regularly.
If you live on a particular kind of food, you eat it. If a machine runs on a particular kind of power or fuel, it uses it in order to function.
gloss_zh: 以…（为食）；（机器）用（某种动力或燃料运转）

senses.concept_en: If you are on a particular income, that is the income that you have.
Taxes or profits that are obtained from something are referred to as taxes or profits on it.
When you buy something or pay for something, you spend money on it.
When you spend time or energy on a particular activity, you spend time or energy doing it.

only.translation:
a. 唯一的, 仅有的, 最佳的
adv. 只有, 仅仅, 只能
conj. 但是, 不过

senses.concept_en: You use only to indicate the one thing that is true, appropriate, or necessary in a particular situation, in contrast to all the other things that are not true, appropriate, or necessary.
gloss_zh: （表示比较而言唯一真实、恰当或必要的情况）只，只有

senses.concept_en: You use only to introduce the thing which must happen before the thing mentioned in the main part of the sentence can happen.
gloss_zh: （引出发生的必要条件）只有…（才）

senses.concept_en: If you talk about the only person or thing involved in a particular situation, you mean there are no others involved in it.
An only child is a child who has no brothers or sisters.

You use only to indicate that something is no more important, interesting, or difficult, for example, than you say it is, especially when you want to correct a wrong idea that someone may get or has already got.
gloss_zh: （尤用于想要纠正错误观点时）只不过，仅…而已

senses.concept_en: You use only to emphasize how small an amount is or how short a length of time is.
gloss_zh: （强调数量少或时间短）才，仅仅

senses.concept_en: You use only to emphasize that you are talking about a small part of an amount or group, not the whole of it.
gloss_zh: （强调是其中的一小部分，而非全部）只，仅仅

senses.concept_en: Only is used after 'can' or 'could' to emphasize that it is impossible to do anything except the rather inadequate or limited action that is mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于 can 或 could 之后，强调除此以外别无可为）只（能）

senses.concept_en: You can use only in the expressions I only wish or I only hope in order to emphasize what you are hoping or wishing.
Only can be used to add a comment which slightly changes or limits what you have just said.
gloss_zh: （用于表示稍加改动或限定）只是，不过

senses.concept_en: Only can be used after a clause with 'would' to indicate why something is not done.
gloss_zh: （用于含有 would 的从句后，引出未做某事的原因）要不是，若非

senses.concept_en: You can use only before an infinitive to introduce an event which happens immediately after one you have just mentioned, and which is rather surprising or unfortunate.
You can use only to emphasize how appropriate a certain course of action or type of behaviour is.
gloss_zh: （强调行动或行为恰当）完全，真正

senses.concept_en: You can use only in front of a verb to indicate that the result of something is unfortunate or undesirable and is likely to make the situation worse rather than better.
gloss_zh: （用于动词前，表示结果令人遗憾或不受欢迎）愈加，只（会）

organic.translation:
a. 器官的, 有机的, 组织的, 根本的
[医] 器官的, 有生命的, 有机的, 器质的

senses.concept_en: Organic methods of farming and gardening use only natural animal and plant products to help the plants or animals grow and be healthy, rather than using chemicals.
gloss_zh: 有机的；绿色的；无农害的；不使用化肥的

senses.concept_en: Organic substances are of the sort produced by or found in living things.
Organic change or development happens gradually and naturally rather than suddenly.
gloss_zh: （变化或发展）逐渐的，自然的，演进的

senses.concept_en: If a community or structure is an organic whole, each part of it is necessary and fits well with the other parts.
gloss_zh: （社群或结构）有机的，统一的，不可分割的

outside.translation:
n. 外面, 外表, 外界
a. 外面的, 外表的, 外界的
adv. 外面, 外表, 外界

senses.concept_en: The outside of something is the part which surrounds or encloses the rest of it.
If you are outside, you are not inside a building but are quite close to it.
gloss_zh: 在外面；在室外；在建筑物近旁

senses.concept_en: If you are outside a room, you are not in it but are in the passage or area next to it.
When you talk about the outside world, you are referring to things that happen or exist in places other than your own home or community.
People or things outside a country, town, or region are not in it.
On a road with two separate carriageways, the outside lanes are the ones which are closest to its centre.
gloss_zh: （车道）靠近路中间的，快车道的

senses.concept_en: Outside people or organizations are not part of a particular organization or group.
Outside a particular institution or field of activity means in other fields of activity or in general life.
Something that is outside a particular range of things is not included within it.
Something that happens outside a particular period of time happens at a different time from the one mentioned.

over.translation:
adv. 结束, 越过, 从头到尾
prep. 在...之上, 遍于...之上, 越过
a. 上面的
vt. 越过

senses.concept_en: If one thing is over another thing or is moving over it, the first thing is directly above the second, either resting on it, or with a space between them.
gloss_zh: 在…的上方；在…的上面；在…的上空

senses.concept_en: If one thing is over another thing, it is supported by it and its ends are hanging down on each side of it.
If one thing is over another thing, it covers part or all of it.
gloss_zh: （部分或完全地）覆盖在…的上面

senses.concept_en: If you lean over an object, you bend your body so that the top part of it is above the object.
If you look over or talk over an object, you look or talk across the top of it.
gloss_zh: 从…上面（看过去）；隔着…（交谈）

senses.concept_en: If a window has a view over an area of land or water, you can see the land or water through the window.
If someone or something goes over a barrier, obstacle, or boundary, they get to the other side of it by going across it, or across the top of it.
If someone or something moves over an area or surface, they move across it, from one side to the other.
If something is on the opposite side of a road or river, you can say that it is over the road or river.
If you go over to a place, you go to that place.
You can use over to indicate a particular position or place a short distance away from someone or something.
You use over to say that someone or something falls towards or onto the ground, often suddenly or violently.
If something rolls over or is turned over, its position changes so that the part that was facing upwards is now facing downwards
If something is over a particular amount, measurement, or age, it is more than that amount, measurement, or age.
If you say that you have some food or money over, you mean that it remains after you have used all that you need.
If you do something over, you do it again or start doing it again from the beginning.
If an activity is over or all over, it is completely finished.
If you are over an illness or an experience, it has finished and you have recovered from its effects.
gloss_zh: 从（某一疾病或经历）中恢复过来

senses.concept_en: If you have control or influence over someone or something, you are able to control them or influence them.
You use over to indicate what a disagreement or feeling relates to or is caused by.
If something happens over a particular period of time or over something such as a meal, it happens during that time or during the meal.
You use over to indicate that you give or receive information using a telephone, radio, or other piece of electrical equipment.
When people such as the police or the army are using a radio to communicate, they say 'Over' to indicate that they have finished speaking and are waiting for a reply.
gloss_zh: （无线电通讯用语）完毕，请回答

senses.concept_en: In cricket, an over consists of six correctly bowled balls.
gloss_zh: （板球运动中）一轮6个（未让对方得分的）有效投球

owner.translation:
n. 拥有者, 物主, 所有人
[经] 所有者, 物主, 业主

senses.concept_en: See also:home owner;landowner; The owner of something is the person to whom it belongs.

past.translation:
n. 过去, 昔时, 往事, 早年经历, 过去时
a. 过去的, 结束的, 卸任的, 过去时的
prep. 越过, 晚于, 超越, 超出...的可能性(能力、范围等)
pass的过去分词

senses.concept_en: The past is the time before the present, and the things that have happened.
Your past consists of all the things that you have done or that have happened to you.
Past events and things happened or existed before the present time.
You use past to talk about a period of time that has just finished. For example, if you talk about the past five years, you mean the period of five years that has just finished.
If a situation is past, it has ended and no longer exists.

See also:past perfect; In grammar, the past tenses of a verb are the ones used to talk about things that happened at some time before the present. The simple past tense uses the past form of a verb, which for regular verbs ends in '-ed', as in 'They walked back to the car'.
You use past when you are stating a time which is thirty minutes or less after a particular hour. For example, if it is twenty past six, it is twenty minutes after six o'clock.
If it is past a particular time, it is later than that time.
If you go past someone or something, you go near them and keep moving, so that they are then behind you.
If you look or point past a person or thing, you look or point at something behind them.
If something is past a place, it is on the other side of it.
If someone or something is past a particular point or stage, they are no longer at that point or stage.
gloss_zh: 超过，超出（某一点或阶段）

senses.concept_en: If you are past doing something, you are no longer able to do it. For example, if you are past caring, you do not care about something any more because so many bad things have happened to you.

patient.translation:
n. 病人, 承受者
a. 忍耐的, 容忍的, 有耐性的, 坚忍的

senses.concept_en: A patient is a person who is receiving medical treatment from a doctor or hospital. A patient is also someone who is registered with a particular doctor

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are patient, you stay calm and do not get annoyed, for example when something takes a long time, or when someone is not doing what you want them to do.

people.translation:
n. 人, 人民, 民族, 平民
vt. 使住满人, 居住于

senses.concept_en: People are men, women, and children. People is normally used as the plural of person, instead of 'persons'.
gloss_zh: 人，人们（通常用作person的复数）

senses.concept_en: The people is sometimes used to refer to ordinary men and women, in contrast to the government or the upper classes.
gloss_zh: （与政府或上流社会相对的）人民，民众，大众

senses.concept_en: A people is all the men, women, and children of a particular country or race.
If a place or country is peopled by a particular group of people, that group of people live there.
If something such as a story or a time in history is peopled with people of a particular kind, those people occur or exist in it.
gloss_zh: （某种类型的人）出现，存在，充斥于（故事或历史时期）

percent.translation:
n. 百分比, 百分数, 部分
[机] 百分率
percent.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

plan.translation:
n. 计划, 方案, 策略, 方法, 进度表, 程序表, 平面图, 设计图, 轮廓, 示意图
vt. 计划, 设计, 意欲
vi. 订计划

senses.concept_en: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand.
If you plan what you are going to do, you decide in detail what you are going to do, and you intend to do it.
If you have plans, you are intending to do a particular thing.
gloss_zh: （有做某一特定事的）计划，打算，意向

senses.concept_en: When you plan something that you are going to make, build, or create, you decide what the main parts of it will be and do a drawing of how it should be made.
gloss_zh: 设计；绘制…的图样（或图表）

senses.concept_en: A plan of something that is going to be built or made is a detailed diagram or drawing of it.

popular.translation:
a. 通俗的, 流行的, 受欢迎的, 大众的, 人民的, 普及的
[经] 大众的, 通俗的, 普及的
popular.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is popular is enjoyed or liked by a lot of people.
gloss_zh: 受喜爱的；受欢迎的；当红的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is popular is liked by most people, or by most people in a particular group.
Popular newspapers, television programmes, or forms of art are aimed at ordinary people and not at experts or intellectuals.
gloss_zh: （报纸、电视节目、艺术形式等）通俗的，流行的，大众化的

senses.concept_en: Popular ideas, feelings, or attitudes are approved of or held by most people.
Popular is used to describe political activities which involve the ordinary people of a country, and not just members of political parties.

preliminary.translation:
n. 初步做法, 初步措施, 预试, 预选赛
a. 初步的, 开始的, 预备的
preliminary.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: Preliminary activities or discussions take place at the beginning of an event, often as a form of preparation.
A preliminary is something that you do at the beginning of an activity, often as a form of preparation.
A preliminary is the first part of a competition to see who will go on to the main competition.

priority.translation:
n. 优先权, 优先
[计] 优先级
priority.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.
gloss_zh: 优先事项；最重要的事；当务之急

problem.translation:
n. 问题, 难题
a. 成问题的, 难处理的

senses.concept_en: A problem is a situation that is unsatisfactory and causes difficulties for people.
A problem is a puzzle that requires logical thought or mathematics to solve it.
gloss_zh: （通过逻辑思考或数学运算解决的）问题，习题，题

senses.concept_en: Problem children or problem families have serious problems or cause serious problems for other people.
gloss_zh: （儿童或家庭）有严重问题的，引起严重问题的

produce.translation:
n. 生产品, 物产, 后代
vt. 产生, 生产, 提出, 出示
vi. 生产, 制造
produce.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl gre

senses.concept_en: To produce something means to cause it to happen.
If you produce something, you make or create it.
When things or people produce something, it comes from them or slowly forms from them, especially as the result of a biological or chemical process.
If you produce evidence or an argument, you show it or explain it to people in order to make them agree with you.
If you produce an object from somewhere, you show it or bring it out so that it can be seen.
If someone produces something such as a film, a magazine, or a CD, they organize it and decide how it should be done.
gloss_zh: 上演（戏剧）；制作（电影、电视节目）；灌制（唱片）

senses.concept_en: Produce is food or other things that are grown in large quantities to be sold.

product.translation:
n. 产品, 结果, 乘积
[化] 生产物

senses.concept_en: A product is something that is produced and sold in large quantities, often as a result of a manufacturing process.
If you say that someone or something is a product of a situation or process, you mean that the situation or process has had a significant effect in making them what they are.

project.translation:
n. 计划, 设计, 事业
vt. 计划, 设计, 投掷, 发射, 使凸出, 放映
vi. 凸出
project.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A project is a task that requires a lot of time and effort.
A project is a detailed study of a subject by a pupil or student.
If something is projected, it is planned or expected.
If you project someone or something in a particular way, you try to make people see them in that way. If you project a particular feeling or quality, you show it in your behaviour.
If you project feelings or ideas on to other people, you imagine that they have the same ideas or feelings as you.
gloss_zh: 把（情感、想法）投射转移（到他人身上）

senses.concept_en: If you project a film or picture onto a screen or wall, you make it appear there.
If something projects, it sticks out above or beyond a surface or edge.

protest.translation:
n. 抗议, 反对, 抗议书, 断言
v. 反对, 抗议, 断言
protest.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you protest against something or about something, you say or show publicly that you object to it. In American English, you usually say that you protest it.
A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.
If you protest that something is the case, you insist that it is the case, when other people think that it may not be.
A protest that something is true is a strong declaration that it is true.

prove.translation:
vt. 证明, 查验, 检验, 勘探, 显示
vi. 证明是

senses.concept_en: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.
If you prove that something is true, you show by means of argument or evidence that it is definitely true.
If you prove yourself to have a certain good quality, you show by your actions that you have it.

provide.translation:
vt. 提供, 供应, 规定, 预备
vi. 作准备, 抚养, 规定
provide.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: If you provide something that someone needs or wants, or if you provide them with it, you give it to them or make it available to them.
If a law or agreement provides that something will happen, it states that it will happen.

public.translation:
n. 公众, 民众
a. 公众的, 公共的, 公立的, 公用的
public.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: You can refer to people in general, or to all the people in a particular country or community, as the public .
You can refer to a set of people in a country who share a common interest, activity, or characteristic as a particular kind of public .
gloss_zh: 志趣相投（或从事同一类活动、具有共同特征）的群体

senses.concept_en: Public means relating to all the people in a country or community.
Public means relating to the government or state, or things that are done for the people by the state.
gloss_zh: 政府的；国家的；公共事务的

senses.concept_en: Public buildings and services are provided for everyone to use.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A public place is one where people can go about freely and where you can easily be seen and heard.
If someone is a public figure or in public life, many people know who they are because they are often mentioned in newspapers and on television.
Public is used to describe statements, actions, and events that are made or done in such a way that any member of the public can see them or be aware of them.
gloss_zh: （声明、事件等）公开的，公之于众的

senses.concept_en: If a fact is made public or becomes public, it becomes known to everyone rather than being kept secret.
gloss_zh: 公之于众的；公开的；人人皆知的

publish.translation:
vt. 出版, 发行, 公开, 发表, 宣传, 公布
vi. 出版, 发行

senses.concept_en: When a company publishes a book or magazine, it prints copies of it, which are sent to shops to be sold.
When the people in charge of a newspaper or magazine publish a piece of writing or a photograph, they print it in their newspaper or magazine.
If someone publishes a book or an article that they have written, they arrange to have it published.
If you publish information or an opinion, you make it known to the public by having it printed in a newspaper, magazine, or official document.

quick.translation:
a. 快的, 迅速的, 敏捷的, 灵敏的, 急速的
adv. 快
n. 新长出的肉, 要害, 核心, 感觉敏锐部位

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is quick moves or does things with great speed.
Quicker is sometimes used to mean 'at a greater speed', and quickest to mean 'at the greatest speed'. Quick is sometimes used to mean 'with great speed'. Some people consider this to be non-standard.
gloss_zh: （quicker 有时表示“以更快的速度”，quickest表示“以最快的速度”，quick有时表示“以很快的速度”，但有些人认为这种用法并不规范）

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is quick takes or lasts only a short time.
gloss_zh: 短暂的;持续时间很短的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Quick means happening without delay or with very little delay.
gloss_zh: 立刻发生的;很快发生的

senses.concept_en: Quick is sometimes used to mean 'with very little delay'.
gloss_zh: 迅速发生地;很快发生地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are quick to do something, you do not hesitate to do it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has a quick temper, they are easily made angry.
gloss_zh: 性情急躁的;容易发怒的

rational.translation:
a. 理性的, 合理的
n. 有理数
rational.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Rational decisions and thoughts are based on reason rather than on emotion.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A rational person is someone who is sensible and is able to make decisions based on intelligent thinking rather than on emotion.

rebuild.translation:
vt. 改建, 重建, 改造
vi. 重建

senses.concept_en: When people rebuild something such as a building or a city, they build it again after it has been damaged or destroyed.
When people rebuild something such as an institution, a system, or an aspect of their lives, they take action to bring it back to its previous condition.
gloss_zh: 重建，重组，复原（机构、制度或生活的某些方面）

senses.concept_en: If doctors rebuild part of someone's body that has been damaged, they operate on that person to make them well again.
gloss_zh: 复原，修复（身体某一部分）

recommendation.translation:
n. 推荐, 介绍, 推荐信, 劝告
[经] 建议书

senses.concept_en: The recommendations of a person or a committee are their suggestions or advice on what is the best thing to do.
A recommendation of something is the suggestion that someone should have or use it because it is good.

remain.translation:
vi. 保持, 逗留, 剩余
[法] 停留, 居住, 继续

senses.concept_en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.
If you remain in a place, you stay there and do not move away.
You can say that something remains when it still exists.
If something remains to be done, it has not yet been done and still needs to be done.
The remains of something are the parts of it that are left after most of it has been taken away or destroyed.
The remains of a person or animal are the parts of their body that are left after they have died, sometimes after they have been dead for a long time.
Historical remains are things that have been found from an earlier period of history, usually buried in the ground, for example parts of buildings and pieces of pottery.
You can use remain in expressions such as the fact remains that or the question remains whether to introduce and emphasize something that you want to talk about.
gloss_zh: （事实、问题等）仍然是（表示强调）

renew.translation:
vt. 使更新, 使恢复, 复兴, 修补, 补充, 继续, 重订, 重申, 续借
vi. 更新, 重新开始

senses.concept_en: If you renew an activity, you begin it again.
If you renew a relationship with someone, you start it again after you have not seen them or have not been friendly with them for some time.
When you renew something such as a licence or a contract, you extend the period of time for which it is valid.
gloss_zh: 延长（执照、合同等）的有效期;使续签

senses.concept_en: You can say that something is renewed when it grows again or is replaced after it has been destroyed or lost.
gloss_zh: 使（受到损毁或丢失后）重获新生

rent.translation:
n. 租金, 房租, 出租物, 裂缝, 破裂处, 分裂
vt. 租用, 租出
vi. 出租
a. 分裂的, 破裂的
rend的过去式和过去分词
rent.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you rent something, you regularly pay its owner a sum of money in order to be able to have it and use it yourself.
If you rent something to someone, you let them have it and use it in exchange for a sum of money which they pay you regularly.
Rent is the amount of money that you pay regularly to use a house, flat, or piece of land.
Rent is the past tense and past participle of rend .

reopen.translation: v. 重开, 再开始, 再开

repair.translation:
n. 修理, 补救, 修复
vt. 修理, 修补, 补救, 恢复, 补偿
vi. 修理, 修补, 补救, 恢复, 去, 常去, 集合
repair.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you repair something that has been damaged or is not working properly, you mend it.
If you repair a relationship or someone's reputation after it has been damaged, you do something to improve it.
A repair is something that you do to mend a machine, building, piece of clothing, or other thing that has been damaged or is not working properly.
If someone repairs to a particular place, they go there.

report.translation:
n. 报告, 报道, 传说, 案情报告, 爆炸声, 成绩单
vt. 报告, 汇报, 转述, 报道, 揭发, 使报到
vi. 报告, 写报道, 报到
[计] 报告

senses.concept_en: If you report something that has happened, you tell people about it.
If you report on an event or subject, you tell people about it, because it is your job or duty to do so.
gloss_zh: （就某个事件或主题）报告情况，报道

senses.concept_en: A report is a news article or broadcast which gives information about something that has just happened.
A report is an official document which a group of people issue after investigating a situation or event.
If you give someone a report on something, you tell them what has been happening.
If you say that there are reports that something has happened, you mean that some people say it has happened but you have no direct evidence of it.
If someone reports you to a person in authority, they tell that person about something wrong that you have done.
If you report to a person or place, you go to that person or place and say that you are ready to start work or say that you are present.
If you say that one employee reports to another, you mean that the first employee is told what to do by the second one and is responsible to them.
A school report is an official written account of how well or how badly a pupil has done during the term or year that has just finished.
A report is a sudden loud noise, for example the sound of a gun being fired or an explosion.

return.translation:
n. 回来, 返回, 来回票, 归还, 报答, 利润率, 报告书
a. 返回的, 回程的, 报答的, 反向的, 重现的, 复原的
vi. 返回, 归还, 回来
vt. 归还, 还, 回报, 产生, 反射, 报告, 申报, 退回
[计] 返回

senses.concept_en: When you return to a place, you go back there after you have been away.
Your return is your arrival back at a place where you had been before.
If you return something that you have borrowed or taken, you give it back or put it back.
If you return something somewhere, you put it back where it was.
If you return someone's action, you do the same thing to them as they have just done to you. If you return someone's feeling, you feel the same way towards them as they feel towards you.
If a feeling or situation returns, it comes back or happens again after a period when it was not present.
If you return to a state that you were in before, you start being in that state again.
If you return to a subject that you have mentioned before, you begin talking about it again.
If you return to an activity that you were doing before, you start doing it again.
gloss_zh: 重新开始，继续（某项活动）

senses.concept_en: When a judge or jury returns a verdict, they announce whether they think the person on trial is guilty or not.
See also:day return; A return ticket is a ticket for a journey from one place to another and then back again.
The return trip or journey is the part of a journey that takes you back to where you started from.
The return on an investment is the profit that you get from it.
See also:tax return; A tax return is an official form that you fill in with details about your income and personal situation, so that the income tax you owe can be calculated.
Returns are the results of votes after an election.

rise.translation:
n. 上升, 增加, 上涨, 高地, 升高, 出现
vi. 升起, 起身, 起立, 上升, 上涨, 增长, 高耸, 起义, 浮现
vt. 使飞起

senses.concept_en: If something rises, it moves upwards.
When you rise, you stand up.
When you rise, you get out of bed.
When the sun or moon rises, it appears in the sky.
You can say that something rises when it appears as a large tall shape.
If the level of something such as the water in a river rises, it becomes higher.
If land rises, it slopes upwards.
A rise is an area of ground that slopes upwards.
If an amount rises, it increases.
A rise in the amount of something is an increase in it.
A rise is an increase in your wages or your salary.
The rise of a movement or activity is an increase in its popularity or influence.
gloss_zh: （运动或活动的）兴起,抬头，高涨

senses.concept_en: If the wind rises, it becomes stronger.
If a sound rises or if someone's voice rises, it becomes louder or higher.
If a sound rises from a group of people, it comes from them.
If an emotion rises in someone, they suddenly feel it very intensely so that it affects their behaviour.
If your colour rises or if a blush rises in your cheeks, you turn red because you feel angry, embarrassed, or excited.
gloss_zh: （因为生气、尴尬或兴奋）脸红，涨红脸

senses.concept_en: When the people in a country rise, they try to defeat the government or army that is controlling them.
If someone rises to a higher position or status, they become more important, successful, or powerful.
gloss_zh: 升职;升迁;地位提高;变得更成功

senses.concept_en: The rise of someone is the process by which they become more important, successful, or powerful.
gloss_zh: 升迁;日益成功;地位的提高

roof.translation:
n. 屋顶, 室顶
vt. 给...盖屋顶, 遮蔽

senses.concept_en: The roof of a building is the covering on top of it that protects the people and things inside from the weather.
The roof of a car or other vehicle is the top part of it, which protects passengers or goods from the weather.
The roof of your mouth is the highest part of the inside of your mouth.
The roof of an underground space such as a cave or mine is the highest part of it.

rule.translation:
n. 规则, 统治, 控制, 支配, 规律, 标准, 章程, 破折号, 铅线
vt. 规定, 统治, 管理, 控制, 支配, 裁决
vi. 统治, 管辖, 裁定
[计] 规则, 水线
rule.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: Rules are instructions that tell you what you are allowed to do and what you are not allowed to do.
A rule is a statement telling people what they should do in order to achieve success or a benefit of some kind.
gloss_zh: 行事准则;指导方针;应做的事

senses.concept_en: The rules of something such as a language or a science are statements that describe the way that things usually happen in a particular situation.
If something is the rule, it is the normal state of affairs.
The person or group that rules a country controls its affairs.
If something rules your life, it influences or restricts your actions in a way that is not good for you.
When someone in authority rules that something is true or should happen, they state that they have officially decided that it is true or should happen.
If you rule a straight line, you draw it using something that has a straight edge.

safely.translation: adv. 安全地, 确实地

senses.concept_en: If something is done safely, it is done in a way that makes it unlikely that anyone will be harmed.
You also use safely to say that there is no risk of a situation being changed.

safety.translation:
n. 安全, 保险, 平安, 保安设备
vt. 保护, 防护
safety.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Safety is the state of being safe from harm or danger.
If you reach safety, you reach a place where you are safe from danger.
If you are concerned about the safety of something, you are concerned that it might be harmful or dangerous.
gloss_zh: 安全程度;安全性;无害;无危险

senses.concept_en: If you are concerned for someone's safety, you are concerned that they might be in danger.
Safety features or measures are intended to make something less dangerous.

sale.translation:
n. 出售, 卖, 拍卖, 销售额, 廉价出售
[经] 卖, 出售; 销售(货)
sale.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: The sale of goods is the act of selling them for money.
The sales of a product are the quantity of it that is sold.
The part of a company that deals with sales deals with selling the company's products.
A sale is an occasion when a shop sells things at less than their normal price.
A sale is an event when goods are sold to the person who offers the highest price.

save.translation:
n. 救球
vt. 解救, 挽救, 储蓄, 保存, 节省, 保留
vi. 挽救, 节省, 救球
prep. 除...之外
[计] 保存
save.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: If you save someone or something, you help them to avoid harm or to escape from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.
If you save, you gradually collect money by spending less than you get, usually in order to buy something that you want.
If you save something such as time or money, you prevent the loss or waste of it.
If you save something, you keep it because it will be needed later.
If someone or something saves you from an unpleasant action or experience, they change the situation so that you do not have to do it or experience it.
If you save data in a computer, you give the computer an instruction to store the data on a tape or disk.
If a goalkeeper saves, or saves a shot, they succeed in preventing the ball from going into the goal.
You can use save to introduce the only things, people, or ideas that your main statement does not apply to.

sell.translation:
vt. 卖, 背叛, 销售, 出卖
vi. 卖, 销售
n. 卖, 推销术, 失望

senses.concept_en: If you sell something that you own, you let someone have it in return for money.
If a shop sells a particular thing, it is available for people to buy there.
If something sells for a particular price, that price is paid for it.
If something sells, it is bought by the public, usually in fairly large quantities.
Something that sells a product makes people want to buy the product.
If you sell someone an idea or proposal, or sell someone on an idea, you convince them that it is a good one.

seller.translation:
n. 销售者
[化] 卖方

senses.concept_en: A seller of a type of thing is a person or company that sells that type of thing.
In a business deal, the seller is the person who is selling something to someone else.
See also:best seller; If you describe a product as, for example, a big seller, you mean that large numbers of it are being sold.

serious.translation:
a. 严肃的, 认真的, 重要的, 严重的
[电] 严重的
serious.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Serious problems or situations are very bad and cause people to be worried or afraid.
gloss_zh: 严重的;危急的;令人担忧的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Serious matters are important and deserve careful and thoughtful consideration.
gloss_zh: 重要的;需要认真考虑的;严肃的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When important matters are dealt with in a serious way, they are given careful and thoughtful consideration.
Serious music or literature requires concentration to understand or appreciate it.
gloss_zh: （音乐、文学作品）严肃的，非供消遣（或娱乐）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is serious about something, they are sincere about what they are saying, doing, or intending to do.
gloss_zh: 认真的;当真的;真心的;郑重其事的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Serious people are thoughtful and quiet, and do not laugh very often.
gloss_zh: （人）若有所思的，庄重的，严肃的

senses.concept_en: Serious money is a very large amount of money.
Seven is the number 7.

several.translation:
a. 几个的, 一些的, 各自的
pron. 几个
