senses.concept_en: Several is used to refer to an imprecise number of people or things that is not large but is greater than two.

sharply.translation:
adv. 锐利地, 严厉地, 厉害地
[经] 剧烈地

shop.translation:
n. 商店, 工厂, 车间
vi. 购物, 到处寻找
vt. 选购

senses.concept_en: A shop is a building or part of a building where things are sold.
When you shop, you go to shops and buy things.
You can refer to a place where a particular service is offered as a particular type of shop .
You can refer to a place where things are made or done as a particular kind of shop .
If you shop someone, you report them to the police for doing something illegal.

shopper.translation:
n. 购物者
[经] 顾客, 购物的人

show.translation:
n. 显示, 表现, 展览, 卖弄, 炫耀, 外观, 演出, 洋相
vt. 表示, 显示, 展现, 陈列, 演出, 表明, 指出, 带领
vi. 露面, 显现, 演出
[计] 显示

senses.concept_en: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.
If a picture, chart, film, or piece of writing shows something, it represents it or gives information about it.
gloss_zh: （图画、图表、影像或文章）描绘，描述，展示，说明

senses.concept_en: If you show someone something, you give it to them, take them to it, or point to it, so that they can see it or know what you are referring to.
gloss_zh: 给…看;向…出示（或展示）;指给…看

senses.concept_en: If you show someone to a room or seat, you lead them there.
If you show someone how to do something, you do it yourself so that they can watch you and learn how to do it.
If something shows or if you show it, it is visible or noticeable.
If you show a particular attitude, quality, or feeling, or if it shows, you behave in a way that makes this attitude, quality, or feeling clear to other people.
gloss_zh: 表现，体现，流露出（态度、品质或情感）;（态度等）体现，流露

senses.concept_en: If something shows a quality or characteristic or if that quality or characteristic shows itself, it can be noticed or observed.
gloss_zh: 显示出，表露出，流露出（某种品质或特征）;（品质或特征）表露，显示

senses.concept_en: A show of a feeling or quality is an attempt by someone to make it clear that they have that feeling or quality.
gloss_zh: （情感、品质等的）流露，表露，体现

senses.concept_en: If you say that something is for show, you mean that it has no real purpose and is done just to give a good impression.
If a company shows a profit or a loss, its accounts indicate that it has made a profit or a loss.
If a person you are expecting to meet does not show, they do not arrive at the place where you expect to meet them.
A television or radio show is a programme on television or radio.
A show in a theatre is an entertainment or concert, especially one that includes different items such as music, dancing, and comedy.
gloss_zh: （尤指包括音乐、舞蹈、滑稽剧等不同内容的）演出，表演

senses.concept_en: If someone shows a film or television programme, it is broadcast or appears on television or in the cinema.
A show is a public exhibition of things, such as works of art, fashionable clothes, or things that have been entered in a competition.
To show things such as works of art means to put them in an exhibition where they can be seen by the public.
In a horse race, if a horse shows, it finishes first, second, or third.
gloss_zh: （赛马比赛中赛马）名列前三甲

senses.concept_en: A show home, house, or flat is one of a group of new homes. The building company decorates it and puts furniture in it, and people who want to buy one of the homes come and look round it.

since.translation:
prep. 自...以后, 自...以来
adv. 自那时以后
conj. 既然, 自...以后, 自...以来

senses.concept_en: You use since when you are mentioning a time or event in the past and indicating that a situation has continued from then until now.
gloss_zh: （表示某情况自过去某时间点或某个事件以来一直持续到现在）自…以后，从…以来

senses.concept_en: You use since to mention a time or event in the past when you are describing an event or situation that has happened after that time.
gloss_zh: （表示某事件或情况从过去某时间或某个事件之后一直发生）自…以来,在…之后

senses.concept_en: When you are talking about an event or situation in the past, you use since to indicate that another event happened at some point later in time.
gloss_zh: （表示过去某事或某情况发生后不久又发生了另一件事）此后，后来

senses.concept_en: You use since to introduce reasons or explanations.
Six is the number 6.
In cricket, if a player hits a six, they score six runs by hitting the ball so that it crosses the boundary at the edge of the playing area before it touches the ground.
gloss_zh: （板球中）得 6 分的击球，以 6 分记的击球

senses.concept_en: Sixty is the number 60.

When you talk about the sixties, you are referring to numbers between 60 and 69. For example, if you are in your sixties, you are aged between 60 and 69. If the temperature is in the sixties, it is between 60 and 69 degrees.
gloss_zh: 六十几（指 60 至 69 之间的数字）

senses.concept_en: The sixties is the decade between 1960 and 1969.
gloss_zh: 二十世纪六十年代（指1960年至1969年）

so.translation:
adv. 如此, 如是, 如...那样
conj. 所以, 因此
pron. 这样

senses.concept_en: You use so to refer back to something that has just been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 如此，这样（指已经提到的事）

senses.concept_en: You use so when you are saying that something which has just been said about one person or thing is also true of another one.
gloss_zh: 同样，也一样（指后者跟前者一样）

senses.concept_en: You use the structures as...so and just as...so when you want to indicate that two events or situations are similar in some way.
gloss_zh: （表示两个事件或情况在某方面相似）正如…，也…

senses.concept_en: If you say that a state of affairs is so, you mean that it is the way it has been described.
gloss_zh: （指某一情况）就是这样，事实如此

senses.concept_en: You can use so with actions and gestures to show a person how to do something, or to indicate the size, height, or length of something.
gloss_zh: （向别人示范）这样，像这样;（用手势比划大小、高度或长度）这么，那么

senses.concept_en: You use so and so that to introduce the result of the situation you have just mentioned.
You use so ,so that, and so as to introduce the reason for doing the thing that you have just mentioned.
You can use so in stories and accounts to introduce the next event in a series of events or to suggest a connection between two events.
gloss_zh: （在叙述过程中引出一系列事件中的下一件或说明两件事情之间的联系）此后，于是

senses.concept_en: You can use so in conversations to introduce a new topic, or to introduce a question or comment about something that has been said.
gloss_zh: （表示开始新话题、引入新问题或对刚说过的问题进行评论）那么，这么

senses.concept_en: You can use so in conversations to show that you are accepting what someone has just said.
gloss_zh: （谈话中表示接受别人的说法）的确，确实

senses.concept_en: You can use so in front of adjectives and adverbs to emphasize the quality that they are describing.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词和副词之前强调所描述的特性）如此，这么，多么，太

senses.concept_en: You can use so...that and so...as to emphasize the degree of something by mentioning the result or consequence of it.
gloss_zh: 如此…（以致…）;到…的程度（以致…）

sole.translation:
n. 脚掌, 鞋底, 底部
a. 唯一的, 仅有的, 单独的, 独身的
vt. 上鞋底, 触底

senses.concept_en: The sole thing or person of a particular type is the only one of that type.
If you have sole charge or ownership of something, you are the only person in charge of it or who owns it.
gloss_zh: （控制权或所有权）唯一的，独占的

senses.concept_en: The sole of your foot or of a shoe or sock is the underneath surface of it.
A sole is a kind of flat fish that you can eat.

solution.translation:
n. 解决, 解答, 溶液
[化] 溶液

senses.concept_en: A solution to a problem or difficult situation is a way of dealing with it so that the difficulty is removed.
The solution to a puzzle is the answer to it.
A solution is a liquid in which a solid substance has been dissolved.

soon.translation: adv. 不久, 早, 快, 宁可

senses.concept_en: If something is going to happen soon, it will happen after a short time. If something happened soon after a particular time or event, it happened a short time after it.

space.translation:
n. 位置, 空间, 距离, 太空, 空白, 间隔, (期刊等的)篇幅
vt. 隔开, 分隔
vi. 留间隔
[计] 空白, 空格校验
space.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: You use space to refer to an area that is empty or available. The area can be any size. For example, you can refer to a large area outside as a large open space or to a small area between two objects as a small space .
A particular kind of space is the area that is available for a particular activity or for putting a particular kind of thing in.
gloss_zh: （活动或储藏用的）空间，场所，面积

senses.concept_en: If a place gives a feeling of space, it gives an impression of being large and open.
If you give someone space to think about something or to develop as a person, you allow them the time and freedom to do this.
gloss_zh: （思考问题、个人成长所需的）时间，余地，空间

senses.concept_en: The amount of space for a topic to be discussed in a document is the number of pages available to discuss the topic.
gloss_zh: （文件中用于讨论某个话题的）版面，篇幅

senses.concept_en: A space of time is a period of time.
Space is the area beyond the Earth's atmosphere, where the stars and planets are.
Space is the whole area within which everything exists.
If you space a series of things, you arrange them so that they are not all together but have gaps or intervals of time between them.

specify.translation:
vt. 详列, 指定, 说明
[计] 指定

senses.concept_en: If you specify something, you give information about what is required or should happen in a certain situation.
If you specify what should happen or be done, you explain it in an exact and detailed way.

spend.translation:
vt. 花费, 浪费, 度过, 消耗, 消磨
vi. 花费, 用尽

senses.concept_en: When you spend money, you pay money for things that you want.
If you spend time or energy doing something, you use your time or effort doing it.
If you spend a period of time in a place, you stay there for a period of time.
The spend on a particular thing is the amount of money that is spent on it, or will be spent.

spring.translation:
n. 春天, 弹簧, 跳跃, 弹性, 活力, 泉, 源泉
a. 春天的
vi. 跳, 弹跳, 涌出, 生长, 裂开, 高耸
vt. 使跳起, 使爆炸, 突然提出

stall.translation:
n. 厩, 停车处, 牧师职位, 货摊, 托辞, 拖延
vt. 关入厩, 停顿, 推托, 支吾, 使陷于泥中
vi. 被关在厩内, 陷于泥中, 停止, 支吾

senses.concept_en: If a process stalls, or if someone or something stalls it, the process stops but may continue at a later time.
If you stall, you try to avoid doing something until later.
If you stall someone, you prevent them from doing something until a later time.
If a vehicle stalls or if you accidentally stall it, the engine stops suddenly.
A stall is a large table on which you put goods that you want to sell, or information that you want to give people.
The stalls in a theatre or concert hall are the seats on the ground floor directly in front of the stage.
gloss_zh: （戏院、音乐厅的）正厅前排座位

senses.concept_en: A stall is a small enclosed area in a room which is used for a particular purpose, for example a shower.
gloss_zh: （淋浴间等房间里的）小分隔间

start.translation:
n. 惊起, 出发, 开端, 起点, 吃惊, 有利条件
vi. 开始, 出发, 启动, 跳起, 吃惊, 出现, 松动, 脱落, 起价, 参赛
vt. 使惊起, 开动, 发动, 启动, 开始, 创办, 提议, 使松动, 使脱落, 起用
[计] 起始

senses.concept_en: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it.
When something starts, or if someone starts it, it takes place from a particular time.
If you start by doing something, or if you start with something, you do that thing first in a series of actions.
You use start to say what someone's first job was. For example, if their first job was that of a factory worker, you can say that they started as a factory worker.
See also:start-up; When someone starts something such as a new business, they create it or cause it to begin.
If you start an engine, car, or machine, or if it starts, it begins to work.
gloss_zh: 开动，发动（发动机、汽车、机器等）

senses.concept_en: If you start, your body suddenly moves slightly as a result of surprise or fear.

steady.translation:
a. 稳定的, 不动摇的, 沉着的, 稳固的, 坚定的, 经常的
vt. 使稳定, 使坚定
vi. 变为沉着, 稳固
steady.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A steady situation continues or develops gradually without any interruptions and is not likely to change quickly.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If an object is steady, it is firm and does not shake or move about.
gloss_zh: 稳定的;牢固的;不摇晃的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you look at someone or speak to them in a steady way, you look or speak in a calm, controlled way.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person as steady, you mean that they are sensible and reliable.
If you steady something or if it steadies, it stops shaking or moving about.
If you steady yourself, you control your voice or expression, so that people will think that you are calm and not nervous.
You say 'steady on' to someone to tell them to calm down or to be careful about what they are saying.

structural.translation:
a. 结构的, 建筑的
[医] 结构的

senses.concept_en: Structural means relating to or affecting the structure of something.

success.translation: n. 成功, 成就, 胜利

senses.concept_en: Success is the achievement of something that you have been trying to do.
Success is the achievement of a high position in a particular field, for example in business or politics.
The success of something is the fact that it works in a satisfactory way or has the result that is intended.
gloss_zh: （某事所取得的）成功，良好表现

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is a success achieves a high position, makes a lot of money, or is admired a great deal.

such.translation: a. 如此的, 这样的

senses.concept_en: You use such to refer back to the thing or person that you have just mentioned, or a thing or person like the one that you have just mentioned. You use such as and such...as to introduce a reference to the person or thing that has just been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 这样的;那样的;上述的;诸如此类的

senses.concept_en: You use such...as to link something or someone with a clause in which you give a description of the kind of thing or person that you mean.
You use such...as to introduce one or more examples of the kind of thing or person that you have just mentioned.
You use such before noun groups to emphasize the extent of something or to emphasize that something is remarkable.
gloss_zh: （用于名词词组前强调某事的程度或某事了不起）如此，这样，非常

senses.concept_en: You use such...that in order to emphasize the degree of something by mentioning the result or consequence of it.
gloss_zh: （用于强调程度）如此…，非常…（以至于…）

senses.concept_en: You use such...that or such...as in order to say what the result or consequence of something that you have just mentioned is.

suffer.translation:
vt. 遭受, 经历, 忍受
vi. 受痛苦, 受损害

senses.concept_en: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.
gloss_zh: 遭受，经受（疼痛）;感到（痛苦）

senses.concept_en: If you suffer from an illness or from some other bad condition, you are badly affected by it.
gloss_zh: （因疾病或处于其他不利境地而）受苦，受难，受折磨

senses.concept_en: If you suffer something bad, you are in a situation in which something painful, harmful, or very unpleasant happens to you.
gloss_zh: 遭遇，遭受，蒙受（不好的事）

senses.concept_en: If you suffer, you are badly affected by an event or situation.
If something suffers, it does not succeed because it has not been given enough attention or is in a bad situation.
gloss_zh: （因不够关注或处于不利境况而）失利，失败，不成功

summer.translation:
n. 夏季, 全盛时期
vi. 避暑, 过夏天
[计] 加法器

senses.concept_en: See also:high summer;Indian summer; Summer is the season between spring and autumn. In the summer the weather is usually warm or hot.

supermarket.translation:
n. 超级市场
[经] 超级市场, 自助售货商店

senses.concept_en: A supermarket is a large shop which sells all kinds of food and some household goods.

supply.translation:
n. 补给, 供给, 供应品
vt. 补给, 供给, 提供, 补充
vi. 替代
supply.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: If you supply someone with something that they want or need, you give them a quantity of it.
You can use supplies to refer to food, equipment, and other essential things that people need, especially when these are provided in large quantities.
gloss_zh: （尤指大量的）补给，补给品，日用物资

senses.concept_en: A supply of something is an amount of it which someone has or which is available for them to use.
Supply is the quantity of goods and services that can be made available for people to buy.
If you supply a missing word or piece of information, for example in a puzzle, you say or write it because you know it.

suspend.translation:
vt. 悬, 吊, 使悬浮, 暂停, 中止, 推迟
vi. 暂停, 中止, 悬浮, 停止偿付债务
[计] 暂停
suspend.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.
If someone is suspended, they are prevented from holding a particular job or position for a fixed length of time or until a decision is made about them.
If something is suspended from a high place, it is hanging from that place.

talk.translation:
n. 谈话, 交谈, 会谈, 讲话, 演讲, 空谈, 谣言, 方言, 语言
vi. 讲话, 演讲, 说话, 谈话, 交流, 闲聊, 说闲话
vt. 讲, 说, 讨论, 谈论
[计] 对话类, 聊天

senses.concept_en: When you talk, you use spoken language to express your thoughts, ideas, or feelings.
If you talk to someone, you have a conversation with them. You can also say that two people talk .
If you talk to someone, you tell them about the things that are worrying you. You can also say that two people talk .
If you talk on or about something, you make an informal speech telling people what you know or think about it.
Talks are formal discussions intended to produce an agreement, usually between different countries or between employers and employees.
gloss_zh: （通常指国家、劳资间为达成某种协定的）谈判，商谈

senses.concept_en: If one group of people talks to another, or if two groups talk, they have formal discussions in order to do a deal or produce an agreement.
When different countries or different sides in a dispute talk, or talk to each other, they discuss their differences in order to try and settle the dispute.
If people are talking about another person or are talking, they are discussing that person.
If someone talks when they are being held by police or soldiers, they reveal important or secret information, usually unwillingly.
gloss_zh: （通常指不情愿地）供出，招认，招供

senses.concept_en: If you talk a particular language or talk with a particular accent, you use that language or have that accent when you speak.
gloss_zh: 讲，说，操（某种语言或口音）

senses.concept_en: If you talk something such as politics or sport, you discuss it.

You can use talk to say what you think of the ideas that someone is expressing. For example, if you say that someone is talking sense, you mean that you think the opinions they are expressing are sensible.
You can say that you are talking a particular thing to draw attention to your topic or to point out a characteristic of what you are discussing.

If you say that something such as an idea or threat is just talk, or all talk, you mean that it does not mean or matter much, because people are exaggerating about it or do not really intend to do anything about it.

team.translation:
n. 队, 组
vt. 把马(牛)套在同一辆车上, 把...编成一组
vi. 驾驶卡车, 协作
team.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.
You can refer to any group of people who work together as a team .

test.translation:
n. 测试, 试验, 化验, 检验, 考验, 甲壳
vt. 测试, 试验, 化验
vi. 接受测验, 进行测试
test.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: When you test something, you try it, for example by touching it or using it for a short time, in order to find out what it is, what condition it is in, or how well it works.
A test is a deliberate action or experiment to find out how well something works.
If you test someone, you ask them questions or tell them to perform certain actions in order to find out how much they know about a subject or how well they are able to do something.
A test is a series of questions that you must answer or actions that you must perform in order to show how much you know about a subject or how well you are able to do something.
If you test someone, you deliberately make things difficult for them in order to see how they react.
If an event or situation is a test of a person or thing, it reveals their qualities or effectiveness.
If you are tested for a particular disease or medical condition, you are examined or go through various procedures in order to find out whether you have that disease or condition.
A medical test is an examination of a part of your body in order to check that you are healthy or to find out what is wrong with you.
A test is a sports match between two international teams, usually in cricket, rugby union, or rugby league.
gloss_zh: （常指板球、橄榄球的）国际锦标赛

than.translation:
conj. 比, 除...外
prep. 比

senses.concept_en: You use than after a comparative adjective or adverb in order to link two parts of a comparison.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词、副词的比较级之后，连接比较对象）比

senses.concept_en: You use than when you are stating a number, quantity, or value approximately by saying that it is above or below another number, quantity, or value.
gloss_zh: （数目、数量、价值等）比…（多、少、重要或次要等）

senses.concept_en: You use than in order to link two parts of a contrast, for example in order to state a preference.
gloss_zh: 与其说，而不是（连接对比的对象，以表示优先考虑等）

that.translation:
a. 那, 那个
conj. 以致, 因为
pron. 那
adv. 那么, 那样

senses.concept_en: You use that to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.
gloss_zh: 那，那个（指代前面句子里提到的）

senses.concept_en: You use that to refer to someone or something already mentioned.
gloss_zh: 那个人,那个（用来指代已经提到的人或物）

senses.concept_en: When you have been talking about a particular period of time, you use that to indicate that you are still referring to the same period. You use expressions such as that morning or that afternoon to indicate that you are referring to an earlier period of the same day.
gloss_zh: 那，那个（指已经谈到过的特定时期）

senses.concept_en: You use that in expressions such as that of and that which to introduce more information about something already mentioned, instead of repeating the noun which refers to it.
gloss_zh: （用于 that of, that which 等短语中引出有关上文提到的某事物的更多信息，而避免重复相关名词）

senses.concept_en: You use that in front of words or expressions which express agreement, responses, or reactions to what has just been said.
gloss_zh: 那个，那（用于对前述内容表示同意或作出应答的词和词组前）

senses.concept_en: You use that to introduce a person or thing that you are going to give details or information about.
gloss_zh: 那一个，那个（引出将要更加详细介绍的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use that when you are referring to someone or something which is a distance away from you in position or time, especially when you indicate or point to them. When there are two or more things near you, that refers to the more distant one.
gloss_zh: 那个（指代在时间、空间上离自己稍远的人或物，尤用于指示;有两个以上的事物时，that 指较远的那个）

senses.concept_en: You use that when you are identifying someone or asking about their identity.
You can use that when you expect the person you are talking to to know what or who you are referring to, without needing to identify the particular person or thing fully.
gloss_zh: （不需明确指出的情况下谈话对方即可能知道所指的人或物）那个

senses.concept_en: If something is not that bad, funny, or expensive for example, it is not as bad, funny, or expensive as it might be or as has been suggested.
gloss_zh: 不太，不那么（坏、滑稽、昂贵等）

senses.concept_en: You can use that to emphasize the degree of a feeling or quality.
gloss_zh: 那么，那样（用于强调感情或品质的程度之深）

senses.concept_en: You can use that after many verbs, adjectives, nouns, and expressions to introduce a clause in which you report what someone has said, or what they think or feel.
gloss_zh: （用于动词、形容词、名词、短语之后，引导间接引语从句）

senses.concept_en: You use that after 'it' and a link verb and an adjective to comment on a situation or fact.
gloss_zh: （用于“it+系动词+形容词”结构之后，表示评论）

senses.concept_en: You use that to introduce a clause which gives more information to help identify the person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，以提供更多有关谈论对象的信息）

senses.concept_en: You use that after expressions with 'so' and 'such' in order to introduce the result or effect of something.
gloss_zh: （用在 so，such 之后，引出结果或影响）

senses.concept_en: You use the at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.
gloss_zh: （用于名词短语之前，指代已经提及或指明的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use the at the beginning of a noun group when the first noun is followed by an 'of' phrase or a clause which identifies the person or thing.
gloss_zh: （当名词后接 of 短语或表明身份的从句时，该名词前用the）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of some nouns that refer to something in our general experience of the world.
gloss_zh: （用于某些表示人们共有经历的名词前）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of nouns that refer to people, things, services, or institutions that are associated with everyday life.
gloss_zh: （用于和日常生活相关的人、物、服务、机构的名词前）

senses.concept_en: You use the instead of a possessive determiner, especially when you are talking about a part of someone's body or a member of their family.
gloss_zh: （用于代替所有格限定词，尤在谈论身体某一部分或家庭某一成员时）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of a singular noun when you want to make a general statement about things or people of that type.
gloss_zh: （用于单数名词前，表示一类人或事物）

senses.concept_en: You use the with the name of a musical instrument when you are talking about someone's ability to play the instrument.
gloss_zh: （谈论是否会演奏乐器时，用于乐器名称前）

senses.concept_en: You use the with nationality adjectives and nouns to talk about the people who live in a country.
gloss_zh: （用于表示国籍的形容词和名词以谈论一国全体国民）

senses.concept_en: You use the with words such as 'rich', 'poor', 'old', or 'unemployed' to refer to all people of a particular type.
gloss_zh: （与 rich, poor, old, unemployed 等形容词连用，表示某一类人）

senses.concept_en: If you want to refer to a whole family or to a married couple, you can make their surname into a plural and use the in front of it.
gloss_zh: （用于姓氏的复数前，表示一家人或夫妻）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of an adjective when you are referring to a particular thing that is described by that adjective.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词前，表示其修饰的某个事物）

senses.concept_en: You use the to indicate that you have enough of the thing mentioned for a particular purpose.
gloss_zh: （表示拥有为某一特定目的所需的足够的某物）

senses.concept_en: You use the with some titles, place names, and other names.
gloss_zh: （与某些称号、地名和其他名称连用）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of numbers such as first, second, and third.
You use the in front of numbers when they refer to decades.
You use the in front of superlative adjectives and adverbs.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词和副词的最高级前）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of each of two comparative adjectives or adverbs when you are describing how one amount or quality changes in relation to another.
gloss_zh: 越…越…（用于两个比较级前，表示其中一个随另一个发生量或质的变化）

senses.concept_en: When you express rates, prices, and measurements, you can use the to say how many units apply to each of the items being measured.
gloss_zh: 每，一（表示速度、价格、度量等）

senses.concept_en: You use the to indicate that something or someone is the most famous, important, or best thing of its kind. In spoken English, you put more stress on it, and in written English, you often underline it or write it in capitals or italics.
gloss_zh: （表示某人或某物是同类中最有名、最重要或最好的。口语中 the 要重读；书面语中常加下划线或用大写、斜体）

senses.concept_en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.
You use their instead of 'his or her' to indicate that something belongs or relates to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people think this use is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （代替 his or her，而不指明是男是女;有人认为这种用法不对）

senses.concept_en: You use these at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.
gloss_zh: （用于名词词组前，指代已提及的人或事物）这些

senses.concept_en: You use these to introduce people or things that you are going to talk about.
gloss_zh: （引出将要提及的人或事物）这些

senses.concept_en: In spoken English, people use these to introduce people or things into a story.
gloss_zh: （口语中用来引出故事中的人或物）一些

senses.concept_en: You use these when you are identifying someone or asking about their identity.
gloss_zh: 这些，他们（用以说明或询问身份）

senses.concept_en: You use these to refer to people or things that are near you, especially when you touch them or point to them.
gloss_zh: 这些（指离自己近的人或物，尤指所触碰或指向的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use these when you refer to something which you expect the person you are talking to to know about, or when you are checking that you are both thinking of the same person or thing.
gloss_zh: 这些（用于指代认为谈话对象了解具体所指的事物，或确认双方所想的是相同的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use these in the expression these days to mean 'at the present time'.
You use they to refer to a group of people, animals, or things.
You use they instead of 'he or she' to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people think this use is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （用以代替he or she，而不指明是男是女;有人认为这种用法不对）

senses.concept_en: You use they in expressions such as 'they say' or 'they call it' to refer to people in general when you are making general statements about what people say, think, or do.
gloss_zh: （用于 they say，they call it 等表达中表示泛指）他们

this.translation:
pron. 这, 本
a. 这, 本
adv. 这么

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer back to a particular person or thing that has been mentioned or implied.
gloss_zh: （指代先前提及的人或物）这，这个

senses.concept_en: You use this to introduce someone or something that you are going to talk about.
gloss_zh: （引出将要谈论的人或物）下面（这个），以下

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.
gloss_zh: 这一点（指前一句或几句话中提到的观点或情况）

senses.concept_en: In spoken English, people use this to introduce a person or thing into a story.
gloss_zh: （叙述时引出新出现的人或物）这个，一个

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer to a person or thing that is near you, especially when you touch them or point to them. When there are two or more people or things near you, this refers to the nearest one.
gloss_zh: 这个，这位（尤指所触碰或指向的离自己较近的人或物，有两个以上时，用于指最近的一个）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you refer to a general situation, activity, or event which is happening or has just happened and which you feel involved in.
gloss_zh: 这个，这（指代正在发生或刚刚发生的与自己有关的一般情况、活动或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you refer to the place you are in now or to the present time.
gloss_zh: 这，该，此（指当前所处地点或时间）

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer to the next occurrence in the future of a particular day, month, season, or festival.
gloss_zh: 本，今，这个，下一个（指接下来将要发生某事的特定时间）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you are indicating the size or shape of something with your hands.
gloss_zh: 这么，这样（用于用手比划大小、形状时）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you are going to specify how much you know or how much you can tell someone.
gloss_zh: 这么，这样（用于说明自己知道或能告知的内容）

senses.concept_en: You use this in order to say who you are or what organization you are representing, when you are speaking on the telephone, radio, or television.
gloss_zh: （用于电话、广播或电视中，表明身份或所代表的机构）我是，这里是

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer to the medium of communication that you are using at the time of speaking or writing.
gloss_zh: 这个（指说话、写作时的媒介）

thrive.translation:
vi. 繁荣, 兴旺, 茁壮成长
[经] 兴旺, 繁荣, 旺盛
thrive.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If someone or something thrives, they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong.
gloss_zh: 欣欣向荣;茁壮成长;兴旺发达

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone thrives on a particular situation, you mean that they enjoy it or that they can deal with it very well, especially when other people find it unpleasant or difficult.
gloss_zh: （尤指在别人觉得困难的时候）以…为乐，可以出色应对

time.translation:
n. 时间, 时侯, 时机, 时期, 期限, 次数, 节拍, 暂停, 规定时间
vt. 测定...的时间, 记录...的时间, 计时, 定时
a. 时间的, 记时的, 定时的, 定期的, 分期的
[计] DOS内部命令:用于显示或设定系统的时间

senses.concept_en: Time is what we measure in minutes, hours, days, and years.
You use time to ask or talk about a specific point in the day, which can be stated in hours and minutes and is shown on clocks.
See also:opening time; The time when something happens is the point in the day when it happens or is supposed to happen.
You use time to refer to the system of expressing time and counting hours that is used in a particular part of the world.
You use time to refer to the period that you spend doing something or when something has been happening.
gloss_zh: （用来做某事或某事发生的）时间

senses.concept_en: If you say that something has been happening for a time, you mean that it has been happening for a fairly long period of time.

You use time to refer to a period of time or a point in time, when you are describing what is happening then. For example, if something happened at a particular time, that is when it happened. If it happens at all times, it always happens.
gloss_zh: （某事发生的）一段（或特定）时间

senses.concept_en: You use time or times to talk about a particular period in history or in your life.

You can use the times to refer to the present time and to modern fashions, tastes, and developments. For example, if you say that someone keeps up with the times, you mean they are fashionable or aware of modern developments. If you say they are behind the times, you mean they are unfashionable or not aware of them.
When you describe the time that you had on a particular occasion or during a particular part of your life, you are describing the sort of experience that you had then.
Your time is the amount of time that you have to live, or to do a particular thing.
If you say it is time for something, time to do something, or time you did something, you mean that this thing ought to happen or be done now.
When you talk about a time when something happens, you are referring to a specific occasion when it happens.
You use time after numbers to say how often something happens.
You use times after numbers when comparing one thing to another and saying, for example, how much bigger, smaller, better, or worse it is.
You use times in arithmetic to link numbers or amounts that are multiplied together to reach a total.
Someone's time in a race is the amount of time it takes them to finish the race.
The time of a piece of music is the number of beats that the piece has in each bar.
If you time something for a particular time, you plan or decide to do it or cause it to happen at this time.
gloss_zh: 给…确定时间;为…安排时间

senses.concept_en: If you time an action or activity, you measure how long someone takes to do it or how long it lasts.

to.translation:
prep. 到, 向, 趋于
adv. 向前

senses.concept_en: You use to when indicating the place that someone or something visits, moves towards, or points at.
If you go to an event, you go where it is taking place.
If something is attached to something larger or fixed to it, the two things are joined together.
You use to when indicating the position of something. For example, if something is to your left, it is nearer your left side than your right side.
When you give something to someone, they receive it.
You use to to indicate who or what an action or a feeling is directed towards.
gloss_zh: （表示动作或情感的对象）对，于

senses.concept_en: You use to with certain nouns and adjectives to show that a following noun is related to them.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词、形容词连用，表示关联）对于，关于

senses.concept_en: If you say something to someone, you want that person to listen and understand what you are saying.

You use to when indicating someone's reaction to something or their feelings about a situation or event. For example, if you say that something happens to someone's surprise you mean that they are surprised when it happens.
You use to when indicating the person whose opinion you are stating.
You use to when indicating what something or someone is becoming, or the state or situation that they are progressing towards.
To can be used as a way of introducing the person or organization you are employed by, when you perform some service for them.
You use to to indicate that something happens until the time or amount mentioned is reached.
You use to when indicating the last thing in a range of things, usually when you are giving two extreme examples of something.
If someone goes from place to place or from job to job, they go to several places, or work in several jobs, and spend only a short time in each one.
You use to when you are stating a time which is less than thirty minutes before an hour. For example, if it is 'five to eight', it is five minutes before eight o'clock.
You use to when giving ratios and rates.
You use to when indicating that two things happen at the same time. For example, if something is done to music, it is done at the same time as music is being played.
If you push or shut a door to, you close it but may not shut it completely.
You use to before the base form of a verb to form the to-infinitive. You use the to-infinitive after certain verbs, nouns, and adjectives, and after words such as 'how', 'which', and 'where'.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前构成不定式;不定式用于某些动词、名词、形容词以及 how，which, where 等词之后）。

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb to indicate the purpose or intention of an action. in order to
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示动作的目的或意图）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb when you are commenting on a statement that you are making, for example when saying that you are being honest or brief, or that you are summing up or giving an example.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示对自己要说的话加以说明）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb in exclamations when you are emphasizing a very strong emotion, such as a desire or wish, or a regret or disappointment.
gloss_zh: （用于感叹句中的动词原形前，强调某一强烈情感）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb when indicating what situation follows a particular action.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示某一动作之后的情形）

senses.concept_en: You use to with 'too' and 'enough' in expressions like too much to and old enough to

today.translation:
n. 今天, 当今, 现在
adv. 今天, 当今

senses.concept_en: You use today to refer to the day on which you are speaking or writing.
You can refer to the present period of history as today .

toward.translation:
prep. 向, 对于, 为了
a. 即将来临的, 进行中的

town.translation:
n. 城镇, 市, 镇
[法] 城镇, 城市, 闹市

senses.concept_en: A town is a place with many streets and buildings, where people live and work. Towns are larger than villages and smaller than cities. Many places that are called towns in Britain would be called cities in the United States.
You use town in order to refer to the town where you live.
You use town in order to refer to the central area of a town where most of the shops and offices are.
gloss_zh: 市中心;（城镇的）商业中心；闹市区

senses.concept_en: If you refer to the town, you are referring to town and city areas in general, as opposed to country areas.

trade.translation:
n. 贸易, 商业, 交易, 生意, 职业, 顾客, 信风
vi. 进行交易, 做买卖, 经商, 对换, 购物
vt. 用...进行交换
trade.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Trade is the activity of buying, selling, or exchanging goods or services between people, firms, or countries.
When people, firms, or countries trade, they buy, sell, or exchange goods or services between themselves.
gloss_zh: 做买卖;做生意;从事贸易

senses.concept_en: A trade is a particular area of business or industry.
Someone's trade is the kind of work that they do, especially when they have been trained to do it over a period of time.
If someone trades one thing for another or if two people trade things, they agree to exchange one thing for the other thing.
If you trade places with someone or if the two of you trade places, you move into the other person's position or situation, and they move into yours.
In professional sports, for example football or baseball, if a player is traded from one team to another, they leave one team and begin playing for another.
gloss_zh: 使（足球、棒球等职业运动员）转会

senses.concept_en: If two people or groups trade something such as blows, insults, or jokes, they hit each other, insult each other, or tell each other jokes.

training.translation:
n. 训练, 培养
[医] 训练
training.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Training is the process of learning the skills that you need for a particular job or activity.
Training is physical exercise that you do regularly in order to keep fit or to prepare for an activity such as a race.
gloss_zh: （为了健身或体育活动而进行的）训练，锻炼

transformation.translation:
n. 变形, 变质, 变化, 改革, 变换
[化] 转化; 变换

senses.concept_en: Twelve is the number 12.
Twenty is the number 20.

When you talk about the twenties, you are referring to numbers between 20 and 29. For example, if you are in your twenties, you are aged between 20 and 29. If the temperature is in the twenties, the temperature is between 20 and 29 degrees.
gloss_zh: （20 至 29 之间的数字）二十几

senses.concept_en: The twenties is the decade between 1920 and 1929.
gloss_zh: 二十世纪二十年代（1920 至 1929 年间）

senses.concept_en: Two is the number 2.

under.translation:
prep. 在...之下, 低于
a. 下面的, 从属的
adv. 在下面

senses.concept_en: If a person or thing is under something, they are at a lower level than that thing, and may be covered or hidden by it.
In a place such as a sea, river, or swimming pool, if someone or something is under the water, they are fully in the water and covered by it.
If you go under something, you move from one side to the other of something that is at a higher level than you.
Something that is under a layer of something, especially clothing, is covered by that layer.
gloss_zh: 在（尤指一层衣服）的里面（或底下）

senses.concept_en: You can use under before a noun to indicate that a person or thing is being affected by something or is going through a particular process.
If something happens under particular circumstances or conditions, it happens when those circumstances or conditions exist.
If something happens under a law, agreement, or system, it happens because that law, agreement, or system says that it should happen.
gloss_zh: 根据，按照，依照（法律、协定、制度等）

senses.concept_en: If something happens under a particular person or government, it happens when that person or government is in power.
gloss_zh: 在（…领导）下；在（…当政）期间；在（…统治）之下

senses.concept_en: If you study or work under a particular person, that person teaches you or tells you what to do.
gloss_zh: 在…指导下（学习）；在…手下（工作）

senses.concept_en: If you do something under a particular name, you use that name instead of your real name.
gloss_zh: 用（…之名）；以（…的名义）；假借（…之名）

senses.concept_en: You use under to say which section of a list, book, or system something is in.
If something or someone is under a particular age or amount, they are less than that age or amount
gloss_zh: （年龄或数量）不足，低于，在…以下

urgent.translation:
a. 紧急的, 急迫的, 催逼的
[经] 紧急的, 急迫的
urgent.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl gre

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is urgent, it needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you speak in an urgent way, you show that you are anxious for people to notice something or to do something.

vegetable.translation:
n. 蔬菜, 植物, 无精打采之人
a. 蔬菜的, 植物的

senses.concept_en: Vegetables are plants such as cabbages, potatoes, and onions which you can cook and eat.
Vegetable matter comes from plants.
If someone refers to a brain-damaged person as a vegetable, they mean that the person cannot move, think, or speak.

venture.translation:
n. 冒险, 风险
vt. 敢于, 冒...的危险
vi. 冒险

senses.concept_en: A venture is a project or activity which is new, exciting, and difficult because it involves the risk of failure.
gloss_zh: 风险项目（或活动）;冒险事业

senses.concept_en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous.
If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.
gloss_zh: 斗胆提出（问题）;冒险发表（陈述）

senses.concept_en: If you venture to do something that requires courage or is risky, you do it.
If you venture into an activity, you do something that involves the risk of failure because it is new and different.

visitor.translation:
n. 参观者, 游客, 访客
[法] 视察人, 检视人, 检查员

senses.concept_en: A visitor is someone who is visiting a person or place.

wall.translation:
n. 墙, 墙壁, 垣, 内壁, 分界物, 屏障
a. 墙的
vt. 给...建墙, 禁闭, 用墙围住
[计] 背景墙

senses.concept_en: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.
A wall is a long narrow vertical structure made of stone or brick that surrounds or divides an area of land.
The wall of something that is hollow is its side.
A wall of something is a large amount of it forming a high vertical barrier.
gloss_zh: 屏障;堆成墙的大量物品

senses.concept_en: You can describe something as a wall of a particular kind when it acts as a barrier and prevents people from understanding something.

water.translation:
n. 水, 雨水, 海水, 水位, 水面, 流水
vt. 给...浇水, 供以水, 注入水, 使湿
vi. 流泪, 流口水, 加水
a. 水的, 水上的, 水生的, 含水的

senses.concept_en: Water is a clear thin liquid that has no colour or taste when it is pure. It falls from clouds as rain and enters rivers and seas. All animals and people need water in order to live.
You use waters to refer to a large area of sea, especially the area of sea which is near to a country and which is regarded as belonging to it.
You sometimes use waters to refer to a situation which is very complex or difficult.
If you water plants, you pour water over them in order to help them to grow.
If your eyes water, tears build up in them because they are hurting or because you are upset.
See also:mouth-watering; If you say that your mouth is watering, you mean that you can smell or see some nice food and you might mean that your mouth is producing a liquid.

weak.translation:
a. 不牢固的, 弱的, 虚弱的, 软弱的, 无力的, 无权力的, (论据等)不充分的
[经] 疲软的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is weak, they are not healthy or do not have good muscles, so that they cannot move quickly or carry heavy things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has an organ or sense that is weak, it is not very effective or powerful, or is likely to fail.
gloss_zh: （器官或感官）功能差的，受损伤的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as weak, you mean that they are not very confident or determined, so that they are often frightened or worried, or easily influenced by other people.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone's voice or smile as weak, you mean that it is not very loud or big, suggesting that the person lacks confidence, enthusiasm, or physical strength.
gloss_zh: （声音或笑容）微弱的，不热情的，无力的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If an object or surface is weak, it breaks easily and cannot support a lot of weight or resist a lot of strain.
gloss_zh: 不牢固的;易破的;易坏的

senses.concept_en: A weak physical force does not have much power or intensity.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If individuals or groups are weak, they do not have any power or influence.
gloss_zh: 无权力的;无权威的;无影响力的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A weak government or leader does not have much control, and is not prepared or able to act firmly or severely.
gloss_zh: （政府或领导人） 软弱无力的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something such a country's currency, economy, industry, or government as weak, you mean that it is not successful, and may be likely to fail or collapse.
gloss_zh: （货币、经济、产业、政府等）疲软的，有崩溃危险的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something such as an argument or case is weak, it is not convincing or there is little evidence to support it.
gloss_zh: （论据等）不充分的，没有说服力的;（逻辑）不周密的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A weak drink, chemical, or drug contains very little of a particular substance, for example because a lot of water has been added to it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Your weak points are the qualities or talents you do not possess, or the things you are not very good at.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can say that someone has a weak chin to indicate that their chin is not large, especially when you want to suggest that they do not have a strong character.
gloss_zh: （下巴）瘦小的;（尤暗指）性格懦弱的

weather.translation:
n. 天气, 气象, 处境
a. 迎风的
vt. 使受风吹雨打, 侵蚀, 使风化, 经受住
vi. 风化, 受侵蚀, 经受风雨

senses.concept_en: The weather is the condition of the atmosphere in one area at a particular time, for example if it is raining, hot, or windy.
If something such as wood or rock weathers or is weathered, it changes colour or shape as a result of the wind, sun, rain, or cold.
If you weather a difficult time or a difficult situation, you survive it and are able to continue normally after it has passed or ended. to weather the storm
A week is a period of seven days. Some people consider that a week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.
A week is a period of about seven days.
gloss_zh: 一周时间;七天左右的时间

senses.concept_en: Your working week is the hours that you spend at work during a week.
gloss_zh: 工作周（指一周的工作时间）

senses.concept_en: The week is the part of the week that does not include Saturday and Sunday.
gloss_zh: （除去星期六和星期日的）星期，周，礼拜

senses.concept_en: You use week in expressions such as 'a week on Monday', 'a week next Tuesday', and 'tomorrow week' to mean exactly one week after the day that you mention.
You use week in expressions such as 'a week last Monday', 'a week ago this Tuesday', and 'a week ago yesterday' to mean exactly one week before the day that you mention.

weekend.translation: n. 周末, 周末休假

senses.concept_en: A weekend is Saturday and Sunday.

what.translation:
pron. 什么
interj. 怎么, 多么
a. 什么的
adv. 到什么程度

senses.concept_en: You use what in questions when you ask for specific information about something that you do not know.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句中询问所不知道的信息）什么

senses.concept_en: You use what after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, when you are referring to a situation that is unknown or has not been specified.
gloss_zh: （尤用于动词和形容词后以引导关系从句）

senses.concept_en: You use what at the beginning of a clause in structures where you are changing the order of the information to give special emphasis to something.
gloss_zh: （用在强调句型的句首）所…的（是…）

senses.concept_en: You use what in expressions such as what is called and what amounts to when you are giving a description of something.
You use what to indicate that you are talking about the whole of an amount that is available to you.
You say 'What' to express surprise.
You use what in exclamations to emphasize an opinion or reaction.
gloss_zh: （用在感叹句中强调某种意见或反应）多么

senses.concept_en: You use what to indicate that you are making a guess about something such as an amount or value.

when.translation:
conj. 当...的时候
adv. 何时, 什么时候
pron. 什么时侯
n. 时间

senses.concept_en: You use when to ask questions about the time at which things happen.
If something happens when something else is happening, the two things are happening at the same time.
gloss_zh: （表示两事同时发生）在…时，当…时

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce a clause in which you mention something which happens at some point during an activity, event, or situation.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，表示某事发生于另一活动、事件或情形期间）在…的过程中

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce a clause where you mention the circumstances under which the event in the main clause happened or will happen.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，说明主句动作已经发生或将要发生时的情况）其时

senses.concept_en: You use when after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause where you mention the time at which something happens.
gloss_zh: （尤用于动词和形容词后引导从句，表示某事发生的时间）什么时候,何时

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce a clause which specifies or refers to the time at which something happens.
gloss_zh: （用于引导从句，限定或指示某事发生的时间）…的时候

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce the reason for an opinion, comment, or question.
gloss_zh: （用于引出某个观点、评论或问题的原因）既然，考虑到

senses.concept_en: You use when in order to introduce a fact or comment which makes the other part of the sentence rather surprising or unlikely.
gloss_zh: （用于引出使句子的其他部分显得让人吃惊或不大可能的事实或评论）虽然，然而,可是

where.translation:
adv. 在哪里
pron. 哪里
n. 地点

senses.concept_en: You use where to ask questions about the place something is in, or is coming from or going to.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句）在哪里，从哪里，到哪里

senses.concept_en: You use where after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention the place in which something is situated or happens.
gloss_zh: （尤用于动词和形容词后引导从句，表示某物所在或某事发生的地点）那里，那儿

senses.concept_en: You use where to ask questions about a situation, a stage in something, or an aspect of something.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句）在哪一地点,在哪一阶段，在哪方面

senses.concept_en: You use where after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention a situation, a stage in something, or an aspect of something.
gloss_zh: （尤用于某些动词和形容词后，引导表示地点、某事物所处状态、阶段等的从句）在哪儿，从哪儿

senses.concept_en: You use where to introduce a clause that contrasts with the other parts of the sentence.
gloss_zh: （用于引导从句进行对比）然而

whether.translation:
conj. 是否, 不论
pron. 两个中的哪一个

senses.concept_en: You use whether when you are talking about a choice or doubt between two or more alternatives.
gloss_zh: （表示选择或怀疑）是否，是不是

senses.concept_en: You use whether to say that something is true in any of the circumstances that you mention.

while.translation:
n. 一会儿, (一段)时间
conj. 当...的时候, 虽然
vt. 消磨

senses.concept_en: If something happens while something else is happening, the two things are happening at the same time.
gloss_zh: （表示两件事同时发生）当…的时候，在…时

senses.concept_en: If something happens while something else happens, the first thing happens at some point during the time that the second thing is happening.
gloss_zh: （表示某一件事是在另一件事发生过程中的某一时间点发生的）当…的时候，在…时

senses.concept_en: You use while at the beginning of a clause to introduce information which contrasts with information in the main clause.
You use while, before making a statement, in order to introduce information that partly conflicts with your statement.
A while is a period of time.
You use who in questions when you ask about the name or identity of a person or group of people.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句，询问人的姓名或身份）谁

senses.concept_en: You use who after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause where you talk about the identity of a person or a group of people.
gloss_zh: （尤用在动词和形容词后引导从句，说明人的身份）谁

senses.concept_en: You use who at the beginning of a relative clause when specifying the person or group of people you are talking about or when giving more information about them.
gloss_zh: （用于进行限定说明或提供更多信息的关系从句的句首）

with.translation: prep. 和...在一起, 以, 由于

senses.concept_en: If one person is with another, they are together in one place.
If something is put with or is with something else, they are used at the same time.
If you do something with someone else, you both do it together or are both involved in it.
If you fight, argue, or compete with someone, you oppose them.
gloss_zh: 和，与，同（…打斗、争论或竞争）

senses.concept_en: If you do something with a particular tool, object, or substance, you do it using that tool, object, or substance.
gloss_zh: 用，使用（某种工具、物品或材料）

senses.concept_en: If someone stands or goes somewhere with something, they are carrying it.
Someone or something with a particular feature or possession has that feature or possession.
gloss_zh: 有，拥有（某种特征或所有物）

senses.concept_en: Someone with an illness has that illness.
If something is filled or covered with a substance or with things, it has that substance or those things in it or on it.
If you are, for example, pleased or annoyed with someone or something, you have that feeling towards them.
You use with to indicate what a state, quality, or action relates to, involves, or affects.
You use with when indicating the way that something is done or the feeling that a person has when they do something.
gloss_zh: 用（某种方式）；带着（某种感情）

senses.concept_en: You use with when indicating a sound or gesture that is made when something is done, or an expression that a person has on their face when they do something.
gloss_zh: 伴着（声音或手势）;带着（表情）

senses.concept_en: You use with to indicate the feeling that makes someone have a particular appearance or type of behaviour.
gloss_zh: 由于，因为（某种感情而使某人有某种表现或行为）

senses.concept_en: You use with when mentioning the position or appearance of a person or thing at the time that they do something, or what someone else is doing at that time.
gloss_zh: （表示以某姿势、外表或伴随某事件做某事）与…同时，随着

senses.concept_en: You use with to introduce a current situation that is a factor affecting another situation.
You use with when making a comparison or contrast between the situations of different people or things.
If something increases or decreases with a particular factor, it changes as that factor changes.
gloss_zh: 随着，跟着（…的变化而变化）

senses.concept_en: If something moves with a wind or current, it moves in the same direction as the wind or current.
gloss_zh: 与（风、水流等）方向一致；顺着…

senses.concept_en: If someone says that they are with you, they mean that they understand what you are saying.
If someone says that they are with you, they mean that they support or approve of what you are doing.

without.translation:
prep. 没有, 不, 在...之外
adv. 在外面, 户外
n. 外面, 外部

senses.concept_en: You use without to indicate that someone or something does not have or use the thing mentioned.
If one thing happens without another thing, or if you do something without doing something else, the second thing does not happen or occur.
gloss_zh: 在没有（发生或做某事）的情况下

senses.concept_en: If you do something without a particular feeling, you do not have that feeling when you do it.
If you do something without someone else, they are not in the same place as you are or are not involved in the same action as you.

wooden.translation: a. 木制的, 呆笨的, 木然的

senses.concept_en: Wooden objects are made of wood.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe an actor as wooden, you are critical of them because their performance is not at all lively or natural.
gloss_zh: （演员）呆板的，死板的，无活力的

work.translation:
n. 工作, 劳动, 职业, 行为, 功, 作品, 成果, 产品, 工程
vi. 工作, 劳动, 做, 运转, 起作用, 被加工
vt. 使工作, 使转动, 开动, 使用, 经营, 使逐渐变得, 造成

senses.concept_en: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
People who have work or who are in work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
When you work, you do the things that you are paid or required to do in your job.
Your work consists of the things you are paid or required to do in your job.
When you work, you spend time and effort doing a task that needs to be done or trying to achieve something.
Work is the place where you do your job.
Work is something which you produce as a result of an activity or as a result of doing your job.
A work is something such as a painting, book, or piece of music produced by an artist, writer, or composer.
gloss_zh: （艺术家、作家、作曲家等的）作品；著作

senses.concept_en: If someone is working on a particular subject or question, they are studying or researching it.
If you work with a person or a group of people, you spend time and effort trying to help them in some way.
If a machine or piece of equipment works, it operates and performs a particular function.
If an idea, system, or way of doing something works, it is successful, effective, or satisfactory.
If a drug or medicine works, it produces a particular physical effect.
If something works in your favour, it helps you in some way. If something works to your disadvantage, it causes problems for you in some way.
gloss_zh: 产生（有利或不利的）影响

senses.concept_en: If something or someone works their magic or works their charms on a person, they have a powerful positive effect on them.
gloss_zh: 对…产生（神奇的影响）;使…深受（魅力感染）

senses.concept_en: If your mind or brain is working, you are thinking about something or trying to solve a problem.
If you work on an assumption or idea, you act as if it were true or base other ideas on it, until you have more information.
gloss_zh: 以（某种假定或思想）为基础（或前提）

senses.concept_en: If you work a particular area or type of place, you travel around that area or work in those places as part of your job, for example trying to sell something there.
gloss_zh: 在（某地或某类场所）工作;在…奔波

senses.concept_en: If you work someone, you make them spend time and effort doing a particular activity or job.
If someone, often a politician or entertainer, works a crowd, they create a good relationship with the people in the crowd and get their support or interest.
gloss_zh: （常指政客或艺人）博得，赢得（众人的支持或欢心）

senses.concept_en: When people work the land, they do all the tasks involved in growing crops.
When a mine is worked, minerals such as coal or gold are removed from it.
If you work a machine or piece of equipment, you use or control it.
If something works into a particular state or condition, it gradually moves so that it is in that state or condition.
If you work a substance such as dough or clay, you keep pressing it to make it have a particular texture.
If you work a material such as metal, leather, or stone, you cut, sew, or shape it in order to make something or to create a design.
If you work with a particular substance or material, you use it in order to make something or to create a design.
gloss_zh: 使用，采用（某种材料或物质）

senses.concept_en: If you work a part of your body, or if it works, you move it.
A works is a place where something is manufactured or where an industrial process is carried out. Works is used to refer to one or to more than one of these places.
Works are activities such as digging the ground or building on a large scale.
You can say the works after listing things such as someone's possessions or requirements, to emphasize that they possess or require everything you can think of in a particular category.
gloss_zh: （某种类型的）全部物件，全套物品

worker.translation:
n. 工人, 劳动者
[经] 工人, 劳工, 劳动者

senses.concept_en: A particular kind of worker does the kind of work mentioned.
Workers are people who are employed in industry or business and who are not managers.
See also:care worker;caseworker;dock worker;social worker;teleworker;youth worker; You can use worker to say how well or badly someone works.

worry.translation:
n. 担心, 烦恼, 忧虑, 苦恼, 撕咬
vt. 使烦恼, 使焦虑, 使苦恼, 困扰, 折磨, 撕咬
vi. 烦恼, 担心, 撕咬

senses.concept_en: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.
If someone or something worries you, they make you anxious because you keep thinking about problems or unpleasant things that might be connected with them.
If someone or something does not worry you, you do not dislike them or you are not annoyed by them.
Worry is the state or feeling of anxiety and unhappiness caused by the problems that you have or by thinking about unpleasant things that might happen.
A worry is a problem that you keep thinking about and that makes you unhappy.
gloss_zh: 使人担心（或发愁）的问题；烦心事

senses.concept_en: You use would when you are saying what someone believed, hoped, or expected to happen or be the case.
gloss_zh: （表示曾经相信、希望或期待）将，将会

senses.concept_en: You use would when saying what someone intended to do.
You use would when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible situation.
gloss_zh: （表示可能出现的情况的结果或影响）会，将会

senses.concept_en: You use would, or would have with a past participle, to indicate that you are assuming or guessing that something is true, because you have good reasons for thinking it.
gloss_zh: （would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示有充分理由认为或猜测是某种情况）肯定，一定，应该

senses.concept_en: You use would in the main clause of some 'if' and 'unless' sentences to indicate something you consider to be fairly unlikely to happen.
gloss_zh: （用于if，unless等引导的条件状语从句的主句，表示认为某事不大可能发生）就，该

senses.concept_en: You use would to say that someone was willing to do something. You use would not to indicate that they refused to do something.
You use would not to indicate that something did not happen, often in spite of a lot of effort.
gloss_zh: （表示尽管付出很大努力却没有发生）就（不），偏（不）

senses.concept_en: You use would, especially with 'like', 'love', and 'wish', when saying that someone wants to do or have a particular thing or wants a particular thing to happen. would rather
gloss_zh: （尤与like, love 和 wish 连用，表示想做某事或拥有某物，或希望某事发生）要，会

senses.concept_en: You use would with 'if' clauses in questions when you are asking for permission to do something.
gloss_zh: （用于带if从句的疑问句中，表示请求许可做某事）会

senses.concept_en: You use would, usually in questions with 'like', when you are making a polite offer or invitation.
gloss_zh: （通常在疑问句中与 like 连用，表示礼貌地给予或邀请）

senses.concept_en: You use would, usually in questions, when you are politely asking someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （通常用于疑问句中，表示礼貌地请求某人做某事）请

senses.concept_en: You say that someone would do something when it is typical of them and you are critical of it. You emphasize the word would when you use it in this way.
gloss_zh: （用于批评，表示对某人做某事并不感到意外，此时 would 须重读）

senses.concept_en: You use would, or sometimes would have with a past participle, when you are expressing your opinion about something or seeing if people agree with you, especially when you are uncertain about what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示发表看法或了解他人是否赞同自己的看法，尤用于对自己的话没有把握时）

senses.concept_en: You use I would when you are giving someone advice in an informal way.
gloss_zh: （用于以随便的口气向人提出建议）我（就）会

senses.concept_en: You use you would in negative sentences with verbs such as 'guess' and 'know' when you want to say that something is not obvious, especially something surprising.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句，与 guess, know 等动词连用，表示某事不明显，尤用于某事令人吃惊时）

senses.concept_en: You use would to talk about something which happened regularly in the past but which no longer happens.
gloss_zh: （表示某事过去惯常发生, 而现在不再发生了）就，会

senses.concept_en: You use would have with a past participle when you are saying what was likely to have happened by a particular time.
gloss_zh: （would have 与过去分词连用，表示某个时间前可能发生的事情）就，会

senses.concept_en: You use would have with a past participle when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible event in the past.
gloss_zh: （would have 与过去分词连用，表示过去可能发生的事情的结果或影响）就，会

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone would have liked or preferred something, you mean that they wanted to do it or have it but were unable to.
You use would, usually in negative sentences, to criticize something that someone has done and to express your disapproval of it.
gloss_zh: （通常用于否定句，批评某人所为，表示不满）（不）会

write.translation:
vt. 书写, 著述, 写, 写满, 写信给
vi. 写, 写字, 写信, 写作, 作曲
[计] 书写器

senses.concept_en: When you write something on a surface, you use something such as a pen or pencil to produce words, letters, or numbers on the surface.
If you write something such as a book, a poem, or a piece of music, you create it and record it on paper or perhaps on a computer.
Someone who writes creates books, stories, or articles, usually for publication.
gloss_zh: 写作，著述（通常以出版为目的）

senses.concept_en: When you write to someone or write them a letter, you give them information, ask them something, or express your feelings in a letter. In American English, you can also write someone. nothing to write home about
gloss_zh: 写（信）;给…写信（美国英语亦可用 write someone）

senses.concept_en: If someone writes that something is the case, they say it in a letter, book, or article.
When someone writes something such as a cheque, receipt, or prescription, they put the necessary information on it and usually sign it.
If you write to a computer or a disk, you record data on it.

year.translation:
n. 年, 年度, 年龄
[经] 年度

senses.concept_en: See also:leap year; A year is a period of twelve months or 365 or 366 days, beginning on the first of January and ending on the thirty-first of December.
A year is any period of twelve months.
Year is used to refer to the age of a person. For example, if someone or something is twenty years old or twenty years of age, they have lived or existed for twenty years.

A school year or academic year is the period of time in each twelve months when schools or universities are open and students are studying there. In Britain and the United States, the school year starts in September.
gloss_zh: 学年（英国和美国的学年从9月开始）

senses.concept_en: You can refer to someone who is, for example, in their first year at school or university as a first year.
A financial or business year is an exact period of twelve months which businesses or institutions use as a basis for organizing their finances.
You can use years to emphasize that you are referring to a long time.
You can refer to the time you spend in a place or doing an activity as your years there or your years of doing that activity.
gloss_zh: （在某地或做某事的）年头，时期

young.translation:
a. 年轻的, 无经验的, 朝气蓬勃的
n. 青年们, 幼小动物, 崽

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A young person, animal, or plant has not lived or existed for very long and is not yet mature.
gloss_zh: 年幼的;幼小的;未成熟的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use young to describe a time when a person or thing was young.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is young in appearance or behaviour looks or behaves as if they are young.
gloss_zh: （显得）年轻的;（显得）岁数不大的

senses.concept_en: The young of an animal are its babies.

article.title: Saving the Mill in Cold Creek
article.summary_zh: 林师傅带领工人克服严寒危机，保障毛纺厂如期完成冬季生产。
article.body:
Last November, Master Lin stared at the wall calendar in his small office. A sudden shortage of water threatened the village wool factory, where fifty families earned their living. The local stream had dropped to a dangerous level, which prompted Lin to act before the ground froze completely. He decided to compile a clear list of every working tool, pipe, and machine in the building. Lin knew that the village needed to weave three thousand heavy blankets before the New Year, or many families would suffer severe financial losses during the winter months.

As December arrived, a bitter chill settled over the northern valley, and worries began to mount among the workers. Some younger men fell into despair because the main wooden wheel stopped turning when thick ice blocked the canal. However, several faithful workers remained at the factory every morning, wearing thick coats and protective boots to guard against the freezing wind. They brought buckets of warm water and dry wood from the forest, determined to keep the rooms warm enough for the wool thread so that it would not break in the cold air.

One morning, Lin used a long iron rod to poke at the hard ice that filled the pipe. A loud cracking noise startled three workers who stood nearby, making them jump back toward the stone wall. To clear the ice without breaking the metal, the men poured warm salt water over the joints, watching the ice slowly dissolve. Lin opened a tap to drain the remaining dirty water into an empty ditch outside. He often warned his young helpers that lazy work was an evil habit that could destroy an entire shop in a single day.

To prevent future trouble, Lin guided the conversion of their old water system into a cleaner, closed system. He chose to delegate the daily pipe checks to two young mechanics who showed great care. In the evening, Lin helped the village clerk compose a formal letter to request spare parts from the county center. He insisted that every replacement part must reach an acceptable quality standard before workers used it. Even in the midst of heavy work and tight time limits, Lin never allowed anyone to rush past a safety check.

By mid-January, the cold wind did not cease, but the village factory achieved steady stability. A large proportion of the finished blankets passed inspection, and trucks carried them directly to the town hall. In the big room, Lin arranged a modest exhibit of the blankets so that town leaders could examine the thick cloth and bright colors. The successful delivery brought a true sense of triumph to the villagers, proving that honest work and careful planning could overcome the hardest season.

The successful delivery brought a true sense of triumph to the villagers, proving that honest work and careful planning could overcome the hardest season.

senses.concept_en: If you guard against something, you are careful to prevent it from happening, or to avoid being affected by it.
If you are in the midst of doing something, you are doing it at the moment.
If something happens in the midst of an event, it happens during it.
If someone or something is in the midst of a group of people or things, they are among them or surrounded by them.

a.translation:
第一个字母 A; 一个; 第一的
art. [计] 累加器, 加法器, 地址, 振幅, 模拟, 区域, 面积, 汇编, 组件, 异步

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are referring to someone or something for the first time or when people may not know which particular person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （指初次提及或非特指的人或物）一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are referring to any person or thing of a particular type and do not want to be specific.
gloss_zh: （一类人或事物中非特指的）任何一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of an uncount noun when that noun follows an adjective, or when the noun is followed by words that describe it more fully.
gloss_zh: （用于前加形容词或后加修饰语的不可数名词之前）一（种）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of a mass noun when you want to refer to a single type or make of something.
You use a in quantifiers such as a lot ,a little, and a bit.
gloss_zh: （用于表示数量的词组中）许多/少许/一点

senses.concept_en: You use a or an to refer to someone or something as a typical member of a group, class, or type.
gloss_zh: （一类人或事物中典型的）一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of days, months, or festivals when you are referring to one particular instance of that day, month, or festival.
gloss_zh: （用于日子、月份或节日的名称之前以表示特例）一个

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are saying what someone is or what job they have.
You use a or an in front of the names of people as a way of indicating that you do not know them or anything about them and you are saying their name for the first time.
gloss_zh: （用于不为说话人所知的首次提到的人名前）某一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of people when you want to refer to someone else who has the same qualities or character as the person named.
gloss_zh: （用于人名前，表示与该人有相同特性或品质）类似…的一个（或一位）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of a surname when you want to refer to someone who belongs to the family with that surname.
gloss_zh: （用于姓氏前，表示某人属于某姓氏家族）一位姓…的人

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of artists to refer to one individual painting or sculpture created by them.
gloss_zh: （用于艺术家名字前）一幅…的画，一件…的雕塑作品

senses.concept_en: You use a or an instead of the number 'one', especially with words of measurement such as 'hundred', 'hour', and 'metre', and with fractions such as 'half', 'quarter', and 'third'.
gloss_zh: （代替数字one使用，尤用于hundred，hour和metre等表示度量的单词之前以及half, quarter和third等分数之前）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in expressions such as eight hours a day to express a rate or ratio.
gloss_zh: （用于表示比率的短语中）每一

acceptable.translation: a. 可接受的, 合意的, 可忍受的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Acceptable activities and situations are those that most people approve of or consider to be normal.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is acceptable to someone, they agree to consider it, use it, or allow it to happen.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as acceptable, you mean that it is good enough or fairly good.

derivation.breakdown_zh: accept 接受 + -able 可…的：可接受的

achieve.translation:
vt. 完成, 达到
vi. 如愿以偿
achieve.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you achieve a particular aim or effect, you succeed in doing it or causing it to happen, usually after a lot of effort.

act.translation:
n. 行动, 行为, 幕, 法案
vi. 行动, 表演, 假装, 见效, 表现, 担当
vt. 扮演, 装作
[计] 先进通信技术, 先进计算机工艺, 自动代码翻译技术

senses.concept_en: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.
If you act on advice or information, you do what has been advised or suggested.
If someone acts in a particular way, they behave in that way.
If someone or something acts as a particular thing, they have that role or function.
If someone acts in a particular way, they pretend to be something that they are not.
When professionals such as lawyers act for you, or act on your behalf, they are employed by you to deal with a particular matter.
If a force or substance acts on someone or something, it has a certain effect on them.
If you act, or act a part in a play or film, you have a part in it.
An act is a single thing that someone does.
If you say that someone's behaviour is an act, you mean that it does not express their real feelings.
An Act is a law passed by the government.
An act in a play, opera, or ballet is one of the main parts into which it is divided.
An act in a show is a short performance which is one of several in the show.

against.translation: prep. 反对, 对着, 倚靠

senses.concept_en: If one thing is leaning or pressing against another, it is touching it.
If you are against something such as a plan, policy, or system, you think it is wrong, bad, or stupid.
If you compete against someone in a game, you try to beat them.
If you take action against someone or something, you try to harm them.
If you take action against a possible future event, you try to prevent it.
If you do something against someone's wishes, advice, or orders, you do not do what they want you to do or tell you to do.
gloss_zh: 违背，违抗（愿望、劝告或命令）

senses.concept_en: If you do something in order to protect yourself against something unpleasant or harmful, you do something which will make its effects on you less serious if it happens.
If something is against the law or against the rules, there is a law or a rule which says that you must not do it.
If you are moving against a current, tide, or wind, you are moving in the opposite direction to it.
If something happens or is considered against a particular background of events, it is considered in relation to those events, because those events are relevant to it.
If something is measured or valued against something else, it is measured or valued by comparing it with the other thing.
The odds against something happening are the chances or odds that it will not happen.

air.translation:
n. 空气, 旋律, 态度
vt. 晾, 使通风, 夸耀

senses.concept_en: Air is the mixture of gases which forms the earth's atmosphere and which we breathe.
The air is the space around things or above the ground.
Air is used to refer to travel in aircraft.
An air is a simple tune which can be easily recognized and remembered.
If you say that someone or something has a particular air, you mean that they give this general impression.
gloss_zh: 神态;感觉;总体印象;氛围

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is putting on airs or giving themselves airs, you are criticizing them for behaving as if they are better than other people.
gloss_zh: 矫揉造作；装腔作势；做作

senses.concept_en: If a broadcasting company airs a television or radio programme, they show it on television or broadcast it on the radio.
gloss_zh: （通过电视或无线电）播送，播放

senses.concept_en: If you air your opinions, you make them known to people.
If you air a room or building, you let fresh air into it.
If you air clothing or bedding, you put it somewhere warm to make sure that it is completely dry.

allow.translation:
vt. 允许, 同意给予, 承认
vi. 容许, 猜想
[计] 允许命令

senses.concept_en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.
If you are allowed something, you are given permission to have it or are given it.
If you allow something to happen, you do not prevent it.
If one thing allows another thing to happen, the first thing creates the opportunity for the second thing to happen.
If you allow a particular length of time or a particular amount of something for a particular purpose, you include it in your planning.
If you allow that something is true, you admit or agree that it is true.
Someone or something that is situated or moving among a group of things or people is surrounded by them.
If you are among people of a particular kind, you are with them and having contact with them.
gloss_zh: 与…在一起;在…的集体之中

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is among a group, they are a member of that group and share its characteristics.
