If you want to focus on something that is happening within a particular group of people, you can say that it is happening among that group.
If something happens among a group of people, it happens within the whole of that group or between the members of that group.
If something such as a feeling, opinion, or situation exists among a group of people, most of them have it or experience it.
gloss_zh: 对…中的大多数成员而论；据…的普遍看法

senses.concept_en: You use among before a noun to mention a group when talking about a smaller group within it.
If something applies to a particular person or thing among others, it also applies to other people or things.
If something is shared among a number of people, some of it is given to all of them.
If people talk, fight, or agree among themselves, they do it together, without involving anyone else.
gloss_zh: 在…内部（谈论、争斗或达成一致）

and.translation:
conj. 和, 与
[计] 与

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two or more words, groups, or clauses.
gloss_zh: （连接两个以上的单词、词组或子句）和，与，同

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two words or phrases that are the same in order to emphasize the degree of something, or to suggest that something continues or increases over a period of time.
gloss_zh: （连接两个相同的单词或短语，以强调某事物的程度、暗示某事继续发生或在一段时间内不断增加）接连，越…越…

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two statements about events when one of the events follows the other.
gloss_zh: （连接两件相继发生的事件）然后，就

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two statements when the second statement continues the point that has been made in the first statement.
gloss_zh: （连接两句话，第二句话的意思是第一句的延伸）则，而

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two clauses when the second clause is a result of the first clause.
gloss_zh: （连接两个从句，表示因果关系）那么，于是

senses.concept_en: You use and to interrupt yourself in order to make a comment on what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （表示停顿，以便对所说的话进行评论）再说，而

senses.concept_en: You use and at the beginning of a sentence to introduce something else that you want to add to what you have just said. Some people think that starting a sentence with and is ungrammatical, but it is now quite common in both spoken and written English.
gloss_zh: （用于句首，引出补充说明）还有，不过

senses.concept_en: You use and to introduce a question which follows logically from what someone has just said.
gloss_zh: （用以引导与某人之谈话有关的问句）那么，还有

senses.concept_en: And is used by broadcasters and people making announcements to change a topic or to start talking about a topic they have just mentioned.
gloss_zh: （广播员等用以转换话题或讨论刚才提及的话题）也

senses.concept_en: You use and to indicate that two numbers are to be added together.
And is used before a fraction that comes after a whole number.
You use and in numbers larger than one hundred, after the words 'hundred' or 'thousand' and before other numbers.
gloss_zh: （用在大于一百的数字中，置于百位或千位之后，十位及个位之前）

senses.concept_en: You use anyone or anybody in statements with negative meaning to indicate in a general way that nobody is present or involved in an action.
You use anyone or anybody in questions and conditional clauses to ask or talk about whether someone is present or doing something.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句或条件从句）任何人

senses.concept_en: You use anyone or anybody before words which indicate the kind of person you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于描述所谈论的人的词语前）…人

senses.concept_en: You use anyone or anybody to refer to a person when you are emphasizing that it could be any person out of a very large number of people.
gloss_zh: （用于强调）任何人，随便哪个人

arrange.translation:
v. 安排, 排列, 达成协议
[计] 重排

senses.concept_en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.
If you arrange with someone to do something, you make plans with them to do it.
If you arrange something for someone, you make it possible for them to have it or to do it.
If you arrange things somewhere, you place them in a particular position, usually in order to make them look attractive or tidy.
If a piece of music is arranged by someone, it is changed or adapted so that it is suitable for particular instruments or voices, or for a particular performance.
When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it at the end of a journey.
When you arrive at a place, you come to it for the first time in order to stay, live, or work there.
When something such as letter or meal arrives, it is brought or delivered to you.
When something such as a new product or invention arrives, it becomes available.
gloss_zh: （新产品或发明）出现，到来，问世

senses.concept_en: When a particular moment or event arrives, it happens, especially after you have been waiting for it or expecting it.
gloss_zh: （尤指经过等待或期盼后）来临，到来

senses.concept_en: When you arrive at something such as a decision, you decide something after thinking about it or discussing it.
When a baby arrives, it is born.
If you say that someone has arrived, you mean that they have become successful or famous.

as.translation:
adv. 同样地, 例如
prep. 做为, 当作
conj. 当...之时, 以...的方式, 像...一样, 因为
[计] 高级系统, 先进系统, 辅助存储器, 自治系统

senses.concept_en: If something happens as something else happens, it happens at the same time.
gloss_zh: （表示两件事情同时发生）当…的时候，在…的同时

senses.concept_en: You use as when you are indicating what someone or something is or is thought to be, or what function they have.
If you do something as a child or as a teenager, for example, you do it when you are a child or a teenager.
You use as to say how something happens or is done, or to indicate that something happens or is done in the same way as something else.
You use as in expressions like as a result and as a consequence to indicate how two situations or events are related to each other.
You use as to introduce short clauses which comment on the truth of what you are saying.
You can use as to mean 'because' when you are explaining the reason for something.

at.translation:
prep. 在, 向, 对
[计] 地址转换器, 异常传输, 自动订票

senses.concept_en: You use at to indicate the place or event where something happens or is situated.
If someone is at school or college, or at a particular school or college, they go there regularly to study.
If you are at something such as a table, a door, or someone's side, you are next to it or them.
When you are describing where someone or something is, you can say that they are at a certain distance. You can also say that one thing is at an angle in relation to another thing.
gloss_zh: 从相隔（一段距离）的地方;呈…角度

senses.concept_en: If something happens at a particular time, that is the time when it happens or begins to happen.
If you do something at a particular age, you do it when you are that age.
You use at to express a rate, frequency, level, or price.
gloss_zh: 以，达（某一速度、频率、水平或价格）

senses.concept_en: You use at before a number or amount to indicate a measurement.
If you look at someone or something, you look towards them. If you direct an object or a comment at someone, you direct it towards them.
gloss_zh: 朝（某人或某物看）；向（某人掷物）；冲（某人说话）

senses.concept_en: You can use at after verbs such as 'smile' or 'wave' and before nouns referring to people to indicate that you have put on an expression or made a gesture which someone is meant to see or understand.
If you point or gesture at something, you move your arm or head in its direction so that it will be noticed by someone you are with.
If you are working at something, you are dealing with it. If you are aiming at something, you are trying to achieve it.
gloss_zh: 致力于;定位于;期望达到

senses.concept_en: If something is done at someone's invitation or request, it is done as a result of it.
You use at to say that someone or something is in a particular state or condition.
You use at before a possessive pronoun and a superlative adjective to say that someone or something has more of a particular quality than at any other time.
gloss_zh: （用于所有格代词和形容词最高级前，表示某人或某物在此时的某一特征最鲜明）

senses.concept_en: You use at to say how something is being done.
You use at to show that someone is doing something repeatedly.
You use at to indicate an activity or task when saying how well someone does it.
You use at to indicate what someone is reacting to.

back.translation:
a. 后面的
vt. 使后退, 支持
vi. 倒退, 背靠
adv. 向后地
n. 背部, 后面

senses.concept_en: If you move back, you move in the opposite direction to the one in which you are facing or in which you were moving before.
If you go back somewhere, you return to where you were before.
If someone or something is back in a particular state, they were in that state before and are now in it again.
gloss_zh: 恢复原状；回到原来的状态

senses.concept_en: If you give or put something back, you return it to the person who had it or to the place where it was before you took it. If you get or take something back, you then have it again after not having it for a while.
If you put a clock or watch back, you change the time shown on it so that it shows an earlier time, for example when the time changes to winter time or standard time.
If you write or call back, you write to or telephone someone after they have written to or telephoned you. If you look back at someone, you look at them after they have started looking at you.
You can say that you go or come back to a particular point in a conversation to show that you are mentioning or discussing it again.
If something is or comes back, it is fashionable again after it has been unfashionable for some time.
gloss_zh: 再次流行；再度成为潮流

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is kept or situated back from a place, they are at a distance away from it.
If something is held or tied back, it is held or tied so that it does not hang loosely over something.
If you lie or sit back, you move your body backwards into a relaxed sloping or flat position, with your head and body resting on something.
If you look or shout back at someone or something, you turn to look or shout at them when they are behind you.

You use back in expressions like back in London or back at the house when you are giving an account, to show that you are going to start talking about what happened or was happening in the place you mention.
gloss_zh: （表示描述场所的转换）在曾提到过的地方

senses.concept_en: If you talk about something that happened back in the past or several years back, you are emphasizing that it happened quite a long time ago.
If you think back to something that happened in the past, you remember it or try to remember it.
A person's or animal's back is the part of their body between their head and their legs that is on the opposite side to their chest and stomach.
The back of something is the side or part of it that is towards the rear or farthest from the front. The back of something is normally not used or seen as much as the front.
Back is used to refer to the side or part of something that is towards the rear or farthest from the front.
The back of a chair or sofa is the part that you lean against when you sit on it.
The back of something such as a piece of paper or an envelope is the side which is less important.
The back of a book is the part nearest the end, where you can find the index or the notes, for example.
You can use back in expressions such as round the back and out the back to refer generally to the area behind a house or other building.
gloss_zh: （用于round the back, out the back等表达方式中）房屋（或其他建筑物）后的区域

senses.concept_en: You use back in expressions such as out back to refer to the area behind a house or other building. You also use in back to refer to the rear part of something, especially a car or building.
gloss_zh: （用于out back等表达方式中）房屋（或其他建筑物）后的区域；（用于in back等表达方式中）汽车（或建筑物等）的后部

senses.concept_en: In team games such as football and hockey, a back is a player who is concerned mainly with preventing the other team from scoring goals, rather than scoring goals for their own team.
gloss_zh: （足球、曲棍球等运动中的）后卫

senses.concept_en: In American football, a back is a player who stands behind the front line, runs with the ball and attacks rather than defends.
gloss_zh: （美式橄榄球运动中的）进攻后卫

senses.concept_en: If a building backs onto something, the back of it faces in the direction of that thing or touches the edge of that thing.
When you back a car or other vehicle somewhere or when it backs somewhere, it moves backwards.
If you back a person or a course of action, you support them, for example by voting for them or giving them money.
If you back a particular person, team, or horse in a competition, you predict that they will win, and usually you bet money that they will win.
gloss_zh: 预测…获胜；（通常指）下赌注于

senses.concept_en: If a singer is backed by a band or by other singers, they provide the musical background for the singer.

be.translation:
v. 是, 表示, 在
[计] 后端, 总线允许

senses.concept_en: You use be with a present participle to form the continuous tenses of verbs. be going to
gloss_zh: （和现在分词连用构成动词的进行式）

senses.concept_en: You use be with a past participle to form the passive voice.
gloss_zh: （和过去分词连用构成被动语态）

senses.concept_en: You use be with an infinitive to indicate that something is planned to happen, that it will definitely happen, or that it must happen. be about to
gloss_zh: （和不定式连用表示将来的安排或确定会发生的事情）

senses.concept_en: You use be with an infinitive to say or ask what should happen or be done in a particular situation, how it should happen, or who should do it.
gloss_zh: （和不定式连用表示在某种情况下会发生什么事，应该怎样做或应该由谁来做）

senses.concept_en: You use was and were with an infinitive to talk about something that happened later than the time you are discussing, and was not planned or certain at that time.
gloss_zh: （was和were和不定式连用，表示说话时间之后发生的事）

senses.concept_en: You can say that something is to be seen, heard, or found in a particular place to mean that people can see it, hear it, or find it in that place.
gloss_zh: （表示可见到、可听到、可发现等）

senses.concept_en: You use be to introduce more information about the subject, such as its identity, nature, qualities, or position.
gloss_zh: （用于提供与主语相关的信息）

senses.concept_en: You use be, with 'it' as the subject, in clauses where you are describing something or giving your judgment of a situation.
gloss_zh: （以it作主语，用来进行描述或作出判断）

senses.concept_en: You use be with the impersonal pronoun 'there' in expressions like there is and there are to say that something exists or happens.
gloss_zh: （与非人称代词there连用构成there is和there are表示存在或发生）

senses.concept_en: You use be as a link between a subject and a clause and in certain other clause structures, as shown below.
gloss_zh: （表示主语和从句和其他从句结构之间的某种联系）

senses.concept_en: You use be in expressions like the thing is and the point is to introduce a clause in which you make a statement or give your opinion.
gloss_zh: （用在如the thing is和the point is这样的结构中，引导表示陈述或提出观点的从句）

senses.concept_en: You use be in expressions like to be fair ,to be honest, or to be serious to introduce an additional statement or opinion, and to indicate that you are trying to be fair, honest, or serious.
gloss_zh: （用在如to be fair, to be honest或to be serious 这样的结构中表示尽量）

senses.concept_en: The form 'be' is used occasionally instead of the normal forms of the present tense, especially after 'whether'.
gloss_zh: （有时用来代替现在时态中be的几个常规形式，尤用于whether后）

senses.concept_en: If something is, it exists.
senses.register_label: mainly FORMAL or LITERARY 主正式或文

senses.concept_en: To be yourself means to behave in the way that is right and natural for you and your personality.
gloss_zh: 保持真我；按自己的方式行事；显常态

senses.concept_en: You use because when stating the reason for something.
You use because when stating the explanation for a statement you have just made.

before.translation:
prep. 在...之前
conj. 在...之前
adv. 在前

senses.concept_en: If something happens before a particular date, time, or event, it happens earlier than that date, time, or event
If you do one thing before doing something else, you do it earlier than the other thing.
You use before when you are talking about time. For example, if something happened the day before a particular date or event, it happened during the previous day.
If you do something before someone else can do something, you do it when they have not yet done it.
If someone has done something before, they have done it on a previous occasion. If someone has not done something before, they have never done it.
If there is a period of time or if several things are done before something happens, it takes that amount of time or effort for this thing to happen.
If a particular situation has to happen before something else happens, this situation must happen or exist in order for the other thing to happen.
gloss_zh: （必须先具备某一条件）才能；在…之前（必须具备某一条件）

senses.concept_en: If someone is before something, they are in front of it.
If you tell someone that one place is a certain distance before another, you mean that they will come to the first place first.
If you appear or come before an official person or group, you go there and answer questions.
If something happens before a particular person or group, it is seen by or happens while this person or this group is present.
If you have something such as a journey, a task, or a stage of your life before you, you must do it or live through it in the future.
gloss_zh: 摆在…面前；使面对；使面临

senses.concept_en: When you want to say that one person or thing is more important than another, you can say that they come before the other person or thing.
To begin to do something means to start doing it.
When something begins or when you begin it, it takes place from a particular time onwards.
If you begin with something, or begin by doing something, this is the first thing you do.
gloss_zh: 从…开始；从…着手；首先做（某事）

senses.concept_en: You use begin to mention the first thing that someone says.
If one thing began as another, it first existed in the form of the second thing.
If you say that a thing or place begins somewhere, you are talking about one of its limits or edges.
If a word begins with a particular letter, that is the first letter of that word.
If you say that you cannot begin to imagine, understand, or explain something, you are emphasizing that it is almost impossible to explain, understand, or imagine.
gloss_zh: 无法，难以（解释、理解、想象等）

big.translation:
a. 大的, 重要的
adv. 大量地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A big person or thing is large in physical size.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is big consists of many people or things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something such as a problem, increase, or change as a big one, you mean it is great in degree, extent, or importance.
gloss_zh: 严重的；重大的；大幅度的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A big organization employs many people and has many customers.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is big in a particular organization, activity, or place, you mean that they have a lot of influence or authority in it.
If you call someone a big bully or a big coward, you are emphasizing your disapproval of them.
gloss_zh: （强调厌恶之深）十足的，突出的

senses.concept_en: Children often refer to their older brother or sister as their big brother or sister.
Capital letters are sometimes referred to as big letters.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Big words are long or rare words which have meanings that are difficult to understand.

bitter.translation:
a. 苦的, 痛苦的, 怀恨的
adv. 刺骨
v. (使)变苦
bitter.tags: zk gk cet4 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: In a bitter argument or conflict, people argue very angrily or fight very fiercely.
gloss_zh: 激烈的；猛烈的；充满敌意的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is bitter after a disappointing experience or after being treated unfairly, they continue to feel angry about it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bitter experience makes you feel very disappointed. You can also use bitter to emphasize feelings of disappointment.
gloss_zh: （经历或感觉）令人非常失望的，痛苦的，辛酸的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Bitter weather, or a bitter wind, is extremely cold.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bitter taste is sharp, not sweet, and often slightly unpleasant.
Bitter is a kind of beer that is light brown in colour.

blanket.translation:
n. 毛毯, 毯子
vt. 掩盖, 覆盖
a. 总共的

senses.concept_en: A blanket is a large square or rectangular piece of thick cloth, especially one which you put on a bed to keep you warm.
A blanket of something such as snow is a continuous layer of it which hides what is below or beyond it.
You can refer to something such as an unpleasant emotion or an undesirable quality that seems to affect every aspect of a particular situation as a blanket of that emotion or quality.
gloss_zh: （不好的情感、性质等的）弥漫，充斥

senses.concept_en: If something such as snow blankets an area, it covers it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use blanket to describe something when you want to emphasize that it affects or refers to every person or thing in a group, without any exceptions.
gloss_zh: 通用的；全面的；无一例外的

block.translation:
n. 街区, 木块, 石块, 块
vt. 阻塞, 封锁, 使成块状
[计] 块, 数据块

senses.concept_en: A block of flats or offices is a large building containing them.
A block in a town is an area of land with streets on all its sides.
A block of a substance is a large rectangular piece of it.
To block a road, channel, or pipe means to put an object across it or in it so that nothing can pass through it or along it.
If something blocks your view, it prevents you from seeing something because it is between you and that thing.
If you block someone's way, you prevent them from going somewhere or entering a place by standing in front of them.
If you block something that is being arranged, you prevent it from being done.
In some sports, if a player blocks a shot or kick, they stop the ball reaching its target. If one player blocks another, the first stops the second from reaching or moving with the ball.
gloss_zh: （体育运动中）拦截，阻截（进球、对手等）

senses.concept_en: A block of something such as tickets or shares is a large quantity of them, especially when they are all sold at the same time and are in a particular sequence or order.
gloss_zh: （尤指按特定顺序同时售出的）大量，大批，大套（票、股票等）

senses.concept_en: If you have a mental block or a block, you are temporarily unable to do something that you can normally do which involves using, thinking about, or remembering something.
gloss_zh: （短时间的）思维停滞，思维中断

boot.translation:
n. 长靴, 踢, 解雇, 效用
vt. 使穿靴, 踢, 解雇, 有用
[计] 引导, 自举

senses.concept_en: See also:see also wellington; Boots are shoes that cover your whole foot and the lower part of your leg.
Boots are strong, heavy shoes which cover your ankle and which have thick soles. You wear them to protect your feet, for example when you are walking or taking part in sport.
gloss_zh: （步行、运动等时穿的）厚底短筒靴

senses.concept_en: If you boot something such as a ball, you kick it hard.
The boot of a car is a covered space at the back or front, in which you carry things such as luggage and shopping.
To boot a car means to fit a Denver boot to one of its wheels so that it cannot be driven away.

break.translation:
n. 休息, 中断, 破裂处, 绝交, 破晓, 突变
vt. 打破, 弄破, 弄坏, 破坏, 违反, 打断, 削弱, 放弃
vi. 破碎, 决裂, 破晓, 突变, 变弱, 暂停
n. 分隔符
[计] 分隔符; 中断; DOS内部命令:设定扫描中断按键的时机

senses.concept_en: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.
If you break a part of your body such as your leg, your arm, or your nose, or if a bone breaks, you are injured because a bone cracks or splits.
If a surface, cover, or seal breaks or if something breaks it, a hole or tear is made in it, so that a substance can pass through.
gloss_zh: （使）（表层、盖子或密封）破裂；撕开

senses.concept_en: When a tool or piece of machinery breaks or when you break it, it is damaged and no longer works.
If you break a rule, promise, or agreement, you do something that you should not do according to that rule, promise, or agreement.
gloss_zh: 破坏，违反（规则、承诺或协议）

senses.concept_en: If you break free or loose, you free yourself from something or escape from it.
If someone breaks something, especially a difficult or unpleasant situation that has existed for some time, they end it or change it.
gloss_zh: 结束（困难或不利局面）；打破（僵局）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something breaks a silence, they say something or make a noise after a long period of silence.
If there is a break in the cloud or weather, it changes and there is a short period of sunshine or fine weather.
If you break with a group of people or a traditional way of doing things, or you break your connection with them, you stop being involved with that group or stop doing things in that way.
If you break a habit or if someone breaks you of it, you no longer have that habit.
To break someone means to destroy their determination and courage, their success, or their career.
gloss_zh: 瓦解…的决心；使丧失勇气；毁掉…的前程

senses.concept_en: If someone breaks for a short period of time, they rest or change from what they are doing for a short period.

See also:lunch break;tea break; A break is a short period of time when you have a rest or a change from what you are doing, especially if you are working or if you are in a boring or unpleasant situation.
A break is a short holiday.
If you break your journey somewhere, you stop there for a short time so that you can have a rest.
To break the force of something such as a blow or fall means to weaken its effect, for example by getting in the way of it.
When a piece of news breaks, people hear about it from the newspapers, television, or radio.
gloss_zh: （消息在报纸、电视或电台）发布，传播

senses.concept_en: When you break a piece of bad news to someone, you tell it to them, usually in a kind way.
gloss_zh: （通常以委婉的方式）透露，告知（坏消息）

senses.concept_en: A break is a lucky opportunity that someone gets to achieve something.
See also:record-breaking; If you break a record, you beat the previous record for a particular achievement.
See also:daybreak; When day or dawn breaks, it starts to grow light after the night has ended.
When a wave breaks, it passes its highest point and turns downwards, for example when it reaches the shore.
If you break a secret code, you work out how to understand it.
If someone's voice breaks when they are speaking, it changes its sound, for example because they are sad or afraid.
gloss_zh: （因悲伤或害怕嗓音）突变，变调

senses.concept_en: When a boy's voice breaks, it becomes deeper and sounds more like a man's voice.
If the weather breaks or a storm breaks, it suddenly becomes rainy or stormy after a period of sunshine.
In tennis, if you break your opponent's serve, you win a game in which your opponent is serving.
gloss_zh: （网球比赛中）破，赢得（对手的发球局）

bright.translation:
a. 明亮的, 聪明的, 鲜明的, 欢快的
adv. 明亮地, 欢快地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bright colour is strong and noticeable, and not dark.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bright light, object, or place is shining strongly or is full of light.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as bright, you mean that they are quick at learning things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bright idea is clever and original.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone looks or sounds bright, they look or sound cheerful and lively.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If the future is bright, it is likely to be pleasant or successful.
The brights on a car or other vehicle are the headlights when they are switched on fully.
gloss_zh: （汽车或其他车辆）打开的前灯

bring.translation:
vt. 带来, 产生, 促使, 提出
vi. 生产

senses.concept_en: If you bring someone or something with you when you come to a place, they come with you or you have them with you.
If you bring something somewhere, you move it there.
If you bring something that someone wants or needs, you get it for them or carry it to them.
To bring something or someone to a place or position means to cause them to come to the place or move into that position.
If you bring something new to a place or group of people, you introduce it to that place or cause those people to hear or know about it.
To bring someone or something into a particular state or condition means to cause them to be in that state or condition.
If something brings a particular feeling, situation, or quality, it makes people experience it or have it.
If a period of time brings a particular thing, it happens during that time.
If you bring a legal action against someone or bring them to trial, you officially accuse them of doing something illegal.
gloss_zh: （对某人）提起（诉讼）；将（某人）送上（法庭）

senses.concept_en: If a television or radio programme is brought to you by an organization, they make it, broadcast it, or pay for it to be made or broadcast.
gloss_zh: 提供，制作，播出（电视或广播节目）

senses.concept_en: When you are talking, you can say that something brings you to a particular point in order to indicate that you have now reached that point and are going to talk about a new subject.
gloss_zh: 把（某人）带到（或引到）（某话题）

senses.concept_en: If you cannot bring yourself to do something, you cannot do it because you find it too upsetting, embarrassing, or disgusting.
gloss_zh: 强迫（自己）做（令人伤心、窘迫或讨厌的事）

bucket.translation:
n. 桶
[计] 存储桶; 桶
bucket.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A bucket is a round metal or plastic container with a handle attached to its sides. Buckets are often used for holding and carrying water.
Buckets or bucket-loads of something means a large amount of it.
If someone cries buckets, they cry a lot because they are very upset. If it rains buckets, it rains a lot.

building.translation:
n. 建筑物, 建筑
[法] 营造, 建筑, 建筑物

senses.concept_en: A building is a structure that has a roof and walls, for example a house or a factory.

but.translation:
prep. 除了
conj. 但是
adv. 仅仅

senses.concept_en: You use but to introduce something which contrasts with what you have just said, or to introduce something which adds to what you have just said.
You use but when you are about to add something further in a discussion or to change the subject.
You use but after you have made an excuse or apologized for what you are just about to say.
You use but to introduce a reply to someone when you want to indicate surprise, disbelief, refusal, or protest.
gloss_zh: （引出下文，表示惊讶、难以置信、拒绝或抗议）但是，可是

senses.concept_en: But is used to mean 'except'.
But is used to mean 'only'.
You use buts in expressions like 'no buts' and 'ifs and buts' to refer to reasons someone gives for not doing something, especially when you do not think that they are good reasons.

by.translation:
prep. 被, 经, 由, 在...之旁
adv. 经过, 在近处

senses.concept_en: If something is done by a person or thing, that person or thing does it.
If you say that something such as a book, a piece of music, or a painting is by a particular person, you mean that this person wrote it or created it.
gloss_zh: （图书、音乐、绘画等）由…（创作），出自

senses.concept_en: If you do something by a particular means, you do it using that thing.
If you achieve one thing by doing another thing, your action enables you to achieve the first thing.
You use by in phrases such as 'by chance' or 'by accident' to indicate whether or not an event was planned.
gloss_zh: （用于短语中）由于，出于（偶然或意外）

senses.concept_en: If someone is a particular type of person by nature, by profession, or by birth, they are that type of person because of their nature, their profession, or the family they were born into.
gloss_zh: 就（本性、职业或出身）而言

senses.concept_en: If something must be done by law, it happens according to the law. If something is the case by particular standards, it is the case according to the standards.
gloss_zh: 根据，按照（法律或某种标准）

senses.concept_en: If you say what someone means by a particular word or expression, you are saying what they intend the word or expression to refer to.
If you hold someone or something by a particular part of them, you hold that part.
gloss_zh: （用于表示抓住身体某部位或握住物体某部分）

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is by something else is beside it and close to it.
If a person or vehicle goes by you, they move past you without stopping.
If you stop by a place, you visit it for a short time.
If something happens by a particular time, it happens at or before that time.
If you do something by day, you do it during the day. If you do it by night, you do it during the night.
In arithmetic, you use by before the second number in a multiplication or division sum.
You use by to talk about measurements of area. For example, if a room is twenty feet by fourteen feet, it measures twenty feet in one direction and fourteen feet in the other direction.
gloss_zh: 乘（表示长乘宽得出的居室等的面积）

senses.concept_en: If something increases or decreases by a particular amount, that amount is gained or lost.
Things that are made or sold by the million or by the dozen are made or sold in those quantities.
You use by in expressions such as 'minute by minute' and 'drop by drop' to talk about things that happen gradually, not all at once.

calendar.translation:
n. 日历, 日程表
vt. 列入表中
[计] 日历

senses.concept_en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.
A calendar is a particular system for dividing time into periods such as years, months, and weeks, often starting from a particular point in history.
You can use calendar to refer to a series or list of events and activities which take place on particular dates, and which are important for a particular organization, community, or person.
gloss_zh: （某一组织、团体或个人的）日程表，纪事表，大事一览表

canal.translation:
n. 运河, 水道, 管, 沟渠
vt. 开运河
canal.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.
A canal is a narrow tube inside your body for carrying food, air, or other substances.
gloss_zh: （人体内输送食物、空气等的）管,道

care.translation:
n. 小心, 照料, 忧虑
vi. 关心, 介意
vt. 在意, 喜欢

senses.concept_en: If you care about something, you feel that it is important and are concerned about it.
If you care for someone, you feel a lot of affection for them.
If you care for someone or something, you look after them and keep them in a good state or condition.
Children who are in care are looked after by the state because their parents are dead or unable to look after them properly.
If you say that you do not care for something or someone, you mean that you do not like them.
If you say that someone does something when they care to do it, you mean that they do it, although they should do it more willingly or more often.
You can ask someone if they would care for something or if they would care to do something as a polite way of asking if they would like to have or do something.
gloss_zh: 愿意，要（一种有礼貌的询问）

senses.concept_en: If you do something with care, you give careful attention to it because you do not want to make any mistakes or cause any damage.
Your cares are your worries, anxieties, or fears.

careful.translation: a. 小心的, 谨慎的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are careful, you give serious attention to what you are doing, in order to avoid harm, damage, or mistakes. If you are careful to do something, you make sure that you do it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Careful work, thought, or examination is thorough and shows a concern for details.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you tell someone to be careful about doing something, you think that what they intend to do is probably wrong, and that they should think seriously before they do it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are careful with something such as money or resources, you use or spend only what is necessary.

carry.translation:
n. 进位, 射程, 运载
vt. 携带, 运送, 支持, 传送, 包含
vi. 被携带, 能达到
[计] 进位; 进位数

senses.concept_en: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground.
If you carry something, you have it with you wherever you go.
If something carries a person or thing somewhere, it takes them there.
If a person or animal is carrying a disease, they are infected with it and can pass it on to other people or animals.
If an action or situation has a particular quality or consequence, you can say that it carries it.
If a quality or advantage carries someone into a particular position or through a difficult situation, it helps them to achieve that position or deal with that situation.
gloss_zh: 使达到（目标）;帮助…渡过（难关）

senses.concept_en: If you carry an idea or a method to a particular extent, you use or develop it to that extent.
If a newspaper or poster carries a picture or a piece of writing, it contains it or displays it.
In a debate, if a proposal or motion is carried, a majority of people vote in favour of it.
If a crime carries a particular punishment, a person who is found guilty of that crime will receive that punishment.
If a sound carries, it can be heard a long way away.
If a candidate or party carries a state or area, they win the election in that state or area.
gloss_zh: （候选人或党派）在（某州或某选区）获胜

senses.concept_en: If you carry yourself in a particular way, you walk and move in that way.
If a woman is carrying a child, she is pregnant.

cease.translation:
n. 停止
v. 停止, 终了

senses.concept_en: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.
If you cease to do something, you stop doing it.
If you cease something, you stop it happening or working.

center.translation:
n. 中心, 中心点, 中锋
a. 中央的, 位在正中的
vt. 集中, 定中心
vi. 居中
[计] 居中; 中央

check.translation:
n. 检查, 支票, 阻止物, 寄物牌, 象棋中将军
vt. 检查, 阻止, 核对, 寄存, 托运
vi. 逐项相符, 开支票
[计] 复选

senses.concept_en: See also:cross-check; If you check something such as a piece of information or a document, you make sure that it is correct or satisfactory.
If you check on someone or something, you make sure they are in a safe or satisfactory condition.
gloss_zh: 检查，查看（以确保一切正常）

senses.concept_en: If you check something that is written on a piece of paper, you put a mark, like a V with the right side extended, next to it to show that something is correct or has been selected or dealt with.
gloss_zh: 在…上打钩（以确定其正确、已选定或已处理）

senses.concept_en: To check something, usually something bad, means to stop it from spreading or continuing.
If you check yourself or if something checks you, you suddenly stop what you are doing or saying.
When you check your luggage at an airport, you give it to an official so that it can be taken on to your plane.
The check in a restaurant is a piece of paper on which the price of your meal is written and which you are given before you pay.
In a game of chess, you say check when you are attacking your opponent's king.
A pattern of squares, usually of two colours, can be referred to as checks or a check .
gloss_zh: （通常为两种颜色的）方格图案，格子图案

senses.concept_en: A check is the same as a cheque .

chill.translation:
n. 寒冷, 寒意, 失意
a. 寒冷的, 冷漠的
vt. 使寒心, 冷冻
vi. 变冷

senses.concept_en: When you chill something or when it chills, you lower its temperature so that it becomes colder but does not freeze.
When cold weather or something cold chills a person or a place, it makes that person or that place feel very cold.
If you say that something you see, hear, or feel chills you, you mean that it frightens you.
If something sends a chill through you, it gives you a sudden feeling of fear or anxiety.
A chill is a mild illness which can give you a slight fever and headache.
Chill weather is cold and unpleasant.

choose.translation:
vt. 选择, 宁愿, 欲
vi. 作出选择, 愿意
[计] 选取

senses.concept_en: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.
If you choose to do something, you do it because you want to or because you feel that it is right.

clean.translation:
a. 干净的, 清白的, 简洁的
adv. 清洁地, 完全地
vt. 清理, 使干净, 出空
vi. 被搞干净
n. 打扫

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is clean is free from dirt or unwanted marks.
gloss_zh: 干净的;洁净的;无污迹的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You say that people or animals are clean when they keep themselves or their surroundings clean.
gloss_zh: （人或动物）讲卫生的，爱干净的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A clean fuel or chemical process does not create many harmful or polluting substances.
gloss_zh: （燃料或化学作用）无害的，无污染的，清洁的

senses.concept_en: If you clean something or clean dirt off it, you make it free from dirt and unwanted marks, for example by washing or wiping it. If something cleans easily, it is easy to clean.
If you clean a room or house, you make the inside of it and the furniture in it free from dirt and dust.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something such as a book, joke, or lifestyle as clean, you think that they are not sexually immoral or offensive.
gloss_zh: （书籍、笑话、生活方式）文明的，不淫秽的，不下流的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has a clean reputation or record, they have never done anything illegal or wrong.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A clean game or fight is carried out fairly, according to the rules.
gloss_zh: （比赛或打斗）无舞弊行为的，公平的，不违规的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a flavour, smell, or colour as clean, you like it because it is light and fresh.
gloss_zh: （口味、气味或色彩）淡雅的，清新的，明快的

senses.concept_en: A clean sheet of paper has no writing or drawing on it.
If you make a clean break or start, you end a situation completely and start again in a different way.
Clean is used to emphasize that something was done completely.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A clean shape is simple and regular, with definite, smooth edges.
gloss_zh: （形状）规则的，简洁的，边缘平滑的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe an action as clean to indicate that it is carried out simply and quickly without mistakes.
gloss_zh: （动作）干脆利落的，快速无误的

clear.translation:
a. 清楚的, 明确的, 澄清的
adv. 清晰地
vt. 澄清, 清除障碍
vi. 放晴, 变清澈
n. 空隙
[计] 清除

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is clear is obvious and impossible to be mistaken about.
gloss_zh: 明显的;显然的;明白无误的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are clear about something, you understand it completely.
gloss_zh: 完全了解的;明白的;清楚的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your mind or your way of thinking is clear, you are able to think sensibly and reasonably, and you are not affected by confusion or by a drug such as alcohol.
gloss_zh: （头脑或思路）清楚的，清晰的，清醒的，不糊涂的

senses.concept_en: To clear your mind or your head means to free it from confused thoughts or from the effects of a drug such as alcohol.
A clear substance is one which you can see through and which has no colour, like clean water.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A clear colour is bright and strong.
If a surface, place, or view is clear, it is free of unwanted objects or obstacles.
gloss_zh: （表面）收拾干净的;（地方）畅通的;（视野）无阻碍的

senses.concept_en: When you clear an area or place or clear something from it, you remove things from it that you do not want to be there.
If something or someone clears the way or the path for something to happen, they make it possible.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If it is a clear day or if the sky is clear, there is no mist, rain, or cloud.
When fog or mist clears, it gradually disappears.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Clear eyes look healthy, attractive, and shining.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your skin is clear, it is healthy and free from spots.
If you say that your conscience is clear, you mean you do not think you have done anything wrong.
If something or someone is clear of something else, it is not touching it or is a safe distance away from it.
gloss_zh: 不接触的;远离的;在安全距离以外的

senses.concept_en: If you drive clear to a place, especially a place that is far away, you go all the way there without delays.
If an animal or person clears an object or clears a certain height, they jump over the object, or over something that height, without touching it.
When a bank clears a cheque or when a cheque clears, the bank agrees to pay the sum of money mentioned on it.
If a course of action is cleared, people in authority give permission for it to happen.
If someone is cleared, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or mistake.

clerk.translation:
n. 办事员, 职员, 文书
vi. 当店员

senses.concept_en: A clerk is a person who works in an office, bank, or law court and whose job is to look after the records or accounts.
In a hotel, office, or hospital, a clerk is the person whose job is to answer the telephone and deal with people when they arrive.
A clerk is someone who works in a store.
To clerk means to work as a clerk.
gloss_zh: 做文书工作;当接待员（或店员等）

closed.translation:
a. 关闭的, 限于少数人的
[计] 关闭指令

cloth.translation:
n. 布料, 织品, 布
[建] 布

senses.concept_en: Cloth is fabric which is made by weaving or knitting a substance such as cotton, wool, silk, or nylon. Cloth is used especially for making clothes
A cloth is a piece of cloth which you use for a particular purpose, such as cleaning something or covering something.
The cloth is sometimes used to refer to Christian priests and ministers.

coat.translation:
n. 外套
vt. 外面覆盖, 给...穿外套

senses.concept_en: A coat is a piece of clothing with long sleeves which you wear over your other clothes when you go outside.
An animal's coat is the fur or hair on its body.
If you coat something with a substance or in a substance, you cover it with a thin layer of the substance.
A coat of paint or varnish is a thin layer of it on a surface.

cold.translation:
n. 感冒, 寒冷
a. 寒冷的, 冷淡的, 冷静的
adv. 完全地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is cold has a very low temperature or a lower temperature than is normal or acceptable.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If it is cold, or if a place is cold, the temperature of the air is very low.
Cold weather or low temperatures can be referred to as the cold .

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are cold, your body is at an unpleasantly low temperature.
Cold food, such as salad or meat that has been cooked and cooled, is not intended to be eaten hot.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Cold colours or cold light give an impression of coldness.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A cold person does not show much emotion, especially affection, and therefore seems unfriendly and unsympathetic. If someone's voice is cold, they speak in an unfriendly unsympathetic way.
gloss_zh: 冷淡的;冷酷的;不热情的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A cold trail or scent is one which is old and therefore difficult to follow.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is cold when they are trying to guess the answer to a question or puzzle, you mean that they are thinking about it in the wrong way and are going to give a wrong answer.
If you have a cold, you have a mild, very common illness which makes you sneeze a lot and gives you a sore throat or a cough.

color.translation:
n. 颜色, 面色, 颜料, 外貌
vt. 把...涂上颜色, 粉饰, 使脸红, 歪曲
vi. 变色

compile.translation:
vt. 编译, 编辑, 编纂, 收集
[计] 编译
compile.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: When you compile something such as a report, book, or programme, you produce it by collecting and putting together many pieces of information.

completely.translation: adv. 完全地, 十分地, 圆满地

compose.translation:
vt. 组成, 写作, 作曲, 使平静
vi. 创作, 排字
[计] 编写
compose.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: The things that something is composed of are its parts or members. The separate things that compose something are the parts or members that form it.
When someone composes a piece of music, they write it.
If you compose something such as a letter, poem, or speech, you write it, often using a lot of concentration or skill.
If you compose a picture or image, you arrange it in an attractive and artistic way.
If you compose yourself or if you compose your features, you succeed in becoming calm after you have been angry, excited, or upset.
gloss_zh: 使（自己）平静（或镇定）;使（表情）镇静下来

conversion.translation:
n. 转变, 转换, 改变宗教信仰, 换位法
[计] 转换

senses.concept_en: Conversion is the act or process of changing something into a different state or form.
If someone changes their religion or beliefs, you can refer to their conversion to their new religion or beliefs.
gloss_zh: （宗教、信仰等的）改变，皈依，归附

senses.concept_en: In rugby, if a player makes or kicks a conversion, he scores points by kicking the ball over the goal after a try has been scored.
You use could to indicate that someone had the ability to do something. You use could not or couldn't to say that someone was unable to do something
You use could to indicate that something sometimes happened.
You use could have to indicate that something was a possibility in the past, although it did not actually happen.
gloss_zh: 本能够，本可以（表示某事本有可能发生但却并未发生）

senses.concept_en: You use could to indicate that something is possibly true, or that it may possibly happen.
gloss_zh: （表示某事可能属实或可能发生）可能

senses.concept_en: You use could not or couldn't to indicate that it is not possible that something is true.
You use could to talk about a possibility, ability, or opportunity that depends on other conditions.
gloss_zh: （表示可能性、能力或机会）可能

senses.concept_en: You use could when you are saying that one thing or situation resembles another.
You use could, or couldn't in questions, when you are making offers and suggestions.

You use could in questions when you are making a polite request or asking for permission to do something. Speakers sometimes use couldn't instead of 'could' to show that they realize that their request may be refused.
gloss_zh: （用于礼貌地提出请求或征得许可。当说话者意识到可能被拒绝时，可以用 couldn't 代替 could）能，可以

senses.concept_en: People sometimes use structures with if I could or could I as polite ways of interrupting someone or of introducing what they are going to say next.
gloss_zh: （用以礼貌地打断某人或引出将要说的话）请允许我

senses.concept_en: You use could to say emphatically that someone ought to do the thing mentioned, especially when you are annoyed because they have not done it. You use why couldn't in questions to express your surprise or annoyance that someone has not done something.
gloss_zh: （用以强调某人应该做所提及的事情，尤用于当说话者因为其没做该事而生气时）

senses.concept_en: You use could when you are expressing strong feelings about something by saying that you feel as if you want to do the thing mentioned, although you do not do it.
gloss_zh: （表示想要做某事的强烈感情）

senses.concept_en: You use could after 'if' when talking about something that you do not have the ability or opportunity to do, but which you are imagining in order to consider what the likely consequences might be.
gloss_zh: （用在if后以谈论没有能力或机会做但为考虑可能的结果而设想去做的事）

senses.concept_en: You use could not or couldn't with comparatives to emphasize that someone or something has as much as is possible of a particular quality. For example, if you say 'I couldn't be happier', you mean that you are extremely happy.
gloss_zh: （与比较级连用，强调某物或某人具备某种特征的程度）太…，再…不过

senses.concept_en: In speech, you use how could in questions to emphasize that you feel strongly about something bad that has happened.
gloss_zh: 怎么会（用在疑问句中强调对所发生的不愉快之事的感受）

senses.concept_en: A county is a region of Britain, Ireland, or the USA which has its own local government.

crack.translation:
n. 裂缝, 爆裂声
v. (使)爆裂, (使)裂开, (使)发出爆裂声
a. 第一流的
adv. 啪地一声
crack.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.
If something cracks, or if you crack it, it makes a sharp sound like the sound of a piece of wood breaking.
If you crack a hard part of your body, such as your knee or your head, you hurt it by accidentally hitting it hard against something.
When you crack something that has a shell, such as an egg or a nut, you break the shell in order to reach the inside part.
If you crack a problem or a code, you solve it, especially after a lot of thought.
gloss_zh: （尤指经过反复思考）找到…的解决办法，破译（密码）

senses.concept_en: If someone cracks, they lose control of their emotions or actions because they are under a lot of pressure.
If your voice cracks when you are speaking or singing, it changes in pitch because you are feeling a strong emotion.
gloss_zh: （因感情强烈而嗓音）变嘶哑，变沙哑

senses.concept_en: If you crack a joke, you tell it.
A crack is a very narrow gap between two things, or between two parts of a thing.
If you open something such as a door, window, or curtain a crack, you open it only a small amount.
A crack is a line that appears on the surface of something when it is slightly damaged.
A crack is a sharp sound, like the sound of a piece of wood breaking.
If you have or take a crack at something, you make an attempt to do or achieve something.
A crack is a slightly rude or cruel joke.
gloss_zh: （略显粗鲁或刻薄的）笑话，俏皮话

senses.concept_en: See also:crack cocaine; Crack is a very pure form of the drug cocaine.
gloss_zh: 强效可卡因;强力古柯碱

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A crack soldier or sportsman is highly trained and very skilful.
gloss_zh: （士兵或运动员）训练有素的，一流的

daily.translation:
a. 每日的, 日常的
adv. 每日地, 日常地
n. 日报

senses.concept_en: If something happens daily, it happens every day.
Daily quantities or rates relate to a period of one day.
A daily is a newspaper that is published every day of the week except Sunday.

dangerous.translation:
a. 危险的
[法] 危险的, 危害的
dangerous.tags: zk gk cet4 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.
gloss_zh: 危险的;可能带来危害的;不安全的

derivation.breakdown_zh: danger 危险 + -ous 有…的：危险的

day.translation:
n. 天, 日子, 白天, 工作日
[医] 日(一昼夜), 昼, 白天

senses.concept_en: A day is one of the seven twenty-four hour periods of time in a week.
Day is the time when it is light, or the time when you are up and doing things.
You can refer to a particular period in history as a particular day or as particular days .
If you decide to do something, you choose to do it, usually after you have thought carefully about the other possibilities.
If a person or group of people decides something, they choose what something should be like or how a particular problem should be solved.
If an event or fact decides something, it makes it certain that a particular choice will be made or that there will be a particular result.
gloss_zh: （事件或事实）决定，确定（某一选择或结果）

senses.concept_en: If you decide that something is true, you form that opinion about it after considering the facts.
If something decides you to do something, it is the reason that causes you to choose to do it.

delegate.translation:
n. 代表
vt. 委派...为代表
delegate.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A delegate is a person who is chosen to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of other people, especially at a conference or a meeting.
If you delegate duties, responsibilities, or power to someone, you give them those duties, those responsibilities, or that power so that they can act on your behalf.
gloss_zh: 授（权）;把（职责、责任等）委托（给）

senses.concept_en: If you are delegated to do something, you are given the duty of acting on someone else's behalf by making decisions, voting, or doing some particular work.

delivery.translation:
n. 递送, 交付, 分娩, 交货, 引渡
[化] 交货额

senses.concept_en: Delivery or a delivery is the bringing of letters, parcels, or other goods to someone's house or to another place where they want them.
gloss_zh: （信件、包裹等的）递送，投递，运送

senses.concept_en: A delivery of something is the goods that are delivered.
gloss_zh: 递送之物;投递之物;运送之物

senses.concept_en: A delivery person or service delivers things to a place.
You talk about someone's delivery when you are referring to the way in which they give a speech or lecture.
Delivery is the process of giving birth to a baby.

derivation.breakdown_zh: deliver 交付 + -y 名词后缀：交付

despair.translation:
n. 绝望, 失望
vi. 绝望

senses.concept_en: Despair is the feeling that everything is wrong and that nothing will improve.
If you despair, you feel that everything is wrong and that nothing will improve.
If you despair of something, you feel that there is no hope that it will happen or improve. If you despair of someone, you feel that there is no hope that they will improve.
gloss_zh: 对…感到绝望;对…不抱希望

destroy.translation: vt. 破坏, 毁坏, 消灭

senses.concept_en: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.
To destroy someone means to ruin their life or to make their situation impossible to bear.
If an animal is destroyed, it is killed, either because it is ill or because it is dangerous.
gloss_zh: 杀死，消灭（生病或具危险性的动物）

senses.concept_en: If a particular factor determines the nature of a thing or event, it causes it to be of a particular kind.
To determine a fact means to discover it as a result of investigation.
If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.
If you determine to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

directly.translation:
adv. 径直地, 直接地, 直率地, 正好地, 直截了当地, (非正式)立即, 马上
conj. 一...(就...), 一当...就...
[计] 直接的

senses.concept_en: If something is directly above, below, or in front of something, it is in exactly that position.
If you do one action directly after another, you do the second action as soon as the first one is finished.
If something happens directly, it happens without any delay.

dirty.translation:
a. 肮脏的, 卑鄙的
vt. 弄脏
vi. 变脏

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is dirty, it is marked or covered with stains, spots, or mud, and needs to be cleaned.
To dirty something means to cause it to become dirty.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe an action as dirty, you disapprove of it and consider it unfair, immoral, or dishonest.
gloss_zh: 卑劣的;卑鄙的;不道德的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something such as a joke, a book, or someone's language as dirty, you mean that it refers to sex in a way that some people find offensive.
gloss_zh: （笑话、书籍、话语等）淫秽的，下流的，黄色的

senses.concept_en: Dirty is used before words of criticism to emphasize that you do not approve of someone or something.
gloss_zh: （用于批评之词前作强调）可恶的，可恨的

derivation.breakdown_zh: dirt 污物 + -y 形容词后缀：脏的

dissolve.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve it, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.
When an organization or institution is dissolved, it is officially ended or broken up.
When a parliament is dissolved, it is formally ended, so that elections for a new parliament can be held.
When a marriage or business arrangement is dissolved, it is officially ended.
gloss_zh: 解除（婚姻关系）；终止（商业协议）

senses.concept_en: If something such as a problem or feeling dissolves or is dissolved, it becomes weaker and disappears.

ditch.translation:
n. 沟渠
vt. 在...开沟
vi. 开沟
ditch.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A ditch is a long narrow channel cut into the ground at the side of a road or field.
If you ditch something that you have or are responsible for, you abandon it or get rid of it, because you no longer want it.
If someone ditches someone, they end a relationship with that person.
If a pilot ditches an aircraft or if it ditches, the pilot makes an emergency landing.

do.translation: v. 做, 进行, 完成

senses.concept_en: Do is used to form the negative of main verbs, by putting 'not' after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.
gloss_zh: （在do之后、主动词的原形之前加 not，构成主动词的否定式）

senses.concept_en: Do is used to form questions, by putting the subject after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.
gloss_zh: （将主语置于do和主动词的原形之间，构成疑问句）

senses.concept_en: Do is used in question tags.
You use do when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing 'do', or giving a negative or positive answer to a question.
gloss_zh: （对含有do的陈述句或疑问句作肯定或否定回答）

senses.concept_en: Do is used with a negative to tell someone not to behave in a certain way.
gloss_zh: （用在否定句中，表示不让某人做出某种举动）

senses.concept_en: Do is used to give emphasis to the main verb when there is no other auxiliary.
gloss_zh: （在没有其他助动词时，用来强调主动词）

senses.concept_en: Do is used as a polite way of inviting or trying to persuade someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （用以礼貌性地邀请或说服某人做某事）

senses.concept_en: Do can be used to refer back to another verb group when you are comparing or contrasting two things, or saying that they are the same.
gloss_zh: （在进行对比、比较或说明两组事物相同时，用来代替前面的动词词组）

senses.concept_en: You use do after 'so' and 'nor' to say that the same statement is true for two people or groups.
gloss_zh: （与 so 或 nor 连用，表示两人或两组事物的情况相同）

senses.concept_en: When you do something, you take some action or perform an activity or task. Do is often used instead of a more specific verb, to talk about a common action involving a particular thing. For example you can say 'do your teeth' instead of 'brush your teeth'.
gloss_zh: 做，干，进行（常用于代替某个具体的动词）

senses.concept_en: Do can be used to stand for any verb group, or to refer back to another verb group, including one that was in a previous sentence.
gloss_zh: （用来代替任何动词词组或前一个句子中的动词词组）

senses.concept_en: You can use do in a clause at the beginning of a sentence after words like 'what' and 'all', to give special emphasis to the information that comes at the end of the sentence.
gloss_zh: （用于句首从句中 what，all等词之后，以强调句尾的信息）

senses.concept_en: If you do a particular thing with something, you use it in that particular way.
If you do something about a problem, you take action to try to solve it.
If an action or event does a particular thing, such as harm or good, it has that result or effect.
gloss_zh: 造成，产生（好的或坏的结果或影响）

senses.concept_en: You can use do to talk about the degree to which a person, action, or event affects or improves a particular situation.
You can talk about what someone or something does to a person to mean that they have a very harmful effect on them.
If you ask someone what they do, you want to know what their job or profession is.
If you are doing something, you are busy or active in some way, or have planned an activity for some time in the future.
If you say that someone or something does well or badly, you are talking about how successful or unsuccessful they are.
If a person or organization does a particular service or product, they provide that service or sell that product.
You can use do when referring to the speed or rate that something or someone achieves or is able to achieve.
If you do a subject, author, or book, you study them at school or college.
If you do a particular person, accent, or role, you imitate that person or accent, or act that role.
You can use do to say that you are able or unable to behave in a particular way.
If someone does drugs, they take illegal drugs.
If you say that something will do or will do you, you mean that there is enough of it or that it is of good enough quality to meet your requirements or to satisfy you.
A do is a party, dinner party, or other social event.
gloss_zh: 宴会;社交聚会;社交活动

drain.translation:
n. 排水沟, 消耗, 排水
vt. 排出, 喝光, 耗尽
vi. 排水, 流干
drain.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you drain a liquid from a place or object, you remove the liquid by causing it to flow somewhere else. If a liquid drains somewhere, it flows there.
If you drain a place or object, you dry it by causing water to flow out of it. If a place or object drains, water flows out of it until it is dry.
If you drain food or if food drains, you remove the liquid that it has been in, especially after it has been cooked or soaked in water.
A drain is a pipe that carries water or sewage away from a place, or an opening in a surface that leads to the pipe.
If someone drains a glass, they empty it by drinking what is in it.
If the colour or the blood drains or is drained from someone's face, they become very pale. You can also say that someone's face drains or is drained of colour.
If a feeling drains or is drained out of you, it gradually becomes less strong until you no longer feel it.
If something drains you, it leaves you feeling physically and emotionally exhausted.
gloss_zh: 使精疲力竭;使心力交瘁

senses.concept_en: If energy drains or is drained from you, you lose all energy and become very tired.

See also:brain drain; If you say that something is a drain on an organization's finances or resources, you mean that it costs the organization a large amount of money, and you do not consider that it is worth it.
gloss_zh: （金钱或资源的）大量消耗，耗竭，耗费

senses.concept_en: If you say that a country's or a company's resources or finances are drained, you mean that they are used or spent completely.

drop.translation:
n. 滴, 微量, 落下, 空投
vi. 放下, 掉下, 下降
vt. 使滴下, 放下, 丢失, 遗漏
[计] 投入, 投入点, 接入点, 分接点
drop.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: If a level or amount drops or if someone or something drops it, it quickly becomes less.
If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.
If something drops onto something else, it falls onto that thing. If something drops from somewhere, it falls from that place.
If you drop something somewhere or if it drops there, you deliberately let it fall there.
If a person or a part of their body drops to a lower position, or if they drop a part of their body to a lower position, they move to that position, often in a tired and lifeless way.
To drop is used in expressions such as to be about to drop and to dance until you drop to emphasize that you are exhausted and can no longer continue doing something.
If a man drops his trousers, he pulls them down, usually as a joke or to be rude.
If your voice drops or if you drop your voice, you speak more quietly.
If you drop someone or something somewhere, you take them somewhere and leave them there, usually in a car or other vehicle.
gloss_zh: 中途放下（某人）;中途卸下（某物）

senses.concept_en: If you drop an idea, course of action, or habit, you do not continue with it.
If someone is dropped by a sports team or organization, they are no longer included in that team or employed by that organization.
If you drop a game or part of a game in a sports competition, you lose it.
If you drop to a lower position in a sports competition, you move to that position.
A drop of a liquid is a very small amount of it shaped like a little ball. In informal English, you can also use drop when you are referring to a very small amount of something such as a drink.
Drops are a kind of medicine which you put drop by drop into your ears, eyes, or nose.
Fruit or chocolate drops are small round sweets with a fruit or chocolate flavour.
gloss_zh: （水果味或巧克力味的）糖豆，糖果粒

senses.concept_en: You use drop to talk about vertical distances. For example, a thirty-foot drop is a distance of thirty feet between the top of a cliff or wall and the bottom of it.
gloss_zh: 落差;垂直距离;下降距离

dry.translation:
a. 干的, 无酒的, 枯燥无味的, 干燥的
vt. 把...弄干
vi. 变干
n. 干, 干涸

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is dry, there is no water or moisture on it or in it.
When something dries or when you dry it, it becomes dry.
When you dry the dishes after a meal, you wipe the water off the plates, cups, knives, pans, and other things when they have been washed, using a cloth.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that your skin or hair is dry, you mean that it is less oily than, or not as soft as, normal.
gloss_zh: （皮肤或头发）发干的,无水分的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If the weather or a period of time is dry, there is no rain or there is much less rain than average.
gloss_zh: 干旱的;雨量少的;无雨的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A dry place or climate is one that gets very little rainfall.
In the dry means in a place or at a time that is not damp, wet, or rainy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a river, lake, or well is dry, it is empty of water, usually because of hot weather and lack of rain.
gloss_zh: （通常指河流、湖泊或水井由于天热少雨而）干涸的

senses.concept_en: If an oil well is dry, it is no longer producing any oil.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are dry, you need to drink something.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your mouth or throat is dry, it has little or no saliva in it, and so feels very unpleasant, perhaps because you are tense or ill.
gloss_zh: （因紧张、生病等）口干的,喉咙干的

senses.concept_en: A dry cough is one that does not produce any mucus.
If someone has dry eyes, there are no tears in their eyes; often used with negatives or in contexts where you are expressing surprise that they are not crying.
If a country, state, or city is dry, it has laws or rules which forbid anyone to drink, sell, or buy alcoholic drink.
If you say that someone is sucking something dry or milking it dry, you are criticizing them for taking all the good things from it until there is nothing left.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Dry humour is very amusing, but in a subtle and clever way.
gloss_zh: （幽默）不露声色的,含蓄不露的,机敏的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a voice as dry, you mean that it is cold or dull, and does not express any emotions.
gloss_zh: 冷淡的;淡然的;不动感情的;冷冰冰的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something such as a book, play, or activity as dry, you mean that it is dull and uninteresting.
gloss_zh: 枯燥乏味的;干巴巴的;无趣的

senses.concept_en: Dry bread or toast is plain and not covered with butter or jam.
gloss_zh: （面包或吐司）不涂黄油和果酱的

senses.concept_en: Dry sherry or wine does not have a sweet taste.
If something happens during a period of time or an event, it happens continuously, or happens several times between the beginning and end of that period or event.
If something develops during a period of time, it develops gradually from the beginning to the end of that period.
An event that happens during a period of time happens at some point or moment in that period.

earn.translation:
vt. 赚得, 获得, 博得
[计] 欧州科学研究网

senses.concept_en: If you earn money, you receive money in return for work that you do.
If something earns money, it produces money as profit or interest.
If you earn something such as praise, you get it because you deserve it.

empty.translation:
a. 空的, 空虚的, 空腹的, 空洞的
n. 空的东西, 空车
vt. 倒空, 使变空, 使排出
vi. 流空
[计] 空

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An empty place, vehicle, or container is one that has no people or things in it.
An empty gesture, threat, or relationship has no real value or meaning.
gloss_zh: （威胁、关系等）空洞的，无意义的，无效的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person's life or a period of time as empty, you mean that nothing interesting or valuable happens in it.
gloss_zh: （生活或某段时间）空虚的，枯燥无味的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you feel empty, you feel unhappy and have no energy, usually because you are very tired or have just experienced something upsetting.
If you empty a container, or empty something out of it, you remove its contents, especially by tipping it up.
If someone empties a room or place, or if it empties, everyone that is in it goes away.
A river or canal that empties into a lake, river, or sea flows into it.
Empties are bottles or containers which no longer have anything in them.

enough.translation:
n. 充足, 够, 很多
a. 充足的, 足够
adv. 足够
interj. 够了

senses.concept_en: Enough means as much as you need or as much as is necessary.
If you say that something is enough, you mean that you do not want it to continue any longer or get any worse.
You can use enough to say that something is the case to a moderate or fairly large degree.
You use enough in expressions such as strangely enough and interestingly enough to indicate that you think a fact is strange or interesting.

entire.translation:
n. 整个, 全部
a. 全体的, 完全的, 全部的

senses.concept_en: You use entire when you want to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something, for example, the whole of a place, time, or population.

even.translation:
a. 平坦的, 相等的, 连贯的, 均等的, 公平的, 偶数的, 平均的, 平衡的, 恰好的
vt. 使平坦, 使相等
vi. 变平, 成为相等
adv. 甚至, 实际上, 完全, 十分
n. 偶数, 偶校验
[计] 偶数, 偶校验

senses.concept_en: You use even to suggest that what comes just after or just before it in the sentence is rather surprising.
You use even with comparative adjectives and adverbs to emphasize a quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （与形容词、副词的比较级连用）更加，愈发

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An even measurement or rate stays at about the same level.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An even surface is smooth and flat.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If there is an even distribution or division of something, each person, group, or area involved has an equal amount.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An even contest or competition is equally balanced between the two sides who are taking part.
gloss_zh: （比赛、竞争等）平衡的，不相上下的，势均力敌的

senses.concept_en: If you are even with someone, you do not owe them anything, such as money or a favour.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your voice is even, you are speaking in a very controlled way which makes it difficult for people to tell what your feelings are.
An even number can be divided exactly by the number two.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: See also:evens; If there is an even chance that something will happen, it is no more likely that it will happen than it will not happen.
gloss_zh: （成败机会）各半的，对半的，相等的

evening.translation: n. 傍晚, 晚间, 末期

senses.concept_en: The evening is the part of each day between the end of the afternoon and the time when you go to bed.
You use every to indicate that you are referring to all the members of a group or all the parts of something and not only some of them.
You use every in order to say how often something happens or to indicate that something happens at regular intervals.
You use every in front of a number when you are saying what proportion of people or things something happens to or applies to.
You can use every before some nouns, for example 'sign', 'effort', 'reason', and 'intention' in order to emphasize what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （用于名词前表示强调）充足的，完全的

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone's every whim, wish, or desire will be satisfied, you are emphasizing that everything they want will happen or be provided.
gloss_zh: （幻想、愿望、欲望等）所有的，全部的

evil.translation:
n. 邪恶, 不幸, 罪恶
a. 邪恶的, 不幸的, 有害的, 讨厌的

senses.concept_en: Evil is a powerful force that some people believe to exist, and which causes wicked and bad things to happen.
Evil is used to refer to all the wicked and bad things that happen in the world.
If you refer to an evil, you mean a very unpleasant or harmful situation or activity.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as evil, you mean that they are very wicked by nature and take pleasure in doing things that harm other people.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as evil, you mean that you think it causes a great deal of harm to people and is morally bad.
gloss_zh: 危害社会的；道德败坏的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as evil, you mean that you think it is influenced by the devil.
gloss_zh: 受魔鬼影响的;恶魔的;不祥的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe a very unpleasant smell as evil.

examine.translation: v. 检查, 调查, 考试

senses.concept_en: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.
If a doctor examines you, he or she looks at your body, feels it, or does simple tests in order to check how healthy you are.
If an idea, proposal, or plan is examined, it is considered very carefully.
If you are examined, you are given a formal test in order to show your knowledge of a subject.

exhibit.translation:
n. 显示, 显现, 展览品, 陈列品, 展览
vt. 展现, 陈列, 展览
vi. 开展览会

senses.concept_en: If someone or something shows a particular quality, feeling, or type of behaviour, you can say that they exhibit it.

When a painting, sculpture, or object of interest is exhibited, it is put in a public place such as a museum or art gallery so that people can come to look at it. You can also say that animals are exhibited in a zoo.
When artists exhibit, they show their work in public.
An exhibit is a painting, sculpture, or object of interest that is displayed to the public in a museum or art gallery.
An exhibit is a public display of paintings, sculpture, or objects of interest, for example in a museum or art gallery.
An exhibit is an object that a lawyer shows in court as evidence in a legal case.
If you say that someone exhibits something, you mean that they are showing it openly or publicly in order to be admired, noticed, or believed.

factory.translation:
n. 工厂, 产生地, 代理店
[经] 工厂, 代理店, 商行在国外的代理处

senses.concept_en: A factory is a large building where machines are used to make large quantities of goods.

derivation.breakdown_zh: fact 事实 + -ory 场所：制造场所

faithful.translation:
a. 忠实的, 详确的, 可靠的
n. 信徒

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is faithful to a person, organization, idea, or activity remains firm in their belief in them or support for them.
gloss_zh: 忠实的;忠诚的;忠贞不渝的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is faithful to their husband, wife, or lover does not have a sexual relationship with anyone else.
gloss_zh: （对丈夫、妻子或恋人）忠诚的，忠贞的

senses.concept_en: The faithful are the group of people who believe in a particular religion.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A faithful account, translation, or copy of something represents or reproduces the original accurately.
gloss_zh: （叙述、翻译或抄本）如实的，忠实原文的

fall.translation:
n. 落下, 瀑布, 采伐量, 下降, 落差, 降低, 堕落, 秋天
vi. 倒下, 落下, 来临, 失守, 阵亡, 下跌, 减弱, 倾斜, 垮台, 轮到, 变成, 降低
a. 秋天的

senses.concept_en: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downwards onto or towards the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.
If a person or structure that is standing somewhere falls, they move from their upright position, so that they are then lying on the ground.
See also:rainfall;snowfall; When rain or snow falls, it comes down from the sky.
If you fall somewhere, you allow yourself to drop there in a hurried or disorganized way, often because you are very tired.
gloss_zh: （常因疲乏）一头倒下，一下躺倒

senses.concept_en: If something falls, it decreases in amount, value, or strength.
gloss_zh: （数量）减少;（价值）下降;（力量）减弱

senses.concept_en: If a powerful or successful person falls, they suddenly lose their power or position.
If a place falls in a war or election, an enemy army or a different political party takes control of it.
If someone falls in battle, they are killed.

You can use fall to show that someone or something passes into another state. For example, if someone falls ill, they become ill, and if something falls into disrepair, it is then in a state of disrepair.
If you say that something or someone falls into a particular group or category, you mean that they belong in that group or category.
If the responsibility or blame for something falls on someone, they have to take the responsibility or the blame for it.
If silence or a feeling of sadness or tiredness falls on a group of people, they become silent, sad, or tired.
If a celebration or other special event falls on a particular day or date, it happens to be on that day or date.
gloss_zh: （庆典或特别事件）在，适逢（某日）

senses.concept_en: When light or shadow falls on something, it covers it.
