If someone's hair or a garment falls in a certain way, it hangs downwards in that way.
If you say that someone's eyes fell on something, you mean they suddenly noticed it.
When night or darkness falls, night begins and it becomes dark.
You can refer to a waterfall as the falls .
Fall is the season between summer and winter when the weather becomes cooler.
In the Christian religion, the Fall was the occasion when Adam and Eve sinned and God made them leave the Garden of Eden.
gloss_zh: 人类堕落（基督教中指亚当、夏娃违反戒律，被上帝逐出伊甸园）

senses.concept_en: In some sports such as judo and wrestling, a fall is the act of throwing or forcing your opponent to the floor.
gloss_zh: （摔跤中）双肩着地;（柔道中）体落

senses.concept_en: In cricket, when a wicket falls, the team who are fielding get one of the batsmen out.
gloss_zh: （板球中，三柱门）失陷（指击球员出局）

family.translation:
n. 家庭, 家人, 族
a. 家庭的

senses.concept_en: A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.
When people talk about a family, they sometimes mean children.
When people talk about their family, they sometimes mean their ancestors.
You can use family to describe things that belong to a particular family.
You can use family to describe things that are designed to be used or enjoyed by both parents and children.
gloss_zh: 全家共用的;全家共享的

senses.concept_en: A family of animals or plants is a group of related species.
Fifty is the number 50.

When you talk about the fifties, you are referring to numbers between 50 and 59. For example, if you are in your fifties, you are aged between 50 and 59. If the temperature is in the fifties, the temperature is between 50 and 59 degrees.
gloss_zh: 五十几（指 50 到 59 之间的数字）

senses.concept_en: The fifties is the decade between 1950 and 1959.

fill.translation:
vt. 装满, 填充, 弥漫, 供给, 满足, 供应
vi. 充满, 变得沉重
n. 满足, 装满, 充分, 填方
vt. 填充
vi. 填充
[计] 填充

senses.concept_en: If you fill a container or area, or if it fills, an amount of something enters it that is enough to make it full.
If something fills a space, it is so big, or there are such large quantities of it, that there is very little room left.
If you fill a crack or hole, you put a substance into it in order to make the surface smooth again.
If a sound, smell, or light fills a space, or the air, it is very strong or noticeable.
If something fills you with an emotion, or if an emotion fills you, you experience this emotion strongly.
gloss_zh: 使强烈地感到;（感情）充盈于

senses.concept_en: If you fill a period of time with a particular activity, you spend the time in this way.
If something fills a need or a gap, it puts an end to this need or gap by existing or being active.
If something fills a role, position, or function, they have that role or position, or perform that function, often successfully.
If a company or organization fills a job vacancy, they choose someone to do the job. If someone fills a job vacancy, they accept a job that they have been offered.
If you fill yourself with food, you eat so much that you do not feel hungry.
A play, film, or performer that fills a theatre, concert hall, or cinema attracts a very large audience.
gloss_zh: 使爆满;使满座;使座无虚席

senses.concept_en: When a dentist fills someone's tooth, he or she puts a filling in it.
If you fill an order or a prescription, you provide the things that are asked for.

financial.translation:
a. 财政的, 金融的
[经] 财政的, 金融的, 财务的

senses.concept_en: Financial means relating to or involving money.

derivation.breakdown_zh: finance 财政 + -ial 形容词：财政的

finished.translation: a. 完成的, 完结的, 精巧的, 完美的

for.translation:
prep. 为, 因为, 至于
conj. 因为
[计] DOS批处理命令:对一组参数重复执行指定的命令

senses.concept_en: If something is for someone, they are intended to have it or benefit from it.
If you work or do a job for someone, you are employed by them.
If you speak or act for a particular group or organization, you represent them.
If someone does something for you, they do it so that you do not have to do it.
If you feel a particular emotion for someone, you feel it on their behalf.
If you feel a particular emotion for someone or something, they are the object of that emotion, and you feel it when you think about them.
You use for after words such as 'time', 'space', 'money', or 'energy' when you say how much there is or whether there is enough of it in order to be able to do or use a particular thing.
If something is for sale, hire, or use, it is available to be sold, hired, or used.
You use for when you state or explain the purpose of an object, action, or activity.
You use for after nouns expressing reason or cause.
You can use for to introduce a clause which gives the reason why you made the statement in the main clause.
You can use for to introduce the cause of the fact that you have just mentioned.
For is used in conditional sentences, in expressions such as 'if not for' and 'were it not for', to introduce the only thing which prevents the main part of the sentence from being true.
gloss_zh: （用于条件句中）如果不是为了，要不是

senses.concept_en: You use for to say how long something lasts or continues.
You use for to say how far something extends.
If something is bought, sold, or done for a particular amount of money, that amount of money is its price.
If something is planned for a particular time, it is planned to happen then.
If you do something for a particular occasion, you do it on that occasion or to celebrate that occasion.
If you leave for a particular place or if you take a bus, train, plane, or boat for a place, you are going there.
You use for when you make a statement about something in order to say how it affects or relates to someone, or what their attitude to it is.
After some adjective, noun, and verb phrases, you use for to introduce the subject of the action indicated by the following infinitive verb.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词、名词和动词短语后，引出其后动词不定式的主语）

senses.concept_en: You use for when you say that an aspect of something or someone is surprising in relation to other aspects of them.
gloss_zh: 就…而言（表示相对来说不寻常）

senses.concept_en: If you say that you are for a particular activity, you mean that this is what you want or intend to do.
If you say that something is not for you, you mean that you do not enjoy it or that it is not suitable for you.
If it is for you to do something, it is your responsibility or right to do it.
gloss_zh: （表示负有责任或享有权利）由…

senses.concept_en: If you are for something, you agree with it or support it.
You use for after words such as 'argue', 'case', 'evidence', or 'vote' in order to introduce the thing that is being supported or proved.
gloss_zh: （用于 argue, case, evidence, vote 等词后，引出所支持或被证明之事）

senses.concept_en: For is the preposition that is used after some nouns, adjectives, or verbs in order to introduce more information or to indicate what a quality, thing, or action relates to.
gloss_zh: （置于某些名词、形容词或动词后，引出更多信息或与某性质、事物或行为相关的事物）

senses.concept_en: To be named for someone means to be given the same name as them.
You use for with 'every' when you are stating a ratio, to introduce one of the things in the ratio.
gloss_zh: （与 every 连用，引出比率）每…（就有…）

senses.concept_en: You can use for in expressions such as pound for pound or mile for mile when you are making comparisons between the values or qualities of different things.
gloss_zh: （用于比较）每镑对每镑/每英里对每英里

senses.concept_en: If a word or expression has the same meaning as another word or expression, you can say that the first one is another word or expression for the second one.
You use for in a piece of writing when you mention information which will be found somewhere else.
gloss_zh: （引出可在其他地方找到的信息）至于，对于

forest.translation:
n. 森林, 林区
vt. 植树于
forest.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: A forest is a large area where trees grow close together.
A forest of tall or narrow objects is a group of them standing or sticking upright.

formal.translation:
a. 正式的, 形式的, 礼仪的, 拘于礼节的, 拘谨的
n. 正式的社交活动

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Formal speech or behaviour is very correct and serious rather than relaxed and friendly, and is used especially in official situations.
A formal action, statement, or request is an official one.
gloss_zh: （行为、声明或要求）官方的，正式的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Formal occasions are special occasions at which people wear smart clothes and behave according to a set of accepted rules.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Formal clothes are very smart clothes that are suitable for formal occasions.
gloss_zh: （服饰）正规的，正式的，适合正式场合的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is done, written, or studied in a formal way has a very ordered, organized method or style.
gloss_zh: 整齐的;规矩的;井然有序的

senses.concept_en: Formal education or training is given officially, usually in a school, college, or university.
See also:formality; A formal garden or room is arranged in a very regular and controlled way, especially according to certain rules of design.
gloss_zh: （尤指按照某种设计规则）布局匀称的，布置整齐的

derivation.breakdown_zh: form 形式 + -al 形容词后缀：形式的

freeze.translation:
vi. 冻结, 冷冻, 僵硬, 楞住
vt. 使结冰, 使冻住, 使呆住
n. 结冰, 凝固
[计] 冻结

senses.concept_en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.
If you freeze something such as food, you preserve it by storing it at a temperature below freezing point. You can also talk about how well food freezes .
If something such as a pipe or machine freezes, it becomes blocked or stiff with ice or frozen liquid.
gloss_zh: （管子、机器等因液体结冰）冻得堵塞，冻牢

senses.concept_en: When it freezes outside, the temperature falls below freezing point.
If you freeze, you feel extremely cold.
If someone who is moving freezes, they suddenly stop and become completely still and quiet.
If the government or a company freeze things such as prices or wages, they state officially that they will not allow them to increase for a fixed period of time.
If a government freezes a plan or process, they state officially that they will not allow it to continue for a period of time.

See also:freezing;frozen; If someone in authority freezes something such as a bank account, fund, or property, they obtain a legal order which states that it cannot be used or sold for a particular period of time.
gloss_zh: 冻结，查封（银行账户、基金、财产等）

freezing.translation:
a. 冰冻的, 冷冻用的, 严寒的
[化] 冻结; 冻结作用; 凝固; 凝固作用

senses.concept_en: If you say that something is freezing or freezing cold, you are emphasizing that it is very cold
If you say that you are freezing or freezing cold, you emphasizing that you feel very cold.
See also:freeze; Freezing means the same as freezing point .

from.translation: prep. 从, 来自, 根据

senses.concept_en: If something comes from a particular person or thing, or if you get something from them, they give it to you or they are the source of it.
Someone who comes from a particular place lives in that place or originally lived there. Something that comes from a particular place was made in that place.
A person from a particular organization works for that organization.
If someone or something moves or is moved from a place, they leave it or are removed, so that they are no longer there.
If you take one thing or person from another, you move that thing or person so that they are no longer with the other or attached to the other.
If you take something from an amount, you reduce the amount by that much.
From is used in expressions such as away from or absent from to say that someone or something is not present in a place where they are usually found.
If you return from a place or an activity, you return after being in that place or doing that activity.
If you are back from a place or activity, you have left it and have returned to your former place.
If you see or hear something from a particular place, you are in that place when you see it or hear it.
If something hangs or sticks out from an object, it is attached to it or held by it.
You can use from when giving distances. For example, if a place is fifty miles from another place, the distance between the two places is fifty miles.
If a road or railway line goes from one place to another, you can travel along it between the two places.
From is used, especially in the expression made from, to say what substance has been used to make something.
You can use from when you are talking about the beginning of a period of time.
You say from one thing to another when you are stating the range of things that are possible, or when saying that the range of things includes everything in a certain category.
If something changes from one thing to another, it stops being the first thing and becomes the second thing.
You use from after some verbs and nouns when mentioning the cause of something.
You use from when you are giving the reason for an opinion.
From is used after verbs with meanings such as 'protect', 'free', 'keep', and 'prevent' to introduce the action that does not happen, or that someone does not want to happen.
gloss_zh: （用于 protect, free, keep, prevent 等动词后）免于

future.translation:
n. 未来, 将来
a. 将来的, 未来的

senses.concept_en: The future is the period of time that will come after the present, or the things that will happen then.
gloss_zh: 未来;将来;将来发生的事

senses.concept_en: Future things will happen or exist after the present time. for future reference
Someone's future, or the future of something, is what will happen to them or what they will do after the present time.
If you say that someone or something has a future, you mean that they are likely to be successful or to survive.
gloss_zh: 成功的可能;未来的希望

senses.concept_en: When people trade in futures, they buy stocks and shares, commodities such as coffee or oil, or foreign currency at a price that is agreed at the time of purchase for items which are delivered some time in the future.

In grammar, the future tense of a verb is the one used to talk about things that are going to happen. In English, this applies to verb groups consisting of 'will' or 'shall' and the base form of a verb. The future perfect tense of a verb is used to talk about things that will have happened at some time in the future.

great.translation:
a. 大的, 非常的, 主要的, 重大的, 崇高的, 伟大的
adv. 顺利地, 得意地
n. 全部, 大人物, 大师

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use great to describe something that is very large. Great is more formal than big .

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Great means large in amount or degree.
gloss_zh: （数量或程度）大的，巨大的，超乎寻常的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use great to describe something that is important, famous, or exciting.
gloss_zh: 重大的；闻名的；令人激动的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe someone who is successful and famous for their actions, knowledge, or skill as great .
gloss_zh: 伟大的；著名的； 卓越的；优秀的

senses.concept_en: The greats in a particular subject or field of activity are the people who have been most successful or famous in it.
The greats of popular modern music are records that have been successful and that continue to be popular.
If you describe someone or something as great, you approve of them or admire them.
gloss_zh: 美妙的；好极了的；了不起的

senses.concept_en: If you feel great, you feel very healthy, energetic, and enthusiastic.
gloss_zh: 十分健康的；精力旺盛的；充满热情的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use great in order to emphasize the size or degree of a characteristic or quality.
You say great in order to emphasize that you are pleased or enthusiastic about something.
You say great in order to emphasize that you are angry or annoyed about something.
gloss_zh: 哼，这倒好（表示气愤、恼火等）

senses.concept_en: See also:greater; Great is used as part of the name of a species of plant or animal when there is another species of the same plant or animal which is smaller and has different characteristics.
gloss_zh: （用于同类动植物中较大者的名称前）大

ground.translation:
n. 土地, 战场, 场地, 地面, 范围
a. 土地的, 地面上的
vt. 放在地上, 使搁浅, 打基础, 给...以训练
vi. 搁浅, 落地, 根据, 基于
a. 磨过的
grind的过去式和过去分词

senses.concept_en: The ground is the surface of the earth.
If you say that something takes place on the ground, you mean it takes place on the surface of the earth and not in the air.
The ground is the soil and rock on the earth's surface.
You can refer to land as ground, especially when it has very few buildings or when it is considered to be special in some way.
gloss_zh: （尤指建筑物极少或具有某种特性的）土地

senses.concept_en: You can use ground to refer to an area of land, sea, or air which is used for a particular activity.
A ground is an area of land which is specially designed and made for playing sport or for some other activity. In American English grounds is also used.
gloss_zh: 运动场，…场（美国英语中亦作grounds）

senses.concept_en: The grounds of a large or important building are the garden or area of land which surrounds it.
gloss_zh: （大型或重要建筑周围的）场地，庭院，花园

senses.concept_en: You can use ground to refer to a place or situation in which particular methods or ideas can develop and be successful.
gloss_zh: （适于方法、思想等发展的）地方

senses.concept_en: You can use ground in expressions such as on shaky ground and the same ground to refer to a particular subject, area of experience, or basis for an argument.
Ground is used in expressions such as gain ground ,lose ground, and give ground in order to indicate that someone gets or loses an advantage.
If something is grounds for a feeling or action, it is a reason for it. If you do something on the grounds of a particular thing, that thing is the reason for your action.
If an argument, belief, or opinion is grounded in something, that thing is used to justify it.
gloss_zh: 以…为根据；建立在…基础上

senses.concept_en: If an aircraft or its passengers are grounded, they are made to stay on the ground and are not allowed to take off.
When parents ground a child, they forbid them to go out and enjoy themselves for a period of time, as a punishment.
If a ship or boat is grounded or if it grounds, it touches the bottom of the sea, lake, or river it is on, and is unable to move off.
The ground in an electric plug or piece of electrical equipment is the wire through which electricity passes into the ground and which makes the equipment safe.
Ground meat has been cut into very small pieces in a machine.
Ground is the past tense and past participle of grind .

guard.translation:
n. 守卫者, 警戒, 护卫队, 防护装置
vt. 保卫, 看守, 当心
vi. 防止, 警惕, 警卫, 看守

senses.concept_en: If you guard a place, person, or object, you stand near them in order to watch and protect them.
If you guard someone, you watch them and keep them in a particular place to stop them from escaping.
A guard is someone such as a soldier, police officer, or prison officer who is guarding a particular place or person.
A guard is a specially organized group of people, such as soldiers or policemen, who protect or watch someone or something.
On a train, a guard is a person whose job is to travel on the train in order to help passengers, check tickets, and make sure that the train travels safely and on time.
If you guard some information or advantage that you have, you try to protect it or keep it for yourself.
A guard is a protective device which covers a part of someone's body or a dangerous part of a piece of equipment.
gloss_zh: 保护装置；保护罩；保护器

senses.concept_en: Some regiments in the British Army, or the soldiers in them, are referred to as Guards.
gloss_zh: （英国的）近卫军，禁军，近卫军士兵

guide.translation:
n. 引导者, 导游, 指南, 路标
vt. 指导, 支配, 管理, 带领, 操纵
vi. 任向导
[计] 辅助线

senses.concept_en: In Britain, the Guides is an organization for girls which teaches them to become practical and independent. The Guides used to be called the Girl Guides. In the United States, there is a similar organization called the Girl Scouts.
gloss_zh: （英国的）女童子军（美国为Girl Scout）

senses.concept_en: In Britain, a Guide is a girl who is a member of the Guides.

habit.translation:
n. 习惯, 嗜好, 习性
vt. 使穿衣
habit.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: A habit is something that you do often or regularly.
A habit is an action which is considered bad that someone does repeatedly and finds it difficult to stop doing.
A drug habit is an addiction to a drug such as heroin or cocaine.
gloss_zh: （吸食海洛因、可卡因等的）毒瘾

senses.concept_en: A habit is a piece of clothing shaped like a long loose dress, which a nun or monk wears.
gloss_zh: （修道士或修女穿的）长袍，道袍，道服

hall.translation: n. 门厅, 走廊, 会堂
hall.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: The hall in a house or flat is the area just inside the front door, into which some of the other rooms open.
A hall in a building is a long passage with doors into rooms on both sides of it.
See also:city hall;town hall; A hall is a large room or building which is used for public events such as concerts, exhibitions, and meetings.
If students live in hall in British English, or in a hall in American English, they live in a university or college building called a hall of residence.
Hall is sometimes used as part of the name of a large house in the country.
gloss_zh: （乡间）大庄园，府第（用于住宅名称中）

senses.concept_en: Hall is sometimes used as part of the name of a large building, especially one where public events or concerts take place
gloss_zh: 厅，会堂，礼堂（尤用于礼堂、音乐厅等名称中）

hard.translation:
a. 坚硬的, 硬的, 难的, 艰苦的, 困难的, 坚固的, 猛烈的, 艰难的, 结实的, 确实的
adv. 坚硬地, 努力地, 辛苦地, 接近地, 猛烈地, 牢固地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is hard is very firm and stiff to touch and is not easily bent, cut, or broken.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is hard is very difficult to do or deal with.
If you work hard doing something, you are very active or work intensely, with a lot of effort.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hard work involves a lot of activity and effort.
If you look, listen, or think hard, you do it carefully and with a great deal of attention.
If you strike or take hold of something hard, you strike or take hold of it with a lot of force.
You can use hard to indicate that something happens intensely and for a long time.
gloss_zh: 强烈地;猛烈的;长时间地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a person or their expression is hard, they show no kindness or sympathy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are hard on someone, you treat them severely or unkindly.
gloss_zh: 苛刻的;严厉的;不友善的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is hard on a person or thing, you mean it affects them in a way that is likely to cause them damage or suffering.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you have a hard life or a hard period of time, your life or that period is difficult and unpleasant for you.
gloss_zh: （生活、一段日子）艰难的，艰苦的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A hard winter or a hard frost is a very cold one.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hard colours or sounds are harsh or bright and unpleasant to see or hear.
gloss_zh: （颜色）刺目的，晃眼的;（声音）刺耳的，难听的

senses.concept_en: Hard evidence or facts are definitely true and do not need to be questioned.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Hard water contains a lot of calcium compounds that stop soap making bubbles and sometimes appear as a deposit in kettles and baths.
gloss_zh: （水质）硬的（指含钙化合物较多）

senses.concept_en: Hard drugs are very strong illegal drugs such as heroin or cocaine.
In phonetics, a hard sound is one such as 'c' or 'g' as pronounced in the words 'cat' or 'give', and not as in the words 'cinema' or 'general'.

have.translation:
vt. 有, 怀有, 拿, 进行
aux. 已经

senses.concept_en: You use the forms have and has with a past participle to form the present perfect tense of verbs.
gloss_zh: （have 和 has 与过去分词连用构成动词的现在完成时）

senses.concept_en: You use the form had with a past participle to form the past perfect tense of verbs.
gloss_zh: （had 与过去分词连用构成动词的过去完成时）

senses.concept_en: Have is used in question tags.
You use have when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing 'have', 'has', or 'had', or answering a question.
gloss_zh: （用于对带有 have,has 或 had 的句子作肯定或否定回答）

senses.concept_en: The form having with a past participle can be used to introduce a clause in which you mention an action which had already happened before another action began.
gloss_zh: （having 和过去分词连用，所引导的分句中提到的动作发生在另一个动作开始之前）

senses.concept_en: You can use have followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would be possible to use the same word as a verb. For example, you can say 'I had a look at the photos' instead of 'I looked at the photos.'
gloss_zh: （have 后接名词代替该名词作动词的用法，描述某一动作或事件）
collocations: I had a look at the photos

senses.concept_en: In normal spoken or written English, people use have with a wide range of nouns to talk about actions and events, often instead of a more specific verb. For example people are more likely to say 'we had ice cream' or 'he's had a shock' than 'we ate ice cream', or 'he's suffered a shock'.
gloss_zh: （在英语口语或书面语中，have可以和很多名词连用以代替某个具体的动词，描述某一动作或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use have to say that someone or something owns a particular thing, or when you are mentioning one of their qualities or characteristics.
If you have something to do, you are responsible for doing it or must do it.

You can use have instead of 'there is' to say that something exists or happens. For example, you can say 'you have no alternative' instead of 'there is no alternative', or 'he had a good view from his window' instead of 'there was a good view from his window'.
gloss_zh: （用于代替 there is, 表示某事物存在或发生了某事）
collocations: he had a good view from his window

senses.concept_en: If you have something such as a part of your body in a particular position or state, it is in that position or state.
If you have something done, someone does it for you or you arrange for it to be done.
If someone has something unpleasant happen to them, it happens to them.
If you have someone do something, you persuade, cause, or order them to do it.
If someone has you by a part of your body, they are holding you there and they are trying to hurt you or force you to go somewhere.
gloss_zh: 抓住（某人身体的某部位）

senses.concept_en: If you have something from someone, they give it to you.
If you have an illness or disability, you suffer from it.
If a woman has a baby, she gives birth to it. If she is having a baby, she is pregnant.
You can use have in expressions such as 'I won't have it' or 'I'm not having that', to mean that you will not allow or put up with something.

he.translation:
pron. 他
n. 男孩, 男人, 雄性动物

senses.concept_en: You use he to refer to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, he is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use 'he or she' or 'they'.
gloss_zh: （书面英语中泛指人）他，她（有些人不喜欢这种用法，更倾向于使用 he or she 或 they）

senses.concept_en: In some religions, He is used to refer to God.

heavy.translation:
a. 重的, 巨大的, 沉重的, 笨重的, 过度的
adv. 沉重地
n. 重物, 严肃角色

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is heavy weighs a lot.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use heavy to ask or talk about how much someone or something weighs.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Heavy means great in amount, degree, or intensity.
gloss_zh: 大量的;重大的;严重的;强烈的;剧烈的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is heavy is solid in appearance or structure, or is made of a thick material.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy substance is thick in texture.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy meal is large in amount and often difficult to digest.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is heavy with things is full of them or loaded with them.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a person's breathing is heavy, it is very loud and deep.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy movement or action is done with a lot of force or pressure.
A heavy machine or piece of military equipment is very large and very powerful.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a period of time or a schedule as heavy, you mean it involves a lot of work.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Heavy work requires a lot of strength or energy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is heavy on another thing, you mean that it uses a lot of that thing or too much of that thing.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Air or weather that is heavy is unpleasantly still, hot, and damp.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person's face as heavy, you mean that it looks sad, tired, or unfriendly.
gloss_zh: （表情）沉痛的，疲惫呆滞的，阴郁的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your heart is heavy, you are sad about something.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A situation that is heavy is serious and difficult to cope with.
A heavy is a large strong man who is employed to protect a person or place, often by using violence.
gloss_zh: （雇作保镖或打手的）彪形大汉

help.translation:
n. 帮忙, 帮助者, 补救办法, 有益的东西
vt. 帮助, 帮忙, 接济, 治疗, 款待
vi. 有用, 救命, 招待
[计] 帮助, 帮助程序; DOS外部命令: DOS命令的电子文件帮助程序

senses.concept_en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or money.
If you say that something helps, you mean that it makes something easier to do or get, or that it improves a situation to some extent.
If you help someone go somewhere or move in some way, you give them support so that they can move more easily.
If you help yourself, you try to get yourself out of a difficult situation rather than accept it and think you can do nothing to change it.
If you say that someone or something has been a help or has been some help, you mean that they have helped you to solve a problem.
gloss_zh: 帮助解决困难的人（或事物）

senses.concept_en: Help is action taken to rescue a person who is in danger. You shout 'help!' when you are in danger in order to attract someone's attention so that they can come and rescue you.
In computing, help, or the help menu, is a file that gives you information and advice, for example about how to use a particular program.

If you help yourself to something, you serve yourself or you take it for yourself. If someone tells you to help yourself, they are telling you politely to serve yourself anything you want or to take anything you want.
If someone helps themselves to something, they steal it.

helper.translation:
n. 帮忙者, 有益的东西
[机] 助手

his.translation:
pron. 他的
[化] 组氨酸

senses.concept_en: You use his to indicate that something belongs or relates to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, his is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use 'his or her' or 'their'.
gloss_zh: （书面英语中泛指人）他的，她的（有些人不喜欢这种说法，更倾向于使用 his or her 或 their）

senses.concept_en: In some religions, His is used to refer to God.

honest.translation: a. 诚实的, 坦直的, 可靠的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as honest, you mean that they always tell the truth, and do not try to deceive people or break the law.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are honest in a particular situation, you tell the complete truth or give your sincere opinion, even if this is not very pleasant.
gloss_zh: 坦诚的;直率的;不隐瞒真相的

senses.concept_en: You say 'honest' before or after a statement to emphasize that you are telling the truth and that you want people to believe you.

however.translation:
adv. 然而, 无论如何, 究竟怎样
conj. 然而, 可是

senses.concept_en: You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said.
You use however before an adjective or adverb to emphasize that the degree or extent of something cannot change a situation.
gloss_zh: （后接形容词或副词用于强调）不管怎样，无论多么

senses.concept_en: You use however when you want to say that it makes no difference how something is done.
gloss_zh: 不管用什么方式;无论如何

senses.concept_en: You use however in expressions such as or however long it takes and or however many there were to indicate that the figure you have just mentioned may not be accurate.
You can use however to ask in an emphatic way how something has happened which you are very surprised about. Some speakers of English think that this form is incorrect and prefer to use 'how ever'.
gloss_zh: 究竟怎样，到底如何（用于强调地询问令人吃惊的事情;一些人认为此用法不正确，用how ever较为妥当）

ice.translation:
n. 冰, 冰淇淋, 糖衣, 冷若冰霜, 矜持, 贿赂
vt. 使结冰, 冰镇, 覆以糖衣
vi. 结冰

senses.concept_en: Ice is frozen water.
If you ice a cake, you cover it with icing.
An ice is an ice cream .

in.translation:
prep. 在...期间, 在...之内, 处于...之中, 从事于, 按照, 穿着
adv. 进入, 朝里, 在里面, 在屋里
a. 在里面的, 在朝的
n. 执政者, 交情

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is in something else is enclosed by it or surrounded by it. If you put something in a container, you move it so that it is enclosed by the container.
If something happens in a place, it happens there.
If you are in, you are present at your home or place of work.
When someone comes in, they enter a room or building.
If a train, boat, or plane has come in or is in, it has arrived at a station, port, or airport.
When the sea or tide comes in, the sea moves towards the shore rather than away from it.
Something that is in a window, especially a shop window, is just behind the window so that you can see it from outside.
When you see something in a mirror, the mirror shows an image of it.
If you are dressed in a piece of clothing, you are wearing it.
Something that is covered or wrapped in something else has that thing over or round its surface.
If there is something such as a crack or hole in something, there is a crack or hole on its surface.
If something is in a book, film, play, or picture, you can read it or see it there.
gloss_zh: 在（书、电影、戏剧、图片）之中

senses.concept_en: If you are in something such as a play or a race, you are one of the people taking part.
Something that is in a group or collection is a member of it or part of it.
You use in to specify a general subject or field of activity.
If something happens in a particular year, month, or other period of time, it happens during that time.
If something happens in a particular situation, it happens while that situation is going on.
If you do something in a particular period of time, that is how long it takes you to do it.
If something will happen in a particular length of time, it will happen after that length of time.
You use in to indicate roughly how old someone is. For example, if someone is in their fifties, they are between 50 and 59 years old.
You use in to indicate roughly how many people or things do something.
You use in to express a ratio, proportion, or probability.
If something or someone is in a particular state or situation, that is their present state or situation.
You use in to indicate the feeling or desire which someone has when they do something, or which causes them to do it.
gloss_zh: 带着，充满（某种情感或愿望）

senses.concept_en: If a particular quality or ability is in you, you naturally have it.
You use in when saying that someone or something has a particular quality.
You use in to indicate how someone is expressing something.
You use in in expressions such as in a row or in a ball to describe the arrangement or shape of something.
gloss_zh: （表示排列或形状）成一排/呈球形

senses.concept_en: If something is in a particular colour, it has that colour.
You use in to specify which feature or aspect of something you are talking about.
If you say that something is in, or is the in thing, you mean it is fashionable or popular.
gloss_zh: 时髦的;流行的;受欢迎的

senses.concept_en: You use in with a present participle to indicate that when you do something, something else happens as a result.

insist.translation: v. 坚持, 坚决主张, 强调
insist.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: If you insist that something should be done, you say so very firmly and refuse to give in about it. If you insist on something, you say firmly that it must be done or provided.
gloss_zh: 坚持;坚决认为（或主张、要求）

senses.concept_en: If you insist that something is the case, you say so very firmly and refuse to say otherwise, even though other people do not believe you.

inspection.translation:
n. 检验, 检查, 视察
[医] 检查, 视察, 监督, 望诊

derivation.breakdown_zh: inspect 检查 + -ion 名词后缀：检查行为

into.translation: prep. 进入...之内, 朝..., 深入...之中, 成为...状况

senses.concept_en: If you put one thing into another, you put the first thing inside the second.
If you go into a place or vehicle, you move from being outside it to being inside it.
If one thing goes into another, the first thing moves from the outside to the inside of the second thing, by breaking or damaging the surface of it.
gloss_zh: （打破或损坏表面而）进入,插入

senses.concept_en: If one thing gets into another, the first thing enters the second and becomes part of it.
If you are walking or driving a vehicle and you bump into something or crash into something, you hit it accidentally.
When you get into a piece of clothing, you put it on.
If someone or something gets into a particular state, they start being in that state.
If you talk someone into doing something, you persuade them to do it.
If something changes into something else, it then has a new form, shape, or nature.
If something is cut or split into a number of pieces or sections, it is divided so that it becomes several smaller pieces or sections.
An investigation into a subject or event is concerned with that subject or event.
If you move or go into a particular career or business, you start working in it.
gloss_zh: 进入,转向（某一职业、行业）

senses.concept_en: If something continues into a period of time, it continues until after that period of time has begun.
If you are very interested in something and like it very much, you can say that you are into it.

iron.translation:
n. 铁, 熨斗, 铁器, 坚强, 烙铁, 镣铐
vt. 烫平, 熨, 用铁包
vi. 烫平

senses.concept_en: See also:cast-iron; Iron is an element which usually takes the form of a hard, dark grey metal. It is used to make steel, and also forms part of many tools, buildings, and vehicles. Very small amounts of iron occur in your blood and in food.
An iron is an electrical device with a flat metal base. You heat it until the base is hot, then rub it over clothes to remove creases.
If you iron clothes, you remove the creases from them using an iron.
You can use iron to describe the character or behaviour of someone who is very firm in their decisions and actions, or who can control their feelings well.
Iron is used in expressions such as an iron hand and iron discipline to describe strong, harsh, or unfair methods of control which do not allow people much freedom.

it.translation:
pron. 它
[计] 信息论, 输入终端, 智能终端, 内捕获

senses.concept_en: You use it to refer to an object, animal, or other thing that has already been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 它（指物体、动物或上文已提及的其他事物）

senses.concept_en: You use it to refer to a child or baby whose sex you do not know or whose sex is not relevant to what you are saying.
You use it to refer in a general way to a situation that you have just described.
You use it before certain nouns, adjectives, and verbs to introduce your feelings or point of view about a situation.
gloss_zh: （用于某些名词、形容词、动词前说明对某情况的感受、观点）

senses.concept_en: You use it in passive clauses which report a situation or event.
gloss_zh: （用于被动句中引出一个情况或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use it with some verbs that need a subject or object, although there is no noun that it refers to.
gloss_zh: （与动词连用,作形式主语或宾语）

senses.concept_en: You use it as the subject of 'be', to say what the time, day, or date is.
gloss_zh: （用作 be动词的主语,指钟点、星期、日期）

senses.concept_en: You use it as the subject of a link verb to describe the weather, the light, or the temperature.
gloss_zh: （用作系动词的主语，描述天气、光线或温度）

senses.concept_en: You use it when you are telling someone who you are, or asking them who they are, especially at the beginning of a phone call. You also use it in statements and questions about the identity of other people.
gloss_zh: （尤用于刚接通电话时询问、告知身份）

senses.concept_en: When you are emphasizing or drawing attention to something, you can put that thing immediately after it and a form of the verb 'be'.
gloss_zh: （与动词 be 连用，强调突出某物）

joint.translation:
n. 连接处, 接合, 关节
a. 共同的, 联合的, 连接的, 合办的
vt. 连接, 接合, 使有接头
vi. 贴合, 长节

senses.concept_en: Joint means shared by or belonging to two or more people.
A joint is a part of your body such as your elbow or knee where two bones meet and are able to move together.
See also:dovetail joint; A joint is the place where two things are fastened or fixed together.
gloss_zh: 接合处；连接点；接头；接缝

senses.concept_en: A joint is a fairly large piece of meat which is suitable for roasting.
You can refer to a cheap place where people go for some form of entertainment as a joint .
gloss_zh: 廉价娱乐场所；下等娱乐场所

senses.concept_en: A joint is a cigarette which contains cannabis or marijuana.

jump.translation:
n. 跳跃, 跳动, 暴涨, 惊跳
vt. 跳跃, 跃过, 突升, 使跳跃
vi. 跳跃, 跳, 跳动, 暴涨
[计] 转移, 跳转

senses.concept_en: If you jump, you bend your knees, push against the ground with your feet, and move quickly upwards into the air.
If you jump from something above the ground, you deliberately push yourself into the air so that you drop towards the ground.
If you jump something such as a fence, you move quickly up and through the air over or across it.
If you jump somewhere, you move there quickly and suddenly.
If something makes you jump, it makes you make a sudden movement because you are frightened or surprised.
gloss_zh: （因害怕或吃惊）猛地一跳，突然一跳

senses.concept_en: If an amount or level jumps, it suddenly increases or rises by a large amount in a short time.
If someone jumps a queue, they move to the front of it and are served or dealt with before it is their turn.
If someone jumps on you or jumps you, they attack you suddenly or unexpectedly.
gloss_zh: 突然袭击；出其不意地攻击

senses.concept_en: If you jump at an offer or opportunity, you accept it quickly and eagerly.
gloss_zh: 迫不及待地接受，欣然应承（建议或机会）

senses.concept_en: If someone jumps on you, they quickly criticize you if you do something that they do not approve of.
gloss_zh: 毫不犹豫地批评；立即责备

keep.translation:
n. 生计, 维持, 保持
vt. 保持, 保存, 遵守, 看守, 整理, 维持, 履行, 经营, 拘留, 记帐
vi. 保持, 继续不断

senses.concept_en: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it.
If you keep or you are kept in a particular position or place, you remain in it.

If you keep off something or keep away from it, you avoid it. If you keep out of something, you avoid getting involved in it. You can also say that you keep someone off ,away from or out of something.
If someone or something keeps you from a particular action, they prevent you from doing it.
If you try to keep from doing something, you try to stop yourself from doing it.
If you keep something from someone, you do not tell them about it.
If you keep doing something, you do it repeatedly or continue to do it.
Keep is used with some nouns to indicate that someone does something for a period of time or continues to do it. For example, if you keep a grip on something, you continue to hold or control it.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词连用，表示持续一段时间或继续做某事）持续，继续（持有或控制）

senses.concept_en: If you keep something, you continue to have it in your possession and do not throw it away, give it away, or sell it.
If you keep something in a particular place, you always have it or store it in that place so that you can use it whenever you need it.
When you keep something such as a promise or an appointment, you do what you said you would do.
If you keep a record of a series of events, you write down details of it so that they can be referred to later.
If you keep yourself or keep someone else, you support yourself or the other person by earning enough money to provide food, clothing, money, and other necessary things.
Someone's keep is the cost of food and other things that they need in their daily life.
If you keep animals, you own them and take care of them.
If you keep a business such as a small shop or hotel, you own it and manage it.
If someone or something keeps you, they delay you and make you late.
If food keeps for a certain length of time, it stays fresh and suitable to eat for that time.
You can say or ask how someone is keeping as a way of saying or asking whether they are well.
gloss_zh: （用于询问健康状况）保持健康

senses.concept_en: A keep is the main tower of a medieval castle, in which people lived.

know.translation: v. 知道, 了解, 认识, 确信

senses.concept_en: If you know a fact, a piece of information, or an answer, you have it correctly in your mind.
If you know someone, you are familiar with them because you have met them and talked to them before.
If you say that you know of something, you mean that you have heard about it but you do not necessarily have a lot of information about it.
If you know about a subject, you have studied it or taken an interest in it, and understand part or all of it.
If you know a language, you have learned it and can understand it.
If you know something such as a place, a work of art, or an idea, you have visited it, seen it, read it, or heard about it, and so you are familiar with it.
If you know how to do something, you have the necessary skills and knowledge to do it.
You can say that someone knows that something is happening when they become aware of it.
If you know something or someone, you recognize them when you see them or hear them.
If someone or something is known as a particular name, they are called by that name.
If you know someone or something as a person or thing that has particular qualities, you consider that they have those qualities.
If you know someone as a person with a particular job or role, you are familiar with them in that job or role, rather than in any other.
People sometimes say 'What do you know!' when they are very surprised about something.
gloss_zh: （表示惊讶）你看怪不怪，真没想到

large.translation:
a. 大的, 大量的, 宽大的, 广博的
adv. 大大地, 夸大地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A large thing or person is greater in size than usual or average.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A large amount or number of people or things is more than the average amount or number.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A large organization or business does a lot of work or commercial activity and employs a lot of people.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Large is used to indicate that a problem or issue which is being discussed is very important or serious.

last.translation:
a. 最后的, 末尾的, 最近的
vi. 持续, 支持, 维持
vt. 使维持, 够...用
adv. 最后, 后来
n. 最后, 末尾, 鞋楦头

senses.concept_en: You use last in expressions such as last Friday ,last night, and last year to refer, for example, to the most recent Friday, night, or year.
gloss_zh: （表示最近过去的）刚过去的星期五/昨晚/去年

senses.concept_en: The last event, person, thing, or period of time is the most recent one.
If something last happened on a particular occasion, that is the most recent occasion on which it happened.
The last thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes after all the others of the same kind.
If you do something last, you do it after everyone else does, or after you do everything else.
If you are the last to do or know something, everyone else does or knows it before you.
Last is used to refer to the only thing, person, or part of something that remains.
You use last before numbers to refer to a position that someone has reached in a competition after other competitors have been knocked out.
gloss_zh: （竞赛中）最后留下的，排位在前的

senses.concept_en: You can use last to indicate that something is extremely undesirable or unlikely.
gloss_zh: 最不想要的；最不可能的

senses.concept_en: The last you see of someone or the last you hear of them is the final time that you see them or talk to them.
If an event, situation, or problem lasts for a particular length of time, it continues to exist or happen for that length of time.
gloss_zh: 持续，延续，维持（一段时间）

senses.concept_en: If something lasts for a particular length of time, it continues to be able to be used for that time, for example because there is some of it left or because it is in good enough condition.
gloss_zh: 够用，保持可用状态（一段时间）

senses.concept_en: You can use last in expressions such as last the game ,last the course, and last the week, to indicate that someone manages to take part in an event or situation right to the end, especially when this is very difficult for them.

lazy.translation:
a. 懒惰的, 怠惰的, 缓慢的
vi. 懒散

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is lazy, they do not want to work or make any effort to do anything.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use lazy to describe an activity or event in which you are very relaxed and which you do or take part in without making much effort.
gloss_zh: 令人精神松弛的；令人懒洋洋的

senses.concept_en: If you describe something as lazy, you mean that it moves or flows slowly and gently.

leader.translation:
n. 领导者, 社论, 指挥, 领袖, 领唱者, 前导字符
[计] 前导字符

senses.concept_en: The leader of a group of people or an organization is the person who is in control of it or in charge of it.
The leader at a particular point in a race or competition is the person who is winning at that point.
gloss_zh: （比赛或竞赛中的）领先者，占先者

senses.concept_en: The leader among a range of products or companies is the one that is most successful.
gloss_zh: （产品或公司中的）首屈一指者，佼佼者

senses.concept_en: The leader of an orchestra is the most senior violin player, who acts as a deputy to the conductor.
The leader of an orchestra is the conductor.
A leader in a newspaper is a piece of writing which gives the editor's opinion on an important news item.
A leader in a newspaper is the most important story in it.

letter.translation:
n. 信, 字母, 证书, 字面意义, 铅字, 学问, 出租人
vt. 写字母于, 在...上刻字母, 用字母标明
vi. 写印刷体字
[计] 字母

senses.concept_en: If you write a letter to someone, you write a message on paper and send it to them, usually by post.
Letters are written symbols which represent one of the sounds in a language.

If a student earns a letter in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.
gloss_zh: （校队队衣的）校名首字母标志（以嘉许优秀运动员）

senses.concept_en: If a student letters in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.
gloss_zh: 赢得佩戴校名首字母标志的荣誉

level.translation:
n. 水平, 水准, 平地
a. 同高的, 平坦的, 齐平的, 水平的
vt. 弄平, 夷平, 使同等, 瞄准, 对准
vi. 变平, 拉平
[计] 级别
level.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: A level is a point on a scale, for example a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.
See also:sea level; The level of a river, lake, or ocean or the level of liquid in a container is the height of its surface.
In cookery, a level spoonful of a substance such as flour or sugar is an amount that fills the spoon exactly, without going above the top edge.
If something is at a particular level, it is at that height.
If one thing is level with another thing, it is at the same height as it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When something is level, it is completely flat with no part higher than any other.
If you draw level with someone or something, you get closer to them until you are by their side.
If you draw level with someone, you manage to improve your performance until it is the same as theirs, by scoring the same number of points or goals as them.
In sport, if a player or team levels the score, they score a goal or win some points so that their team has the same number of points or goals as the opposing team.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you keep your voice level, you speak in a deliberately calm and unemotional way.
gloss_zh: （语气）平稳的，平静的，不动声色的

senses.concept_en: If someone or something such as a violent storm levels a building or area of land, they destroy it completely or make it completely flat.
If an accusation or criticism is levelled at someone, they are accused of doing wrong or they are criticized for something they have done.
gloss_zh: 使（指责、批评等）针对；使矛头指向

senses.concept_en: If you level an object at someone or something, you lift it and point it in their direction.
If you level with someone, you tell them the truth and do not keep anything secret.

limit.translation:
n. 界限, 边界, 限度, 极限, 限制
vt. 限制, 限定

senses.concept_en: A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.
A limit of a particular kind is the largest or smallest amount of something such as time or money that is allowed because of a rule, law, or decision.
The limit of an area is its boundary or edge.
The limits of a situation are the facts involved in it which make only some actions or results possible.
If you limit something, you prevent it from becoming greater than a particular amount or degree.
If you limit yourself to something, or if someone or something limits you, the number of things that you have or do is reduced.
If something is limited to a particular place or group of people, it exists only in that place, or is had or done only by that group.

list.translation:
n. 目录, 名单, 明细表, 布条, 条纹, 列表, 序列, 数据清单
vt. 列出, 列于表上, 记入名单内, 装布条
vi. 列于表上
[计] 列表, 序列, 数据清单
list.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts gre

senses.concept_en: See also:Civil List;hit list;honours list;laundry list;mailing list;shopping list;waiting list; A list of things such as names or addresses is a set of them which all belong to a particular category, written down one below the other.
A list of things is a set of them that you think of as being in a particular order.
To list several things such as reasons or names means to write or say them one after another, usually in a particular order.
To list something in a particular way means to include it in that way in a list or report.
gloss_zh: （以特定方式）把…列入单子（或报告）；登录

senses.concept_en: If a company is listed, or if it lists, on a stock exchange, it obtains an official quotation for its shares so that people can buy and sell them.
gloss_zh: （使）上市；把（证券）列入上市证券表

senses.concept_en: In sailing, if something, especially a ship, lists, it leans over to one side.

living.translation:
n. 生活, 生计, 生存
a. 活的, 逼真的, 现存的

senses.concept_en: The work that you do for a living is the work that you do in order to earn the money that you need.
You use living when you are talking about the quality of people's daily lives.
gloss_zh: 生活质量；生活素质；生活（方式）

senses.concept_en: You use living to talk about the places where people relax when they are not working.
The living are people who are alive, rather than people who have died.

local.translation:
a. 地方性的, 当地的, 局部的, 乡土的, 本地的
n. 当地居民, 本地新闻, 局部
[计] 本地的; 局部

senses.concept_en: Local means existing in or belonging to the area where you live, or to the area that you are talking about.
gloss_zh: 本地的；本地的；地方性的

senses.concept_en: Local government is elected by people in one area of a country and controls aspects such as education, housing, and transport within that area.
Your local is a pub which is near where you live and where you often go for a drink.
gloss_zh: （常去的）邻近小酒馆，本地酒吧

senses.concept_en: A local anaesthetic or condition affects only a small area of your body.

long.translation:
a. 长的, 长久的, 冗长的, 做多头的
vi. 渴望, 热望, 极想
adv. 长久, 始终
n. 长时间, 长信号, 长整型
[计] 长, 长整型

senses.concept_en: Long means a great amount of time or for a great amount of time.
gloss_zh: 长时间的；长久的；长期的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A long event or period of time lasts for a great amount of time or takes a great amount of time.
gloss_zh: （事件或时期）持续时间长的，花长时间的

senses.concept_en: You use long to ask or talk about amounts of time.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A long speech, book, film, or list contains a lot of information or a lot of items and takes a lot of time to listen to, read, watch, or deal with.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a period of time or work as long, you mean it lasts for more hours or days than is usual, or seems to last for more time than it actually does.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has a long memory, they are able to remember things that happened far back in the past.
Long is used in expressions such as all year long ,the whole day long, and your whole life long to say and emphasize that something happens for the whole of a particular period of time.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is long measures a great distance from one end to the other.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A long distance is a great distance. A long journey or route covers a great distance.
A long piece of clothing covers the whole of someone's legs or more of their legs than usual. Clothes with long sleeves cover the whole of someone's arms.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use long to talk or ask about the distance something measures from one end to the other.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a distance as long, you mean it seems to be greater than it actually is.
See also:longing; If you long for something, you want it very much.

loss.translation:
n. 损失, 遗失, 失败, 输, 错过, 伤亡
[化] 损失; 损耗

senses.concept_en: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than before.
Loss of life occurs when people die.
The loss of a relative or friend is their death.
gloss_zh: （亲人或朋友的）丧故，亡故，逝世

senses.concept_en: If a business makes a loss, it earns less than it spends.
Loss is the feeling of sadness you experience when someone or something you like is taken away from you.
A loss is the disadvantage you suffer when a valuable and useful person or thing leaves or is taken away.
The loss of something such as heat, blood, or fluid is the gradual reduction of it or of its level in a system or in someone's body.
gloss_zh: （热量、血液、液体等的）流失，散失，减少

loud.translation:
a. 大声的, 不断的, 喧吵的
adv. 高声地, 大声地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a noise is loud, the level of sound is very high and it can be easily heard. Someone or something that is loud produces a lot of noise.
gloss_zh: （声音）响亮的；（声源）发出响亮声音的；吵闹的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is loud in their support for or criticism of something, they express their opinion very often and in a very strong way.
gloss_zh: （对某事的支持或批评）强烈的，激烈的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something, especially a piece of clothing, as loud, you dislike it because it has very bright colours or very large, bold patterns which look unpleasant.
gloss_zh: （尤指衣服）大红大绿的，花里胡哨的，俗艳的

machine.translation:
n. 机器, 机械装置, 机构, 自动售货机, 机械般工作的人
vt. 以机器制造

senses.concept_en: A machine is a piece of equipment which uses electricity or an engine in order to do a particular kind of work.
If you machine something, you make it or work on it using a machine.
gloss_zh: 用机器制造;用机器加工

senses.concept_en: You can use machine to refer to a large and well-controlled system or organization.
If you say that someone is a machine, you mean that they are so tired or bored that they do their work without thinking.
gloss_zh: （由于工作过于劳累或乏味）机械般工作的人，做工作不动脑筋的人

main.translation:
n. 主要部分, 干线, 体力, 力量, 主群组
a. 主要的, 重要的, 全力的
[计] 主群组
main.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: The main thing is the most important one of several similar things in a particular situation.
The mains are the pipes which supply gas or water to buildings, or which take sewage away from them.
gloss_zh: （室内煤气、自来水或污水的）总管道，主管道

senses.concept_en: The mains are the wires which supply electricity to buildings, or the place where the wires end inside the building.

make.translation:
vt. 制造, 安排, 创造, 构成, 使得, 产生, 造成, 整理, 布置, 引起, 到达, 进行
vi. 开始, 前进, 增大, 被制造, 被处理
n. 制造, 构造, 性情

senses.concept_en: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.
gloss_zh: （与大量名词连用，表示做动作、说某事等）做出，作出

senses.concept_en: You can use make with certain nouns to indicate that someone does something well or badly. For example, if you make a success of something, you do it successfully, and if you make a mess of something, you do it very badly.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词连用）把…做（好），把…搞（糟）

senses.concept_en: If you make as if to do something or make to do something, you behave in a way that makes it seem that you are just about to do it.
gloss_zh: 摆出…的姿态;做出…的样子

senses.concept_en: In cricket, if a player makes a particular number of runs, they score that number of runs. In baseball or American football, if a player makes a particular score, they achieve that score.
gloss_zh: （在板球、棒球、橄榄球比赛中）得（分）

senses.concept_en: If something makes you do something, it causes you to do it.
If you make someone do something, you force them to do it.

You use make to talk about causing someone or something to be a particular thing or to have a particular quality. For example, to make someone a star means to cause them to become a star, and to make someone angry means to cause them to become angry.
gloss_zh: 使成为（某种人或物）;使具有（某种特性）

senses.concept_en: If you say that one thing or person makes another seem, for example, small, stupid, or good, you mean that they cause them to seem small, stupid, or good in comparison, even though they are not.
If you make yourself understood, heard, or known, you succeed in getting people to understand you, hear you, or know that you are there.
gloss_zh: 使自己（被理解、听见、知晓等）

senses.concept_en: If you make someone something, you appoint them to a particular job, role, or position.
If you make something into something else, you change it in some way so that it becomes that other thing.
To make a total or score a particular amount means to increase it to that amount.
gloss_zh: 使（总数）升为;使（分数）达到

senses.concept_en: When someone makes a friend or an enemy, someone becomes their friend or their enemy, often because of a particular thing they have done.
To make something means to produce, construct, or create it.
If someone makes a film or television programme, they are involved in creating or producing it.
gloss_zh: 拍摄（电影）;制作（电视节目）

senses.concept_en: If you make a meal or a drink, you prepare it.
If you make a note or list, you write something down in that form.
If you make rules or laws, you decide what these should be.
If you make money, you get it by working for it, by selling something, or by winning it.
If something makes something else, it is responsible for the success of that thing.
gloss_zh: （某事物）使（其他事物）变得成功

senses.concept_en: The make of something such as a car or radio is the name of the company that made it

You can use make to say that someone or something has the right qualities for a particular task or role. For example, if you say that someone will make a good politician, you mean that they have the right qualities to be a good politician.
If people make a particular pattern such as a line or a circle, they arrange themselves in this way.
You can use make to say what two numbers add up to.
If someone makes a particular team or makes a particular high position, they do so well that they are put in that team or get that position.
gloss_zh: 成为…的一员;加入;谋得（高级职务）

senses.concept_en: If you make a place in or by a particular time, you get there in or by that time, often with some difficulty.
You use make it when saying what you calculate or guess an amount to be.
You use make it when saying what time your watch says it is.

man.translation:
n. 男人, 人类, 人
vt. 为...配备人手, 操纵, 使振奋
[计] 城域网, 手册

senses.concept_en: A man is an adult male human being.
Man and men are sometimes used to refer to all human beings, including both males and females. Some people dislike this use.
gloss_zh: 人，人类（此用法仍有争议）

senses.concept_en: If you say that a man is, for example, a gambling man or an outdoors man, you mean that he likes gambling or outdoor activities.
If you say that a man is, for example, a London man or an Oxford man, you mean that he comes from London or Oxford, or went to university there.
gloss_zh: （来自某地的）人；（在某地上过学的）人

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a particular company's or organiza-tion's man, you mean a man who works for or represents that company or organization.
gloss_zh: （某公司或组织的男性）职员，代表

senses.concept_en: If you say that a man is someone's man, you mean that he always supports that person or does what they want.
Some people refer to a woman's husband, lover, or boyfriend as her man .
In the armed forces, the men are soldiers, sailors, marines, or airmen of lower rank, as opposed to the officers.
Male workers are sometimes referred to as men, especially if they do physical work or work for a more senior person.
gloss_zh: （尤指从事体力劳动或为上级工作的）男工，男雇员，男下属

senses.concept_en: One man sometimes addresses another as 'man' when he is angry or impatient with him.
gloss_zh: （对男子的称呼，表示生气或不耐烦）老兄，老弟，小伙子

senses.concept_en: In very informal social situations, man is sometimes used as a greeting or form of address to a man.
gloss_zh: （在非正式场合中用以称呼男子）老弟,老兄

senses.concept_en: If you man something such as a place or machine, you operate it or are in charge of it.
gloss_zh: 在…岗位上工作;操作（机器等）

many.translation:
n. 多数, 多数人
a. 许多的
pron. 许多

senses.concept_en: You use many to indicate that you are talking about a large number of people or things.
You use many in expressions such as 'not many', 'not very many', and 'too many' when replying to questions about numbers of things or people.
You use many followed by 'a' and a noun to emphasize that there are a lot of people or things involved in something.
gloss_zh: （用于 a + 单数名词之前表示强调）许多，很多

senses.concept_en: You use many after 'how' to ask questions about numbers or quantities. You use many after 'how' in reported clauses to talk about numbers or quantities.
You use many with 'as' when you are comparing numbers of things or people.
gloss_zh: （用于比较物或人的数量，与 as 连用）

senses.concept_en: You use many to mean 'many people'.
The many means a large group of people, especially the ordinary people in society, considered as separate from a particular small group.

master.translation:
n. 主人, 硕士, 大师, 母机
a. 主人的, 主要的
vt. 征服, 控制, 精通
master.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: A servant's master is the man that he or she works for.
A dog's master is the man or boy who owns it.
See also:past master; If you say that someone is a master of a particular activity, you mean that they are extremely skilled at it.
If you are master of a situation, you have complete control over it.
If you master something, you learn how to do it properly or you succeed in understanding it completely.
If you master a difficult situation, you succeed in controlling it.
See also:headmaster;housemaster; A master is a male teacher.
See also:old master; A famous male painter of the past is often called a master .
A master copy of something such as a film or a tape recording is an original copy that can be used to produce other copies.
gloss_zh: （电影、录音等）原始拷贝的，母盘的，母带的

senses.concept_en: The master of a ship that carries passengers or goods is its captain.
A master's degree can be referred to as a master's .
Master is sometimes used by the followers of a male religious teacher or leader as a way of referring to him or addressing him.
gloss_zh: 长老（信徒对宗教法师或领袖的称呼）

senses.concept_en: In the past, Master was used before a boy's name as a polite way of referring to him or addressing him. Nowadays, Master can be written before a boy's name when addressing a letter to him.
gloss_zh: （旧时的）少爷，小主人;君（现在用于信件中对男孩的称谓）

mechanic.translation:
n. 机械工, 技工
a. 手工的

senses.concept_en: A mechanic is someone whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially car engines.
gloss_zh: （尤指修理汽车的）技工，机修工，修理工

senses.concept_en: The mechanics of a process, system, or activity are the way in which it works or the way in which it is done.
gloss_zh: （过程、系统、动作等）运作方式;（具体的）方法，技巧

senses.concept_en: Mechanics is the part of physics that deals with the natural forces that act on moving or stationary objects.

metal.translation:
n. 金属, 金属制品, 合金, 本质, 质料
a. 金属制的
vt. 以金属覆盖
metal.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: See also:base metal; Metal is a hard substance such as iron, steel, gold, or lead.

mid.translation:
a. 中间的, 中央的, 中部的
prep. 在...之中

midst.translation:
n. 中间
prep. 在...中间

modest.translation:
a. 谦逊的, 羞怯的, 端庄的, 适度的
[经] 适当的
modest.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A modest house or other building is not large or expensive.
gloss_zh: （房屋等）不太大的，不算昂贵的，普通的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use modest to describe something such as an amount, rate, or improvement which is fairly small.
gloss_zh: （数量、比率或改进程度）不太高的，适度的，适中的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe a woman as modest when she avoids doing or wearing anything that might cause men to have sexual feelings towards her. You can also describe her clothes or behaviour as modest .
gloss_zh: （女性或其衣着）端庄的，保守的;（行为）正派的，检点的

senses.concept_en: A month is one of the twelve periods of time that a year is divided into, for example January or February.
A month is a period of about four weeks.

morning.translation: n. 早晨, 早上, 初期

senses.concept_en: The morning is the part of each day between the time that people usually wake up and 12 o'clock noon or lunchtime.
gloss_zh: 早晨;上午（从人们通常醒来到中午或午餐前的一段时间）

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a particular time in the morning, you mean a time between 12 o'clock midnight and 12 o'clock noon.
gloss_zh: 凌晨，早晨，上午（从子夜到中午的这段时间）

mount.translation:
n. 乘骑用马, 框, 衬纸, 山
vi. 乘马, 爬上, 增长
vt. 爬上, 使上马, 装上, 装裱, 安放, 制作...的标本, 设置, 上演
[计] 安装

senses.concept_en: If you mount a campaign or event, you organize it and make it take place.
If something mounts, it increases in intensity.
If something mounts, it increases in quantity.
If you mount the stairs or a platform, you go up the stairs or go up onto the platform.
If you mount a horse or cycle, you climb on to it so that you can ride it.
A mount is a horse.
If you mount an object on something, you fix it there firmly.
If you mount an exhibition or display, you organize and present it.
Mount is used as part of the name of a mountain.

must.translation:
n. 必须, 未发酵葡萄汁, 绝对必要的事物
aux. 必须

senses.concept_en: You use must to indicate that you think it is very important or necessary for something to happen. You use must not or mustn't to indicate that you think it is very important or necessary for something not to happen.
You use must to indicate that it is necessary for something to happen, usually because of a rule or law.
gloss_zh: （通常因为规定或法律）必须，应当

senses.concept_en: You use must to indicate that you are fairly sure that something is the case.
gloss_zh: （用于表示肯定推测）一定，谅必

senses.concept_en: You use must, or must have with a past participle, to indicate that you believe that something is the case, because of the available evidence.
gloss_zh: （用于表示据已知情况推测）很可能是，想必是，肯定是

senses.concept_en: If you say that one thing must have happened in order for something else to happen, you mean that it is necessary for the first thing to have happened before the second thing can happen.
gloss_zh: （用于表示前者为后者的前提）应该已经（发生）

senses.concept_en: You use must to express your intention to do something.
gloss_zh: （用于表示意图）一定要，坚持要

senses.concept_en: You use must to make suggestions or invitations very forcefully.
gloss_zh: （用于表示建议或邀请）务必，一定要

senses.concept_en: You use must in remarks and comments where you are expressing sympathy.
You use must in conversation in expressions such as 'I must say' and 'I must admit' in order to emphasize a point that you are making.
You use must in expressions such as 'it must be noted' and 'it must be remembered' in order to draw the reader's or listener's attention to what you are about to say.
gloss_zh: （用于引起读者或听众的注意）一定要注意/一定记住

senses.concept_en: You use must in questions to express your anger or irritation about something that someone has done, usually because you do not understand their behaviour.
gloss_zh: （用于问句中表示生气）偏偏，非要

senses.concept_en: You use must in exclamations to express surprise or shock.
gloss_zh: （用于感叹句，表示惊讶或震惊）一定是，准是

senses.concept_en: If you refer to something as a must, you mean that it is absolutely necessary.
gloss_zh: 必不可少的事物;一定要做的事

nearby.translation:
a. 附近的, 近旁的
adv. 在附近, 近旁地
prep. 在...附近

senses.concept_en: If something is nearby, it is only a short distance away.

need.translation:
n. 需要, 必须, 缺乏
vt. 需要, 必需
vi. 贫困, 有必要
aux. 需要

senses.concept_en: If you need something, or need to do something, you cannot successfully achieve what you want or live properly without it.
gloss_zh: （为做成某事或正常生活）要求有，必须有，需要

senses.concept_en: If an object or place needs something doing to it, that action should be done to improve the object or place. If a task needs doing, it should be done to improve a particular situation.
gloss_zh: （表示某一做法对某事物或地方有益）应该，应当，需要

senses.concept_en: If there is a need for something, that thing would improve a situation or something cannot happen without it.
If you say that someone needn't do something, you are telling them not to do it, or advising or suggesting that they should not do it.
gloss_zh: 不必，没有必要（用于告知或建议）

senses.concept_en: If you tell someone that they needn't do something, or that something needn't happen, you are telling them that that thing is not necessary, in order to make them feel better.
gloss_zh: （与否定词连用）不必，没有必要

senses.concept_en: You use needn't when you are giving someone permission not to do something.
gloss_zh: （与否定词连用）准许不做，可以不做

senses.concept_en: If something need not be true, it is not necessarily true or not always true.
If someone needn't have done something, it was not necessary or useful for them to do it, although they did it.
gloss_zh: （与否定词连用）本来不必，本来不需要

senses.concept_en: You use need in expressions such as I need hardly say and I needn't add to emphasize that the person you are talking to already knows what you are going to say.
gloss_zh: （与否定词连用）无需说，不必说

senses.concept_en: You can use need in expressions such as 'Need I say more' and 'Need I go on' when you want to avoid stating an obvious consequence of something you have just said.
gloss_zh: 还需要再说吗;还要我继续说吗

never.translation:
adv. 从不, 决不, 不曾
[法] 永不, 决不, 从来没有

senses.concept_en: Never means at no time in the past or at no time in the future.
Never means 'not in any circumstances at all'.
Never is used to refer to the past and means 'not'.
You say 'never!' to indicate how surprised or shocked you are by something that someone has just said.
You say 'Well, I never' to indicate that you are very surprised about something that you have just seen or found out.
gloss_zh: （表示惊讶）我真没看到（或发现、想到）过

new.translation:
a. 新的, 陌生的, 最近的, 不熟悉的
[法] 新发现的, 新的, 重新开始的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is new has been recently created, built, or invented or is in the process of being created, built, or invented.
gloss_zh: 新的;刚出现的;新做的;新建的

senses.concept_en: Something that is new has not been used or owned by anyone.
You use new to describe something which has replaced another thing, for example because you no longer have the old one, or it no longer exists, or it is no longer useful.
New is used to describe something that has only recently been discovered or noticed.
A new day or year is the beginning of the next day or year.
gloss_zh: （一天或一年）新开始的，初始的

senses.concept_en: New is used to describe someone or something that has recently acquired a particular status or position.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are new to a situation or place, or if the situation or place is new to you, you have not previously seen it or had any experience of it.
New potatoes, carrots, or peas are produced early in the season for such vegetables and are usually small with a sweet flavour.
gloss_zh: （土豆、胡萝卜、豆子等）时鲜的，早的

noise.translation:
n. 噪音, 杂音, 响声, 喧闹
vt. 谣传
vi. 喧闹
[计] 噪声

senses.concept_en: Noise is a loud or unpleasant sound.
A noise is a sound that someone or something makes.
If someone makes noises of a particular kind about something, they say things that indicate their attitude to it in a rather indirect or vague way.

northern.translation:
n. 北方人
a. 北方的, 向北的, 自北方来的

senses.concept_en: Northern means in or from the north of a region, state, or country.
gloss_zh: 北的;（在）北部的;来自北部的

not.translation:
adv. 不, 非, 未
[计] 非

senses.concept_en: You use not with verbs to form negative statements.
gloss_zh: （与动词连用构成否定句）不，非，没有

senses.concept_en: You use not to form questions to which you expect the answer 'yes'.
gloss_zh: （构成期望得到肯定回答的疑问句）

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in questions which imply that someone should have done something, or to express surprise that something is not the case.
gloss_zh: （通常以 n't 的形式出现在问句中，用于推断某人应已做某事或表示惊讶）

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in question tags after a positive statement.
gloss_zh: （通常用 n't 的形式，用于肯定陈述后的附加疑问句）是吗? 不是吗?

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in polite suggestions.
gloss_zh: （通常以 n't 的形式，表示礼貌的建议）

senses.concept_en: You use not to represent the negative of a word, group, or clause that has just been used.
gloss_zh: （用于表示对刚提及的单词、词组或从句的否定）不，没有

senses.concept_en: You can use not in front of 'all' or 'every' when you want to say something that applies only to some members of the group that you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于 all 或 every 前，表示部分否定）并非，不是

senses.concept_en: If something is not always the case, you mean that sometimes it is the case and sometimes it is not.
You can use not or not even in front of 'a' or 'one' to emphasize that there is none at all of what is being mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于 a 或 one 前加强语气）（一个…）也不，（一个…）也没有

senses.concept_en: You can use not in front of a word referring to a distance, length of time, or other amount to say that the actual distance, time, or amount is less than the one mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于表示距离、时间或其他数量的词前）不到，少于

senses.concept_en: You use not when you are contrasting something that is true with something that is untrue. You use this especially to indicate that people might think that the untrue statement is true.
gloss_zh: （用于对比真实和不真实的情况，尤用于可能使人产生误解的陈述）不是

senses.concept_en: You use not in expressions such as 'not only', 'not just', and 'not simply' to emphasize that something is true, but it is not the whole truth.
gloss_zh: （用于not only，not just, not simply 等短语中，强调某事物的真实性，但不是全部事实）

senses.concept_en: You use of to combine two nouns when the first noun identifies the feature of the second noun that you want to talk about.
gloss_zh: （用于连接两个名词，其中前者表示后者的特定方面）

senses.concept_en: You use of to combine two nouns, or a noun and a present participle, when the second noun or present participle defines or gives more information about the first noun.
gloss_zh: （用于连接两个名词或名词与现在分词，其中后者对前者进行界定或补充信息）

senses.concept_en: You use of after nouns referring to actions to specify the person or thing that is affected by the action or that performs the action. For example, 'the kidnapping of the child' refers to an action affecting a child; 'the arrival of the next train' refers to an action performed by a train.
gloss_zh: （用于指称动作的名词后说明该动作的对象或主体）

senses.concept_en: You use of after words and phrases referring to quantities or groups of things to indicate the substance or thing that is being measured.
gloss_zh: （用于指称数量或组群的词和短语后表示计量的对象）
