senses.concept_en: You use of after the name of someone or something to introduce the institution or place they belong to or are connected with.
gloss_zh: （用于人或事物的名称后引出其所属或相关的机构或地方）

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun referring to a container to form an expression referring to the container and its contents.
gloss_zh: （用于指称容器的名词后，说明容器及其所含物）

senses.concept_en: You use of after a count noun and before an uncount noun when you want to talk about an individual piece or item.
gloss_zh: （用在可数名词后、不可数名词前表示某一单个物品）

senses.concept_en: You use of to indicate the materials or things that form something.
gloss_zh: （表示材料或成分）由…制成（或组成）的

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun which specifies a particular part of something, to introduce the thing that it is a part of.
gloss_zh: （用于名词后表示其为某事物的一部分）

senses.concept_en: You use of after some verbs to indicate someone or something else involved in the action.
gloss_zh: （用于某些动词后表示动作所涉及的人或事物）关于，由于

senses.concept_en: You use of after some adjectives to indicate the thing that a feeling or quality relates to.
gloss_zh: （用于某些形容词后表示与情感或特性相关的事物）对，为

senses.concept_en: You use of before a word referring to the person who performed an action when saying what you think about the action.
gloss_zh: （用于指称施动者的单词前说明对该动作的看法）出自…，在…一方

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun which describes someone or something, to introduce the person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于描述名词后引出所指的人或事物）

senses.concept_en: If something is more of or less of a particular thing, it is that thing to a greater or smaller degree.
gloss_zh: （表示程度）更大/较小程度上的…

senses.concept_en: You use of to indicate a characteristic or quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （表示某人或某事物具有的特点或特性）

senses.concept_en: You use of after the verb 'be' to indicate a characteristic or quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （用于be动词后表示某人或某事物具有的特点或特性）

senses.concept_en: You use of to specify an amount, value, or age.
You use of after a noun such as 'month' or 'year' to indicate the length of time that some state or activity continues.
gloss_zh: （用于年、月等名词后表示状态或活动的持续时间）

senses.concept_en: You can use of to say what time it is by indicating how many minutes there are before the hour mentioned.
gloss_zh: （表示时间离某一钟点差几分）在…之前

office.translation:
n. 办公室, 部, 公职, 职责
[化] 办公室

senses.concept_en: An office is a room or a part of a building where people work sitting at desks.
An office is a department of an organization, especially the government, where people deal with a particular kind of administrative work.
An office is a small building or room where people can go for information, tickets, or a service of some kind.
gloss_zh: （问询、购票或提供服务的）处，所

senses.concept_en: A doctor's or dentist's office is a place where a doctor or dentist sees their patients.
If someone holds office in a government, they have an important job or position of authority.
If something often happens, it happens many times or much of the time.
You use how often to ask questions about frequency. You also use often in reported clauses and other statements to give information about the frequency of something.
gloss_zh: （用于询问或说明某事发生的频率）（多）常

old.translation:
n. 以前, 往昔
a. 老的, 旧的, 古老的, 年长的, 老练的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.
gloss_zh: 年老的；年纪大的；不年轻的

senses.concept_en: You use old to talk about how many days, weeks, months, or years someone or something has lived or existed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is old has existed for a long time.
gloss_zh: 古老的；长久的；历史悠久的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is old is no longer in good condition because of its age or because it has been used a lot.
You use old to refer to something that is no longer used, that no longer exists, or that has been replaced by something else.
gloss_zh: 旧时的；过去的；从前的；过时的

senses.concept_en: You use old to refer to something that used to belong to you, or to a person or thing that used to have a particular role in your life.
gloss_zh: 原来（属于自己）的；原先（生活中）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An old friend, enemy, or rival is someone who has been your friend, enemy, or rival for a long time.
gloss_zh: （朋友）相识已久的；（敌人）结有宿怨的；（对手）长期竞争的

senses.concept_en: You can use old to express affection when talking to or about someone you know.

one.translation:
n. 一(个)
pron. 一, 任何人
num. 一, 一个
a. 一致的, 完整的

senses.concept_en: One is the number 1.
If you say that someone or something is the one person or thing of a particular kind, you are emphasizing that they are the only person or thing of that kind.
One can be used instead of 'a' to emphasize the following noun.
gloss_zh: （用于代替a以强调之后的名词）

senses.concept_en: You can use one instead of 'a' to emphasize the following adjective or expression.
gloss_zh: （用于代替a以强调之后的形容词或短语）

senses.concept_en: You can use one in front of someone's name to indicate that you have not met them or heard of them before.
gloss_zh: （用于人名前，表示未曾相识或听闻的）某一个

senses.concept_en: You can use one to refer to the first of two or more things that you are comparing.
gloss_zh: （表示与其他的作比较）这一个

senses.concept_en: You can use one or ones instead of a noun when it is clear what type of thing or person you are referring to and you are describing them or giving more information about them.
gloss_zh: （用于代替名词，指代某类明确的人或事物）

senses.concept_en: You use ones to refer to people in general.
You can use one instead of a noun group when you have just mentioned something and you want to describe it or give more information about it.
gloss_zh: （用于代替名词词组，表示刚提到过的事物）

senses.concept_en: You can use one when you have been talking or writing about a group of people or things and you want to say something about a particular member of the group.
gloss_zh: （特指一群人或事物中的）一人，一个

senses.concept_en: You use one in expressions such as 'one of the biggest airports' or 'one of the most experienced players' to indicate that something or someone is bigger or more experienced than most other things or people of the same kind.
collocations: one of the most experienced players

senses.concept_en: You can use one when referring to a time in the past or in the future. For example, if you say that you did something one day, you mean that you did it on a day in the past. one day
You can use one to refer to a question, joke, remark, or subject of discussion.
gloss_zh: （指代问题、笑话、评论、讨论的主题等）一个

senses.concept_en: You can use one to refer to an alcoholic drink.
You use one to make statements about people in general which also apply to themselves. One can be used as the subject or object of a sentence.
gloss_zh: （泛指包括自己的人，可作句子的主语或宾语）一个人，任何人

open.translation:
n. 公开, 户外, 空旷
a. 开着的, 开放的, 开阔的, 营业着的, 公开的, 悬而未决的
vt. 打开, 公开, 开放
vi. 展开, 开始, 展现
[计] 打开指令; 打开语句

senses.concept_en: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.
If you open something such as a bottle, box, parcel, or envelope, you move, remove, or cut part of it so you can take out what is inside.
gloss_zh: 将（瓶、盒等）开封；拆开（包裹、信封等）

senses.concept_en: If you open something such as a book, an umbrella, or your hand, or if it opens, the different parts of it move away from each other so that the inside of it can be seen.
If you open a computer file, you give the computer an instruction to display it on the screen.
When you open your eyes or your eyes open, you move your eyelids upwards, for example when you wake up, so that you can see.
If you open your arms, you stretch them wide apart in front of you, usually in order to put them round someone.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you stand or sit in an open way, the front of your body is fully exposed and you are not bending forward or at an angle to someone.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person or their character as open, you mean they are honest and do not want or try to hide anything or to deceive anyone.
gloss_zh: 坦率的；诚恳的；不作伪的

senses.concept_en: If you describe a situation, attitude, or way of behaving as open, you mean it is not kept hidden or secret.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are open to suggestions or ideas, you are ready and willing to consider or accept them.
gloss_zh: 愿意接受（建议、观点等）的；虚怀若谷的

senses.concept_en: If you say that a system, person, or idea is open to something such as abuse or criticism, you mean they might receive abuse or criticism because of their qualities, effects, or actions.
gloss_zh: 容易招致（滥用、批评等）的；易受（攻击）的

senses.concept_en: If you say that a fact or question is open to debate, interpretation, or discussion, you mean that people are uncertain whether it is true, what it means, or what the answer is.
gloss_zh: 悬而未决的；尚未决定的

senses.concept_en: If people open something such as a blocked road or a border, or if it opens, people can then pass along it or through it.
gloss_zh: 开放（被封的道路、边界等）；开通

senses.concept_en: If a place opens into another, larger place, you can move from one directly into the other.
An open area is a large area that does not have many buildings or trees in it.
An open structure or object is not covered or enclosed.
gloss_zh: 敞开的；无遮盖的；无围挡的

senses.concept_en: An open wound is one from which a liquid such as blood is coming.
If you open your shirt or coat, you undo the buttons or pull down the zip.
gloss_zh: 把（衣服）解开；把…的拉链拉开

senses.concept_en: When a shop, office, or public building opens or is opened, its doors are unlocked and the public can go in.
When a public building, factory, or company opens or when someone opens it, it starts operating for the first time.
gloss_zh: 为（大楼、工厂、公司等）举行揭幕典礼；开设；开办；开张

senses.concept_en: If something such as a meeting or series of talks opens, or if someone opens it, it begins.

If an event such as a meeting or discussion opens with a particular activity or if a particular activity opens an event, that activity is the first thing that happens or is dealt with. You can also say that someone such as a speaker or singer opens by doing a particular thing.
On the stock exchange, the price at which currencies, shares, or commodities open is their value at the start of that day's trading.
When a film, play, or other public event opens, it begins to be shown, be performed, or take place for a limited period of time.
If you open an account with a bank or a commercial organization, you begin to use their services.
If an opportunity or choice is open to you, you are able to do a particular thing if you choose to.
gloss_zh: （机会、选择等）可利用的，可得到的

senses.concept_en: To open opportunities or possibilities means the same as to open them up.
gloss_zh: （使）（机会、可能性等）出现;（使）产生

senses.concept_en: You can use open to describe something that anyone is allowed to take part in or accept.
gloss_zh: 人人可以参加（或接受）的；开放的

senses.concept_en: See also:opening; If something such as an offer or job is open, it is available for someone to accept or apply for.
gloss_zh: （提议等）有效的；（职位等）空缺的，可申请的

or.translation:
conj. 或, 或者
[计] 或

senses.concept_en: You use or to link two or more alternatives.
gloss_zh: （连接两个或两个以上选择的可能性）或，或者，还是

senses.concept_en: You use or to give another alternative, when the first alternative is introduced by 'either' or 'whether'.
gloss_zh: （与 either 或 whether 连用，给出另一个选择项）或，还是，就是

senses.concept_en: You use or between two numbers to indicate that you are giving an approximate amount.
gloss_zh: （用于两个数字之间表示概数）或，大约

senses.concept_en: You use or to introduce a comment which corrects or modifies what you have just said.
gloss_zh: （用于对刚说过的话进行更正或补充）或者说

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone should do something or something unpleasant will happen, you are warning them that if they do not do it, the unpleasant thing will happen.
You use or to introduce something which is evidence for the truth of a statement you have just made.
gloss_zh: （用于证明刚刚所作陈述的真实性）否则，要不然

outside.translation:
n. 外面, 外表, 外界
a. 外面的, 外表的, 外界的
adv. 外面, 外表, 外界

senses.concept_en: The outside of something is the part which surrounds or encloses the rest of it.
If you are outside, you are not inside a building but are quite close to it.
gloss_zh: 在外面；在室外；在建筑物近旁

senses.concept_en: If you are outside a room, you are not in it but are in the passage or area next to it.
When you talk about the outside world, you are referring to things that happen or exist in places other than your own home or community.
People or things outside a country, town, or region are not in it.
On a road with two separate carriageways, the outside lanes are the ones which are closest to its centre.
gloss_zh: （车道）靠近路中间的，快车道的

senses.concept_en: Outside people or organizations are not part of a particular organization or group.
Outside a particular institution or field of activity means in other fields of activity or in general life.
Something that is outside a particular range of things is not included within it.
Something that happens outside a particular period of time happens at a different time from the one mentioned.

over.translation:
adv. 结束, 越过, 从头到尾
prep. 在...之上, 遍于...之上, 越过
a. 上面的
vt. 越过

senses.concept_en: If one thing is over another thing or is moving over it, the first thing is directly above the second, either resting on it, or with a space between them.
gloss_zh: 在…的上方；在…的上面；在…的上空

senses.concept_en: If one thing is over another thing, it is supported by it and its ends are hanging down on each side of it.
If one thing is over another thing, it covers part or all of it.
gloss_zh: （部分或完全地）覆盖在…的上面

senses.concept_en: If you lean over an object, you bend your body so that the top part of it is above the object.
If you look over or talk over an object, you look or talk across the top of it.
gloss_zh: 从…上面（看过去）；隔着…（交谈）

senses.concept_en: If a window has a view over an area of land or water, you can see the land or water through the window.
If someone or something goes over a barrier, obstacle, or boundary, they get to the other side of it by going across it, or across the top of it.
If someone or something moves over an area or surface, they move across it, from one side to the other.
If something is on the opposite side of a road or river, you can say that it is over the road or river.
If you go over to a place, you go to that place.
You can use over to indicate a particular position or place a short distance away from someone or something.
You use over to say that someone or something falls towards or onto the ground, often suddenly or violently.
If something rolls over or is turned over, its position changes so that the part that was facing upwards is now facing downwards
If something is over a particular amount, measurement, or age, it is more than that amount, measurement, or age.
If you say that you have some food or money over, you mean that it remains after you have used all that you need.
If you do something over, you do it again or start doing it again from the beginning.
If an activity is over or all over, it is completely finished.
If you are over an illness or an experience, it has finished and you have recovered from its effects.
gloss_zh: 从（某一疾病或经历）中恢复过来

senses.concept_en: If you have control or influence over someone or something, you are able to control them or influence them.
You use over to indicate what a disagreement or feeling relates to or is caused by.
If something happens over a particular period of time or over something such as a meal, it happens during that time or during the meal.
You use over to indicate that you give or receive information using a telephone, radio, or other piece of electrical equipment.
When people such as the police or the army are using a radio to communicate, they say 'Over' to indicate that they have finished speaking and are waiting for a reply.
gloss_zh: （无线电通讯用语）完毕，请回答

senses.concept_en: In cricket, an over consists of six correctly bowled balls.
gloss_zh: （板球运动中）一轮6个（未让对方得分的）有效投球

overcome.translation:
vt. 战胜, 克服, 胜过
vi. 得胜
overcome.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.
If you are overcome by a feeling or event, it is so strong or has such a strong effect that you cannot think clearly.
gloss_zh: （感情上）受到极大影响，承受不起

senses.concept_en: If you are overcome by smoke or a poisonous gas, you become very ill or die from breathing it in.

derivation.breakdown_zh: come 来 + over- 越过：战胜

part.translation:
n. 部分, 局部, 零件, 要素, 等分, 职责, 角色, 部位
vt. 分开, 分离, 断绝, 区别, 分配
vi. 分开, 断裂, 分手
a. 部分的, 局部的
adv. 部分地, 有些

senses.concept_en: A part of something is one of the pieces, sections, or elements that it consists of.
A part for a machine or vehicle is one of the smaller pieces that is used to make it.
Part of something is some of it.
If you say that something is part one thing, part another, you mean that it is to some extent the first thing and to some extent the second thing.

You can use part when you are talking about the proportions of substances in a mixture. For example, if you are told to use five parts water to one part paint, the mixture should contain five times as much water as paint.
A part in a play or film is one of the roles in it which an actor or actress can perform.
Your part in something that happens is your involvement in it.
If something or someone is part of a group or organization, they belong to it or are included in it.
The part in someone's hair is the line running from the front to the back of their head where their hair lies in different directions.
If things that are next to each other part or if you part them, they move in opposite directions, so that there is a space between them.
If you part your hair in the middle or at one side, you make it lie in two different directions so that there is a straight line running from the front of your head to the back.
When two people part, or if one person parts from another, they leave each other.
If you are parted from someone you love, you are prevented from being with them.

pass.translation:
n. 经过, 要隘, 途径, 通行, 护照, 及格
vt. 经过, 越过, 通过, 批准, 度过, 传递, 忽略
vi. 经过, 变化, 流通, 及格, 宣判, 终止, 消逝, 被忽略, 不叫牌, 传递
[计] 遍

senses.concept_en: To pass someone or something means to go past them without stopping.
When someone or something passes in a particular direction, they move in that direction.
If something such as a road or pipe passes along a particular route, it goes along that route.
If you pass something through, over, or round something else, you move or push it through, over, or round that thing.
If you pass something to someone, you take it in your hand and give it to them.
If something passes or is passed from one person to another, the second person then has it instead of the first.
If you pass information to someone, you give it to them because it concerns them.
If you pass the ball to someone in your team in a game such as football, basketball, hockey, or rugby, you kick, hit, or throw it to them.
When a period of time passes, it happens and finishes.
If you pass a period of time in a particular way, you spend it in that way.
If you pass through a stage of development or a period of time, you experience it.
If an amount passes a particular total or level, it becomes greater than that total or level.
If someone or something passes a test, they are considered to be of an acceptable standard.
A pass in an examination, test, or course is a successful result in it.
If someone in authority passes a person or thing, they declare that they are of an acceptable standard or have reached an acceptable standard.
When people in authority pass a new law or a proposal, they formally agree to it or approve it.
When a judge passes sentence on someone, he or she says what their punishment will be.
If you pass comment or pass a comment, you say something.
If something passes without comment, or passes unnoticed, nobody comments on it, reacts to it, or notices it.
If someone or something passes for or passes as something that they are not, they are accepted as that thing or mistaken for that thing.
If someone makes you an offer or asks you a question and you say that you will pass on it, you mean that you do not want to accept or answer it now.
If someone passes water or passes urine, they urinate.
A pass is a document that allows you to do something.
A pass is a narrow path or route between mountains.
If someone makes a pass at you, they try to begin a romantic or sexual relationship with you.

past.translation:
n. 过去, 昔时, 往事, 早年经历, 过去时
a. 过去的, 结束的, 卸任的, 过去时的
prep. 越过, 晚于, 超越, 超出...的可能性(能力、范围等)
pass的过去分词

senses.concept_en: The past is the time before the present, and the things that have happened.
Your past consists of all the things that you have done or that have happened to you.
Past events and things happened or existed before the present time.
You use past to talk about a period of time that has just finished. For example, if you talk about the past five years, you mean the period of five years that has just finished.
If a situation is past, it has ended and no longer exists.

See also:past perfect; In grammar, the past tenses of a verb are the ones used to talk about things that happened at some time before the present. The simple past tense uses the past form of a verb, which for regular verbs ends in '-ed', as in 'They walked back to the car'.
You use past when you are stating a time which is thirty minutes or less after a particular hour. For example, if it is twenty past six, it is twenty minutes after six o'clock.
If it is past a particular time, it is later than that time.
If you go past someone or something, you go near them and keep moving, so that they are then behind you.
If you look or point past a person or thing, you look or point at something behind them.
If something is past a place, it is on the other side of it.
If someone or something is past a particular point or stage, they are no longer at that point or stage.
gloss_zh: 超过，超出（某一点或阶段）

senses.concept_en: If you are past doing something, you are no longer able to do it. For example, if you are past caring, you do not care about something any more because so many bad things have happened to you.

pipe.translation:
n. 管, 导管, 输送管, 管状器官, 声带, 尖细的声音, 烟斗, 笛, 管乐器
vt. 以管输送, 吹哨子, 吹奏, 尖声唱
vi. 吹笛, 尖叫, 吹长哨发令
[计] 管道

senses.concept_en: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.
gloss_zh: （通常指金属或塑料制的）管子，管道

senses.concept_en: A pipe is an object which is used for smoking tobacco. You put the tobacco into the cup-shaped part at the end of the pipe, light it, and breathe in the smoke through a narrow tube.
A pipe is a simple musical instrument in the shape of a tube with holes in it. You play a pipe by blowing into it while covering and uncovering the holes with your fingers.
Pipes are the same as bagpipes .
An organ pipe is one of the long hollow tubes in which air vibrates and produces a musical note.
If liquid or gas is piped somewhere, it is transferred from one place to another through a pipe.
gloss_zh: 用管子输送，用管道运输（液体或气体）

senses.concept_en: If someone, especially a child, pipes something, they say it in a high-pitched voice.
In some computer systems, a pipe is a method of passing information from one program to another.
gloss_zh: （一些计算机系统中用来在程序间传送信息的）管道

planning.translation:
n. 计划的制订, 策划, 设计, 规划
[计] 计划, 规划

poke.translation:
n. 刺, 戳, 袋子
vt. 戳, 捅, 拨弄, 刺
vi. 戳, 刺, 捅, 搜索, 伸出, 行动散慢
[计] 存数

senses.concept_en: If you poke someone or something, you quickly push them with your finger or with a sharp object.
If you poke one thing into another, you push the first thing into the second thing.
If something pokes out of or through another thing, you can see part of it appearing from behind or underneath the other thing.
If you poke your head through an opening or if it pokes through an opening, you push it through, often so that you can see something more easily.

pour.translation:
n. 流出, 倾泻, 骤雨
vt. 倒, 灌, 注, 倾泻, 诉说, 倾吐
vi. 倾泻, 蜂涌而来, 下大雨

senses.concept_en: If you pour a liquid or other substance, you make it flow steadily out of a container by holding the container at an angle.
gloss_zh: 使（液体等）连续流出；倾倒；倒出

senses.concept_en: If you pour someone a drink, you put some of the drink in a cup or glass so that they can drink it.
When a liquid or other substance pours somewhere, for example through a hole, it flows quickly and in large quantities.
When it rains very heavily, you can say that it is pouring.
If people pour into or out of a place, they go there quickly and in large numbers.
If something such as information pours into a place, a lot of it is obtained or given.

prevent.translation: v. 预防, 防止, 阻止, 妨碍
prevent.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: To prevent something means to ensure that it does not happen.
To prevent someone from doing something means to make it impossible for them to do it

prompt.translation:
n. 激励, 提示, 提醒物, 提词, 付款期限
a. 迅速的, 敏捷的, 立刻的, 提词员的
vt. 激励, 鼓动, 提示
adv. 准时地
[计] 提示符; DOS内部命令:设定DOS命令行的提示符
prompt.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: To prompt someone to do something means to make them decide to do it.
If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you prompt an actor, you tell them what their next line is when they have forgotten what comes next.
gloss_zh: 鼓励，提示（说话者）；给（演员）提词

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A prompt action is done without any delay.
gloss_zh: 迅速的；即刻的；立即的；及时的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

proportion.translation:
n. 比例, 比率, 均衡, 部分, 面积
vt. 使成比例, 使均衡

senses.concept_en: A proportion of a group or an amount is a part of it.
The proportion of one kind of person or thing in a group is the number of people or things of that kind compared to the total number of people or things in the group.
The proportion of one amount to another is the relationship between the two amounts in terms of how much there is of each thing.
If you refer to the proportions of something, you are referring to its size, usually when this is extremely large.
gloss_zh: （通常指极其巨大的事物的）大小，尺寸

senses.concept_en: If you refer to the proportions in a work of art or design, you are referring to the relative sizes of its different parts.
gloss_zh: （艺术品或设计的各部分之间的）比例

protective.translation:
a. 给予保护的, 保护的
[医] 保护的, 防护的, 保护剂, 保护物, 油绸

senses.concept_en: Protective means designed or intended to protect something or someone from harm.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is protective towards you, they look after you and show a strong desire to keep you safe.

prove.translation:
vt. 证明, 查验, 检验, 勘探, 显示
vi. 证明是

senses.concept_en: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.
If you prove that something is true, you show by means of argument or evidence that it is definitely true.
If you prove yourself to have a certain good quality, you show by your actions that you have it.

quality.translation:
n. 品质, 特性, 才能, 质量
a. 优质的
[计] 品质
quality.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: The quality of something is how good or bad it is.
Something of quality is of a high standard.
Someone's qualities are the good characteristics that they have which are part of their nature.
You can describe a particular characteristic of a person or thing as a quality .
The quality papers or the quality press are the more serious newspapers which give detailed accounts of world events, as well as reports on business, culture, and society.

reach.translation:
n. 伸出, 延伸, 区域, 范围, 流域, 岬
vt. 到达, 达到, 伸出, 延伸, 影响
vi. 达到, 延伸, 伸出手, 传到

senses.concept_en: When someone or something reaches a place, they arrive there.
If someone or something has reached a certain stage, level, or amount, they are at that stage, level, or amount.
gloss_zh: 达到，到达（一定阶段、程度或数量）

senses.concept_en: If you reach somewhere, you move your arm and hand to take or touch something.
If you can reach something, you are able to touch it by stretching out your arm or leg.
If you try to reach someone, you try to contact them, usually by telephone.
If something reaches a place, point, or level, it extends as far as that place, point, or level.
When people reach an agreement or a decision, they succeed in achieving it.
gloss_zh: 取得（一致意见）；达成（协议）；作出（决定）

senses.concept_en: Someone's or something's reach is the distance or limit to which they can stretch, extend, or travel.
gloss_zh: 可达到的距离；所能及的限度

senses.concept_en: If a place or thing is within reach, it is possible to have it or get to it. If it is out of reach, it is not possible to have it or get to it.
gloss_zh: （伸手）可及之距离;（可接受的）范围

remain.translation:
vi. 保持, 逗留, 剩余
[法] 停留, 居住, 继续

senses.concept_en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change.
If you remain in a place, you stay there and do not move away.
You can say that something remains when it still exists.
If something remains to be done, it has not yet been done and still needs to be done.
The remains of something are the parts of it that are left after most of it has been taken away or destroyed.
The remains of a person or animal are the parts of their body that are left after they have died, sometimes after they have been dead for a long time.
Historical remains are things that have been found from an earlier period of history, usually buried in the ground, for example parts of buildings and pieces of pottery.
You can use remain in expressions such as the fact remains that or the question remains whether to introduce and emphasize something that you want to talk about.
gloss_zh: （事实、问题等）仍然是（表示强调）

replacement.translation:
n. 归还, 更换, 代替者
[医] 复位, 置换

senses.concept_en: See also:hormone replacement therapy; If you refer to the replacement of one thing by another, you mean that the second thing takes the place of the first.
Someone who takes someone else's place in an organization, government, or team can be referred to as their replacement .
gloss_zh: 替补（成员或队员）；接替者

request.translation:
n. 请求, 需要, 申请书
vt. 请求, 要求, 邀请
[计] 请求
request.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.
If you request someone to do something, you politely or formally ask them to do it.
If you make a request, you politely or formally ask someone to do something.
A request is a song or piece of music which someone has asked a performer or disc jockey to play.

rod.translation:
n. 竿, 笞鞭, 小枝
[化] 棒

senses.concept_en: See also:fishing rod;lightning rod; A rod is a long, thin metal or wooden bar.

room.translation:
n. 房间, 空位, 场所
vi. 住宿, 居住
vt. 留宿

senses.concept_en: A room is one of the separate sections or parts of the inside of a building. Rooms have their own walls, ceilings, floors, and doors, and are usually used for particular activities. You can refer to all the people who are in a room as the room .
gloss_zh: 房间;屋子;室;房间里的所有人

senses.concept_en: If you talk about your room, you are referring to the room that you alone use, especially your bedroom at home or your office at work.
gloss_zh: 私人房间（尤指卧室或办公室）

senses.concept_en: A room is a bedroom in a hotel.
If you room with someone, you share a rented room, apartment, or house with them, for example when you are a student.
See also:leg room;standing room; If there is room somewhere, there is enough empty space there for people or things to be fitted in, or for people to move freely or do what they want to.
If there is room for a particular kind of behaviour or action, people are able to behave in that way or to take that action.

rush.translation:
n. 匆促, 冲进, 急流, 灯心草
vi. 冲, 奔, 闯, 赶紧, 匆促行事, 涌现
vt. 使冲, 匆忙地做, 突袭, 飞跃, 用灯心草做
a. 紧急的
rush.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: If you rush somewhere, you go there quickly.
If people rush to do something, they do it as soon as they can, because they are very eager to do it.
A rush is a situation in which you need to go somewhere or do something very quickly.
If there is a rush for something, many people suddenly try to get it or do it.
The rush is a period of time when many people go somewhere or do something.
If you rush something, you do it in a hurry, often too quickly and without much care.
If you rush someone or something to a place, you take them there quickly.
If you rush into something or are rushed into it, you do it without thinking about it for long enough.
gloss_zh: （未经充分考虑而）匆忙做，仓促做，草率地做

senses.concept_en: If you rush something or someone, you move quickly and forcefully at them, often in order to attack them.
If air or liquid rushes somewhere, it flows there suddenly and quickly.
If you experience a rush of a feeling, you suddenly experience it very strongly.
Rushes are plants with long thin stems that grow near water.
In film-making, the rushes of a film are the parts of it that have been filmed but have not yet been edited.

safety.translation:
n. 安全, 保险, 平安, 保安设备
vt. 保护, 防护
safety.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Safety is the state of being safe from harm or danger.
If you reach safety, you reach a place where you are safe from danger.
If you are concerned about the safety of something, you are concerned that it might be harmful or dangerous.
gloss_zh: 安全程度;安全性;无害;无危险

senses.concept_en: If you are concerned for someone's safety, you are concerned that they might be in danger.
Safety features or measures are intended to make something less dangerous.

salt.translation:
n. 盐, 风趣, 刺激
a. 含盐的, 咸的, 风趣的, 辛辣的
vt. 加盐于, 用盐腌

senses.concept_en: Salt is a strong-tasting substance, in the form of white powder or crystals, which is used to improve the flavour of food or to preserve it. Salt occurs naturally in sea water.
When you salt food, you add salt to it.
Salts are substances that are formed when an acid reacts with an alkali.
gloss_zh: 盐，盐类（酸和碱的化合物）

season.translation:
n. 季节, 时节, 当令期, 时期
vt. 给...调味, 使成熟, 使老练, 缓和
vi. 变干燥

senses.concept_en: The seasons are the main periods into which a year can be divided and which each have their own typical weather conditions.
You can use season to refer to the period during each year when a particular activity or event takes place. For example, the planting season is the period when a particular plant or crop is planted.
gloss_zh: （一年中某项活动或某一事件发生的）节期，时期

senses.concept_en: You can use season to refer to the period when a particular fruit, vegetable, or other food is ready for eating and is widely available.
gloss_zh: （水果、蔬菜等的）当令期，上市期

senses.concept_en: You can use season to refer to a fixed period during each year when a particular sport is played.
A season is a period in which a play or show, or a series of plays or shows, is performed in one place.
gloss_zh: （戏剧、表演的）上演期，会演期，献演期

senses.concept_en: A season of films is several of them shown as a series because they are connected in some way.
The holiday or vacation season is the time when most people have their holiday.
If you season food with salt, pepper, or spices, you add them to it in order to improve its flavour.
If wood is seasoned, it is made suitable for making into furniture or for burning, usually by being allowed to dry out gradually.
gloss_zh: 对（木材）作干燥处理;风干，晒干（木材）

sense.translation:
n. 感应, 感觉, 感官, 意识, 观念, 情理, 知觉, 理智
vt. 感觉, 觉察, 检测
[计] 阅读; 检测
sense.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: See also:sixth sense; Your senses are the physical abilities of sight, smell, hearing, touch, and taste.
gloss_zh: 感觉官能（即视觉、嗅觉、听觉、触觉、味觉）

senses.concept_en: If you sense something, you become aware of it or you realize it, although it is not very obvious.
See also:sense of occasion; If you have a sense that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you may not have firm, clear evidence for this belief.
If you have a sense of guilt or relief, for example, you feel guilty or relieved.
If you have a sense of something such as duty or justice, you are aware of it and believe it is important.
See also:sense of humour; Someone who has a sense of timing or style has a natural ability with regard to timing or style. You can also say that someone has a bad sense of timing or style.
See also:common sense; Sense is the ability to make good judgments and to behave sensibly.
gloss_zh: 理智;头脑;良好的判断力

senses.concept_en: If you say that there is no sense or little sense in doing something, you mean that it is not a sensible thing to do because nothing useful would be gained by doing it.
A sense of a word or expression is one of its possible meanings.
to see sense

settle.translation:
n. 有背长椅
vt. 决定, 整理, 安放, 使定居, 使平静, 支付, 安排, 解决, 结算
vi. 停留, 下陷, 沉淀, 澄清, 安下心来, 结清, 定居, 安家
settle.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If people settle an argument or problem, or if something settles it, they solve it, for example by making a decision about who is right or about what to do.
If people settle a legal dispute or if they settle, they agree to end the dispute without going to a court of law, for example by paying some money or by apologizing.
If you settle a bill or debt, you pay the amount that you owe.
gloss_zh: 付清（欠款）;结算（账单）;结（账）

senses.concept_en: If something is settled, it has all been decided and arranged.
To settle money on someone means to formally give it to them, for example in a will.
gloss_zh: （以遗嘱等正式方式）赠予,授予

senses.concept_en: When people settle a place or in a place, or when a government settles them there, they start living there permanently.
gloss_zh: 在…定居;使定居;把…安置在

senses.concept_en: If you settle yourself somewhere or settle somewhere, you sit down or make yourself comfortable.
If something settles or if you settle it, it sinks slowly down and becomes still.
If your eyes settle on or upon something, you stop looking around and look at that thing for some time.
When birds or insects settle on something, they land on it from above.

several.translation:
a. 几个的, 一些的, 各自的
pron. 几个

senses.concept_en: Several is used to refer to an imprecise number of people or things that is not large but is greater than two.

severe.translation:
a. 严格的, 尖锐的, 严肃的, 严重的, 严厉的, 朴素的
[法] 严厉的, 苛刻的, 严重的
severe.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use severe to indicate that something bad or undesirable is great or intense.
gloss_zh: 十分严重的;极为恶劣的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Severe punishments or criticisms are very strong or harsh.
gloss_zh: （惩罚、批评）严厉的，严重的，苛刻的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe the appearance of someone or something as severe, you do not like its plain appearance and lack of decoration.
gloss_zh: （外貌、外观）简朴的，朴素的,不加修饰的

shop.translation:
n. 商店, 工厂, 车间
vi. 购物, 到处寻找
vt. 选购

senses.concept_en: A shop is a building or part of a building where things are sold.
When you shop, you go to shops and buy things.
You can refer to a place where a particular service is offered as a particular type of shop .
You can refer to a place where things are made or done as a particular kind of shop .
If you shop someone, you report them to the police for doing something illegal.

shortage.translation:
n. 不足, 缺乏
[化] 缺额

senses.concept_en: If there is a shortage of something, there is not enough of it.

show.translation:
n. 显示, 表现, 展览, 卖弄, 炫耀, 外观, 演出, 洋相
vt. 表示, 显示, 展现, 陈列, 演出, 表明, 指出, 带领
vi. 露面, 显现, 演出
[计] 显示

senses.concept_en: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people.
If a picture, chart, film, or piece of writing shows something, it represents it or gives information about it.
gloss_zh: （图画、图表、影像或文章）描绘，描述，展示，说明

senses.concept_en: If you show someone something, you give it to them, take them to it, or point to it, so that they can see it or know what you are referring to.
gloss_zh: 给…看;向…出示（或展示）;指给…看

senses.concept_en: If you show someone to a room or seat, you lead them there.
If you show someone how to do something, you do it yourself so that they can watch you and learn how to do it.
If something shows or if you show it, it is visible or noticeable.
If you show a particular attitude, quality, or feeling, or if it shows, you behave in a way that makes this attitude, quality, or feeling clear to other people.
gloss_zh: 表现，体现，流露出（态度、品质或情感）;（态度等）体现，流露

senses.concept_en: If something shows a quality or characteristic or if that quality or characteristic shows itself, it can be noticed or observed.
gloss_zh: 显示出，表露出，流露出（某种品质或特征）;（品质或特征）表露，显示

senses.concept_en: A show of a feeling or quality is an attempt by someone to make it clear that they have that feeling or quality.
gloss_zh: （情感、品质等的）流露，表露，体现

senses.concept_en: If you say that something is for show, you mean that it has no real purpose and is done just to give a good impression.
If a company shows a profit or a loss, its accounts indicate that it has made a profit or a loss.
If a person you are expecting to meet does not show, they do not arrive at the place where you expect to meet them.
A television or radio show is a programme on television or radio.
A show in a theatre is an entertainment or concert, especially one that includes different items such as music, dancing, and comedy.
gloss_zh: （尤指包括音乐、舞蹈、滑稽剧等不同内容的）演出，表演

senses.concept_en: If someone shows a film or television programme, it is broadcast or appears on television or in the cinema.
A show is a public exhibition of things, such as works of art, fashionable clothes, or things that have been entered in a competition.
To show things such as works of art means to put them in an exhibition where they can be seen by the public.
In a horse race, if a horse shows, it finishes first, second, or third.
gloss_zh: （赛马比赛中赛马）名列前三甲

senses.concept_en: A show home, house, or flat is one of a group of new homes. The building company decorates it and puts furniture in it, and people who want to buy one of the homes come and look round it.

single.translation:
a. 单身的, 单程的, 单一的, 个别的, 孤独的, 专一的
n. 一个, 单打, 单程票
vt. 选出
vi. 击出一垒打
[计] 单精度型

senses.concept_en: You use single to emphasize that you are referring to one thing, and no more than one thing.
You use single to indicate that you are considering something on its own and separately from other things like it.
Someone who is single is not married. You can also use single to describe someone who does not have a girlfriend or boyfriend.
A single room is a room intended for one person to stay or live in.
A single bed is wide enough for one person to sleep in.
A single ticket is a ticket for a journey from one place to another but not back again.
A single or a CD single is a CD which has a few short songs on it. You can also refer to the main song on a CD as a single .
gloss_zh: （只录几首短歌的）单曲唱片;（激光唱片上的）主打歌曲，单曲

senses.concept_en: Singles is a game of tennis or badminton in which one player plays another. The plural singles can be used to refer to one or more of these matches.
In cricket, a single is a hit from which one run is scored. In baseball, a single is a hit by which a batter reaches first base.
gloss_zh: （板球中的）一分打;（棒球中的）一垒打

slowly.translation: adv. 慢慢地, 迟缓地

small.translation:
a. 小的, 少的, 小型的, 低微的, 小气的, 细微的
adv. 些微地
n. 狭小部分

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A small person, thing, or amount of something is not large in physical size.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A small group or quantity consists of only a few people or things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A small child is a very young child.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use small to describe something that is not significant or great in degree.
gloss_zh: 不重要的;无足轻重的;程度小的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Small businesses or companies employ a small number of people and do business with a small number of clients.
gloss_zh: （企业或公司）小规模的，小型的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone speaks in a small voice, they speak in a quiet, high voice because they are frightened or ashamed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone makes you look or feel small, they make you look or feel stupid or ashamed.
The small of your back is the bottom part of your back that curves in slightly.

so.translation:
adv. 如此, 如是, 如...那样
conj. 所以, 因此
pron. 这样

senses.concept_en: You use so to refer back to something that has just been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 如此，这样（指已经提到的事）

senses.concept_en: You use so when you are saying that something which has just been said about one person or thing is also true of another one.
gloss_zh: 同样，也一样（指后者跟前者一样）

senses.concept_en: You use the structures as...so and just as...so when you want to indicate that two events or situations are similar in some way.
gloss_zh: （表示两个事件或情况在某方面相似）正如…，也…

senses.concept_en: If you say that a state of affairs is so, you mean that it is the way it has been described.
gloss_zh: （指某一情况）就是这样，事实如此

senses.concept_en: You can use so with actions and gestures to show a person how to do something, or to indicate the size, height, or length of something.
gloss_zh: （向别人示范）这样，像这样;（用手势比划大小、高度或长度）这么，那么

senses.concept_en: You use so and so that to introduce the result of the situation you have just mentioned.
You use so ,so that, and so as to introduce the reason for doing the thing that you have just mentioned.
You can use so in stories and accounts to introduce the next event in a series of events or to suggest a connection between two events.
gloss_zh: （在叙述过程中引出一系列事件中的下一件或说明两件事情之间的联系）此后，于是

senses.concept_en: You can use so in conversations to introduce a new topic, or to introduce a question or comment about something that has been said.
gloss_zh: （表示开始新话题、引入新问题或对刚说过的问题进行评论）那么，这么

senses.concept_en: You can use so in conversations to show that you are accepting what someone has just said.
gloss_zh: （谈话中表示接受别人的说法）的确，确实

senses.concept_en: You can use so in front of adjectives and adverbs to emphasize the quality that they are describing.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词和副词之前强调所描述的特性）如此，这么，多么，太

senses.concept_en: You can use so...that and so...as to emphasize the degree of something by mentioning the result or consequence of it.
gloss_zh: 如此…（以致…）;到…的程度（以致…）

some.translation:
pron. 一些, 一部分, 若干
adv. 大约
a. 一些的, 少许的, 某一的

senses.concept_en: You use some to refer to a quantity of something or to a number of people or things, when you are not stating the quantity or number precisely.
gloss_zh: 一些，有些（表示不确切的数量或数目）

senses.concept_en: You use some to emphasize that a quantity or number is fairly large. For example, if an activity takes some time, it takes quite a lot of time.
gloss_zh: （表示数量或数目相当大）好些，大量

senses.concept_en: You use some to emphasize that a quantity or number is fairly small. For example, if something happens to some extent, it happens a little.
gloss_zh: （表示数量或数目相当小）有几分，有点儿

senses.concept_en: If you refer to some of the people or things in a group, you mean a few of them but not all of them. If you refer to some of a particular thing, you mean a part of it but not all of it.
If you refer to some person or thing, you are referring to that person or thing but in a vague way, without stating precisely which person or thing you mean.
You can use some in front of a number to indicate that it is approximate.
Some is used to mean to a small extent or degree.
You can use some in front of a noun in order to express your approval or disapproval of the person or thing you are mentioning.
gloss_zh: （表示赞同或不赞同）也叫，也算；了不起的，好极的

spare.translation:
n. 剩余, 备用品, 备件, 备用零件, 备用轮胎
a. 多余的, 备用的, 空闲的, 节约的, 瘦的
vi. 节约, 省掉, 宽恕
vt. 节约, 省用, 剩下, 饶恕, 赦免

senses.concept_en: You use spare to describe something that is the same as things that you are already using, but that you do not need yet and are keeping ready in case another one is needed.
You use spare to describe something that is not being used by anyone, and is therefore available for someone to use.
If you have something such as time, money, or space to spare, you have some extra time, money, or space that you have not used or which you do not need.
gloss_zh: 剩余，剩下（时间、金钱或空间）

senses.concept_en: If you spare time or another resource for a particular purpose, you make it available for that purpose.
gloss_zh: 抽出，拨出（金钱或其他资源）

senses.concept_en: If a person or a place is spared, they are not harmed, even though other people or places have been.
If you spare someone an unpleasant experience, you prevent them from suffering it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is described as spare is tall and not at all fat.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something such as a room that is spare is very plain with no unnecessary features.
gloss_zh: 简单的;不加修饰的;简朴的

stability.translation:
n. 安定, 稳定性, 坚实, 巩固
[化] 稳定性

stand.translation:
n. 站立, 站住, 停顿, 讲台, 看台, 立场, 法院证人席
vi. 站, 立, 坐落, 停滞, 位于, 坚持, 维持原状
vt. 忍受, 使站立, 抵挡

senses.concept_en: When you are standing, your body is upright, your legs are straight, and your weight is supported by your feet.
When someone who is sitting stands, they change their position so that they are upright and on their feet.
If you stand aside or stand back, you move a short distance sideways or backwards, so that you are standing in a different place.
If something such as a building or a piece of furniture stands somewhere, it is in that position, and is upright.
You can say that a building is standing when it remains after other buildings around it have fallen down or been destroyed.
gloss_zh: （建筑物在周围其他建筑物倒塌或被毁后）依然存在，矗立

senses.concept_en: If you stand something somewhere, you put it there in an upright position.
If you leave food or a mixture of something to stand, you leave it without disturbing it for some time.
gloss_zh: （将食物或调拌物等）搁置不动

senses.concept_en: If you take or make a stand, you do something or say something in order to make it clear what your attitude to a particular thing is.
If you ask someone where or how they stand on a particular issue, you are asking them what their attitude or view is.
If you do not know where you stand with someone, you do not know exactly what their attitude to you is.
You can use stand instead of 'be' when you are describing the present state or condition of something or someone.
If a decision, law, or offer stands, it still exists and has not been changed or cancelled.
If something that can be measured stands at a particular level, it is at that level.
You can describe how tall or high someone or something is by saying that they stand a particular height.
If something can stand a situation or a test, it is good enough or strong enough to experience it without being damaged, harmed, or shown to be inadequate.
gloss_zh: 经得起，承受得住（困难、考验）

senses.concept_en: If you cannot stand something, you cannot bear it or tolerate it.
If you cannot stand someone or something, you dislike them very strongly.
If you stand to gain something, you are likely to gain it. If you stand to lose something, you are likely to lose it.
gloss_zh: 可能获得/ 可能失去

senses.concept_en: If you stand in an election, you are a candidate in it.
If you stand someone a meal or a drink, you buy it for them.
See also:newsstand; A stand is a small shop or stall, outdoors or in a large public building.
gloss_zh: （设在户外或大型公共建筑物内的）小店，售货摊

senses.concept_en: A stand at a sports ground is a large structure where people sit or stand to watch what is happening.
A stand is an object or piece of furniture that is designed for supporting or holding a particular kind of thing.
A stand is an area where taxis or buses can wait to pick up passengers.
gloss_zh: （出租车、公共汽车的）停车候客处

senses.concept_en: In a law court, the stand is the place where a witness stands to answer questions.

standard.translation:
n. 标准, 规格, 旗, 军旗, 本位
a. 标准的, 合规格的
[计] 标准
standard.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A standard is a level of quality or achievement, especially a level that is thought to be acceptable.
A standard is something that you use in order to judge the quality of something else.
See also:double standard; Standards are moral principles which affect people's attitudes and behaviour.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use standard to describe things which are usual and normal.
A standard work or text on a particular subject is one that is widely read and often recommended.
gloss_zh: （作品等）受广泛阅读的，最受推崇的，最具权威性的

star.translation:
n. 星, 恒星, 星形物, 运气, 明星
vt. 以星状物装饰, 用星号标, 使成为明星
vi. 变成明星

senses.concept_en: See also:morning star;shooting star; A star is a large ball of burning gas in space. Stars appear to us as small points of light in the sky on clear nights.
You can refer to a shape or an object as a star when it has four, five, or more points sticking out of it in a regular pattern.

You can say how many stars something such as a hotel or restaurant has as a way of talking about its quality, which is often indicated by a number of star-shaped symbols. The more stars something has, the better it is.
Famous actors, musicians, and sports players are often referred to as stars .
If an actor or actress stars in a play or film, he or she has one of the most important parts in it.
gloss_zh: （在戏剧或电影中）担任主角，主演

senses.concept_en: If a play or film stars a famous actor or actress, he or she has one of the most important parts in it.
Predictions about people's lives which are based on astrology and appear regularly in a newspaper or magazine are sometimes referred to as the stars .

startle.translation:
n. 惊愕, 惊恐
vt. 吃惊, 使惊愕
vi. 惊起
startle.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If something sudden and unexpected startles you, it surprises and frightens you slightly.

steady.translation:
a. 稳定的, 不动摇的, 沉着的, 稳固的, 坚定的, 经常的
vt. 使稳定, 使坚定
vi. 变为沉着, 稳固
steady.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A steady situation continues or develops gradually without any interruptions and is not likely to change quickly.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If an object is steady, it is firm and does not shake or move about.
gloss_zh: 稳定的;牢固的;不摇晃的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you look at someone or speak to them in a steady way, you look or speak in a calm, controlled way.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person as steady, you mean that they are sensible and reliable.
If you steady something or if it steadies, it stops shaking or moving about.
If you steady yourself, you control your voice or expression, so that people will think that you are calm and not nervous.
You say 'steady on' to someone to tell them to calm down or to be careful about what they are saying.

stone.translation:
n. 石头, 宝石, 果核, 纪念碑, 结石
vt. 投扔石子, 铺石头
a. 石的, 石制的, 完全的
stone.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Stone is a hard solid substance found in the ground and often used for building houses.
A stone is a small piece of rock that is found on the ground.
A stone is a large piece of stone put somewhere in memory of a person or event, or as a religious symbol.
gloss_zh: （作为宗教标志的）石碑;纪念碑

senses.concept_en: Stone is used in expressions such as set in stone and tablets of stone to suggest that an idea or rule is firm and fixed, and cannot be changed.
gloss_zh: （表示观念或规则固定而不可改变）板上钉钉，铁板钉钉

senses.concept_en: You can refer to a jewel as a stone .
A stone is a small hard ball of minerals and other substances which sometimes forms in a person's kidneys or gall bladder.
The stone in a plum, cherry, or other fruit is the large hard seed in the middle of it.
If you stone a fruit, you remove its stone.
If people stone someone or something, they throw stones at them.
A stone is a measurement of weight, especially the weight of a person, equal to 14 pounds or 6.35 kilograms
gloss_zh: 英石（重量单位，相当于 14 磅或6.35公斤）

stop.translation:
n. 停止, 车站, 逗留, 填塞, 障碍, (风琴的)音栓
vi. 停止, 被塞住
vt. 塞住, 堵塞, 阻止, 击落, 停止, 终止, 断绝

senses.concept_en: If you have been doing something and then you stop doing it, you no longer do it.
If you stop something happening, you prevent it from happening or prevent it from continuing.
If an activity or process stops, it is no longer happening.
If something such as machine stops or is stopped, it is no longer moving or working.
gloss_zh: （机器等）停止运转;（使）停止工作

senses.concept_en: When a moving person or vehicle stops or is stopped, they no longer move and they remain in the same place.
gloss_zh: （使）（移动着的人或车）停下;把…拦住

senses.concept_en: If something that is moving comes to a stop or is brought to a stop, it slows down and no longer moves.
If someone does not stop to think or to explain, they continue with what they are doing without taking any time to think about or explain it.
If you say that a quality or state stops somewhere, you mean that it exists or is true up to that point, but no further.
A stop is a place where buses or trains regularly stop so that people can get on and off.
If you stop somewhere on a journey, you stay there for a short while.
A stop is a time or place at which you stop during a journey.
In music, organ stops are the knobs at the side of the organ, which you pull or push in order to control the type of sound that comes out of the pipes.

stream.translation:
n. 水流, 小河, 流出, 趋势, 人潮
vt. 流出, 流动, 展开
vi. 流, 涌, 飘扬
[计] 流
stream.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky gre

senses.concept_en: A stream is a small narrow river.
A stream of smoke, air, or liquid is a narrow moving mass of it.
A stream of vehicles or people is a long moving line of them.
A stream of things is a large number of them occurring one after another.
gloss_zh: 一连串;接二连三;源源不断

senses.concept_en: If a liquid streams somewhere, it flows or comes out in large amounts.
If your eyes are streaming, liquid is coming from them, for example because you have a cold. You can also say that your nose is streaming .
If people or vehicles stream somewhere, they move there quickly and in large numbers.
When light streams into or out of a place, it shines strongly into or out of it.
If something such as a flag or someone's hair streams in the wind, it is blown so that it is almost horizontal.
In a school, a stream is a group of children of the same age and ability who are taught together.
gloss_zh: （把孩子按年龄和能力编在一起的）班，组

senses.concept_en: To stream pupils means to divide them into groups according to their ability.

successful.translation:
a. 成功的, 一帆风顺的, 顺利的
[经] 成功的
successful.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is successful achieves what it was intended to achieve. Someone who is successful achieves what they intended to achieve.
gloss_zh: 达到目的的;有成效的;成功的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is successful is popular or makes a lot of money.
gloss_zh: 获得成功的;受欢迎的;获利匪浅的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is successful achieves a high position in what they do, for example in business or politics.

sudden.translation:
n. 突然, 忽然
a. 突然的, 意外的, 快速的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Sudden means happening quickly and unexpectedly.

suffer.translation:
vt. 遭受, 经历, 忍受
vi. 受痛苦, 受损害

senses.concept_en: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.
gloss_zh: 遭受，经受（疼痛）;感到（痛苦）

senses.concept_en: If you suffer from an illness or from some other bad condition, you are badly affected by it.
gloss_zh: （因疾病或处于其他不利境地而）受苦，受难，受折磨

senses.concept_en: If you suffer something bad, you are in a situation in which something painful, harmful, or very unpleasant happens to you.
gloss_zh: 遭遇，遭受，蒙受（不好的事）

senses.concept_en: If you suffer, you are badly affected by an event or situation.
If something suffers, it does not succeed because it has not been given enough attention or is in a bad situation.
gloss_zh: （因不够关注或处于不利境况而）失利，失败，不成功

system.translation:
n. 系统, 体系, 制度, 方式, 秩序, 分类原则
[计] 系统; 体制; 体系
system.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A system is a way of working, organizing, or doing something which follows a fixed plan or set of rules. You can use system to refer to an organization or institution that is organized in this way.
A system is a set of devices powered by electricity, for example a computer or an alarm.
A system is a set of equipment or parts such as water pipes or electrical wiring, which is used to supply water, heat, or electricity.
A system is a network of things that are linked together so that people or things can travel from one place to another or communicate.
Your system is your body's organs and other parts that together perform particular functions.
A system is a particular set of rules, especially in mathematics or science, which is used to count or measure things.
gloss_zh: （尤指数学或科学中的）体系,体制

senses.concept_en: People sometimes refer to the government or administration of a country as the system .
gloss_zh: 政府;现行体制;公共行政

tap.translation:
n. 轻打, 水龙头
vt. 轻打, 轻敲, 敲打出, 选择, 装上嘴子, 使流出, 开发, 分接, 向...乞讨
vi. 轻叩, 轻拍, 啪塔啪塔地走
[计] 接头
tap.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A tap is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas from a pipe or container, for example on a sink.
If you tap something, you hit it with a quick light blow or a series of quick light blows.
If you tap your fingers or feet, you make a regular pattern of sound by hitting a surface lightly and repeatedly with them, especially while you are listening to music.
gloss_zh: （尤指听音乐时，用手指或脚）敲节拍，打拍子

senses.concept_en: If you tap a resource or situation, you make use of it by getting from it something that you need or want.
gloss_zh: 开发，发掘，利用（资源、形势）

senses.concept_en: See also:phone-tapping;wiretap; If someone taps your telephone, they attach a special device to the line so that they can secretly listen to your conversations.

that.translation:
a. 那, 那个
conj. 以致, 因为
pron. 那
adv. 那么, 那样

senses.concept_en: You use that to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.
gloss_zh: 那，那个（指代前面句子里提到的）

senses.concept_en: You use that to refer to someone or something already mentioned.
gloss_zh: 那个人,那个（用来指代已经提到的人或物）

senses.concept_en: When you have been talking about a particular period of time, you use that to indicate that you are still referring to the same period. You use expressions such as that morning or that afternoon to indicate that you are referring to an earlier period of the same day.
gloss_zh: 那，那个（指已经谈到过的特定时期）

senses.concept_en: You use that in expressions such as that of and that which to introduce more information about something already mentioned, instead of repeating the noun which refers to it.
gloss_zh: （用于 that of, that which 等短语中引出有关上文提到的某事物的更多信息，而避免重复相关名词）

senses.concept_en: You use that in front of words or expressions which express agreement, responses, or reactions to what has just been said.
gloss_zh: 那个，那（用于对前述内容表示同意或作出应答的词和词组前）

senses.concept_en: You use that to introduce a person or thing that you are going to give details or information about.
gloss_zh: 那一个，那个（引出将要更加详细介绍的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use that when you are referring to someone or something which is a distance away from you in position or time, especially when you indicate or point to them. When there are two or more things near you, that refers to the more distant one.
gloss_zh: 那个（指代在时间、空间上离自己稍远的人或物，尤用于指示;有两个以上的事物时，that 指较远的那个）

senses.concept_en: You use that when you are identifying someone or asking about their identity.
You can use that when you expect the person you are talking to to know what or who you are referring to, without needing to identify the particular person or thing fully.
gloss_zh: （不需明确指出的情况下谈话对方即可能知道所指的人或物）那个

senses.concept_en: If something is not that bad, funny, or expensive for example, it is not as bad, funny, or expensive as it might be or as has been suggested.
gloss_zh: 不太，不那么（坏、滑稽、昂贵等）

senses.concept_en: You can use that to emphasize the degree of a feeling or quality.
gloss_zh: 那么，那样（用于强调感情或品质的程度之深）

senses.concept_en: You can use that after many verbs, adjectives, nouns, and expressions to introduce a clause in which you report what someone has said, or what they think or feel.
gloss_zh: （用于动词、形容词、名词、短语之后，引导间接引语从句）

senses.concept_en: You use that after 'it' and a link verb and an adjective to comment on a situation or fact.
gloss_zh: （用于“it+系动词+形容词”结构之后，表示评论）

senses.concept_en: You use that to introduce a clause which gives more information to help identify the person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，以提供更多有关谈论对象的信息）

senses.concept_en: You use that after expressions with 'so' and 'such' in order to introduce the result or effect of something.
gloss_zh: （用在 so，such 之后，引出结果或影响）

senses.concept_en: You use the at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.
gloss_zh: （用于名词短语之前，指代已经提及或指明的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use the at the beginning of a noun group when the first noun is followed by an 'of' phrase or a clause which identifies the person or thing.
gloss_zh: （当名词后接 of 短语或表明身份的从句时，该名词前用the）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of some nouns that refer to something in our general experience of the world.
gloss_zh: （用于某些表示人们共有经历的名词前）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of nouns that refer to people, things, services, or institutions that are associated with everyday life.
gloss_zh: （用于和日常生活相关的人、物、服务、机构的名词前）

senses.concept_en: You use the instead of a possessive determiner, especially when you are talking about a part of someone's body or a member of their family.
gloss_zh: （用于代替所有格限定词，尤在谈论身体某一部分或家庭某一成员时）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of a singular noun when you want to make a general statement about things or people of that type.
gloss_zh: （用于单数名词前，表示一类人或事物）

senses.concept_en: You use the with the name of a musical instrument when you are talking about someone's ability to play the instrument.
gloss_zh: （谈论是否会演奏乐器时，用于乐器名称前）

senses.concept_en: You use the with nationality adjectives and nouns to talk about the people who live in a country.
gloss_zh: （用于表示国籍的形容词和名词以谈论一国全体国民）

senses.concept_en: You use the with words such as 'rich', 'poor', 'old', or 'unemployed' to refer to all people of a particular type.
gloss_zh: （与 rich, poor, old, unemployed 等形容词连用，表示某一类人）

senses.concept_en: If you want to refer to a whole family or to a married couple, you can make their surname into a plural and use the in front of it.
gloss_zh: （用于姓氏的复数前，表示一家人或夫妻）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of an adjective when you are referring to a particular thing that is described by that adjective.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词前，表示其修饰的某个事物）

senses.concept_en: You use the to indicate that you have enough of the thing mentioned for a particular purpose.
gloss_zh: （表示拥有为某一特定目的所需的足够的某物）

senses.concept_en: You use the with some titles, place names, and other names.
gloss_zh: （与某些称号、地名和其他名称连用）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of numbers such as first, second, and third.
You use the in front of numbers when they refer to decades.
You use the in front of superlative adjectives and adverbs.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词和副词的最高级前）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of each of two comparative adjectives or adverbs when you are describing how one amount or quality changes in relation to another.
gloss_zh: 越…越…（用于两个比较级前，表示其中一个随另一个发生量或质的变化）

senses.concept_en: When you express rates, prices, and measurements, you can use the to say how many units apply to each of the items being measured.
gloss_zh: 每，一（表示速度、价格、度量等）

senses.concept_en: You use the to indicate that something or someone is the most famous, important, or best thing of its kind. In spoken English, you put more stress on it, and in written English, you often underline it or write it in capitals or italics.
gloss_zh: （表示某人或某物是同类中最有名、最重要或最好的。口语中 the 要重读；书面语中常加下划线或用大写、斜体）

senses.concept_en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.
You use their instead of 'his or her' to indicate that something belongs or relates to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people think this use is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （代替 his or her，而不指明是男是女;有人认为这种用法不对）

senses.concept_en: You use they to refer to a group of people, animals, or things.
You use they instead of 'he or she' to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people think this use is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （用以代替he or she，而不指明是男是女;有人认为这种用法不对）

senses.concept_en: You use they in expressions such as 'they say' or 'they call it' to refer to people in general when you are making general statements about what people say, think, or do.
gloss_zh: （用于 they say，they call it 等表达中表示泛指）他们

thick.translation:
a. 厚的, 粗壮的, 浓的, 迟钝的, 浑浊的, 多雾的, 过分的, 口齿不清的
adv. 厚地, 密地, 浓浓地
n. 最浓处, 最厚处, 最密集处
[计] 暗, 粗线

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is thick has a large distance between its two opposite sides.
You can use thick to talk or ask about how wide or deep something is.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something that consists of several things is thick, it has a large number of them very close together.
gloss_zh: 浓的;密的;密集的;茂密的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is thick with another thing, the first thing is full of or covered with the second.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Thick clothes are made from heavy cloth, so that they will keep you warm in cold weather.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Thick smoke, fog, or cloud is difficult to see through.
gloss_zh: （烟、雾、云）浓的，混浊的，能见度低的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Thick liquids are fairly stiff and solid and do not flow easily.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone's voice is thick, they are not speaking clearly, for example because they are ill, upset, or drunk.
gloss_zh: （声音）不清楚的，沙哑的，低沉的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A thick accent is very obvious and easy to identify.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as thick, you think they are stupid.

thousand.translation:
num. 千
a. 成千的, 许多的
n. 许许多多

senses.concept_en: A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000.
If you refer to thousands of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

thread.translation:
n. 线, 丝, 纤维, 线索
vt. 穿线于, 穿过, 通过, 用线穿成
vi. 穿过
[计] 线索, 线程
thread.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl gre

senses.concept_en: Thread or a thread is a long very thin piece of a material such as cotton, nylon, or silk, especially one that is used in sewing.
The thread of an argument, a story, or a situation is an aspect of it that connects all the different parts together.
A thread of something such as liquid, light, or colour is a long thin line or piece of it.
You can refer to clothes as threads .
The thread on a screw, or on something such as a lid or a pipe, is the raised spiral line of metal or plastic around it which allows it to be fixed in place by twisting.
If you thread your way through a group of people or things, or thread through it, you move through it carefully or slowly, changing direction frequently as you move.
If you thread a long thin object through something, you pass it through one or more holes or narrow spaces.
gloss_zh: 使（细长的物体）穿过;使穿进

senses.concept_en: If you thread small objects such as beads onto a string or thread, you join them together by pushing the string through them.
When you thread a needle, you put a piece of thread through the hole in the top of the needle in order to sew with it.

threaten.translation:
vt. 恐吓, 威胁, 预示...的凶兆
vi. 威胁, 恫吓, 可能来临

senses.concept_en: If a person threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.
If something or someone threatens a person or thing, they are likely to harm that person or thing.
If something unpleasant threatens to happen, it seems likely to happen.
Three is the number 3.

tight.translation:
a. 紧的, 密封的, 吝啬的, 严厉的
adv. 紧紧地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Tight clothes or shoes are rather small and fit closely to your body.
If you hold someone or something tight, you hold them firmly and securely.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Tight controls or rules are very strict.
Something that is shut tight is shut very firmly.
gloss_zh: 紧紧地;密不透风地;滴水不漏地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Skin, cloth, or string that is tight is stretched or pulled so that it is smooth or straight.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Tight is used to describe a group of things or an amount of something that is closely packed together.
gloss_zh: 紧密的;密集的;装得满满的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a part of your body is tight, it feels rather uncomfortable and painful, for example because you are ill, anxious, or angry.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A tight group of people is one whose members are closely linked by beliefs, feelings, or interests.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A tight bend or corner is one that changes direction very quickly so that you cannot see very far round it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A tight schedule or budget allows very little time or money for unexpected events or expenses.
gloss_zh: （日程、预算）紧张的，回旋余地不大的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A tight contest is one where none of the competitors has a clear advantage or looks likely to win, so that it is difficult to say who the winner will be.
gloss_zh: （比赛双方）比分接近的，不相上下的，势均力敌的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is tight, you disapprove of them because they are unwilling to spend their money.
gloss_zh: 小气的;抠门儿的;吝啬的

time.translation:
n. 时间, 时侯, 时机, 时期, 期限, 次数, 节拍, 暂停, 规定时间
vt. 测定...的时间, 记录...的时间, 计时, 定时
a. 时间的, 记时的, 定时的, 定期的, 分期的
[计] DOS内部命令:用于显示或设定系统的时间

senses.concept_en: Time is what we measure in minutes, hours, days, and years.
You use time to ask or talk about a specific point in the day, which can be stated in hours and minutes and is shown on clocks.
See also:opening time; The time when something happens is the point in the day when it happens or is supposed to happen.
You use time to refer to the system of expressing time and counting hours that is used in a particular part of the world.
You use time to refer to the period that you spend doing something or when something has been happening.
gloss_zh: （用来做某事或某事发生的）时间

senses.concept_en: If you say that something has been happening for a time, you mean that it has been happening for a fairly long period of time.

You use time to refer to a period of time or a point in time, when you are describing what is happening then. For example, if something happened at a particular time, that is when it happened. If it happens at all times, it always happens.
gloss_zh: （某事发生的）一段（或特定）时间

senses.concept_en: You use time or times to talk about a particular period in history or in your life.

You can use the times to refer to the present time and to modern fashions, tastes, and developments. For example, if you say that someone keeps up with the times, you mean they are fashionable or aware of modern developments. If you say they are behind the times, you mean they are unfashionable or not aware of them.
When you describe the time that you had on a particular occasion or during a particular part of your life, you are describing the sort of experience that you had then.
Your time is the amount of time that you have to live, or to do a particular thing.
If you say it is time for something, time to do something, or time you did something, you mean that this thing ought to happen or be done now.
When you talk about a time when something happens, you are referring to a specific occasion when it happens.
You use time after numbers to say how often something happens.
You use times after numbers when comparing one thing to another and saying, for example, how much bigger, smaller, better, or worse it is.
You use times in arithmetic to link numbers or amounts that are multiplied together to reach a total.
Someone's time in a race is the amount of time it takes them to finish the race.
The time of a piece of music is the number of beats that the piece has in each bar.
If you time something for a particular time, you plan or decide to do it or cause it to happen at this time.
gloss_zh: 给…确定时间;为…安排时间

senses.concept_en: If you time an action or activity, you measure how long someone takes to do it or how long it lasts.

to.translation:
prep. 到, 向, 趋于
adv. 向前

senses.concept_en: You use to when indicating the place that someone or something visits, moves towards, or points at.
If you go to an event, you go where it is taking place.
If something is attached to something larger or fixed to it, the two things are joined together.
You use to when indicating the position of something. For example, if something is to your left, it is nearer your left side than your right side.
When you give something to someone, they receive it.
You use to to indicate who or what an action or a feeling is directed towards.
gloss_zh: （表示动作或情感的对象）对，于

senses.concept_en: You use to with certain nouns and adjectives to show that a following noun is related to them.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词、形容词连用，表示关联）对于，关于

senses.concept_en: If you say something to someone, you want that person to listen and understand what you are saying.

You use to when indicating someone's reaction to something or their feelings about a situation or event. For example, if you say that something happens to someone's surprise you mean that they are surprised when it happens.
You use to when indicating the person whose opinion you are stating.
You use to when indicating what something or someone is becoming, or the state or situation that they are progressing towards.
To can be used as a way of introducing the person or organization you are employed by, when you perform some service for them.
You use to to indicate that something happens until the time or amount mentioned is reached.
You use to when indicating the last thing in a range of things, usually when you are giving two extreme examples of something.
If someone goes from place to place or from job to job, they go to several places, or work in several jobs, and spend only a short time in each one.
You use to when you are stating a time which is less than thirty minutes before an hour. For example, if it is 'five to eight', it is five minutes before eight o'clock.
You use to when giving ratios and rates.
You use to when indicating that two things happen at the same time. For example, if something is done to music, it is done at the same time as music is being played.
If you push or shut a door to, you close it but may not shut it completely.
You use to before the base form of a verb to form the to-infinitive. You use the to-infinitive after certain verbs, nouns, and adjectives, and after words such as 'how', 'which', and 'where'.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前构成不定式;不定式用于某些动词、名词、形容词以及 how，which, where 等词之后）。

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb to indicate the purpose or intention of an action. in order to
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示动作的目的或意图）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb when you are commenting on a statement that you are making, for example when saying that you are being honest or brief, or that you are summing up or giving an example.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示对自己要说的话加以说明）
