senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb in exclamations when you are emphasizing a very strong emotion, such as a desire or wish, or a regret or disappointment.
gloss_zh: （用于感叹句中的动词原形前，强调某一强烈情感）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb when indicating what situation follows a particular action.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示某一动作之后的情形）

senses.concept_en: You use to with 'too' and 'enough' in expressions like too much to and old enough to

tool.translation:
n. 工具, 机床, 傀儡
vt. 用工具加工
vi. 使用工具

senses.concept_en: See also:machine tool; A tool is any instrument or simple piece of equipment that you hold in your hands and use to do a particular kind of work. For example, spades, hammers, and knives are all tools.
You can refer to anything that you use for a particular purpose as a particular type of tool .

If you describe someone as a tool of a particular person, group, or system, you mean that they are controlled and used by that person, group, or system, especially to do unpleasant or dishonest things.
gloss_zh: 受人利用的人;工具;傀儡

toward.translation:
prep. 向, 对于, 为了
a. 即将来临的, 进行中的

town.translation:
n. 城镇, 市, 镇
[法] 城镇, 城市, 闹市

senses.concept_en: A town is a place with many streets and buildings, where people live and work. Towns are larger than villages and smaller than cities. Many places that are called towns in Britain would be called cities in the United States.
You use town in order to refer to the town where you live.
You use town in order to refer to the central area of a town where most of the shops and offices are.
gloss_zh: 市中心;（城镇的）商业中心；闹市区

senses.concept_en: If you refer to the town, you are referring to town and city areas in general, as opposed to country areas.

triumph.translation:
n. 凯旋, 胜利, 欢欣
vi. 得胜, 成功
triumph.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.
gloss_zh: 非凡的成功;杰出的成就

senses.concept_en: Triumph is a feeling of great satisfaction and pride resulting from a success or victory.
gloss_zh: （成功或获胜时的）极大的满足，狂喜，骄傲

senses.concept_en: If someone or something triumphs, they gain complete success, control, or victory, often after a long or difficult struggle.

trouble.translation:
n. 烦恼, 麻烦, 困难, 动乱, 故障
vt. 困扰, 麻烦, 使烦恼, 折磨
vi. 烦恼, 费心

senses.concept_en: You can refer to problems or difficulties as trouble .
If you say that one aspect of a situation is the trouble, you mean that it is the aspect which is causing problems or making the situation unsatisfactory.
gloss_zh: 麻烦;问题;引起麻烦的事

senses.concept_en: Your troubles are the things that you are worried about.
If you have kidney trouble or back trouble, for example, there is something wrong with your kidneys or your back.
If there is trouble somewhere, especially in a public place, there is fighting or rioting there.
If you tell someone that it is no trouble to do something for them, you are saying politely that you can or will do it, because it is easy or convenient for you.
If you say that a person or animal is no trouble, you mean that they are very easy to look after.
gloss_zh: 需劳神费力的人（或动物）

senses.concept_en: If something troubles you, it makes you feel rather worried.
If a part of your body troubles you, it causes you physical pain or discomfort.
If you say that someone does not trouble to do something, you are critical of them because they do not behave in the way that they should do, and you think that this would require very little effort.
You use trouble in expressions such as I'm sorry to trouble you when you are apologizing to someone for disturbing them in order to ask them something.

truck.translation:
n. 卡车, 货车, 对...进行交易, 来往, 实物工资, (供应市场的)蔬菜, 废物, 废话
vt. 对...进行交易, 交往, 以卡车运输
vi. 驾驶卡车, 以物易物

senses.concept_en: A truck is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.
A truck is an open vehicle used for carrying goods on a railway.
gloss_zh: （铁路）运货车皮，敞篷货运火车

senses.concept_en: When something or someone is trucked somewhere, they are driven there in a lorry.
gloss_zh: 用卡车装运;用货车运送

true.translation:
a. 真实的, 正确的, 忠诚的, 可靠的, 纯粹的, 正式的
n. 真实, 准确
adv. 真实地, 准确地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is true, it is based on facts rather than being invented or imagined, and is accurate and reliable.
gloss_zh: 基于事实的;真实的;如实的;可信的

senses.concept_en: You use true to emphasize that a person or thing is sincere or genuine, often in contrast to something that is pretended or hidden.
gloss_zh: （感情）真实的，真挚的；（物品）真的，真正的,正品的

senses.concept_en: If you use true to describe something or someone, you approve of them because they have all the characteristics or qualities that such a person or thing typically has.
gloss_zh: 纯粹的;真正的;名副其实的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that a fact is true of a particular person or situation, you mean that it is valid or relevant for them.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use true in order to admit that a fact or opinion is real or valid before indicating that you think that it is not important or relevant in the circumstances.
If you are true to someone, you remain committed and loyal to them. If you are true to an idea or promise, you remain committed to it and continue to act according to it.
gloss_zh: 忠实的;忠诚的;恪守（诺言、思想等）的

turn.translation:
n. 转弯, 转动, 旋转, 翻转, 一圈, 顺次, 改动, 变化, 性格, 特色, 形状, 转折
vt. 使旋转, 转弯, 转动, 使转向, 驱赶, 阻挡, 兑换, 改写, 使作对, 绕过, 使流通
vi. 转动, 转弯, 转向, 翻转, 回转, 改变, 转身, 变成, 变质, 晕眩, 易脱手

senses.concept_en: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction.
When you turn something, you move it so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction, or is in a very different position.
gloss_zh: 转动;使转向;使改变方向

senses.concept_en: When something such as a wheel turns, or when you turn it, it continually moves around in a particular direction.
When you turn something such as a key, knob, or switch, or when it turns, you hold it and twist your hand, in order to open something or make it start working.
gloss_zh: 转动，旋动（钥匙、把手、开关等）

senses.concept_en: When you turn in a particular direction or turn a corner, you change the direction in which you are moving or travelling.
The point where a road, path, or river turns, is the point where it has a bend or curve in it.
When the tide turns, it starts coming in or going out.
When someone turns a cartwheel or a somersault, they do a cartwheel or somersault.
When you turn a page of a book or magazine, you move it so that is flat against the previous page, and you can read the next page.
If you turn a weapon or an aggressive feeling on someone, you point it at them or direct it at them.
If you turn to a particular page in a book or magazine, you open it at that page.
If you turn your attention or thoughts to a particular subject or if you turn to it, you start thinking about it or discussing it.
gloss_zh: 开始思考;开始讨论;把（注意力等）转向

senses.concept_en: If you turn to someone, you ask for their help or advice.
If you turn to a particular activity, job, or way of doing something, you start doing or using it.
To turn or be turned into something means to become that thing.
You can use turn before an adjective to indicate that something or someone changes by acquiring the quality described by the adjective.
If something turns a particular colour or if something turns it a particular colour, it becomes that colour.
You can use turn to indicate that there is a change to a particular kind of weather. For example, if it turns cold, the weather starts being cold.
If a situation or trend takes a particular kind of turn, it changes so that it starts developing in a different or opposite way.
gloss_zh: （时局或趋势的）逆转，转变，变化

senses.concept_en: In sports, if a game turns, or is turned, something significant happens which changes the way the game is developing.
If a business turns a profit, it earns more money than it spends.
When someone turns a particular age, they pass that age. When it turns a particular time, it passes that time.
Turn is used in expressions such as the turn of the century and the turn of the year to refer to a period of time when one century or year is ending and the next one is beginning.
When someone turns a wooden or metal object that they are making, they shape it using a special tool.
If it is your turn to do something, you now have the duty, chance, or right to do it, when other people have done it before you or will do it after you.
gloss_zh: （依次轮流时的）轮班，次序，轮番

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is having a turn, you mean they feel suddenly very unwell for a short period of time.
Two is the number 2.

use.translation:
n. 使用, 习惯, 使用价值, 用法, 使用权
vt. 使用, 利用, 运用, 耗费
vi. 惯常

senses.concept_en: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.
If you use a supply of something, you finish it so that none of it is left.
If someone uses drugs, they take drugs regularly, especially illegal ones.
You can say that someone uses the toilet or bathroom as a polite way of saying that they go to the toilet.
gloss_zh: 用（洗手间或卫生间）（礼貌说法）

senses.concept_en: If you use a particular word or expression, you say or write it, because it has the meaning that you want to express.
If you use a particular name, you call yourself by that name, especially when it is not the name that you usually call yourself.

If you say that someone uses people, you disapprove of them because they make others do things for them in order to benefit or gain some advantage from it, and not because they care about the other people.
Your use of something is the action or fact of your using it.
If you have a use for something, you need it or can find something to do with it.
If something has a particular use, it is intended for a particular purpose.
If you have the use of something, you have the permission or ability to use it.
A use of a word is a particular meaning that it has or a particular way in which it can be used.
Your use of a particular name is the fact of your calling yourself by it.

valley.translation:
n. 山谷, 溪谷, 流域, 凹地
[医] 谷

senses.concept_en: A valley is a low stretch of land between hills, especially one that has a river flowing through it.

village.translation:
n. 村庄
a. 乡村的, 村庄的

senses.concept_en: A village consists of a group of houses, together with other buildings such as a church and a school, in a country area.
You refer to the people who live in a village, especially the people who have lived there for most or all of their lives, as the villagers .

wall.translation:
n. 墙, 墙壁, 垣, 内壁, 分界物, 屏障
a. 墙的
vt. 给...建墙, 禁闭, 用墙围住
[计] 背景墙

senses.concept_en: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.
A wall is a long narrow vertical structure made of stone or brick that surrounds or divides an area of land.
The wall of something that is hollow is its side.
A wall of something is a large amount of it forming a high vertical barrier.
gloss_zh: 屏障;堆成墙的大量物品

senses.concept_en: You can describe something as a wall of a particular kind when it acts as a barrier and prevents people from understanding something.

warm.translation:
a. 暖和的, 暖的, 温暖的, 热烈的, 兴奋的, 激烈的, 多情的, 色情的
vt. 使温暖, 弄热, 使兴奋, 使充满仇恨
vi. 变暖和, 变温暖, 取暖, 激动, 同情, 爱好
n. 暖, 保暖物

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is warm has some heat but not enough to be hot

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Warm clothes and blankets are made of a material such as wool which protects you from the cold.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Warm colours have red or yellow in them rather than blue or green, and make you feel comfortable and relaxed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A warm person is friendly and shows a lot of affection or enthusiasm in their behaviour.
If you warm a part of your body or if something hot warms it, it stops feeling cold and starts to feel hotter.
If you warm to a person or an idea, you become fonder of the person or more interested in the idea.
gloss_zh: （对某人）产生好感;（对想法）开始感兴趣

warn.translation:
vt. 警告, 提醒, 通知
vi. 发出警告

senses.concept_en: If you warn someone about something such as a possible danger or problem, you tell them about it so that they are aware of it.
If you warn someone not to do something, you advise them not to do it so that they can avoid possible danger or punishment

watch.translation:
n. 观察, 手表, 看守, 守护, 监视, 值班人
vt. 看, 注视, 照顾, 看守, 守护, 监视
vi. 观看, 注视, 守侯

senses.concept_en: If you watch someone or something, you look at them, usually for a period of time, and pay attention to what is happening.
If you watch something on television or an event such as a sports match, you spend time looking at it, especially when you see it from the beginning to the end.
gloss_zh: 看，观看（电视节目、比赛等）

senses.concept_en: If you watch a situation or event, you pay attention to it or you are aware of it, but you do not influence it.
gloss_zh: 对…保持关注;掌握…的情况

senses.concept_en: If you watch people, especially children or animals, you are responsible for them, and make sure that they are not in danger.
gloss_zh: 照看，看护（尤指孩子或动物）

senses.concept_en: If you watch someone, you follow them secretly or spy on them.
If you tell someone to watch a particular person or thing, you are warning them to be careful that the person or thing does not get out of control or do something unpleasant.
A watch is a period of carefully looking and listening, often while other people are asleep and often as a military duty, so that you can warn them of danger or an attack.
A watch is a small clock which you wear on a strap on your wrist, or on a chain.

water.translation:
n. 水, 雨水, 海水, 水位, 水面, 流水
vt. 给...浇水, 供以水, 注入水, 使湿
vi. 流泪, 流口水, 加水
a. 水的, 水上的, 水生的, 含水的

senses.concept_en: Water is a clear thin liquid that has no colour or taste when it is pure. It falls from clouds as rain and enters rivers and seas. All animals and people need water in order to live.
You use waters to refer to a large area of sea, especially the area of sea which is near to a country and which is regarded as belonging to it.
You sometimes use waters to refer to a situation which is very complex or difficult.
If you water plants, you pour water over them in order to help them to grow.
If your eyes water, tears build up in them because they are hurting or because you are upset.
See also:mouth-watering; If you say that your mouth is watering, you mean that you can smell or see some nice food and you might mean that your mouth is producing a liquid.

wear.translation:
n. 穿着, 戴, 使用, 耗损, 服装, 耐久性
vt. 穿着, 戴, 留(须、发等), 呈现, 磨损, 磨成, 耗损, 使疲乏, 消磨
vi. 磨损, 变旧, 耐久, 渐变, 渐渐消失

senses.concept_en: When you wear something such as clothes, shoes, or jewellery, you have them on your body or on part of your body.
If you wear your hair or beard in a particular way, you have it cut or styled in that way.
If you wear a particular expression, that expression is on your face and shows the emotions that you are feeling.
You use wear to refer to clothes that are suitable for a certain time or place. For example, evening wear is clothes suitable for the evening.
Wear is the amount or type of use that something has over a period of time.
gloss_zh: 耐用性;使用率;使用形式

senses.concept_en: Wear is the damage or change that is caused by something being used a lot or for a long time.
If something wears, it becomes thinner or weaker because it is constantly being used over a long period of time.
You can use wear to talk about how well something lasts over a period of time. For example, if something wears well, it still seems quite new or useful after a long time or a lot of use.

weave.translation:
n. 编法, 织法, 编织式样
vt. 编织, 组合, 编排, 使迂回前进
vi. 纺织, 迂回行进

senses.concept_en: If you weave cloth or a carpet, you make it by crossing threads over and under each other using a frame or machine called a loom.
A particular weave is the way in which the threads are arranged in a cloth or carpet.
If you weave something such as a basket, you make it by crossing long plant stems or fibres over and under each other.
If you weave your way somewhere, you move between and around things as you go there.
If you weave a story, you invent a complicated story.
If you weave details into a story or design, you include them, so that they are closely linked together or become an important part of the story or design.
gloss_zh: 将（素材等）编入（故事或设计中）

wheel.translation:
n. 轮子, 车轮, 轮, 方向盘, 旋转, 机构, 重要人物
vt. 使旋转, 转动, 使转向
vi. 旋转, 转弯, 盘旋
wheel.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: The wheels of a vehicle are the circular objects which are fixed underneath it and which enable it to move along the ground.
A wheel is a circular object which forms a part of a machine, usually a moving part.

The wheel of a car or other vehicle is the circular object that is used to steer it. The wheel is used in expressions to talk about who is driving a vehicle. For example, if someone is at the wheel of a car, they are driving it.
People sometimes refer to a car as wheels .
If you wheel an object that has wheels somewhere, you push it along.
If something such as a group of animals or birds wheels, it moves in a circle.
If you wheel around, you turn around suddenly where you are standing, often because you are surprised, shocked, or angry.
gloss_zh: （因惊讶、震惊或生气）突然转身

senses.concept_en: You use wheel in expressions such as the wheel of fortune to refer to the changes that take place in life, especially when you are referring to the fact that the same situations occur more than once.
gloss_zh: （尤指多次发生相同的情形）命运之轮

senses.concept_en: People talk about the wheels of an organization or system to mean the way in which it operates. to oil the wheels

when.translation:
conj. 当...的时候
adv. 何时, 什么时候
pron. 什么时侯
n. 时间

senses.concept_en: You use when to ask questions about the time at which things happen.
If something happens when something else is happening, the two things are happening at the same time.
gloss_zh: （表示两事同时发生）在…时，当…时

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce a clause in which you mention something which happens at some point during an activity, event, or situation.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，表示某事发生于另一活动、事件或情形期间）在…的过程中

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce a clause where you mention the circumstances under which the event in the main clause happened or will happen.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，说明主句动作已经发生或将要发生时的情况）其时

senses.concept_en: You use when after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause where you mention the time at which something happens.
gloss_zh: （尤用于动词和形容词后引导从句，表示某事发生的时间）什么时候,何时

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce a clause which specifies or refers to the time at which something happens.
gloss_zh: （用于引导从句，限定或指示某事发生的时间）…的时候

senses.concept_en: You use when to introduce the reason for an opinion, comment, or question.
gloss_zh: （用于引出某个观点、评论或问题的原因）既然，考虑到

senses.concept_en: You use when in order to introduce a fact or comment which makes the other part of the sentence rather surprising or unlikely.
gloss_zh: （用于引出使句子的其他部分显得让人吃惊或不大可能的事实或评论）虽然，然而,可是

where.translation:
adv. 在哪里
pron. 哪里
n. 地点

senses.concept_en: You use where to ask questions about the place something is in, or is coming from or going to.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句）在哪里，从哪里，到哪里

senses.concept_en: You use where after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention the place in which something is situated or happens.
gloss_zh: （尤用于动词和形容词后引导从句，表示某物所在或某事发生的地点）那里，那儿

senses.concept_en: You use where to ask questions about a situation, a stage in something, or an aspect of something.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句）在哪一地点,在哪一阶段，在哪方面

senses.concept_en: You use where after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause in which you mention a situation, a stage in something, or an aspect of something.
gloss_zh: （尤用于某些动词和形容词后，引导表示地点、某事物所处状态、阶段等的从句）在哪儿，从哪儿

senses.concept_en: You use where to introduce a clause that contrasts with the other parts of the sentence.
gloss_zh: （用于引导从句进行对比）然而

which.translation: pron. 哪一个, 那一个

senses.concept_en: You use which in questions when there are two or more possible answers or alternatives.
You use which to refer to a choice between two or more possible answers or alternatives.
gloss_zh: （用于指明在两个或多个答案或选项中所作出的选择）哪个，哪些

senses.concept_en: You use which at the beginning of a relative clause when specifying the thing that you are talking about or when giving more information about it.
gloss_zh: （用于关系从句句首，具体说明所谈论的事物或提供关于它的更多信息）

senses.concept_en: You use which to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences, especially when you want to give your opinion about it.
gloss_zh: （用来回指前面句子表达的观点或状况）这，那

senses.concept_en: You use who in questions when you ask about the name or identity of a person or group of people.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句，询问人的姓名或身份）谁

senses.concept_en: You use who after certain words, especially verbs and adjectives, to introduce a clause where you talk about the identity of a person or a group of people.
gloss_zh: （尤用在动词和形容词后引导从句，说明人的身份）谁

senses.concept_en: You use who at the beginning of a relative clause when specifying the person or group of people you are talking about or when giving more information about them.
gloss_zh: （用于进行限定说明或提供更多信息的关系从句的句首）

wind.translation:
n. 风, 气息, 气味, 呼吸, 风声, 趋势, 空谈, 卷绕, 弯曲
vt. 使通风, 嗅出, 使喘气, 吹号角, 上发条, 缠绕, 包, 绞起, 吊起, 使弯曲, 使迂回
vi. 嗅出猎物, 吹响号角, 卷曲, 蜿蜒, 迂回, 缠绕

senses.concept_en: A wind is a current of air that is moving across the earth's surface.
Journalists often refer to a trend or factor that influences events as a wind of a particular kind.
gloss_zh: （影响事件的）趋势（或因素）（常作新闻用语）

senses.concept_en: If you are winded by something such as a blow, the air is suddenly knocked out of your lungs so that you have difficulty breathing for a short time.
Wind is the air that you sometimes swallow with food or drink, or gas that is produced in your intestines, which causes an uncomfortable feeling.
If you wind a baby, you hit its back gently in order to help it to release air from its stomach.
The wind section of an orchestra or band is the group of people who produce musical sounds by blowing into their instruments.
If a road, river, or line of people winds in a particular direction, it goes in that direction with a lot of bends or twists in it.
gloss_zh: （道路、河流或一队人）蜿蜒向前，曲折而行，迂回

senses.concept_en: When you wind something flexible around something else, you wrap it around it several times.
When you wind a mechanical device, for example a watch or a clock, you turn a knob, key, or handle on it several times in order to make it operate.
gloss_zh: 给（钟表等）上发条;给…上弦

senses.concept_en: To wind a tape or film back or forward means to make it move towards its starting or ending position.

winter.translation:
n. 冬季, 萧条期, 衰退期
a. 冬天的
vt. 使度过冬天
vi. 过冬

senses.concept_en: Winter is the season between autumn and spring. In the winter the weather is usually cold.
If an animal or plant winters somewhere or is wintered there, it spends the winter there.
If you winter somewhere, you spend the winter there.

without.translation:
prep. 没有, 不, 在...之外
adv. 在外面, 户外
n. 外面, 外部

senses.concept_en: You use without to indicate that someone or something does not have or use the thing mentioned.
If one thing happens without another thing, or if you do something without doing something else, the second thing does not happen or occur.
gloss_zh: 在没有（发生或做某事）的情况下

senses.concept_en: If you do something without a particular feeling, you do not have that feeling when you do it.
If you do something without someone else, they are not in the same place as you are or are not involved in the same action as you.

wood.translation:
n. 木材, 木制品
vt. 植林于, 给...添加木柴
vi. 收集木材
wood.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Wood is the material which forms the trunks and branches of trees.
A wood is a fairly large area of trees growing near each other. You can refer to one or several of these areas as woods, and this is the usual form in American English.
gloss_zh: 树林，林子（美国英语通常用woods）

wooden.translation: a. 木制的, 呆笨的, 木然的

senses.concept_en: Wooden objects are made of wood.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe an actor as wooden, you are critical of them because their performance is not at all lively or natural.
gloss_zh: （演员）呆板的，死板的，无活力的

wool.translation:
n. 羊毛, 毛织物, 毛线, 绒线
[医] 羊毛, 绒毛, 棉[花]

senses.concept_en: Wool is the hair that grows on sheep and on some other animals.
Wool is a material made from animal's wool that is used to make things such as clothes, blankets, and carpets.

work.translation:
n. 工作, 劳动, 职业, 行为, 功, 作品, 成果, 产品, 工程
vi. 工作, 劳动, 做, 运转, 起作用, 被加工
vt. 使工作, 使转动, 开动, 使用, 经营, 使逐渐变得, 造成

senses.concept_en: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
People who have work or who are in work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
When you work, you do the things that you are paid or required to do in your job.
Your work consists of the things you are paid or required to do in your job.
When you work, you spend time and effort doing a task that needs to be done or trying to achieve something.
Work is the place where you do your job.
Work is something which you produce as a result of an activity or as a result of doing your job.
A work is something such as a painting, book, or piece of music produced by an artist, writer, or composer.
gloss_zh: （艺术家、作家、作曲家等的）作品；著作

senses.concept_en: If someone is working on a particular subject or question, they are studying or researching it.
If you work with a person or a group of people, you spend time and effort trying to help them in some way.
If a machine or piece of equipment works, it operates and performs a particular function.
If an idea, system, or way of doing something works, it is successful, effective, or satisfactory.
If a drug or medicine works, it produces a particular physical effect.
If something works in your favour, it helps you in some way. If something works to your disadvantage, it causes problems for you in some way.
gloss_zh: 产生（有利或不利的）影响

senses.concept_en: If something or someone works their magic or works their charms on a person, they have a powerful positive effect on them.
gloss_zh: 对…产生（神奇的影响）;使…深受（魅力感染）

senses.concept_en: If your mind or brain is working, you are thinking about something or trying to solve a problem.
If you work on an assumption or idea, you act as if it were true or base other ideas on it, until you have more information.
gloss_zh: 以（某种假定或思想）为基础（或前提）

senses.concept_en: If you work a particular area or type of place, you travel around that area or work in those places as part of your job, for example trying to sell something there.
gloss_zh: 在（某地或某类场所）工作;在…奔波

senses.concept_en: If you work someone, you make them spend time and effort doing a particular activity or job.
If someone, often a politician or entertainer, works a crowd, they create a good relationship with the people in the crowd and get their support or interest.
gloss_zh: （常指政客或艺人）博得，赢得（众人的支持或欢心）

senses.concept_en: When people work the land, they do all the tasks involved in growing crops.
When a mine is worked, minerals such as coal or gold are removed from it.
If you work a machine or piece of equipment, you use or control it.
If something works into a particular state or condition, it gradually moves so that it is in that state or condition.
If you work a substance such as dough or clay, you keep pressing it to make it have a particular texture.
If you work a material such as metal, leather, or stone, you cut, sew, or shape it in order to make something or to create a design.
If you work with a particular substance or material, you use it in order to make something or to create a design.
gloss_zh: 使用，采用（某种材料或物质）

senses.concept_en: If you work a part of your body, or if it works, you move it.
A works is a place where something is manufactured or where an industrial process is carried out. Works is used to refer to one or to more than one of these places.
Works are activities such as digging the ground or building on a large scale.
You can say the works after listing things such as someone's possessions or requirements, to emphasize that they possess or require everything you can think of in a particular category.
gloss_zh: （某种类型的）全部物件，全套物品

worker.translation:
n. 工人, 劳动者
[经] 工人, 劳工, 劳动者

senses.concept_en: A particular kind of worker does the kind of work mentioned.
Workers are people who are employed in industry or business and who are not managers.
See also:care worker;caseworker;dock worker;social worker;teleworker;youth worker; You can use worker to say how well or badly someone works.

worry.translation:
n. 担心, 烦恼, 忧虑, 苦恼, 撕咬
vt. 使烦恼, 使焦虑, 使苦恼, 困扰, 折磨, 撕咬
vi. 烦恼, 担心, 撕咬

senses.concept_en: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.
If someone or something worries you, they make you anxious because you keep thinking about problems or unpleasant things that might be connected with them.
If someone or something does not worry you, you do not dislike them or you are not annoyed by them.
Worry is the state or feeling of anxiety and unhappiness caused by the problems that you have or by thinking about unpleasant things that might happen.
A worry is a problem that you keep thinking about and that makes you unhappy.
gloss_zh: 使人担心（或发愁）的问题；烦心事

senses.concept_en: You use would when you are saying what someone believed, hoped, or expected to happen or be the case.
gloss_zh: （表示曾经相信、希望或期待）将，将会

senses.concept_en: You use would when saying what someone intended to do.
You use would when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible situation.
gloss_zh: （表示可能出现的情况的结果或影响）会，将会

senses.concept_en: You use would, or would have with a past participle, to indicate that you are assuming or guessing that something is true, because you have good reasons for thinking it.
gloss_zh: （would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示有充分理由认为或猜测是某种情况）肯定，一定，应该

senses.concept_en: You use would in the main clause of some 'if' and 'unless' sentences to indicate something you consider to be fairly unlikely to happen.
gloss_zh: （用于if，unless等引导的条件状语从句的主句，表示认为某事不大可能发生）就，该

senses.concept_en: You use would to say that someone was willing to do something. You use would not to indicate that they refused to do something.
You use would not to indicate that something did not happen, often in spite of a lot of effort.
gloss_zh: （表示尽管付出很大努力却没有发生）就（不），偏（不）

senses.concept_en: You use would, especially with 'like', 'love', and 'wish', when saying that someone wants to do or have a particular thing or wants a particular thing to happen. would rather
gloss_zh: （尤与like, love 和 wish 连用，表示想做某事或拥有某物，或希望某事发生）要，会

senses.concept_en: You use would with 'if' clauses in questions when you are asking for permission to do something.
gloss_zh: （用于带if从句的疑问句中，表示请求许可做某事）会

senses.concept_en: You use would, usually in questions with 'like', when you are making a polite offer or invitation.
gloss_zh: （通常在疑问句中与 like 连用，表示礼貌地给予或邀请）

senses.concept_en: You use would, usually in questions, when you are politely asking someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （通常用于疑问句中，表示礼貌地请求某人做某事）请

senses.concept_en: You say that someone would do something when it is typical of them and you are critical of it. You emphasize the word would when you use it in this way.
gloss_zh: （用于批评，表示对某人做某事并不感到意外，此时 would 须重读）

senses.concept_en: You use would, or sometimes would have with a past participle, when you are expressing your opinion about something or seeing if people agree with you, especially when you are uncertain about what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示发表看法或了解他人是否赞同自己的看法，尤用于对自己的话没有把握时）

senses.concept_en: You use I would when you are giving someone advice in an informal way.
gloss_zh: （用于以随便的口气向人提出建议）我（就）会

senses.concept_en: You use you would in negative sentences with verbs such as 'guess' and 'know' when you want to say that something is not obvious, especially something surprising.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句，与 guess, know 等动词连用，表示某事不明显，尤用于某事令人吃惊时）

senses.concept_en: You use would to talk about something which happened regularly in the past but which no longer happens.
gloss_zh: （表示某事过去惯常发生, 而现在不再发生了）就，会

senses.concept_en: You use would have with a past participle when you are saying what was likely to have happened by a particular time.
gloss_zh: （would have 与过去分词连用，表示某个时间前可能发生的事情）就，会

senses.concept_en: You use would have with a past participle when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible event in the past.
gloss_zh: （would have 与过去分词连用，表示过去可能发生的事情的结果或影响）就，会

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone would have liked or preferred something, you mean that they wanted to do it or have it but were unable to.
You use would, usually in negative sentences, to criticize something that someone has done and to express your disapproval of it.
gloss_zh: （通常用于否定句，批评某人所为，表示不满）（不）会

year.translation:
n. 年, 年度, 年龄
[经] 年度

senses.concept_en: See also:leap year; A year is a period of twelve months or 365 or 366 days, beginning on the first of January and ending on the thirty-first of December.
A year is any period of twelve months.
Year is used to refer to the age of a person. For example, if someone or something is twenty years old or twenty years of age, they have lived or existed for twenty years.

A school year or academic year is the period of time in each twelve months when schools or universities are open and students are studying there. In Britain and the United States, the school year starts in September.
gloss_zh: 学年（英国和美国的学年从9月开始）

senses.concept_en: You can refer to someone who is, for example, in their first year at school or university as a first year.
A financial or business year is an exact period of twelve months which businesses or institutions use as a basis for organizing their finances.
You can use years to emphasize that you are referring to a long time.
You can refer to the time you spend in a place or doing an activity as your years there or your years of doing that activity.
gloss_zh: （在某地或做某事的）年头，时期

young.translation:
a. 年轻的, 无经验的, 朝气蓬勃的
n. 青年们, 幼小动物, 崽

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A young person, animal, or plant has not lived or existed for very long and is not yet mature.
gloss_zh: 年幼的;幼小的;未成熟的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use young to describe a time when a person or thing was young.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is young in appearance or behaviour looks or behaves as if they are young.
gloss_zh: （显得）年轻的;（显得）岁数不大的

senses.concept_en: The young of an animal are its babies.

article.title: The Tube Mail Experiment
article.summary_zh: 工程师布朗克服试验事故与质疑，成功建成地下气压邮件系统。
article.body:
In 1865, the postal service in the capital faced a serious problem. Important letters took hours to travel between government offices. A young prince decided to support a bold proposal by an engineer named Robert Brown. Brown suggested a radical method to improve the delivery of messages across roughly two miles of crowded streets. Instead of relying on boys on foot or horses, Brown wanted to push metal containers through underground iron pipes using air pressure.

At the central station, workers installed a steam engine to control the air inside the system. By pumping air out of one end of a pipe, the machine produced a vacuum that pulled a small container through the dark tube. Brown proved that this efficient design could move papers faster than any runner. However, workers could not finish the difficult task overnight, because laying pipes under stone roads required considerable money and labor. Every morning, a clerk sorted the letters, gathered a tall stack of official papers, and locked them inside the container before each run.

On the day of the first public trial, an accident almost destroyed the project. Brown stood by the iron pipe to watch the arrival of the container. Suddenly, he heard a faint sound like a scream coming from the wall. A loose iron cover gave way, which caused a sudden change in pressure and made a heavy metal door slam against the wall. Then, a loud explosion of trapped steam burst from the pipe. The shock wave shook the tables and made several wooden boxes tumble to the floor. Fortunately, the strong iron pipes did not break, and none of the visitors suffered injuries.

The noisy blast caused immediate fear among the observers. Several older men began to mutter complaints under their breath, calling the engine unsafe. One clerk stood dumb with terror, staring at the smoke with wide eyes. The chief inspector stepped forward and raised a strong objection against the entire plan, claiming that city streets should never hold such dangerous machines. In response, Brown calmly explained the true merit of his idea. He argued that whereas bad weather and muddy roads constantly slowed down horse carriages, underground pipes protected the mail from external delay.

To win back their trust, Brown promised to execute further safety checks before opening the line to the public. He worked for two weeks to improve the sealing compound on every pipe joint so that air would not escape. This extra care increased the reliability of the system, and later tests ran without any trouble. The prince recognized Brown’s success and felt an obligation to support new technology for the nation. Although the early accident had partially damaged the engineer’s reputation, his tubes soon carried thousands of letters every week between the capital's busiest offices.

senses.concept_en: If you do one thing instead of another, you do the first thing and not the second thing, as the result of a choice or a change of behaviour.
If you go somewhere on foot, you walk, rather than using any form of transport.
If something slows down or is if something slows it down, it starts to move or happen more slowly.
If someone slows down or if something slows them down, they become less active.

senses.gloss_zh: （尤指经过千辛万苦）赢回，夺回
senses.concept_en: If you win back something that you have lost, you get it again, especially as a result of a great effort.

a.translation:
第一个字母 A; 一个; 第一的
art. [计] 累加器, 加法器, 地址, 振幅, 模拟, 区域, 面积, 汇编, 组件, 异步

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are referring to someone or something for the first time or when people may not know which particular person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （指初次提及或非特指的人或物）一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are referring to any person or thing of a particular type and do not want to be specific.
gloss_zh: （一类人或事物中非特指的）任何一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of an uncount noun when that noun follows an adjective, or when the noun is followed by words that describe it more fully.
gloss_zh: （用于前加形容词或后加修饰语的不可数名词之前）一（种）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of a mass noun when you want to refer to a single type or make of something.
You use a in quantifiers such as a lot ,a little, and a bit.
gloss_zh: （用于表示数量的词组中）许多/少许/一点

senses.concept_en: You use a or an to refer to someone or something as a typical member of a group, class, or type.
gloss_zh: （一类人或事物中典型的）一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of days, months, or festivals when you are referring to one particular instance of that day, month, or festival.
gloss_zh: （用于日子、月份或节日的名称之前以表示特例）一个

senses.concept_en: You use a or an when you are saying what someone is or what job they have.
You use a or an in front of the names of people as a way of indicating that you do not know them or anything about them and you are saying their name for the first time.
gloss_zh: （用于不为说话人所知的首次提到的人名前）某一（个）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of people when you want to refer to someone else who has the same qualities or character as the person named.
gloss_zh: （用于人名前，表示与该人有相同特性或品质）类似…的一个（或一位）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of a surname when you want to refer to someone who belongs to the family with that surname.
gloss_zh: （用于姓氏前，表示某人属于某姓氏家族）一位姓…的人

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in front of the names of artists to refer to one individual painting or sculpture created by them.
gloss_zh: （用于艺术家名字前）一幅…的画，一件…的雕塑作品

senses.concept_en: You use a or an instead of the number 'one', especially with words of measurement such as 'hundred', 'hour', and 'metre', and with fractions such as 'half', 'quarter', and 'third'.
gloss_zh: （代替数字one使用，尤用于hundred，hour和metre等表示度量的单词之前以及half, quarter和third等分数之前）

senses.concept_en: You use a or an in expressions such as eight hours a day to express a rate or ratio.
gloss_zh: （用于表示比率的短语中）每一

accident.translation:
n. 意外事件, 机遇, 事故, 次要方面
[化] 意外事故; 事故

senses.concept_en: An accident happens when a vehicle hits a person, an object, or another vehicle, causing injury or damage.
If someone has an accident, something unpleasant happens to them that was not intended, sometimes causing injury or death.
gloss_zh: （不幸的）意外遭遇，不测事件;事故

senses.concept_en: If something happens by accident, it happens completely by chance.

across.translation:
prep. 越过, 穿过, 与...相交叉, 在...的对面
adv. 交叉, 到另一边, 在对面, 成十字

senses.concept_en: If someone or something goes across a place or a boundary, they go from one side of it to the other.
If something is situated or stretched across something else, it is situated or stretched from one side of it to the other.
If something is lying across an object or place, it is resting on it and partly covering it.
Something that is across something such as a street, river, or area is on the other side of it.
If you look across at a place, person, or thing, you look towards them.
You use across to say that a particular expression is shown on someone's face.
If someone hits you across the face or head, they hit you on that part.
When something happens across a place or organization, it happens equally everywhere within it.
When something happens across a political, religious, or social barrier, it involves people in different groups. across the board
gloss_zh: 超越，跨越（政治、宗教、社会隔阂等）

senses.concept_en: Across is used in measurements to show the width of something.

against.translation: prep. 反对, 对着, 倚靠

senses.concept_en: If one thing is leaning or pressing against another, it is touching it.
If you are against something such as a plan, policy, or system, you think it is wrong, bad, or stupid.
If you compete against someone in a game, you try to beat them.
If you take action against someone or something, you try to harm them.
If you take action against a possible future event, you try to prevent it.
If you do something against someone's wishes, advice, or orders, you do not do what they want you to do or tell you to do.
gloss_zh: 违背，违抗（愿望、劝告或命令）

senses.concept_en: If you do something in order to protect yourself against something unpleasant or harmful, you do something which will make its effects on you less serious if it happens.
If something is against the law or against the rules, there is a law or a rule which says that you must not do it.
If you are moving against a current, tide, or wind, you are moving in the opposite direction to it.
If something happens or is considered against a particular background of events, it is considered in relation to those events, because those events are relevant to it.
If something is measured or valued against something else, it is measured or valued by comparing it with the other thing.
The odds against something happening are the chances or odds that it will not happen.

air.translation:
n. 空气, 旋律, 态度
vt. 晾, 使通风, 夸耀

senses.concept_en: Air is the mixture of gases which forms the earth's atmosphere and which we breathe.
The air is the space around things or above the ground.
Air is used to refer to travel in aircraft.
An air is a simple tune which can be easily recognized and remembered.
If you say that someone or something has a particular air, you mean that they give this general impression.
gloss_zh: 神态;感觉;总体印象;氛围

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is putting on airs or giving themselves airs, you are criticizing them for behaving as if they are better than other people.
gloss_zh: 矫揉造作；装腔作势；做作

senses.concept_en: If a broadcasting company airs a television or radio programme, they show it on television or broadcast it on the radio.
gloss_zh: （通过电视或无线电）播送，播放

senses.concept_en: If you air your opinions, you make them known to people.
If you air a room or building, you let fresh air into it.
If you air clothing or bedding, you put it somewhere warm to make sure that it is completely dry.
You use almost to indicate that something is not completely the case but is nearly the case.
You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement which contrasts with the statement in the main clause.
You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement which makes the main clause of the sentence seem surprising or unexpected.
gloss_zh: 虽然（表示惊奇或出乎意料）

senses.concept_en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which gives some information that is relevant to the main clause but modifies the strength of that statement.
You use although when admitting a fact about something which you regard as less important than a contrasting fact.
gloss_zh: 尽管;虽然（表示承认所述是事实）

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is situated or moving among a group of things or people is surrounded by them.
If you are among people of a particular kind, you are with them and having contact with them.
gloss_zh: 与…在一起;在…的集体之中

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is among a group, they are a member of that group and share its characteristics.
If you want to focus on something that is happening within a particular group of people, you can say that it is happening among that group.
If something happens among a group of people, it happens within the whole of that group or between the members of that group.
If something such as a feeling, opinion, or situation exists among a group of people, most of them have it or experience it.
gloss_zh: 对…中的大多数成员而论；据…的普遍看法

senses.concept_en: You use among before a noun to mention a group when talking about a smaller group within it.
If something applies to a particular person or thing among others, it also applies to other people or things.
If something is shared among a number of people, some of it is given to all of them.
If people talk, fight, or agree among themselves, they do it together, without involving anyone else.
gloss_zh: 在…内部（谈论、争斗或达成一致）

and.translation:
conj. 和, 与
[计] 与

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two or more words, groups, or clauses.
gloss_zh: （连接两个以上的单词、词组或子句）和，与，同

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two words or phrases that are the same in order to emphasize the degree of something, or to suggest that something continues or increases over a period of time.
gloss_zh: （连接两个相同的单词或短语，以强调某事物的程度、暗示某事继续发生或在一段时间内不断增加）接连，越…越…

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two statements about events when one of the events follows the other.
gloss_zh: （连接两件相继发生的事件）然后，就

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two statements when the second statement continues the point that has been made in the first statement.
gloss_zh: （连接两句话，第二句话的意思是第一句的延伸）则，而

senses.concept_en: You use and to link two clauses when the second clause is a result of the first clause.
gloss_zh: （连接两个从句，表示因果关系）那么，于是

senses.concept_en: You use and to interrupt yourself in order to make a comment on what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （表示停顿，以便对所说的话进行评论）再说，而

senses.concept_en: You use and at the beginning of a sentence to introduce something else that you want to add to what you have just said. Some people think that starting a sentence with and is ungrammatical, but it is now quite common in both spoken and written English.
gloss_zh: （用于句首，引出补充说明）还有，不过

senses.concept_en: You use and to introduce a question which follows logically from what someone has just said.
gloss_zh: （用以引导与某人之谈话有关的问句）那么，还有

senses.concept_en: And is used by broadcasters and people making announcements to change a topic or to start talking about a topic they have just mentioned.
gloss_zh: （广播员等用以转换话题或讨论刚才提及的话题）也

senses.concept_en: You use and to indicate that two numbers are to be added together.
And is used before a fraction that comes after a whole number.
You use and in numbers larger than one hundred, after the words 'hundred' or 'thousand' and before other numbers.
gloss_zh: （用在大于一百的数字中，置于百位或千位之后，十位及个位之前）

any.translation:
a. 任何的
pron. 任何

senses.concept_en: You use any in statements with negative meaning to indicate that no thing or person of a particular type exists, is present, or is involved in a situation.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句）一点，丝毫，若干，任何

senses.concept_en: You use any in questions and conditional clauses to ask whether there is some of a particular thing or some of a particular group of people, or to suggest that there might be.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句或条件从句）若干，一点，什么，任何一个（或一些）

senses.concept_en: You use any in positive statements when you are referring to someone or something of a particular kind that might exist, occur, or be involved in a situation, when their exact identity or nature is not important.
You can also use any to emphasize a comparative adjective or adverb in a negative statement.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句中强调形容词或副词的比较级）任何，丝毫，略微，多少

argue.translation:
vi. 提出理由, 争论, 辩论
vt. 主张, 辩论, 证明, 说服

senses.concept_en: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue .
If you tell someone not to argue with you, you want them to do or believe what you say without protest or disagreement.
If you argue with someone about something, you discuss it with them, with each of you giving your different opinions.
If you argue that something is true, you state it and give the reasons why you think it is true.

If you argue for something, you say why you agree with it, in order to persuade people that it is right. If you argue against something, you say why you disagree with it, in order to persuade people that it is wrong.
If you argue, you support your opinions with evidence in an ordered or logical way.
If you say that no-one can argue with a particular fact or opinion, you are emphasizing that it is obviously true and so everyone must accept it.

arrival.translation:
n. 到达, 抵达, 到达者
[经] 到达, 到达物

senses.concept_en: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, you can refer to their arrival .
When someone starts a new job, you can refer to their arrival in that job.
When something is brought to you or becomes available, you can refer to its arrival .
When a particular time comes or a particular event happens, you can refer to its arrival.
gloss_zh: （某一时间的）到来；（某一事件的）发生

senses.concept_en: You can refer to someone who has just arrived at a place as a new arrival .
When a baby is born, you can refer to its arrival.
You can refer to a baby who has just been born as a new arrival .

derivation.breakdown_zh: arrive 到达 + -al 名词后缀：到达的行为

at.translation:
prep. 在, 向, 对
[计] 地址转换器, 异常传输, 自动订票

senses.concept_en: You use at to indicate the place or event where something happens or is situated.
If someone is at school or college, or at a particular school or college, they go there regularly to study.
If you are at something such as a table, a door, or someone's side, you are next to it or them.
When you are describing where someone or something is, you can say that they are at a certain distance. You can also say that one thing is at an angle in relation to another thing.
gloss_zh: 从相隔（一段距离）的地方;呈…角度

senses.concept_en: If something happens at a particular time, that is the time when it happens or begins to happen.
If you do something at a particular age, you do it when you are that age.
You use at to express a rate, frequency, level, or price.
gloss_zh: 以，达（某一速度、频率、水平或价格）

senses.concept_en: You use at before a number or amount to indicate a measurement.
If you look at someone or something, you look towards them. If you direct an object or a comment at someone, you direct it towards them.
gloss_zh: 朝（某人或某物看）；向（某人掷物）；冲（某人说话）

senses.concept_en: You can use at after verbs such as 'smile' or 'wave' and before nouns referring to people to indicate that you have put on an expression or made a gesture which someone is meant to see or understand.
If you point or gesture at something, you move your arm or head in its direction so that it will be noticed by someone you are with.
If you are working at something, you are dealing with it. If you are aiming at something, you are trying to achieve it.
gloss_zh: 致力于;定位于;期望达到

senses.concept_en: If something is done at someone's invitation or request, it is done as a result of it.
You use at to say that someone or something is in a particular state or condition.
You use at before a possessive pronoun and a superlative adjective to say that someone or something has more of a particular quality than at any other time.
gloss_zh: （用于所有格代词和形容词最高级前，表示某人或某物在此时的某一特征最鲜明）

senses.concept_en: You use at to say how something is being done.
You use at to show that someone is doing something repeatedly.
You use at to indicate an activity or task when saying how well someone does it.
You use at to indicate what someone is reacting to.

back.translation:
a. 后面的
vt. 使后退, 支持
vi. 倒退, 背靠
adv. 向后地
n. 背部, 后面

senses.concept_en: If you move back, you move in the opposite direction to the one in which you are facing or in which you were moving before.
If you go back somewhere, you return to where you were before.
If someone or something is back in a particular state, they were in that state before and are now in it again.
gloss_zh: 恢复原状；回到原来的状态

senses.concept_en: If you give or put something back, you return it to the person who had it or to the place where it was before you took it. If you get or take something back, you then have it again after not having it for a while.
If you put a clock or watch back, you change the time shown on it so that it shows an earlier time, for example when the time changes to winter time or standard time.
If you write or call back, you write to or telephone someone after they have written to or telephoned you. If you look back at someone, you look at them after they have started looking at you.
You can say that you go or come back to a particular point in a conversation to show that you are mentioning or discussing it again.
If something is or comes back, it is fashionable again after it has been unfashionable for some time.
gloss_zh: 再次流行；再度成为潮流

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is kept or situated back from a place, they are at a distance away from it.
If something is held or tied back, it is held or tied so that it does not hang loosely over something.
If you lie or sit back, you move your body backwards into a relaxed sloping or flat position, with your head and body resting on something.
If you look or shout back at someone or something, you turn to look or shout at them when they are behind you.

You use back in expressions like back in London or back at the house when you are giving an account, to show that you are going to start talking about what happened or was happening in the place you mention.
gloss_zh: （表示描述场所的转换）在曾提到过的地方

senses.concept_en: If you talk about something that happened back in the past or several years back, you are emphasizing that it happened quite a long time ago.
If you think back to something that happened in the past, you remember it or try to remember it.
A person's or animal's back is the part of their body between their head and their legs that is on the opposite side to their chest and stomach.
The back of something is the side or part of it that is towards the rear or farthest from the front. The back of something is normally not used or seen as much as the front.
Back is used to refer to the side or part of something that is towards the rear or farthest from the front.
The back of a chair or sofa is the part that you lean against when you sit on it.
The back of something such as a piece of paper or an envelope is the side which is less important.
The back of a book is the part nearest the end, where you can find the index or the notes, for example.
You can use back in expressions such as round the back and out the back to refer generally to the area behind a house or other building.
gloss_zh: （用于round the back, out the back等表达方式中）房屋（或其他建筑物）后的区域

senses.concept_en: You use back in expressions such as out back to refer to the area behind a house or other building. You also use in back to refer to the rear part of something, especially a car or building.
gloss_zh: （用于out back等表达方式中）房屋（或其他建筑物）后的区域；（用于in back等表达方式中）汽车（或建筑物等）的后部

senses.concept_en: In team games such as football and hockey, a back is a player who is concerned mainly with preventing the other team from scoring goals, rather than scoring goals for their own team.
gloss_zh: （足球、曲棍球等运动中的）后卫

senses.concept_en: In American football, a back is a player who stands behind the front line, runs with the ball and attacks rather than defends.
gloss_zh: （美式橄榄球运动中的）进攻后卫

senses.concept_en: If a building backs onto something, the back of it faces in the direction of that thing or touches the edge of that thing.
When you back a car or other vehicle somewhere or when it backs somewhere, it moves backwards.
If you back a person or a course of action, you support them, for example by voting for them or giving them money.
If you back a particular person, team, or horse in a competition, you predict that they will win, and usually you bet money that they will win.
gloss_zh: 预测…获胜；（通常指）下赌注于

senses.concept_en: If a singer is backed by a band or by other singers, they provide the musical background for the singer.

bad.translation:
a. 坏的
n. 坏
adv. 坏地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is bad is unpleasant, harmful, or undesirable.
gloss_zh: 坏的；令人不快的；不合意的；有害的；糟糕的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use bad to indicate that something unpleasant or undesirable is severe or great in degree.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bad idea, decision, or method is not sensible or not correct.
gloss_zh: 不明智的；错误的；不对的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a piece of news, an action, or a sign as bad, you mean that it is unlikely to result in benefit or success.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is bad is of an unacceptably low standard, quality, or amount.
gloss_zh: 不合标准的；劣质的；蹩脚的；不足的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is bad at doing something is not skilful or successful at it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that it is bad that something happens, you mean it is unacceptable, unfortunate, or wrong.
gloss_zh: 难以接受的；令人遗憾的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can say that something is not bad to mean that it is quite good or acceptable, especially when you are rather surprised about this.
gloss_zh: （尤表示惊讶）不错的，不坏的，挺好的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bad person has morally unacceptable attitudes and behaviour.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bad child disobeys rules and instructions or does not behave in a polite and correct way.
gloss_zh: 不听话的；调皮的；捣蛋的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are in a bad mood, you are angry and behave unpleasantly to people.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you feel bad about something, you feel rather sorry or guilty about it.
If you have a bad back, heart, leg, or eye, it is injured, diseased, or weak.
Food that has gone bad is not suitable to eat because it has started to decay.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Bad language is language that contains offensive words such as swear words.
You use because when stating the reason for something.
You use because when stating the explanation for a statement you have just made.

before.translation:
prep. 在...之前
conj. 在...之前
adv. 在前

senses.concept_en: If something happens before a particular date, time, or event, it happens earlier than that date, time, or event
If you do one thing before doing something else, you do it earlier than the other thing.
You use before when you are talking about time. For example, if something happened the day before a particular date or event, it happened during the previous day.
If you do something before someone else can do something, you do it when they have not yet done it.
If someone has done something before, they have done it on a previous occasion. If someone has not done something before, they have never done it.
If there is a period of time or if several things are done before something happens, it takes that amount of time or effort for this thing to happen.
If a particular situation has to happen before something else happens, this situation must happen or exist in order for the other thing to happen.
gloss_zh: （必须先具备某一条件）才能；在…之前（必须具备某一条件）

senses.concept_en: If someone is before something, they are in front of it.
If you tell someone that one place is a certain distance before another, you mean that they will come to the first place first.
If you appear or come before an official person or group, you go there and answer questions.
If something happens before a particular person or group, it is seen by or happens while this person or this group is present.
If you have something such as a journey, a task, or a stage of your life before you, you must do it or live through it in the future.
gloss_zh: 摆在…面前；使面对；使面临

senses.concept_en: When you want to say that one person or thing is more important than another, you can say that they come before the other person or thing.
To begin to do something means to start doing it.
When something begins or when you begin it, it takes place from a particular time onwards.
If you begin with something, or begin by doing something, this is the first thing you do.
gloss_zh: 从…开始；从…着手；首先做（某事）

senses.concept_en: You use begin to mention the first thing that someone says.
If one thing began as another, it first existed in the form of the second thing.
If you say that a thing or place begins somewhere, you are talking about one of its limits or edges.
If a word begins with a particular letter, that is the first letter of that word.
If you say that you cannot begin to imagine, understand, or explain something, you are emphasizing that it is almost impossible to explain, understand, or imagine.
gloss_zh: 无法，难以（解释、理解、想象等）

senses.concept_en: If something is between two things or is in between them, it has one of the things on one side of it and the other thing on the other side.
If people or things travel between two places, they travel regularly from one place to the other and back again.
A relationship, discussion, or difference between two people, groups, or things is one that involves them both or relates to them both.
gloss_zh: 在（两个人、群体或事物）之间

senses.concept_en: If something stands between you and what you want, it prevents you from having it.
If something is between two amounts or ages, it is greater or older than the first one and smaller or younger than the second one.
If something happens between or in between two times or events, it happens after the first time or event and before the second one.
If you must choose between two or more things, you must choose just one of them.
If people or places have a particular amount of something between them, this is the total amount that they have.
When something is divided or shared between people, they each have a share of it.

blast.translation:
n. 一阵风, 爆炸, 枯萎病
vt. 炸, 使枯萎
vi. 炸, 猛攻, 猛烈抨击, 枯萎
blast.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A blast is a big explosion, especially one caused by a bomb.
If something is blasted into a particular place or state, an explosion causes it to be in that place or state. If a hole is blasted in something, it is created by an explosion.
If workers are blasting rock, they are using explosives to make holes in it or destroy it, for example so that a road or tunnel can be built.
To blast someone means to shoot them with a gun.
If someone blasts their way somewhere, they get there by shooting at people or causing an explosion.
gloss_zh: （通过枪击） 冲出（道路）；轰开，炸开（通路）

senses.concept_en: Ifsomething blasts water or air somewhere, it sends out a sudden, powerful stream of it.
If you blast something such as a car horn, or if it blasts, it makes a sudden, loud sound. If something blasts music, or music blasts, the music is very loud.
gloss_zh: （使）（汽车喇叭等）突然发出响亮的声音；（使）（音乐）轰响

senses.concept_en: You can say that a sports player blasts the ball somewhere if he or she gives it a powerful kick or hit.
To blast someone or something means to criticize them strongly.
Some people say 'blast' to show that they are annoyed at something or someone.
If you say that something was a blast, you mean that you enjoyed it very much.
gloss_zh: 有趣的事；开心的事；乐趣

bold.translation:
a. 大胆的
n. 粗体
[计] 粗体

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is bold is not shy or embarrassed in the company of other people.
gloss_zh: （在众人面前）大胆的，放肆的，莽撞的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A bold colour or pattern is very bright and noticeable.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Bold lines or designs are drawn in a clear, strong way.
Bold is print which is thicker and looks blacker than ordinary printed letters.

box.translation:
n. 盒子, 箱, 方框, 一巴掌
vt. 装...入盒中, 装箱, 打耳光
vi. 拳击
[计] 方框

senses.concept_en: A box is a square or rectangular container with hard or stiff sides. Boxes often have lids.
A box is a square or rectangle that is printed or drawn on a piece of paper, a road, or on some other surface.
gloss_zh: （在纸张、道路等上印制或画出的）方格，方框

senses.concept_en: In football, the box is the penalty area of the field.
A box is a small separate area in a theatre or at a sports ground or stadium, where a small number of people can sit to watch the performance or game.
Television is sometimes referred to as the box .
Box is used before a number as a postal address by organizations that receive a lot of mail.
gloss_zh: （用在数字前表示邮政地址）邮政信箱，邮箱

senses.concept_en: Box is a small evergreen tree with dark leaves which is often used to form hedges.
gloss_zh: 黄杨（小型长绿树，常用作篱笆）

senses.concept_en: To box means to fight someone according to the rules of boxing.

boy.translation:
n. 男孩
[法] 男孩, 少年, 儿子

senses.concept_en: A boy is a child who will grow up to be a man.
You can refer to a young man as a boy, especially when talking about relationships between boys and girls.
gloss_zh: 男青年，小伙子（尤用于指青年男女恋爱关系时）

senses.concept_en: Someone's boy is their son.
You can refer to a man as a boy, especially when you are talking about him in an affectionate way.
gloss_zh: 家伙，伙计（尤用于亲切谈论某人时）

senses.concept_en: You can use boy when giving instructions to a horse or dog.
gloss_zh: 家伙，伙计（用于吆喝马或狗时）

senses.concept_en: Some people say 'boy' or 'oh boy' in order to express feelings of excitement or admiration.
gloss_zh: 好家伙（表示激动、羡慕等情感）

break.translation:
n. 休息, 中断, 破裂处, 绝交, 破晓, 突变
vt. 打破, 弄破, 弄坏, 破坏, 违反, 打断, 削弱, 放弃
vi. 破碎, 决裂, 破晓, 突变, 变弱, 暂停
n. 分隔符
[计] 分隔符; 中断; DOS内部命令:设定扫描中断按键的时机

senses.concept_en: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped.
If you break a part of your body such as your leg, your arm, or your nose, or if a bone breaks, you are injured because a bone cracks or splits.
If a surface, cover, or seal breaks or if something breaks it, a hole or tear is made in it, so that a substance can pass through.
gloss_zh: （使）（表层、盖子或密封）破裂；撕开

senses.concept_en: When a tool or piece of machinery breaks or when you break it, it is damaged and no longer works.
If you break a rule, promise, or agreement, you do something that you should not do according to that rule, promise, or agreement.
gloss_zh: 破坏，违反（规则、承诺或协议）

senses.concept_en: If you break free or loose, you free yourself from something or escape from it.
If someone breaks something, especially a difficult or unpleasant situation that has existed for some time, they end it or change it.
gloss_zh: 结束（困难或不利局面）；打破（僵局）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something breaks a silence, they say something or make a noise after a long period of silence.
If there is a break in the cloud or weather, it changes and there is a short period of sunshine or fine weather.
If you break with a group of people or a traditional way of doing things, or you break your connection with them, you stop being involved with that group or stop doing things in that way.
If you break a habit or if someone breaks you of it, you no longer have that habit.
To break someone means to destroy their determination and courage, their success, or their career.
gloss_zh: 瓦解…的决心；使丧失勇气；毁掉…的前程

senses.concept_en: If someone breaks for a short period of time, they rest or change from what they are doing for a short period.

See also:lunch break;tea break; A break is a short period of time when you have a rest or a change from what you are doing, especially if you are working or if you are in a boring or unpleasant situation.
A break is a short holiday.
If you break your journey somewhere, you stop there for a short time so that you can have a rest.
To break the force of something such as a blow or fall means to weaken its effect, for example by getting in the way of it.
When a piece of news breaks, people hear about it from the newspapers, television, or radio.
gloss_zh: （消息在报纸、电视或电台）发布，传播

senses.concept_en: When you break a piece of bad news to someone, you tell it to them, usually in a kind way.
gloss_zh: （通常以委婉的方式）透露，告知（坏消息）

senses.concept_en: A break is a lucky opportunity that someone gets to achieve something.
See also:record-breaking; If you break a record, you beat the previous record for a particular achievement.
See also:daybreak; When day or dawn breaks, it starts to grow light after the night has ended.
When a wave breaks, it passes its highest point and turns downwards, for example when it reaches the shore.
If you break a secret code, you work out how to understand it.
If someone's voice breaks when they are speaking, it changes its sound, for example because they are sad or afraid.
gloss_zh: （因悲伤或害怕嗓音）突变，变调

senses.concept_en: When a boy's voice breaks, it becomes deeper and sounds more like a man's voice.
If the weather breaks or a storm breaks, it suddenly becomes rainy or stormy after a period of sunshine.
In tennis, if you break your opponent's serve, you win a game in which your opponent is serving.
gloss_zh: （网球比赛中）破，赢得（对手的发球局）

breath.translation:
n. 呼吸, 气息, 瞬间
[医] 呼气, 呵气, 口气, 呼吸

senses.concept_en: Your breath is the air that you let out through your mouth when you breathe. If someone has bad breath, their breath smells unpleasant.
When you take a breath, you breathe in once.
If you say that there is not a breath of wind or air, you are emphasizing that there is no wind and the air is very still.
A breath of something, is a small amount of it.

brown.translation:
n. 褐色
a. 褐色的
v. (使)变褐色

senses.concept_en: Something that is brown is the colour of earth or of wood.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can describe a white-skinned person as brown when they have been sitting in the sun until their skin has become darker than usual.
gloss_zh: 皮肤晒成棕色的；皮肤晒黑的

senses.concept_en: If someone browns in the sun they become brown in colour.
A brown person is someone who belongs to a race of people who have brown-coloured skins.
Brown is used to describe grains that have not had their outer layers removed, and foods made from these grains.
When food browns or when you brown food, you cook it, usually for a short time on a high flame.
gloss_zh: （用旺火把）（食物）烤得焦黄；（把…）炸成焦黄色

burst.translation:
n. 破裂, 突发, 爆发
v. 爆裂, 突发, 充满
[计] 二进制位组; 字符组; 脉冲串

senses.concept_en: If something bursts or if you burst it, it suddenly breaks open or splits open and the air or other substance inside it comes out.
If a dam bursts, or if something bursts it, it breaks apart because the force of the river is too great.
If a river bursts its banks, the water rises and goes on to the land.
When a door or lid bursts open, it opens very suddenly and violently because someone pushes it or there is great pressure behind it.
To burst into or out of a place means to enter or leave it suddenly with a lot of energy or force.
If you say that something bursts onto the scene, you mean that it suddenly starts or becomes active, usually after developing quietly for some time.
If you say that someone is about to burst with pride, anger, or another emotion, you are emphasizing the intensity of the emotion they are feeling.
When a firework or bomb bursts in the air, it explodes.
A burst of something is a sudden short period of it.

busy.translation:
a. 忙碌的, 热闹的, 没空的
vt. 使忙
vi. 忙碌
[计] 忙; 忙碌

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When you are busy, you are working hard or concentrating on a task, so that you are not free to do anything else.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A busy time is a period of time during which you have a lot of things to do.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that someone is busy thinking or worrying about something, you mean that it is taking all their attention, often to such an extent that they are unable to think about anything else.
gloss_zh: 全神贯注的；心无旁骛的；埋头于…的

senses.concept_en: If you busy yourself with something, you occupy yourself by dealing with it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A busy place is full of people who are doing things or moving about.
gloss_zh: 热闹的；忙碌的；熙熙攘攘的

senses.concept_en: When a telephone line is busy, you cannot make your call because the line is already being used by someone else.

by.translation:
prep. 被, 经, 由, 在...之旁
adv. 经过, 在近处

senses.concept_en: If something is done by a person or thing, that person or thing does it.
If you say that something such as a book, a piece of music, or a painting is by a particular person, you mean that this person wrote it or created it.
gloss_zh: （图书、音乐、绘画等）由…（创作），出自

senses.concept_en: If you do something by a particular means, you do it using that thing.
If you achieve one thing by doing another thing, your action enables you to achieve the first thing.
You use by in phrases such as 'by chance' or 'by accident' to indicate whether or not an event was planned.
gloss_zh: （用于短语中）由于，出于（偶然或意外）

senses.concept_en: If someone is a particular type of person by nature, by profession, or by birth, they are that type of person because of their nature, their profession, or the family they were born into.
gloss_zh: 就（本性、职业或出身）而言

senses.concept_en: If something must be done by law, it happens according to the law. If something is the case by particular standards, it is the case according to the standards.
gloss_zh: 根据，按照（法律或某种标准）

senses.concept_en: If you say what someone means by a particular word or expression, you are saying what they intend the word or expression to refer to.
If you hold someone or something by a particular part of them, you hold that part.
gloss_zh: （用于表示抓住身体某部位或握住物体某部分）

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is by something else is beside it and close to it.
If a person or vehicle goes by you, they move past you without stopping.
If you stop by a place, you visit it for a short time.
If something happens by a particular time, it happens at or before that time.
If you do something by day, you do it during the day. If you do it by night, you do it during the night.
In arithmetic, you use by before the second number in a multiplication or division sum.
You use by to talk about measurements of area. For example, if a room is twenty feet by fourteen feet, it measures twenty feet in one direction and fourteen feet in the other direction.
gloss_zh: 乘（表示长乘宽得出的居室等的面积）

senses.concept_en: If something increases or decreases by a particular amount, that amount is gained or lost.
Things that are made or sold by the million or by the dozen are made or sold in those quantities.
You use by in expressions such as 'minute by minute' and 'drop by drop' to talk about things that happen gradually, not all at once.

call.translation:
n. 呼叫, 访问, 打电话, 号召, 召集, 要求
vt. 呼叫, 召集, 打电话
vi. 叫喊, 访问, 叫牌
[计] 调用; 呼叫; DOS内部命令:在批处理文件中调用另一个批处理文件

senses.concept_en: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.
gloss_zh: 叫;称呼;将…命名;给…起名字

senses.concept_en: If you call someone or something a particular thing, you suggest they are that thing or describe them as that thing.
If you call something, you say it in a loud voice, because you are trying to attract someone's attention.
If you call someone, you telephone them.
If you call someone such as a doctor or the police, you ask them to come to you, usually by telephoning them.
If you call someone, you ask them to come to you by shouting to them.
When you make a telephone call, you telephone someone.
If someone in authority calls something such as a meeting, rehearsal, or election, they arrange for it to take place at a particular time.
gloss_zh: 召集（会议、排练等）;宣布举行（选举等）

senses.concept_en: If someone is called before a court or committee, they are ordered to appear there, usually to give evidence.
If you call somewhere, you make a short visit there.
When a train, bus, or ship calls somewhere, it stops there for a short time to allow people to get on or off.
gloss_zh: （火车、公共汽车、船舶）停靠,停留

senses.concept_en: To call a game or sporting event means to cancel it, for example because of rain or bad light.
If there is a call for something, someone demands that it should happen.
If there is little or no call for something, very few people want it to be done or provided.
The call of something such as a place is the way it attracts or interests you strongly.
The call of a particular bird or animal is the characteristic sound that it makes.

calmly.translation: adv. 平静地, 安静地, 冷静地

capital.translation:
n. 首都, 大写字母, 资本
a. 首都的, 重要的
capital.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Capital is a large sum of money which you use to start a business, or which you invest in order to make more money.
You can use capital to refer to buildings or machinery which are necessary to produce goods or to make companies more efficient, but which do not make money directly.
gloss_zh: （厂房、机器等）固定资产,资本资产

senses.concept_en: Capital is the part of an amount of money borrowed or invested which does not include interest.
The capital of a country is the city or town where its government or parliament meets.
If a place is the capital of a particular industry or activity, it is the place that is most famous for it, because it happens in that place more than anywhere else.
Capitals or capital letters are written or printed letters in the form which is used at the beginning of sentences or names. 'T', 'B', and 'F' are capitals.
A capital offence is one that is so serious that the person who commits it can be punished by death.
gloss_zh: （犯罪）情节严重的,可判处死刑的

senses.concept_en: A capital is the top part of a stone column, which is sometimes decorated with stone leaves or other patterns.

care.translation:
n. 小心, 照料, 忧虑
vi. 关心, 介意
vt. 在意, 喜欢

senses.concept_en: If you care about something, you feel that it is important and are concerned about it.
If you care for someone, you feel a lot of affection for them.
If you care for someone or something, you look after them and keep them in a good state or condition.
