Children who are in care are looked after by the state because their parents are dead or unable to look after them properly.
If you say that you do not care for something or someone, you mean that you do not like them.
If you say that someone does something when they care to do it, you mean that they do it, although they should do it more willingly or more often.
You can ask someone if they would care for something or if they would care to do something as a polite way of asking if they would like to have or do something.
gloss_zh: 愿意，要（一种有礼貌的询问）

senses.concept_en: If you do something with care, you give careful attention to it because you do not want to make any mistakes or cause any damage.
Your cares are your worries, anxieties, or fears.

carriage.translation:
n. 马车, 客车, 举止, 运输
[经] 搬运费, 运费

senses.concept_en: A carriage is an old-fashioned vehicle, usually for a small number of passengers, which is pulled by horses.
A carriage is one of the separate, long sections of a train that carries passengers.
A carriage is the same as a baby carriage .
Carriage is the cost or action of transporting or delivering goods.
Your carriage is the way you hold your body and head when you are walking, standing, or sitting.

derivation.breakdown_zh: carry 运送 + -age 名词后缀：运费/运输

carry.translation:
n. 进位, 射程, 运载
vt. 携带, 运送, 支持, 传送, 包含
vi. 被携带, 能达到
[计] 进位; 进位数

senses.concept_en: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground.
If you carry something, you have it with you wherever you go.
If something carries a person or thing somewhere, it takes them there.
If a person or animal is carrying a disease, they are infected with it and can pass it on to other people or animals.
If an action or situation has a particular quality or consequence, you can say that it carries it.
If a quality or advantage carries someone into a particular position or through a difficult situation, it helps them to achieve that position or deal with that situation.
gloss_zh: 使达到（目标）;帮助…渡过（难关）

senses.concept_en: If you carry an idea or a method to a particular extent, you use or develop it to that extent.
If a newspaper or poster carries a picture or a piece of writing, it contains it or displays it.
In a debate, if a proposal or motion is carried, a majority of people vote in favour of it.
If a crime carries a particular punishment, a person who is found guilty of that crime will receive that punishment.
If a sound carries, it can be heard a long way away.
If a candidate or party carries a state or area, they win the election in that state or area.
gloss_zh: （候选人或党派）在（某州或某选区）获胜

senses.concept_en: If you carry yourself in a particular way, you walk and move in that way.
If a woman is carrying a child, she is pregnant.

cause.translation:
n. 原因, 目标
vt. 引起, 使产生, 使遭受
cause.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen.
To cause something, usually something bad, means to make it happen.
If you have cause for a particular feeling or action, you have good reasons for feeling it or doing it.
You use cause and effect to talk about the way in which one thing is caused by another.
If one group of people makes common cause with another, they act together in order to achieve a particular aim even though their aims and beliefs are normally very different.
gloss_zh: （为了特定目的）与…联手，与…配合

senses.concept_en: If you say that something is in a good cause or for a good cause, you mean that it is worth doing or giving to because it will help other people, for example by raising money for charity.
gloss_zh: 为了公益事业;为了行善

central.translation:
a. 中央的, 重要的
[医] 中央的, 中心的, 中枢的

senses.concept_en: Something that is central is in the middle of a place or area.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A place that is central is easy to reach because it is in the centre of a city, town, or particular area.
gloss_zh: 位于中央地带的;处于中心的;四通八达的

senses.concept_en: A central group or organization makes all the important decisions that are followed throughout a larger organization or a country.
gloss_zh: 中央的;有最高决策权的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: The central person or thing in a particular situation is the most important one.

derivation.breakdown_zh: centre 中心 + -al 形容词后缀：中心的

change.translation:
n. 变化, 找回的零钱, 找头, 更换
vt. 改变, 更换, 兑换

senses.concept_en: See also:sea change; If there is a change in something, it becomes different.
If you say that something is a change or makes a change, you mean that it is enjoyable because it is different from what you are used to.
If you change from one thing to another, you stop using or doing the first one and start using or doing the second.
When something changes or when you change it, it becomes different.
To change something means to replace it with something new or different.
When you change your clothes or change, you take some or all of your clothes off and put on different ones
A change of clothes is an extra set of clothes that you take with you when you go to stay somewhere or to take part in an activity.
When you change a bed or change the sheets, you take off the dirty sheets and put on clean ones.
When you change a baby or change its nappy or diaper, you take off the dirty one and put on a clean one.
When you change buses, trains, or planes or change, you get off one bus, train, or plane and get on to another in order to continue your journey.
gloss_zh: 转乘，换乘（交通工具）;转车;转机

senses.concept_en: When you change gear or change into another gear, you move the gear lever on a car, bicycle, or other vehicle in order to use a different gear.
Your change is the money that you receive when you pay for something with more money than it costs because you do not have exactly the right amount of money.
See also:small change; Change is coins, rather than paper money.
If you have change for larger notes, bills, or coins, you have the same value in smaller notes, bills, or coins, which you can give to someone in exchange.
When you change money, you exchange it for the same amount of money in a different currency, or in smaller notes, bills, or coins.

check.translation:
n. 检查, 支票, 阻止物, 寄物牌, 象棋中将军
vt. 检查, 阻止, 核对, 寄存, 托运
vi. 逐项相符, 开支票
[计] 复选

senses.concept_en: See also:cross-check; If you check something such as a piece of information or a document, you make sure that it is correct or satisfactory.
If you check on someone or something, you make sure they are in a safe or satisfactory condition.
gloss_zh: 检查，查看（以确保一切正常）

senses.concept_en: If you check something that is written on a piece of paper, you put a mark, like a V with the right side extended, next to it to show that something is correct or has been selected or dealt with.
gloss_zh: 在…上打钩（以确定其正确、已选定或已处理）

senses.concept_en: To check something, usually something bad, means to stop it from spreading or continuing.
If you check yourself or if something checks you, you suddenly stop what you are doing or saying.
When you check your luggage at an airport, you give it to an official so that it can be taken on to your plane.
The check in a restaurant is a piece of paper on which the price of your meal is written and which you are given before you pay.
In a game of chess, you say check when you are attacking your opponent's king.
A pattern of squares, usually of two colours, can be referred to as checks or a check .
gloss_zh: （通常为两种颜色的）方格图案，格子图案

senses.concept_en: A check is the same as a cheque .

chief.translation:
n. 领袖, 酋长, 长官, 主要部分
a. 主要的, 首位的

senses.concept_en: The chief of an organization is the person who is in charge of it.
gloss_zh: （组织机构的）负责人，头儿，首领

senses.concept_en: The chief of a tribe is its leader.
Chief is used in the job titles of the most senior worker or workers of a particular kind in an organization.
gloss_zh: （用于职位头衔）主管的，首席的

senses.concept_en: The chief cause, part, or member of something is the most important one.

city.translation:
n. 城市, 市
[法] 都市, 城市, 市

senses.concept_en: A city is a large town.

claim.translation:
n. 要求, 要求权, 断言, 权利
vt. 要求, 认领, 主张
vi. 提出要求, 主张, 断言
claim.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.
A claim is something which someone says which they cannot prove and which may be false.
If you say that someone claims responsibility or credit for something, you mean they say that they are responsible for it, but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.
gloss_zh: 声称（负有责任或享有功劳）

senses.concept_en: If you claim something, you try to get it because you think you have a right to it.
gloss_zh: 索取，索要（有权拥有的东西）

senses.concept_en: A claim is a demand for something that you think you have a right to.
If someone claims a record, title, or prize, they gain or win it.
gloss_zh: 取得，获得，赢得（纪录、冠军或奖励）

senses.concept_en: If you have a claim on someone or their attention, you have the right to demand things from them or to demand their attention.
If something or someone claims your attention, they need you to spend your time and effort on them.
gloss_zh: 需要，要求（花时间或精力）

senses.concept_en: If you claim money from the government, an insurance company, or another organization, you officially apply to them for it, because you think you are entitled to it according to their rules.
If you claim money or other benefits from your employers, you demand them because you think you deserve or need them.
gloss_zh: （向雇主）索要，索取，讨要（钱、福利）

senses.concept_en: If you say that a war, disease, or accident claims someone's life, you mean that they are killed in it or by it.
gloss_zh: （战争、疾病、事故）夺去（生命），导致（死亡）

clerk.translation:
n. 办事员, 职员, 文书
vi. 当店员

senses.concept_en: A clerk is a person who works in an office, bank, or law court and whose job is to look after the records or accounts.
In a hotel, office, or hospital, a clerk is the person whose job is to answer the telephone and deal with people when they arrive.
A clerk is someone who works in a store.
To clerk means to work as a clerk.
gloss_zh: 做文书工作;当接待员（或店员等）

come.translation:
vi. 过来, 来, 到达, 出现, 开始
interj. 喂

senses.concept_en: When a person or thing comes to a particular place, especially to a place where you are, they move there.

When someone comes to do something, they move to the place where someone else is in order to do it, and they do it. In British English, someone can also come and do something and in American English, someone can come do something. However, you always say that someone came and did something.
gloss_zh: 来（做某事）（除了用 come to do something 表达此意，英国英语中也用 come and do something，美国英语中也用 come do something，但表示过去动作时一定要用 came and did something）

senses.concept_en: When you come to a place, you reach it.
If something comes up to a particular point or down to it, it is tall enough, deep enough, or long enough to reach that point.
If something comes apart or comes to pieces, it breaks into pieces. If something comes off or comes away, it becomes detached from something else.
You use come in expressions such as come to an end or come into operation to indicate that someone or something enters or reaches a particular state or situation.
gloss_zh: 达到，进入（某种状态或境地）

senses.concept_en: If someone comes to do something, they do it at the end of a long process or period of time.
gloss_zh: （经历漫长的过程或时间后）开始（做某事）

senses.concept_en: You can ask how something came to happen when you want to know what caused it to happen or made it possible.
When a particular event or time comes, it arrives or happens.
You can use come before a date, time, or event to mean when that date, time, or event arrives. For example, you can say come the spring to mean 'when the spring arrives'.
gloss_zh: （用于日期、时间或事件之前）当…到来时

senses.concept_en: If a thought, idea, or memory comes to you, you suddenly think of it or remember it.
gloss_zh: 突然被…意识到;突然被…想起

senses.concept_en: If money or property is going to come to you, you are going to inherit or receive it.
If a case comes before a court or tribunal or comes to court, it is presented there so that the court or tribunal can examine it.
gloss_zh: （案件）提交…审理，送交…进行处理

senses.concept_en: If something comes to a particular number or amount, it adds up to it.
If someone or something comes from a particular place or thing, that place or thing is their origin, source, or starting point.
Something that comes from something else or comes of it is the result of it.
If someone comes of a particular family or type of family, they are descended from them.
If someone or something comes first, next, or last, they are first, next, or last in a series, list, or competition.
If a type of thing comes in a particular range of colours, forms, styles, or sizes, it can have any of those colours, forms, styles, or sizes.
gloss_zh: 有，可提供（某种颜色、形状、款式或尺寸）

senses.concept_en: You use come in expressions such as it came as a surprise when indicating a person's reaction to something that happens.
gloss_zh: （用于表示对某事的反应）让人…

senses.concept_en: The next subject in a discussion that you come to is the one that you talk about next.
People say 'Come' to encourage or comfort someone.
To come means to have an orgasm.

complaint.translation:
n. 诉苦, 抱怨, 控诉
[医] 陈诉; 病

senses.concept_en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.
A complaint is a reason for complaining.
gloss_zh: 投诉的原因;不满的原因

senses.concept_en: You can refer to an illness as a complaint, especially if it is not very serious.

compound.translation:
n. 混合物, 复合词, 化合物, 院子
a. 复合的, 混合的, 化合的
vi. 化合, 和解, 妥协
vt. 使复合, 使化合
compound.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: A compound is an enclosed area of land that is used for a particular purpose.
gloss_zh: （作特殊用途的）大院，有围墙的场地

senses.concept_en: In chemistry, a compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements.
If something is a compound of different things, it consists of those things.
Compound is used to indicate that something consists of two or more parts or things.
In grammar, a compound noun, adjective, or verb is one that is made up of two or more words, for example 'fire engine', 'bottle-green', and 'force-feed'.
In grammar, a compound sentence is one that is made up of two or more main clauses.
To compound a problem, difficulty, or mistake means to make it worse by adding to it.

considerable.translation: a. 相当的, 可观的, 重要的
considerable.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Considerable means great in amount or degree.

derivation.breakdown_zh: consider 考虑 + -able 可的：值得考虑的

constantly.translation: adv. 不变地, 不断地, 时常地

container.translation:
n. 容器, 集装箱
[化] 集装箱; 贮存箱; 容器(任何一种)
container.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A container is something such as a box or bottle that is used to hold or store things in.
A container is a very large metal or wooden box used for transporting goods so that they can be loaded easily onto ships and lorries.

control.translation:
n. 控制, 管理, 克制, 控制器, 操纵装置
vt. 控制, 操纵, 抑制
[计] 控制; 控制器
control.tags: zk gk cet4 ky ielts gre

senses.concept_en: Control of an organization, place, or system is the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run.
gloss_zh: （对机构、地方、体系等的）控制权，支配权

senses.concept_en: If you have control of something or someone, you are able to make them do what you want them to do.
If you show control, you prevent yourself behaving in an angry or emotional way.
The people who control an organization or place have the power to take all the important decisions about the way that it is run.
To control a piece of equipment, process, or system means to make it work in the way that you want it to work.
gloss_zh: 控制，操纵（设备、过程、系统等）

senses.concept_en: When a government controls prices, wages, or the activity of a particular group, it uses its power to restrict them.
gloss_zh: 管制，限定，控制（价格、工资、活动等）

senses.concept_en: If you control yourself, or if you control your feelings, voice, or expression, you make yourself behave calmly even though you are feeling angry, excited, or upset.
To control something dangerous means to prevent it from becoming worse or from spreading.
A control is a device such as a switch or lever which you use in order to operate a machine or other piece of equipment.
gloss_zh: 控制按钮;控制装置;操纵装置

senses.concept_en: Controls are the methods that a government uses to restrict increases, for example in prices, wages, or weapons.
Control is used to refer to a place where your documents or luggage are officially checked when you enter a foreign country.
You use could to indicate that someone had the ability to do something. You use could not or couldn't to say that someone was unable to do something
You use could to indicate that something sometimes happened.
You use could have to indicate that something was a possibility in the past, although it did not actually happen.
gloss_zh: 本能够，本可以（表示某事本有可能发生但却并未发生）

senses.concept_en: You use could to indicate that something is possibly true, or that it may possibly happen.
gloss_zh: （表示某事可能属实或可能发生）可能

senses.concept_en: You use could not or couldn't to indicate that it is not possible that something is true.
You use could to talk about a possibility, ability, or opportunity that depends on other conditions.
gloss_zh: （表示可能性、能力或机会）可能

senses.concept_en: You use could when you are saying that one thing or situation resembles another.
You use could, or couldn't in questions, when you are making offers and suggestions.

You use could in questions when you are making a polite request or asking for permission to do something. Speakers sometimes use couldn't instead of 'could' to show that they realize that their request may be refused.
gloss_zh: （用于礼貌地提出请求或征得许可。当说话者意识到可能被拒绝时，可以用 couldn't 代替 could）能，可以

senses.concept_en: People sometimes use structures with if I could or could I as polite ways of interrupting someone or of introducing what they are going to say next.
gloss_zh: （用以礼貌地打断某人或引出将要说的话）请允许我

senses.concept_en: You use could to say emphatically that someone ought to do the thing mentioned, especially when you are annoyed because they have not done it. You use why couldn't in questions to express your surprise or annoyance that someone has not done something.
gloss_zh: （用以强调某人应该做所提及的事情，尤用于当说话者因为其没做该事而生气时）

senses.concept_en: You use could when you are expressing strong feelings about something by saying that you feel as if you want to do the thing mentioned, although you do not do it.
gloss_zh: （表示想要做某事的强烈感情）

senses.concept_en: You use could after 'if' when talking about something that you do not have the ability or opportunity to do, but which you are imagining in order to consider what the likely consequences might be.
gloss_zh: （用在if后以谈论没有能力或机会做但为考虑可能的结果而设想去做的事）

senses.concept_en: You use could not or couldn't with comparatives to emphasize that someone or something has as much as is possible of a particular quality. For example, if you say 'I couldn't be happier', you mean that you are extremely happy.
gloss_zh: （与比较级连用，强调某物或某人具备某种特征的程度）太…，再…不过

senses.concept_en: In speech, you use how could in questions to emphasize that you feel strongly about something bad that has happened.
gloss_zh: 怎么会（用在疑问句中强调对所发生的不愉快之事的感受）

cover.translation:
n. 盖子, 封面, 藉口
vt. 覆盖, 掩饰, 保护, 掩护, 包括
vi. 覆盖

senses.concept_en: If you cover something, you place something else over it in order to protect it, hide it, or close it.
If one thing covers another, it has been placed over it in order to protect it, hide it, or close it.
If one thing covers another, it forms a layer over its surface.
To cover something with or in something else means to put a layer of the second thing over its surface.
If you cover a particular distance, you travel that distance.
To cover someone or something means to protect them from attack, for example by pointing a gun in the direction of people who may attack them, ready to fire the gun if necessary.
Cover is protection from enemy attack that is provided for troops or ships carrying out a particular operation, for example by aircraft.
Cover is trees, rocks, or other places where you shelter from the weather or from an attack, or hide from someone.
An insurance policy that covers a person or thing guarantees that money will be paid by the insurance company in relation to that person or thing.
Insurance cover is a guarantee from an insurance company that money will be paid by them if it is needed.
If a law covers a particular set of people, things, or situations, it applies to them.
If you cover a particular topic, you discuss it in a lecture, course, or book.
gloss_zh: （在演讲、课程或书中）讨论，涉及

senses.concept_en: If journalists, newspapers, or television companies cover an event, they report on it.
If a sum of money covers something, it is enough to pay for it.
A cover is something which is put over an object, usually in order to protect it.
The covers on your bed are the things such as sheets and blankets that you have on top of you.
The cover of a book or a magazine is the outside part of it.
Something that is a cover for secret or illegal activities seems respectable or normal, and is intended to hide the activities.
gloss_zh: （对秘密或违法之事的）掩盖，掩饰

senses.concept_en: If you cover for someone who is doing something secret or illegal, you give false information or do not give all the information you have, in order to protect them.
gloss_zh: （通过提供假信息或不完全的信息来）遮掩，掩盖，包庇

senses.concept_en: If you cover for someone who is ill or away, you do their work for them while they are not there.
To cover a song originally performed by someone else means to record a new version of it.
A cover is the same as a cover version .

crowded.translation: a. 拥挤的, 塞满的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a place is crowded, it is full of people.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a place is crowded, a lot of people live there.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your timetable, your life, or your mind is crowded, it is full of events, activities, or thoughts.

damage.translation:
n. 损害, 伤害
v. 损害

senses.concept_en: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly.
To damage something means to cause it to become less good, pleasant, or successful.
Damage is physical harm that is caused to an object.
Damage consists of the unpleasant effects that something has on a person, situation, or type of activity.
gloss_zh: （对人、情况、行为的）损害，伤害，不良影响

senses.concept_en: If a court of law awards damages to someone, it orders money to be paid to them by a person who has damaged their reputation or property, or who has injured them.

dangerous.translation:
a. 危险的
[法] 危险的, 危害的
dangerous.tags: zk gk cet4 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.
gloss_zh: 危险的;可能带来危害的;不安全的

derivation.breakdown_zh: danger 危险 + -ous 有…的：危险的

dark.translation:
n. 黑暗, 夜, 黄昏, 模糊
a. 黑暗的, 暗的, 深色的, 隐密的, 模糊的, 无知的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When it is dark, there is not enough light to see properly, for example because it is night.
The dark is the lack of light in a place.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as dark, you mean that it is black in colour, or a shade that is close to black.
When you use dark to describe a colour, you are referring to a shade of that colour which is close to black, or seems to have some black in it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has dark hair, eyes, or skin, they have brown or black hair, eyes, or skin.
gloss_zh: （头发、眼睛或肤色）棕色的，黑色的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a white person as dark, you mean that they have brown or black hair, and often a brownish skin.
gloss_zh: （白人）有着棕色（或黑色）头发（且皮肤略带棕色）的，肤色深的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A dark period of time is unpleasant or frightening.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A dark place or area is mysterious and not fully known about.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Dark thoughts are sad, and show that you are expecting something unpleasant to happen.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Dark looks or remarks make you think that the person giving them wants to harm you or that something horrible is going to happen.
gloss_zh: （眼神或话语）阴险的，邪恶的，不祥的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something as dark, you mean that it is related to things that are serious or unpleasant, rather than light-hearted.
gloss_zh: （指与严肃或令人不快的事物相关的）黑色的

day.translation:
n. 天, 日子, 白天, 工作日
[医] 日(一昼夜), 昼, 白天

senses.concept_en: A day is one of the seven twenty-four hour periods of time in a week.
Day is the time when it is light, or the time when you are up and doing things.
You can refer to a particular period in history as a particular day or as particular days .
If you decide to do something, you choose to do it, usually after you have thought carefully about the other possibilities.
If a person or group of people decides something, they choose what something should be like or how a particular problem should be solved.
If an event or fact decides something, it makes it certain that a particular choice will be made or that there will be a particular result.
gloss_zh: （事件或事实）决定，确定（某一选择或结果）

senses.concept_en: If you decide that something is true, you form that opinion about it after considering the facts.
If something decides you to do something, it is the reason that causes you to choose to do it.

delay.translation:
n. 耽搁, 迟滞
v. 耽搁, 延迟
[计] 延迟, 延时
delay.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later
To delay someone or something means to make them late or to slow them down.
If you delay, you deliberately take longer than necessary to do something.
If there is a delay, something does not happen until later than planned or expected.
Delay is a failure to do something immediately or in the required or usual time.

delivery.translation:
n. 递送, 交付, 分娩, 交货, 引渡
[化] 交货额

senses.concept_en: Delivery or a delivery is the bringing of letters, parcels, or other goods to someone's house or to another place where they want them.
gloss_zh: （信件、包裹等的）递送，投递，运送

senses.concept_en: A delivery of something is the goods that are delivered.
gloss_zh: 递送之物;投递之物;运送之物

senses.concept_en: A delivery person or service delivers things to a place.
You talk about someone's delivery when you are referring to the way in which they give a speech or lecture.
Delivery is the process of giving birth to a baby.

derivation.breakdown_zh: deliver 交付 + -y 名词后缀：交付

design.translation:
n. 设计, 图样, 方案, 企图
v. 设计, 计划
design.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.
When someone designs a survey, policy, or system, they plan and prepare it, and decide on all the details of it.
gloss_zh: 设计（调查问卷）;规划;制订

senses.concept_en: Design is the process and art of planning and making detailed drawings of something.
The design of something is the way in which it has been planned and made.
A design is a drawing which someone produces to show how they would like something to be built or made.
A design is a pattern of lines, flowers, or shapes which is used to decorate something.
A design is a general plan or intention that someone has in their mind when they are doing something.
If something is designed for a particular purpose, it is intended for that purpose.

destroy.translation: vt. 破坏, 毁坏, 消灭

senses.concept_en: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.
To destroy someone means to ruin their life or to make their situation impossible to bear.
If an animal is destroyed, it is killed, either because it is ill or because it is dangerous.
gloss_zh: 杀死，消灭（生病或具危险性的动物）

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is difficult is not easy to do, understand, or deal with.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is difficult behaves in an unreasonable and unhelpful way.
gloss_zh: 难相处的;难取悦的;不随和的

do.translation: v. 做, 进行, 完成

senses.concept_en: Do is used to form the negative of main verbs, by putting 'not' after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.
gloss_zh: （在do之后、主动词的原形之前加 not，构成主动词的否定式）

senses.concept_en: Do is used to form questions, by putting the subject after 'do' and before the main verb in its infinitive form, that is the form without 'to'.
gloss_zh: （将主语置于do和主动词的原形之间，构成疑问句）

senses.concept_en: Do is used in question tags.
You use do when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing 'do', or giving a negative or positive answer to a question.
gloss_zh: （对含有do的陈述句或疑问句作肯定或否定回答）

senses.concept_en: Do is used with a negative to tell someone not to behave in a certain way.
gloss_zh: （用在否定句中，表示不让某人做出某种举动）

senses.concept_en: Do is used to give emphasis to the main verb when there is no other auxiliary.
gloss_zh: （在没有其他助动词时，用来强调主动词）

senses.concept_en: Do is used as a polite way of inviting or trying to persuade someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （用以礼貌性地邀请或说服某人做某事）

senses.concept_en: Do can be used to refer back to another verb group when you are comparing or contrasting two things, or saying that they are the same.
gloss_zh: （在进行对比、比较或说明两组事物相同时，用来代替前面的动词词组）

senses.concept_en: You use do after 'so' and 'nor' to say that the same statement is true for two people or groups.
gloss_zh: （与 so 或 nor 连用，表示两人或两组事物的情况相同）

senses.concept_en: When you do something, you take some action or perform an activity or task. Do is often used instead of a more specific verb, to talk about a common action involving a particular thing. For example you can say 'do your teeth' instead of 'brush your teeth'.
gloss_zh: 做，干，进行（常用于代替某个具体的动词）

senses.concept_en: Do can be used to stand for any verb group, or to refer back to another verb group, including one that was in a previous sentence.
gloss_zh: （用来代替任何动词词组或前一个句子中的动词词组）

senses.concept_en: You can use do in a clause at the beginning of a sentence after words like 'what' and 'all', to give special emphasis to the information that comes at the end of the sentence.
gloss_zh: （用于句首从句中 what，all等词之后，以强调句尾的信息）

senses.concept_en: If you do a particular thing with something, you use it in that particular way.
If you do something about a problem, you take action to try to solve it.
If an action or event does a particular thing, such as harm or good, it has that result or effect.
gloss_zh: 造成，产生（好的或坏的结果或影响）

senses.concept_en: You can use do to talk about the degree to which a person, action, or event affects or improves a particular situation.
You can talk about what someone or something does to a person to mean that they have a very harmful effect on them.
If you ask someone what they do, you want to know what their job or profession is.
If you are doing something, you are busy or active in some way, or have planned an activity for some time in the future.
If you say that someone or something does well or badly, you are talking about how successful or unsuccessful they are.
If a person or organization does a particular service or product, they provide that service or sell that product.
You can use do when referring to the speed or rate that something or someone achieves or is able to achieve.
If you do a subject, author, or book, you study them at school or college.
If you do a particular person, accent, or role, you imitate that person or accent, or act that role.
You can use do to say that you are able or unable to behave in a particular way.
If someone does drugs, they take illegal drugs.
If you say that something will do or will do you, you mean that there is enough of it or that it is of good enough quality to meet your requirements or to satisfy you.
A do is a party, dinner party, or other social event.
gloss_zh: 宴会;社交聚会;社交活动

senses.concept_en: A door is a piece of wood, glass, or metal, which is moved to open and close the entrance to a building, room, cupboard, or vehicle.
A door is the space in a wall when a door is open.
The door is the entrance to a large building such as a shop, hotel, or theatre.
gloss_zh: （商店、宾馆、戏院等的）进口，入口

senses.concept_en: Doors is used in expressions such as a few doors down or three doors up to refer to a place that is a particular number of buildings away from where you are.

down.translation:
a. 向下的
adv. 下, 下去, 降下
prep. 往下, 沿着
n. 丘陵, 软毛, 开阔的高地
[计] 向下, 退下命令

senses.concept_en: To go down something such as a slope or a pipe means to go towards the ground or to a lower level.
If you are a particular distance down something, you are that distance below the top or surface of it.
You use down to say that you are looking or facing in a direction that is towards the ground or towards a lower level.
If you put something down, you put it onto a surface.
If you go or look down something such as a road or river, you go or look along it. If you are down a road or river, you are somewhere along it.
If you are travelling to a particular place, you can say that you are going down to that place, especially if you are going towards the south or to a lower level of land.
gloss_zh: （尤指往南方或往地势低的地方）往，朝

senses.concept_en: If you are down a place, you are at that place. If you go down a place, you go to that place. Some people consider this to be non-standard.
If an amount of something goes down, it decreases. If an amount of something is down, it has decreased and is at a lower level than it was.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are feeling down, you are feeling unhappy or depressed.
gloss_zh: 沮丧的;闷闷不乐的;情绪低落的

senses.concept_en: If something is down on paper, it has been written on the paper.
If a piece of equipment, especially a computer system, is down, it is temporarily not working because of a fault.
gloss_zh: （尤指电脑）死机的，发生故障的

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone downs food or a drink, you mean that they eat or drink it.
If something or someone is downed, they fall to the ground because they have been hurt or damaged in some way.
to down tools see
Down consists of the small, soft feathers on young birds. Down is used to make bed-covers and pillows.
See also:downs; Down is very fine hair.

dumb.translation:
a. 哑的, 不说话的, 无声音的
[医] 哑的

senses.concept_en: Someone who is dumb is completely unable to speak.
If someone is dumb on a particular occasion, they cannot speak because they are angry, shocked, or surprised.
gloss_zh: （在某种场合下因愤怒或惊讶而）说不出话的,哑口无言的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you call a person dumb, you mean that they are stupid or foolish.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is dumb, you think that it is silly and annoying.
gloss_zh: 愚蠢的;令人心烦的;令人恼火的

senses.concept_en: Something that is dumb is done or expressed without words.
gloss_zh: 无声的;无言的;不用言语表达的

each.translation:
a. 每个, 每一
adv. 每个
pron. 每个, 个人, 各自

senses.concept_en: If you refer to each thing or each person in a group, you are referring to every member of the group and considering them as individuals.
If you refer to each one of the members of a group, you are emphasizing that something applies to every one of them.
You use each other when you are saying that each member of a group does something to the others or has a particular connection with the others.

early.translation:
a. 早的, 早熟的
adv. 很早, 初

senses.concept_en: Early means before the usual time that a particular event or activity happens.
gloss_zh: （指在通常的时间之前）早,提早,提前

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Early means near the beginning of a day, week, year, or other period of time.
Early means before the time that was arranged or expected.
gloss_zh: （指在原定或预计的时间之前）早，提早,提前

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Early means near the beginning of a period in history, or in the history of something such as the world, a society, or an activity.
gloss_zh: （历史时期或事物存续期）早期的,初期的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Early means near the beginning of something such as a piece of work or a process.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Early refers to plants which flower or crop before or at the beginning of the main season.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Early reports or indications of something are the first reports or indications about it.

efficient.translation: a. 有效率的, 能干的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

end.translation:
n. 结束, 终点, 目标, 末端, 梢, 死亡, 残余
v. 结束, 终结, 终止
[计] 端; 结束

senses.concept_en: The end of something such as a period of time, an event, a book, or a film is the last part of it or the final point in it.
When a situation, process, or activity ends, or when something or someone ends it, it reaches its final point and stops.
An end to something or the end of it is the act or result of stopping it so that it does not continue any longer.
If you say that someone or something ends a period of time in a particular way, you are indicating what the final situation was like. You can also say that a period of time ends in a particular way.
If a period of time ends, it reaches its final point.
If something such as a book, speech, or performance ends with a particular thing or the writer or performer ends it with that thing, its final part consists of the thing mentioned.
gloss_zh: （书、演说、表演等）以…为结尾，以…结束

senses.concept_en: If a situation or event ends in a particular way, it has that particular result.
The two ends of something long and narrow are the two points or parts of it that are furthest away from each other.
The end of a long, narrow object such as a finger or a pencil is the tip or smallest edge of it, usually the part that is furthest away from you.
If an object ends with or in a particular thing, it has that thing on its tip or point, or as its last part.
A journey, road, or river that ends at a particular place stops there and goes no further.
End is used to refer to either of the two extreme points of a scale, or of something that you are considering as a scale.
The other end is one of two places that are connected because people are communicating with each other by telephone or writing, or are travelling from one place to the other.
gloss_zh: （联系、旅行等的）一端，一方，一头

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a particular end of a project or piece of work, you mean a part or aspect of it, for example a part of it that is done by a particular person or in a particular place.
An end is the purpose for which something is done or towards which you are working.
If you say that something ends at a particular point, you mean that it is applied or exists up to that point, and no further.
gloss_zh: 只存在于，仅限于（某一点）

senses.concept_en: You can refer to someone's death as their end, especially when you are talking about the way that they died or might die.
If you end by doing something or end in a particular state, you do that thing or get into that state even though you did not originally intend to.

engine.translation:
n. 引擎, 发动机, 机车
vt. 安装发动机于

senses.concept_en: The engine of a car or other vehicle is the part that produces the power which makes the vehicle move.
An engine is also the large vehicle that pulls a railway train.

engineer.translation:
n. 工程师, 工兵
vt. 设计, 监造, 精明地处理, 策划
engineer.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: See also:chemical engineer;civil engineer;electrical engineer;sound engineer; An engineer is a person who uses scientific knowledge to design, construct, and maintain engines and machines or structures such as roads, railways, and bridges.
An engineer is a person who repairs mechanical or electrical devices.
gloss_zh: 机械修理工;电气修理工；技师

senses.concept_en: An engineer is a person who is responsible for maintaining the engine of a ship while it is at sea.
When a vehicle, bridge, or building is engineered, it is planned and constructed using scientific methods.
gloss_zh: 设计制造（车辆、桥梁、建筑物等）

senses.concept_en: If you engineer an event or situation, you arrange for it to happen, in a clever or indirect way.

entire.translation:
n. 整个, 全部
a. 全体的, 完全的, 全部的

senses.concept_en: You use entire when you want to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something, for example, the whole of a place, time, or population.

escape.translation:
n. 逃亡, 避难设备, 逃跑
vi. 逃脱, 避开, 溜走
vt. 逃避, 避免, 被...忘掉

senses.concept_en: If you escape from a place, you succeed in getting away from it.
Someone's escape is the act of escaping from a particular place or situation.
You can say that you escape when you survive something such as an accident.
If something is an escape, it is a way of avoiding difficulties or responsibilities.

You can use escape to describe things which allow you to avoid difficulties or problems. For example, an escape route is an activity or opportunity that lets you improve your situation. An escape clause is part of an agreement that allows you to avoid having to do something that you do not want to do.
gloss_zh: 使逃避困难的;使规避问题的

senses.concept_en: If something escapes you or escapes your attention, you do not know about it, do not remember it, or do not notice it.
gloss_zh: 为…所不知;逃过…的注意;被…忘记

senses.concept_en: When gas, liquid, or heat escapes, it comes out from a pipe, container, or place.
gloss_zh: （气体、液体、热量等）泄露，逸出，露出

senses.concept_en: You use every to indicate that you are referring to all the members of a group or all the parts of something and not only some of them.
You use every in order to say how often something happens or to indicate that something happens at regular intervals.
You use every in front of a number when you are saying what proportion of people or things something happens to or applies to.
You can use every before some nouns, for example 'sign', 'effort', 'reason', and 'intention' in order to emphasize what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （用于名词前表示强调）充足的，完全的

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone's every whim, wish, or desire will be satisfied, you are emphasizing that everything they want will happen or be provided.
gloss_zh: （幻想、愿望、欲望等）所有的，全部的

execute.translation:
vt. 执行, 实行, 完成, 处死, 制成
[计] 执行
execute.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: To execute someone means to kill them as a punishment for a serious crime.
If you execute a plan, you carry it out.
If you execute a difficult action or movement, you successfully perform it.
When someone executes a work of art, they make or produce it, using an idea as a basis.
If you explain something, you give details about it or describe it so that it can be understood.
If you explain something that has happened, you give people reasons for it, especially in an attempt to justify it.

explosion.translation:
n. 爆发, 激增, 爆炸(声)
[化] 爆炸

senses.concept_en: An explosion is a sudden, violent burst of energy, for example one caused by a bomb.
Explosion is the act of deliberately causing a bomb or similar device to explode.
An explosion is a large rapid increase in the number or amount of something.
An explosion is a sudden violent expression of someone's feelings, especially anger.
gloss_zh: （感情的）迸发，突然发作;（尤指）勃然大怒

senses.concept_en: An explosion is a sudden and serious political protest or violence.
An explosion is a sudden very loud noise.

external.translation:
n. 外部, 外面
a. 外部的, 客观的, 表面的

senses.concept_en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.
External means involving or intended for foreign countries.
External means happening or existing in the world in general and affecting you in some way.
External experts, for example external examiners, come into an organization from outside in order to do a particular job fairly and impartially, or to check that a particular job was done properly.

extra.translation:
n. 额外的事物, 另外的收费
a. 额外的, 特别的
adv. 额外地, 特别地, 非常地

senses.concept_en: You use extra to describe an amount, person, or thing that is added to others of the same kind, or that can be added to others of the same kind.
If something is extra, you have to pay more money for it in addition to what you are already paying for something.
gloss_zh: 费用另计的；额外收费的

senses.concept_en: Extras are additional amounts of money that are added to the price that you have to pay for something.
Extras are things which are not necessary in a situation, activity, or object, but which make it more comfortable, useful, or enjoyable.
The extras in a film are the people who play unimportant parts, for example as members of a crowd.
gloss_zh: （电影中的）临时演员，群众演员

senses.concept_en: You can use extra in front of adjectives and adverbs to emphasize the quality that they are describing.

eye.translation:
n. 眼睛, 视力, 看
vt. 看, 注视

senses.concept_en: Your eyes are the parts of your body with which you see.
If you eye someone or something in a particular way, you look at them carefully in that way.
You use eye when you are talking about a person's ability to judge things or about the way in which they are considering or dealing with things.
An electric eye or infrared eye is a device which can recognize the presence of people or objects by detecting the light or heat coming from them.
People sometimes talk about the eye of the camera when they are talking about something being filmed or photographed, or the way something appears in a photograph or film.
An eye on a potato is one of the dark spots from which new stems grow.
An eye is a small metal loop which a hook fits into, as a fastening on a piece of clothing.
The eye of a needle is the small hole at one end which the thread passes through.
The eye of a storm, tornado, or hurricane is the centre of it.

face.translation:
n. 脸, 面容, 正面, 外观
vt. 面对, 朝, 正视, 面临
vi. 朝, 向
[计] 现场可改变的控制元件

senses.concept_en: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.
If your face is happy, sad, or serious, for example, the expression on your face shows that you are happy, sad, or serious.
The face of a cliff, mountain, or building is a vertical surface or side of it.
gloss_zh: 崖面;山侧;（建筑物的）墙面

senses.concept_en: The face of a clock or watch is the surface with the numbers or hands on it, which shows the time.
If you say that the face of an area, institution, or field of activity is changing, you mean its appearance or nature is changing.
gloss_zh: （地区、机构或活动领域的）外观，面貌

senses.concept_en: If you refer to something as the particular face of an activity, belief, or system, you mean that it is one particular aspect of it, in contrast to other aspects.

If you lose face, you do something which makes you appear weak and makes people respect or admire you less. If you do something in order to save face, you do it in order to avoid appearing weak and losing people's respect or admiration.
If someone or something faces a particular thing, person, or direction, they are positioned opposite them or are looking in that direction.
If you face someone or something, you turn so that you are looking at them.
If you have to face a person or group, you have to stand or sit in front of them and talk to them, although it may be difficult and unpleasant.
If you face or are faced with something difficult or unpleasant, or if it faces you, it is going to affect you and you have to deal with it.
If you face the truth or face the facts, you accept that something is true. If you face someone with the truth or with the facts, you try to make them accept that something is true.
gloss_zh: （使）直面，接受，正视（真理或事实等）

senses.concept_en: If you cannot face something, you do not feel able to do it because it seems so difficult or unpleasant.

faint.translation:
n. 昏厥, 昏倒
a. 模糊的, 微弱的, 无力的
vi. 昏倒, 变得微弱

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A faint sound, colour, mark, feeling, or quality has very little strength or intensity.
gloss_zh: （声音、颜色、标记、感觉或特性）微弱的，暗淡的，虚弱的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A faint attempt at something is one that is made without proper effort and with little enthusiasm.
gloss_zh: 不尽力的;敷衍的;半心半意的

senses.concept_en: If you faint, you lose consciousness for a short time, especially because you are hungry, or because of pain, heat, or shock.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is faint feels weak and unsteady as if they are about to lose consciousness.

fast.translation:
a. 快速的, 紧的
adv. 很快地, 紧紧地, 彻底地
n. 绝食, 斋戒
vi. 绝食, 斋戒

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Fast means happening, moving, or doing something at great speed. You also use fast in questions or statements about speed.
You use fast to say that something happens without any delay.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a watch or clock is fast, it is showing a time that is later than the real time.
If you hold something fast, you hold it tightly and firmly. If something is stuck fast, it is stuck very firmly and cannot move.
If you hold fast to a principle or idea, or if you stand fast, you do not change your mind about it, even though people are trying to persuade you to.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If colours or dyes are fast, they do not come out of the fabrics they are used on when they get wet.
gloss_zh: （颜色或染料）不褪色的，不掉色的

senses.concept_en: A fast way of life is one which involves a lot of enjoyable and expensive or dangerous activities.
gloss_zh: 骄奢淫逸的;刺激而快乐的

senses.concept_en: If you fast, you eat no food for a period of time, usually for either religious or medical reasons, or as a protest.

fear.translation:
n. 恐怖, 害怕, 担心
v. 害怕, 恐惧, 为...担心, 敬畏

senses.concept_en: Fear is the unpleasant feeling you have when you think that you are in danger.
If you fear someone or something, you are frightened because you think that they will harm you.
A fear is a thought that something unpleasant might happen or might have happened.
If you fear something unpleasant or undesirable, you are worried that it might happen or might have happened.
If you say that there is a fear that something unpleasant or undesirable will happen, you mean that you think it is possible or likely.
gloss_zh: （坏事发生的）可能性，机会，几率

senses.concept_en: If you fear for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.
If you have fears for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.
If you fear to do something, you are afraid to do it or you do not wish to do it.
You say that you fear that a situation is the case when the situation is unpleasant or undesirable, and when you want to express sympathy, sorrow, or regret about it.

feel.translation:
vt. 感觉, 觉得, 触摸, 以为
vi. 有知觉, 摸索, 同情
n. 感觉, 觉得, 触摸

senses.concept_en: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.
If you talk about how an experience or event feels, you talk about the emotions and sensations connected with it.
gloss_zh: （经历或事件）给人…感觉，令人有…感觉

senses.concept_en: If you talk about how an object feels, you talk about the physical quality that you notice when you touch or hold it. For example, if something feels soft, you notice that it is soft when you touch it.
If you talk about how the weather feels, you describe the weather, especially the temperature or whether or not you think it is going to rain or snow.
If you feel an object, you touch it deliberately with your hand, so that you learn what it is like, for example what shape it is or whether it is rough or smooth.
If you can feel something, you are aware of it because it is touching you.
If you feel something happening, you become aware of it because of the effect it has on your body.
If you feel yourself doing something or being in a particular state, you are aware that something is happening to you which you are unable to control.
If you feel the presence of someone or something, you become aware of them, even though you cannot see or hear them.
If you feel that something is the case, you have a strong idea in your mind that it is the case.
If you feel that you should do something, you think that you should do it.
If you talk about how you feel about something, you talk about your opinion, attitude, or reaction to it.
If you feel like doing something or having something, you want to do it or have it because you are in the right mood for it and think you would enjoy it.
If you feel the effect or result of something, you experience it.
gloss_zh: 感受，体会，承受（某种后果或影响）

senses.concept_en: The feel of something, for example a place, is the general impression that it gives you.

finish.translation:
n. 完成, 结束, 末道漆, 磨光, 完美
vt. 完成, 结束, 用完, 毁掉
vi. 结束
[计] 完成

senses.concept_en: When you finish doing or dealing with something, you do or deal with the last part of it, so that there is no more for you to do or deal with.
When you finish something that you are making or producing, you reach the end of making or producing it, so that it is complete.
When something such as a course, film, or sale finishes, especially at a planned time, it ends.

You say that someone or something finishes a period of time or an event in a particular way to indicate what the final situation was like. You can also say that a period of time or an event finishes in a particular way.
If someone finishes second, for example, in a race or competition, they are in second place at the end of the race or competition.
To finish means to reach the end of saying something.
The finish of something is the end of it or the last part of it.
The finish of a race is the end of it.
See also:finished; If the surface of something that has been made has a particular kind of finish, it has the appearance or texture mentioned.

first.translation:
adv. 首先, 第一, 优先
a. 第一的
num. 第一
n. 开始, 第一

senses.concept_en: The first thing, person, event, or period of time is the one that happens or comes before all the others of the same kind.
gloss_zh: 最早的;最先的;第一位的

senses.concept_en: If you do something first, you do it before anyone else does, or before you do anything else.
When something happens or is done for the first time, it has never happened or been done before.
An event that is described as a first has never happened before and is important or exciting.
The first you hear of something or the first you know about it is the time when you first become aware of it.
You use first when you are talking about what happens in the early part of an event or experience, in contrast to what happens later.
In order to emphasize your determination not to do a particular thing, you can say that rather than do it, you would do something else first .
gloss_zh: （强调不愿意做某事）宁可，宁愿

senses.concept_en: You use first when you are about to give the first in a series of items.
The first thing, person, or place in a line is the one that is nearest to you or nearest to the front.
gloss_zh: （一列中）离得最近的，最前面的

senses.concept_en: You use first to refer to the best or most important thing or person of a particular kind.
First is used in the title of the job or position of someone who has a higher rank than anyone else with the same basic job title.
gloss_zh: （用于工作或职位的头衔中）最高的

senses.concept_en: In British universities, a first is an honours degree of the highest standard.
gloss_zh: （英国大学的）优等学位，一级荣誉学位

floor.translation:
n. 地板, 楼层, 底部, 底价
vt. 铺地板, 打倒
n. 地面, 地板, 基底
[计] 基底

senses.concept_en: The floor of a room is the part of it that you walk on.
A floor of a building is all the rooms that are on a particular level.
The ocean floor is the ground at the bottom of an ocean. The valley floor is the ground at the bottom of a valley.
The place where official debates and discussions are held, especially between members of parliament, is referred to as the floor .
In a debate or discussion, the floor is the people who are listening to the arguments being put forward but who are not among the main speakers.
The floor of a stock exchange is the large open area where trading is done.
The floor in a place such as a club or disco is the area where people dance.
If you are floored by something, you are unable to respond to it because you are so surprised by it.
See also:floored;flooring;dance floor;first floor;ground floor;shop floor; If someone is floored, especially in boxing, they are hit so hard that they fall over.
gloss_zh: （尤指在拳击比赛中）打倒，击倒

foot.translation:
n. 脚, 步调, 英尺, 底部, 末尾, 步兵
vt. 走在...上, 给...换底, 支付
vi. 跳舞, 步行, 总计

senses.concept_en: Your feet are the parts of your body that are at the ends of your legs, and that you stand on.
The foot of something is the part that is farthest from its top.
The foot of a bed is the end nearest to the feet of the person lying in it.

A foot is a unit for measuring length, height, or depth, and is equal to 12 inches or 30.48 centimetres. When you are giving measurements, the form 'foot' is often used as the plural instead of the plural form 'feet'.
gloss_zh: 英尺（相当于 12 英寸或 30.48 厘米）

senses.concept_en: A foot brake or foot pump is operated by your foot rather than by your hand.
gloss_zh: （刹车或泵）用脚操作的，脚踏的

senses.concept_en: A foot patrol or foot soldiers walk rather than travelling in vehicles or on horseback.
See also:footing; In poetry, a foot is one of the basic units of rhythm into which a line is divided.

for.translation:
prep. 为, 因为, 至于
conj. 因为
[计] DOS批处理命令:对一组参数重复执行指定的命令

senses.concept_en: If something is for someone, they are intended to have it or benefit from it.
If you work or do a job for someone, you are employed by them.
If you speak or act for a particular group or organization, you represent them.
If someone does something for you, they do it so that you do not have to do it.
If you feel a particular emotion for someone, you feel it on their behalf.
If you feel a particular emotion for someone or something, they are the object of that emotion, and you feel it when you think about them.
You use for after words such as 'time', 'space', 'money', or 'energy' when you say how much there is or whether there is enough of it in order to be able to do or use a particular thing.
If something is for sale, hire, or use, it is available to be sold, hired, or used.
You use for when you state or explain the purpose of an object, action, or activity.
You use for after nouns expressing reason or cause.
You can use for to introduce a clause which gives the reason why you made the statement in the main clause.
You can use for to introduce the cause of the fact that you have just mentioned.
For is used in conditional sentences, in expressions such as 'if not for' and 'were it not for', to introduce the only thing which prevents the main part of the sentence from being true.
gloss_zh: （用于条件句中）如果不是为了，要不是

senses.concept_en: You use for to say how long something lasts or continues.
You use for to say how far something extends.
If something is bought, sold, or done for a particular amount of money, that amount of money is its price.
If something is planned for a particular time, it is planned to happen then.
If you do something for a particular occasion, you do it on that occasion or to celebrate that occasion.
If you leave for a particular place or if you take a bus, train, plane, or boat for a place, you are going there.
You use for when you make a statement about something in order to say how it affects or relates to someone, or what their attitude to it is.
After some adjective, noun, and verb phrases, you use for to introduce the subject of the action indicated by the following infinitive verb.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词、名词和动词短语后，引出其后动词不定式的主语）

senses.concept_en: You use for when you say that an aspect of something or someone is surprising in relation to other aspects of them.
gloss_zh: 就…而言（表示相对来说不寻常）

senses.concept_en: If you say that you are for a particular activity, you mean that this is what you want or intend to do.
If you say that something is not for you, you mean that you do not enjoy it or that it is not suitable for you.
If it is for you to do something, it is your responsibility or right to do it.
gloss_zh: （表示负有责任或享有权利）由…

senses.concept_en: If you are for something, you agree with it or support it.
You use for after words such as 'argue', 'case', 'evidence', or 'vote' in order to introduce the thing that is being supported or proved.
gloss_zh: （用于 argue, case, evidence, vote 等词后，引出所支持或被证明之事）

senses.concept_en: For is the preposition that is used after some nouns, adjectives, or verbs in order to introduce more information or to indicate what a quality, thing, or action relates to.
gloss_zh: （置于某些名词、形容词或动词后，引出更多信息或与某性质、事物或行为相关的事物）

senses.concept_en: To be named for someone means to be given the same name as them.
You use for with 'every' when you are stating a ratio, to introduce one of the things in the ratio.
gloss_zh: （与 every 连用，引出比率）每…（就有…）

senses.concept_en: You can use for in expressions such as pound for pound or mile for mile when you are making comparisons between the values or qualities of different things.
gloss_zh: （用于比较）每镑对每镑/每英里对每英里

senses.concept_en: If a word or expression has the same meaning as another word or expression, you can say that the first one is another word or expression for the second one.
You use for in a piece of writing when you mention information which will be found somewhere else.
gloss_zh: （引出可在其他地方找到的信息）至于，对于

senses.concept_en: Fortunately is used to introduce or indicate a statement about an event or situation that is good.

forward.translation:
a. 向前的, 早的, 迅速的, 在前的, 进步的
vt. 促进...的生长, 转寄, 运送
adv. 向前地
[计] 前推, 转信

senses.concept_en: If you move or look forward, you move or look in a direction that is in front of you. In British English, you can also move or look forwards .
Forward means in a position near the front of something such as a building or a vehicle.
If you say that someone looks forward, you approve of them because they think about what will happen in the future and plan for it. In British English, you can also say that someone looks forwards .
If you put a clock or watch forward, you change the time shown on it so that it shows a later time, for example when the time changes to summer time or daylight saving time.
When you are referring to a particular time, if you say that something was true from that time forward, you mean that it became true at that time, and continued to be true afterwards.
You use forward to indicate that something progresses or improves. In British English, you can also use forwards .
gloss_zh: 向前地;前进地;有进展地

senses.concept_en: If you forward something, you cause it to progress or improve.
If something or someone is put forward, or comes forward, they are suggested or offered as suitable for a particular purpose.
If a letter or message is forwarded to someone, it is sent to the place where they are, after having been sent to a different place earlier.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as forward, you mean that they speak very confidently and honestly but they do not always show enough respect for the person they are talking to.
See also:centre-forward; In football, basketball, or hockey, a forward is a player whose usual position is in the opponents' half of the field, and whose usual job is to attack or score goals.
gloss_zh: （足球、篮球或曲棍球等运动的）前锋

from.translation: prep. 从, 来自, 根据

senses.concept_en: If something comes from a particular person or thing, or if you get something from them, they give it to you or they are the source of it.
Someone who comes from a particular place lives in that place or originally lived there. Something that comes from a particular place was made in that place.
A person from a particular organization works for that organization.
If someone or something moves or is moved from a place, they leave it or are removed, so that they are no longer there.
If you take one thing or person from another, you move that thing or person so that they are no longer with the other or attached to the other.
If you take something from an amount, you reduce the amount by that much.
From is used in expressions such as away from or absent from to say that someone or something is not present in a place where they are usually found.
If you return from a place or an activity, you return after being in that place or doing that activity.
If you are back from a place or activity, you have left it and have returned to your former place.
If you see or hear something from a particular place, you are in that place when you see it or hear it.
If something hangs or sticks out from an object, it is attached to it or held by it.
You can use from when giving distances. For example, if a place is fifty miles from another place, the distance between the two places is fifty miles.
If a road or railway line goes from one place to another, you can travel along it between the two places.
From is used, especially in the expression made from, to say what substance has been used to make something.
You can use from when you are talking about the beginning of a period of time.
You say from one thing to another when you are stating the range of things that are possible, or when saying that the range of things includes everything in a certain category.
If something changes from one thing to another, it stops being the first thing and becomes the second thing.
You use from after some verbs and nouns when mentioning the cause of something.
You use from when you are giving the reason for an opinion.
From is used after verbs with meanings such as 'protect', 'free', 'keep', and 'prevent' to introduce the action that does not happen, or that someone does not want to happen.
gloss_zh: （用于 protect, free, keep, prevent 等动词后）免于

further.translation:
a. 更远的, 此外的, 更多的
vt. 促进, 增进, 助长
adv. 更进一步地, 更远地, 此外

senses.concept_en: Further means to a greater extent or degree.
gloss_zh: 进一步地;在更大程度上;在更大范围内

senses.concept_en: If you go or get further with something, or take something further, you make some progress.
gloss_zh: （发展中）进一步地，向前推进地

senses.concept_en: If someone goes further in a discussion, they make a more extreme statement or deal with a point more thoroughly.
gloss_zh: （讨论中）进一步地，更极端地，更彻底地

senses.concept_en: A further thing, number of things, or amount of something is an additional thing, number of things, or amount.
Further means a greater distance than before or than something else.
Further is used in expressions such as 'further back' and 'further ahead' to refer to a point in time that is earlier or later than the time you are talking about.
If you further something, you help it to progress, to be successful, or to be achieved.
You use further to introduce a statement that relates to the same general topic and that gives additional information or makes an additional point.

gather.translation:
n. 集合, 聚集
vi. 聚集, 集合, 渐增
vt. 使聚集, 搜集, 积聚

senses.concept_en: If people gather somewhere or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.
If you gather things, you collect them together so that you can use them.
If you gather information or evidence, you collect it, especially over a period of time and after a lot of hard work.
gloss_zh: （尤指经过一段时间的辛苦工作）收集，搜集（情报、证据等）

senses.concept_en: If something gathers speed, momentum, or force, it gradually becomes faster or more powerful.
gloss_zh: 逐渐增加（速度、动力、力量等）

senses.concept_en: When you gather something such as your strength, courage, or thoughts, you make an effort to prepare yourself to do something.
gloss_zh: 集中（精力、思想等）；鼓起（勇气）；振作（精神）

senses.concept_en: You use gather in expressions such as 'I gather' and 'as far as I can gather' to introduce information that you have found out, especially when you have found it out in an indirect way.
gloss_zh: （用于引出已发现的信息，尤其是间接获得的信息）据我所知，据我了解
collocations: as far as I can gather

senses.concept_en: If you gather fabric or cloth, you make a row of very small folds in it by sewing a thread through it and then pulling the thread tight.

give.translation:
n. 弹性, 适应性
vt. 给, 授予, 供给, 产生, 发表, 付出, 献出, 让出
vi. 捐赠, 支持不住, 让步

senses.concept_en: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as 'She smiled'.
gloss_zh: （与表示身体动作的名词连用，表示该动作）

senses.concept_en: You use give to say that a person does something for another person. For example, if you give someone a lift, you take them somewhere in your car.
You use give with nouns that refer to information, opinions, or greetings to indicate that something is communicated. For example, if you give someone some news, you tell it to them.
gloss_zh: （与表示信息、意见、问候等的名词连用）提供，给出，传递，告诉

senses.concept_en: You use give to say how long you think something will last or how much you think something will be.
People use give in expressions such as I don't give a damn to show that they do not care about something.
If someone or something gives you a particular idea or impression, it causes you to have that idea or impression.
gloss_zh: 使产生（某种想法或印象）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something gives you a particular physical or emotional feeling, it makes you experience it.
gloss_zh: 使身体感到…；使产生（某种情绪）

senses.concept_en: If you give a performance or speech, you perform or speak in public.
If you give something thought or attention, you think about it, concentrate on it, or deal with it.
If you give a party or other social event, you organize it.
If you give someone something that you own or have bought, you provide them with it, so that they have it or can use it.
If you give someone something that you are holding or that is near you, you pass it to them, so that they are then holding it.
To give someone or something a particular power or right means to allow them to have it.
If something gives, it collapses or breaks under pressure.
See also:given; You say that you are given to understand or believe that something is the case when you do not want to say how you found out about it, or who told you.

government.translation:
n. 政府, 内阁
[经] 政府, 政治, 政体
government.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: The government of a country is the group of people who are responsible for governing it.
Government consists of the activities, methods, and principles involved in governing a country or other political unit.

have.translation:
vt. 有, 怀有, 拿, 进行
aux. 已经

senses.concept_en: You use the forms have and has with a past participle to form the present perfect tense of verbs.
gloss_zh: （have 和 has 与过去分词连用构成动词的现在完成时）

senses.concept_en: You use the form had with a past participle to form the past perfect tense of verbs.
gloss_zh: （had 与过去分词连用构成动词的过去完成时）

senses.concept_en: Have is used in question tags.
You use have when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing 'have', 'has', or 'had', or answering a question.
gloss_zh: （用于对带有 have,has 或 had 的句子作肯定或否定回答）

senses.concept_en: The form having with a past participle can be used to introduce a clause in which you mention an action which had already happened before another action began.
gloss_zh: （having 和过去分词连用，所引导的分句中提到的动作发生在另一个动作开始之前）

senses.concept_en: You can use have followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would be possible to use the same word as a verb. For example, you can say 'I had a look at the photos' instead of 'I looked at the photos.'
gloss_zh: （have 后接名词代替该名词作动词的用法，描述某一动作或事件）
collocations: I had a look at the photos

senses.concept_en: In normal spoken or written English, people use have with a wide range of nouns to talk about actions and events, often instead of a more specific verb. For example people are more likely to say 'we had ice cream' or 'he's had a shock' than 'we ate ice cream', or 'he's suffered a shock'.
gloss_zh: （在英语口语或书面语中，have可以和很多名词连用以代替某个具体的动词，描述某一动作或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use have to say that someone or something owns a particular thing, or when you are mentioning one of their qualities or characteristics.
If you have something to do, you are responsible for doing it or must do it.

You can use have instead of 'there is' to say that something exists or happens. For example, you can say 'you have no alternative' instead of 'there is no alternative', or 'he had a good view from his window' instead of 'there was a good view from his window'.
gloss_zh: （用于代替 there is, 表示某事物存在或发生了某事）
collocations: he had a good view from his window

senses.concept_en: If you have something such as a part of your body in a particular position or state, it is in that position or state.
If you have something done, someone does it for you or you arrange for it to be done.
If someone has something unpleasant happen to them, it happens to them.
If you have someone do something, you persuade, cause, or order them to do it.
If someone has you by a part of your body, they are holding you there and they are trying to hurt you or force you to go somewhere.
gloss_zh: 抓住（某人身体的某部位）

senses.concept_en: If you have something from someone, they give it to you.
If you have an illness or disability, you suffer from it.
If a woman has a baby, she gives birth to it. If she is having a baby, she is pregnant.
You can use have in expressions such as 'I won't have it' or 'I'm not having that', to mean that you will not allow or put up with something.

he.translation:
pron. 他
n. 男孩, 男人, 雄性动物

senses.concept_en: You use he to refer to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, he is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use 'he or she' or 'they'.
gloss_zh: （书面英语中泛指人）他，她（有些人不喜欢这种用法，更倾向于使用 he or she 或 they）

senses.concept_en: In some religions, He is used to refer to God.

hear.translation:
vt. 听到, 倾听, 听说, 审理
vi. 听见, 听

senses.concept_en: When you hear a sound, you become aware of it through your ears.
If you hear something such as a lecture or a piece of music, you listen to it.
If you say that you can hear someone saying something, you mean that you are able to imagine hearing it.
When a judge or a court of law hears a case, or evidence in a case, they listen to it officially in order to make a decision about it.
gloss_zh: （法官或法庭）审理（案件），听取（证词）

senses.concept_en: If you hear from someone, you receive a letter or telephone call from them.
In a debate or discussion, if you hear from someone, you listen to them giving their opinion or information.
gloss_zh: （辩论或讨论中）倾听（意见或情况）

senses.concept_en: If you hear some news or information about something, you find out about it by someone telling you, or from the radio or television.
If you have heard of something or someone, you know about them, but not in great detail.

heavy.translation:
a. 重的, 巨大的, 沉重的, 笨重的, 过度的
adv. 沉重地
n. 重物, 严肃角色

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is heavy weighs a lot.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use heavy to ask or talk about how much someone or something weighs.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Heavy means great in amount, degree, or intensity.
gloss_zh: 大量的;重大的;严重的;强烈的;剧烈的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is heavy is solid in appearance or structure, or is made of a thick material.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy substance is thick in texture.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy meal is large in amount and often difficult to digest.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is heavy with things is full of them or loaded with them.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a person's breathing is heavy, it is very loud and deep.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A heavy movement or action is done with a lot of force or pressure.
A heavy machine or piece of military equipment is very large and very powerful.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a period of time or a schedule as heavy, you mean it involves a lot of work.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Heavy work requires a lot of strength or energy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that something is heavy on another thing, you mean that it uses a lot of that thing or too much of that thing.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Air or weather that is heavy is unpleasantly still, hot, and damp.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person's face as heavy, you mean that it looks sad, tired, or unfriendly.
gloss_zh: （表情）沉痛的，疲惫呆滞的，阴郁的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If your heart is heavy, you are sad about something.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A situation that is heavy is serious and difficult to cope with.
A heavy is a large strong man who is employed to protect a person or place, often by using violence.
gloss_zh: （雇作保镖或打手的）彪形大汉

his.translation:
pron. 他的
[化] 组氨酸

senses.concept_en: You use his to indicate that something belongs or relates to a man, boy, or male animal.
In written English, his is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use 'his or her' or 'their'.
gloss_zh: （书面英语中泛指人）他的，她的（有些人不喜欢这种说法，更倾向于使用 his or her 或 their）

senses.concept_en: In some religions, His is used to refer to God.

hold.translation:
n. 把握, 把持力, 柄, 控制, 掌握, 监禁
vt. 保存, 握住, 拿住, 占据, 持有, 拥有
vi. 支持, 持续, 有效
n. 保留
[计] 保留

senses.concept_en: When you hold something, you carry or support it, using your hands or your arms.
Hold is used in expressions such as grab hold of ,catch hold of, and get hold of, to indicate that you close your hand tightly around something, for example to stop something moving or falling.
When you hold someone, you put your arms round them, usually because you want to show them how much you like them or because you want to comfort them.
gloss_zh: （通常为表示喜爱或安慰而）拥抱，抱住

senses.concept_en: If you hold someone in a particular position, you use force to keep them in that position and stop them from moving.
A hold is a particular way of keeping someone in a position using your own hands, arms, or legs.
gloss_zh: （使某人不得动弹的）抓住，夹住

senses.concept_en: When you hold a part of your body, you put your hand on or against it, often because it hurts.
When you hold a part of your body in a particular position, you put it into that position and keep it there.
gloss_zh: 使（身体部位）保持（某种姿势）

senses.concept_en: If one thing holds another in a particular position, it keeps it in that position.
If one thing is used to hold another, it is used to store it.
In a ship or aeroplane, a hold is a place where cargo or luggage is stored.
If a place holds something, it keeps it available for reference or for future use.
If something holds a particular amount of something, it can contain that amount.
If you can hold your drink, you are able to drink large quantities of alcohol without becoming ill or getting drunk.
If a vehicle holds the road well, it remains in close contact with the road and can be controlled safely and easily.
Hold is used with words and expressions indicating an opinion or belief, to show that someone has a particular opinion or believes that something is true.
