Hold is used with words such as 'fear' or 'mystery' to indicate someone's feelings towards something, as if those feelings were a characteristic of the thing itself.
gloss_zh: 带给人，使人感到（害怕、神秘等）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'office', 'power', and 'responsibility' to indicate that someone has a particular position of power or authority.
gloss_zh: 担任（职务）;掌握（权力）;负有（责任）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'permit', 'degree', or 'ticket' to indicate that someone has a particular document that allows them to do something.
gloss_zh: 持有（许可、票证等）;拥有（学位等）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'party', 'meeting', 'talks', 'election', and 'trial' to indicate that people are organizing a particular activity.
gloss_zh: 举行（聚会、会议、会谈、选举、审判等）

senses.concept_en: Hold is used with nouns such as 'conversation', 'interview', and 'talks' to indicate that two or more people meet and discuss something.
See also:holding; Hold is used with nouns such as 'shares' and 'stock' to indicate that someone owns a particular proportion of a business.
Hold is used with words such as 'lead' or 'advantage' to indicate that someone is winning or doing well in a contest.
Hold is used with nouns such as 'attention' or 'interest' to indicate that what you do or say keeps someone interested or listening to you.
gloss_zh: 吸引住（注意力）;保持（兴趣）

senses.concept_en: If you hold someone responsible, liable, or accountable for something, you will blame them if anything goes wrong.
If someone holds you in a place, they keep you there as a prisoner and do not allow you to leave.
If people such as an army or a violent crowd hold a place, they control it by using force.
If you have a hold over someone, you have power or control over them, for example because you know something about them you can use to threaten them or because you are in a position of authority.
gloss_zh: （因握有某人把柄或掌握权力而形成的）控制力，支配力

senses.concept_en: If you ask someone to hold, or to hold the line, when you are answering a telephone call, you are asking them to wait for a short time, for example so that you can find the person they want to speak to.
gloss_zh: （接电话时让对方）稍等，不要挂断

senses.concept_en: If you hold telephone calls for someone, you do not allow people who phone to speak to that person, but take messages instead.
gloss_zh: 代接（电话）并向受话人转告通话内容

senses.concept_en: If something holds at a particular value or level, or is held there, it is kept at that value or level.
If you hold a sound or musical note, you continue making it.
If you hold something such as a train, a lift, or an elevator, you delay it.
If an offer or invitation still holds, it is still available for you to accept.
If a good situation holds, it continues and does not get worse or fail.
If an argument or theory holds, it is true or valid, even after close examination.
If part of a structure holds, it does not fall or break although there is a lot of force or pressure on it.
If laws or rules hold, they exist and remain in force.
If you say that you hold to a particular opinion or belief, you are stating firmly that you continue to have that opinion or belief.
If you hold to a promise or to high standards of behaviour, you keep that promise or continue to behave according to those standards.
gloss_zh: 遵守，恪守（承诺或高尚的行为准则）

senses.concept_en: If someone or something holds you to a promise or to high standards of behaviour, they make you keep that promise or those standards.
gloss_zh: 使遵守，使恪守（承诺或高尚的行为准则）

horse.translation:
n. 马, 骑兵, 脚架
vi. 骑马, 取笑
vt. 使骑马, 系马于

senses.concept_en: A horse is a large animal which people can ride. Some horses are used for pulling ploughs and carts.
When you talk about the horses, you mean horse races in which people bet money on the horse which they think will win.
A vaulting horse is a tall piece of gymnastics equipment for jumping over.

hour.translation: n. 小时, 钟头, 时间, ...点钟, 课时

senses.concept_en: An hour is a period of sixty minutes.
People say that something takes or lasts hours to emphasize that it takes or lasts a very long time, or what seems like a very long time.
A clock that strikes the hour strikes when it is exactly one o'clock, two o'clock, and so on.
You can refer to a particular time or moment as a particular hour .
If you refer, for example, to someone's hour of need or hour of happiness, you are referring to the time in their life when they are or were experiencing that condition or feeling.
You can refer to the period of time during which something happens or operates each day as the hours during which it happens or operates.
gloss_zh: （每天发生或进行某事的）特定时间，固定时间

senses.concept_en: If you refer to the hours involved in a job, you are talking about how long you spend each week doing it and when you do it.

however.translation:
adv. 然而, 无论如何, 究竟怎样
conj. 然而, 可是

senses.concept_en: You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said.
You use however before an adjective or adverb to emphasize that the degree or extent of something cannot change a situation.
gloss_zh: （后接形容词或副词用于强调）不管怎样，无论多么

senses.concept_en: You use however when you want to say that it makes no difference how something is done.
gloss_zh: 不管用什么方式;无论如何

senses.concept_en: You use however in expressions such as or however long it takes and or however many there were to indicate that the figure you have just mentioned may not be accurate.
You can use however to ask in an emphatic way how something has happened which you are very surprised about. Some speakers of English think that this form is incorrect and prefer to use 'how ever'.
gloss_zh: 究竟怎样，到底如何（用于强调地询问令人吃惊的事情;一些人认为此用法不正确，用how ever较为妥当）

idea.translation:
n. 主意, 办法, 理想, 思想, 概念, 意见
[医] 观念, 思想

senses.concept_en: An idea is a plan, suggestion, or possible course of action.
An idea is an opinion or belief about what something is like or should be like.
If someone gives you an idea of something, they give you information about it without being very exact or giving a lot of detail.
If you have an idea of something, you know about it to some extent.
If you have an idea that something is the case, you think that it may be the case, although you are not certain.
The idea of an action or activity is its aim or purpose.
If you have the idea of doing something, you intend to do it.
You can use idea in expressions such as I've no idea or I haven't the faintest idea to emphasize that you do not know something.
gloss_zh: （表示强调）我不知道/我一点儿都不知道

immediate.translation:
a. 立即的, 直接的, 接近的
[医] 直接的, 立即的

senses.concept_en: An immediate result, action, or reaction happens or is done without any delay.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Immediate needs and concerns exist at the present time and must be dealt with quickly.
The immediate person or thing comes just before or just after another person or thing in a sequence.
You use immediate to describe an area or position that is next to or very near a particular place or person.
Your immediate family are the members of your family who are most closely related to you, for example your parents, children, brothers, and sisters.

important.translation:
a. 重要的, 有地位的, 大量的, 显要的, 自负的
[计] 要点

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is important is very significant, is highly valued, or is necessary.
gloss_zh: 重要的;必要的;非常有价值的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is important has influence or power within a society or a particular group.
gloss_zh: 有声望的;有影响的;显要的

improve.translation:
vt. 改良, 提高...的价值, 改善, 利用
vi. 变得更好, 增加

senses.concept_en: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.
If a skill you have improves or you improve a skill, you get better at it.
If you improve after an illness or an injury, your health gets better or you get stronger.
If you improve on a previous achievement of your own or of someone else, you achieve a better standard or result.

in.translation:
prep. 在...期间, 在...之内, 处于...之中, 从事于, 按照, 穿着
adv. 进入, 朝里, 在里面, 在屋里
a. 在里面的, 在朝的
n. 执政者, 交情

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is in something else is enclosed by it or surrounded by it. If you put something in a container, you move it so that it is enclosed by the container.
If something happens in a place, it happens there.
If you are in, you are present at your home or place of work.
When someone comes in, they enter a room or building.
If a train, boat, or plane has come in or is in, it has arrived at a station, port, or airport.
When the sea or tide comes in, the sea moves towards the shore rather than away from it.
Something that is in a window, especially a shop window, is just behind the window so that you can see it from outside.
When you see something in a mirror, the mirror shows an image of it.
If you are dressed in a piece of clothing, you are wearing it.
Something that is covered or wrapped in something else has that thing over or round its surface.
If there is something such as a crack or hole in something, there is a crack or hole on its surface.
If something is in a book, film, play, or picture, you can read it or see it there.
gloss_zh: 在（书、电影、戏剧、图片）之中

senses.concept_en: If you are in something such as a play or a race, you are one of the people taking part.
Something that is in a group or collection is a member of it or part of it.
You use in to specify a general subject or field of activity.
If something happens in a particular year, month, or other period of time, it happens during that time.
If something happens in a particular situation, it happens while that situation is going on.
If you do something in a particular period of time, that is how long it takes you to do it.
If something will happen in a particular length of time, it will happen after that length of time.
You use in to indicate roughly how old someone is. For example, if someone is in their fifties, they are between 50 and 59 years old.
You use in to indicate roughly how many people or things do something.
You use in to express a ratio, proportion, or probability.
If something or someone is in a particular state or situation, that is their present state or situation.
You use in to indicate the feeling or desire which someone has when they do something, or which causes them to do it.
gloss_zh: 带着，充满（某种情感或愿望）

senses.concept_en: If a particular quality or ability is in you, you naturally have it.
You use in when saying that someone or something has a particular quality.
You use in to indicate how someone is expressing something.
You use in in expressions such as in a row or in a ball to describe the arrangement or shape of something.
gloss_zh: （表示排列或形状）成一排/呈球形

senses.concept_en: If something is in a particular colour, it has that colour.
You use in to specify which feature or aspect of something you are talking about.
If you say that something is in, or is the in thing, you mean it is fashionable or popular.
gloss_zh: 时髦的;流行的;受欢迎的

senses.concept_en: You use in with a present participle to indicate that when you do something, something else happens as a result.

increase.translation:
n. 增加, 增进, 利益
vt. 增加, 加大
vi. 增加, 繁殖

senses.concept_en: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount.
If there is an increase in the number, level, or amount of something, it becomes greater.

injury.translation:
n. 伤害, 侮辱
[医] 伤, 损伤
injury.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: An injury is damage done to a person's or an animal's body
If someone suffers injury to their feelings, they are badly upset by something. If they suffer injury to their reputation, their reputation is seriously harmed.

derivation.breakdown_zh: injure 损害 + -y 名词：伤害

inside.translation:
n. 内部, 内脏, 内幕
a. 内部的, 秘密的, 户内的
adv. 在里面
prep. 在...之内

senses.concept_en: Something or someone that is inside a place, container, or object is in it or is surrounded by it.
The inside of something is the part or area that its sides surround or contain.
You can say that someone is inside when they are in prison.
On a wide road, the inside lane is the one which is closest to the edge of the road.
gloss_zh: （马路车道）靠近路边的，慢（道）的

senses.concept_en: Inside information is obtained from someone who is involved in a situation and therefore knows a lot about it.
If you are inside an organization, you belong to it.
Your insides are your internal organs, especially your stomach.
If you say that someone has a feeling inside, you mean that they have it but have not expressed it.
If you do something inside a particular time, you do it before the end of that time.

derivation.breakdown_zh: side 侧 + in- 在内：内部

inspector.translation:
n. 检查员, 巡视员
[化] 检查员

senses.concept_en: An inspector is a person, usually employed by a government agency, whose job is to find out whether people are obeying official regulations.

senses.pos_zh: 可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词
senses.concept_en: In Britain, an inspector is an officer in the police who is higher in rank than a sergeant and lower in rank than a superintendent.
gloss_zh: （英国警察中职位低于警司高于巡佐的）巡官,督察

senses.pos_zh: 可数名词；头衔名词；称呼名词
senses.concept_en: In the United States, an inspector is an officer in the police who is next in rank to a superintendent or police chief.
gloss_zh: （美国警察中仅次于总警监的）督察长

instal.translation: vt. 任命, 使就任, 使就职, 安装, 装置, 设置, 安顿, 安置

instead.translation: adv. 作为替代, 反而

senses.concept_en: If you do not do something, but do something else instead, you do the second thing and not the first thing, as the result of a choice or a change of behaviour.

iron.translation:
n. 铁, 熨斗, 铁器, 坚强, 烙铁, 镣铐
vt. 烫平, 熨, 用铁包
vi. 烫平

senses.concept_en: See also:cast-iron; Iron is an element which usually takes the form of a hard, dark grey metal. It is used to make steel, and also forms part of many tools, buildings, and vehicles. Very small amounts of iron occur in your blood and in food.
An iron is an electrical device with a flat metal base. You heat it until the base is hot, then rub it over clothes to remove creases.
If you iron clothes, you remove the creases from them using an iron.
You can use iron to describe the character or behaviour of someone who is very firm in their decisions and actions, or who can control their feelings well.
Iron is used in expressions such as an iron hand and iron discipline to describe strong, harsh, or unfair methods of control which do not allow people much freedom.

joint.translation:
n. 连接处, 接合, 关节
a. 共同的, 联合的, 连接的, 合办的
vt. 连接, 接合, 使有接头
vi. 贴合, 长节

senses.concept_en: Joint means shared by or belonging to two or more people.
A joint is a part of your body such as your elbow or knee where two bones meet and are able to move together.
See also:dovetail joint; A joint is the place where two things are fastened or fixed together.
gloss_zh: 接合处；连接点；接头；接缝

senses.concept_en: A joint is a fairly large piece of meat which is suitable for roasting.
You can refer to a cheap place where people go for some form of entertainment as a joint .
gloss_zh: 廉价娱乐场所；下等娱乐场所

senses.concept_en: A joint is a cigarette which contains cannabis or marijuana.

labor.translation:
n. 劳动, 努力, 工作, 劳工, 分娩
vi. 劳动, 努力, 苦干
vt. 详细分析, 使厌烦

senses.concept_en: Later is the comparative of late.
You use later to refer to a time or situation that is after the one that you have been talking about or after the present one.
You use later to refer to an event, period of time, or other thing which comes after the one that you have been talking about or after the present one.
You use later to refer to the last part of someone's life or career or the last part of a period of history.

lay.translation:
vt. 放置, 产, 铺设, 布置, 提出, 平息
vi. 下蛋, 打赌
n. 位置, 层, 隐藏处
a. 世俗的, 外行的
lie的过去式
lay.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you lay something somewhere, you put it there in a careful, gentle, or neat way.
If you lay the table or lay the places at a table, you arrange the knives, forks, and other things that people need on the table before a meal.
If you lay something such as carpets, cables, or foundations, you put them into their permanent position.
To lay a trap means to prepare it in order to catch someone or something.
When a female bird lays an egg, it produces an egg by pushing it out of its body.
Lay is used with some nouns to talk about making official preparations for something. For example, if you lay the basis for something or lay plans for it, you prepare it carefully.

Lay is used with some nouns in expressions about accusing or blaming someone. For example, if you lay the blame for a mistake on someone, you say it is their fault, or if the police lay charges against someone, they officially accuse that person of a crime.
If you say that you would lay bets, odds, or money on something happening, you mean that you are very confident that it will happen.
To lay someone means to have sex with them.
Lay is used in expressions such a good lay or an easy lay to describe what someone is like as a sexual partner.
gloss_zh: 床上功夫高者/轻易就上床者

senses.concept_en: You use lay to describe people who are involved with a Christian church but are not members of the clergy or are not monks or nuns.
gloss_zh: （基督教中）平信徒的，世俗的，非神职的

senses.concept_en: You use lay to describe people who are not experts or professionals in a particular subject or activity.
gloss_zh: 业余的；外行的；门外汉的

letter.translation:
n. 信, 字母, 证书, 字面意义, 铅字, 学问, 出租人
vt. 写字母于, 在...上刻字母, 用字母标明
vi. 写印刷体字
[计] 字母

senses.concept_en: If you write a letter to someone, you write a message on paper and send it to them, usually by post.
Letters are written symbols which represent one of the sounds in a language.

If a student earns a letter in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.
gloss_zh: （校队队衣的）校名首字母标志（以嘉许优秀运动员）

senses.concept_en: If a student letters in sports or athletics by being part of the university or college team, they are entitled to wear on their jacket the initial letter of the name of their university or college.
gloss_zh: 赢得佩戴校名首字母标志的荣誉

like.translation:
a. 相似的, 同样的
vt. 喜欢, 愿意, 想
vi. 喜欢, 希望
n. 爱好, 同样的人(或物)
prep. 象, 如同
adv. 可能

senses.concept_en: If you say that one person or thing is like another, you mean that they share some of the same qualities or features.
If you talk about what something or someone is like, you are talking about their qualities or features.
You can use like to introduce an example of the set of things or people that you have just mentioned.
You can use like to say that someone or something is in the same situation as another person or thing.

If you say that someone is behaving like something or someone else, you mean that they are behaving in a way that is typical of that kind of thing or person. Like is used in this way in many fixed expressions, for example to cry like a baby and to watch someone like a hawk.
gloss_zh: （表示行为如同…一样）像孩子一样哭泣/像老鹰一样监视
collocations: to watch someone like a hawk

senses.concept_en: You can use like in expressions such as that's just like her and it wasn't like him to indicate that the person's behaviour is or is not typical of their character.
gloss_zh: （表示行为符合…的特点）她就是这么个人/这一点也不像他

senses.concept_en: Like is sometimes used as a conjunction in order to say that something appears to be the case when it is not. Some people consider this use to be incorrect.
gloss_zh: 好像，似乎（但事实并非如此）（一些人认为此用法不正确）

senses.concept_en: Like is sometimes used as a conjunction in order to indicate that something happens or is done in the same way as something else. Some people consider this use to be incorrect.
gloss_zh: 如同（一些人认为此用法不正确）

senses.concept_en: You can use like in negative expressions such as nothing like it and no place like it to emphasize that there is nothing as good as the situation, thing, or person mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于否定短语中强调以…为最）没有什么能比得上它/没有什么地方能比得上它

senses.concept_en: You can use like in expressions such as nothing like to make an emphatic negative statement.
Some people say like when they are thinking about what to say next or because it has become their habit to say it. Some people do not like this use.
gloss_zh: （表示思考下面的话或用作口头禅）嗯，这个（一些人不喜欢此用法）

senses.concept_en: Some people say like when they are reporting what they or another person said, or what they thought about something. Some people do not like this use.
gloss_zh: （用于重述自己或他人当时的话或自己当时的想法）说，想（一些人不喜欢此用法）

senses.concept_en: If you like something or someone, you think they are interesting, enjoyable, or attractive.
If you ask someone how they like something, you are asking them for their opinion of it and whether they enjoy it or find it pleasant.
If you like something such as a particular course of action or way of behaving, you approve of it.
If you say that you like to do something or that you like something to be done, you mean that you prefer to do it or prefer it to be done as part of your normal life or routine.
If you say that you would like something or would like to do something, you are indicating a wish or desire that you have.
You can say that you would like to say something to indicate that you are about to say it.
If you ask someone if they would like something or would like to do something, you are making a polite offer or invitation.

If you say to someone that you would like something or you would like them to do something, or ask them if they would like to do it, you are politely telling them what you want or what you want them to do.
You can use like in expressions such as like attracts like, when you are referring to two or more people or things that have the same or similar characteristics.
gloss_zh: 同样（或相似）的人（或事物）

senses.concept_en: Someone's likes are the things that they enjoy or find pleasant.

line.translation:
n. 列, 线, 绳, 电线, 线路, 路线, 航线, 作业线, 界线, 战线, 外形, 排, 家系
vt. 排成一行, 顺...排列, 划线于, 加衬里, 使有线条, 使起皱纹
vi. 排队
[计] 线路
line.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: A line is a long thin mark which is drawn or painted on a surface.
The lines on some-one's skin, especially on their face, are long thin marks that appear there as they grow older.
A line of people or things is a number of them arranged one behind the other or side by side.
A line of people or vehicles is a number of them that are waiting one behind another, for example in order to buy something or to go in a particular direction.
gloss_zh: （人、车辆等在等候时排成的）队，队伍

senses.concept_en: A line of a piece of writing is one of the rows of words, numbers, or other symbols in it.
In school, if a child is given lines, he or she is punished by being made to write out a sentence many times or to write out a passage from a book.
A line of a poem, song, or play is a group of words that are spoken or sung together. If an actor learns his or her lines for a play or film, they learn what they have to say.
A particular type of line in a conversation is a remark that is intended to have a particular effect.
You can refer to a long piece of wire, string, or cable as a line when it is used for a particular purpose.
A line is a connection which makes it possible for two people to speak to each other on the telephone.
You can use line to refer to a telephone number which you can ring in order to get information or advice.
A line is a route, especially a dangerous or secret one, along which people move or send messages or supplies.
gloss_zh: （尤指危险或秘密的）路线，线路

senses.concept_en: The line in which something or someone moves is the particular route that they take, especially when they keep moving straight ahead.
A line is a particular route, involving the same stations, roads, or stops along which a train or bus service regularly operates.
A railway line consists of the pieces of metal and wood which form the track that the trains travel along.
A shipping, air, or bus line is a company which provides services for transporting people or goods by sea, air, or bus.
You can use line to refer to the edge, outline, or shape of an object or a person's body.
A state or county line is a boundary between two states or counties.
You can use lines to refer to the set of physical defences or the soldiers that have been established along the boundary of an area occupied by an army.

The particular line that a person has towards a problem is the attitude that they have towards it. For example, if someone takes a hard line on something, they have a firm strict policy which they refuse to change.
You can use line to refer to the way in which someone's thoughts or activities develop, particularly if it is logical.
gloss_zh: （思想或行动的）步骤，方式，方法

senses.concept_en: If you say that something happens along particular lines, or on particular lines, you are giving a general summary or approximate account of what happens, which may not be correct in every detail.
If something is organized on particular lines, or along particular lines, it is organized according to that method or principle.
Your line of business or work is the kind of work that you do.
If someone says that something is your line, or that it is in your line, they mean that it is the sort of thing that you often do because you enjoy doing it.
A line is a particular type of product that a company makes or sells.
You can use line to refer to something connected with a particular activity. For example, something in the sports line is connected with sports.
In a factory, a line is an arrangement of workers or machines where a product passes from one worker to another until it is finished.
You can use line to refer to all the generations of a family, especially when you are considering the social status or the physical characteristics that the various members inherit.
You can use line when you are referring to a number of people who are ranked according to status.
A particular line of people or things is a series of them that has existed over a period of time, when they have all been similar in some way, or done similar things.
gloss_zh: （按时间顺序排的）一系列，一连串

senses.concept_en: If people or things line a road, room, or other place, they are present in large numbers along its edges or sides.
gloss_zh: 沿…排列成行；遍布…的边沿

senses.concept_en: If you line a wall, container, or other object, you put a layer of something such as leaves or paper on the inside surface of it in order to make it stronger, warmer, or cleaner.
If something lines a container or area, especially an area inside a person, animal, or plant, it forms a layer on the inside surface.
gloss_zh: 在（容器或器官）的内壁形成一层

lock.translation:
n. 锁, 刹车, 水闸, 一缕头发
vt. 锁, 锁上, 拘禁, 隐藏, (用锁等)拴住, 刹住
vi. 锁住, (齿轮等)啮合, (船)过闸

senses.concept_en: When you lock something such as a door, drawer, or case, you fasten it, usually with a key, so that other people cannot open it.
The lock on something such as a door or a drawer is the device which is used to keep it shut and prevent other people from opening it. Locks are opened with a key.
If you lock something or someone in a place, room, or container, you put them there and fasten the lock.
gloss_zh: 把… 锁起妥藏；把…关起来

senses.concept_en: If you lock something in a particular position or if it lock there, it is held or fitted firmly in that position.

On a canal or river, a lock is a place where walls have been built with gates at each end so that boats can move to a higher or lower section of the canal or river, by gradually changing the water level inside the gates.
A lock of hair is a small bunch of hairs on your head that grow together and curl or curve in the same direction.
Your locks are your hair.

loose.translation:
n. 发射, 放任, 放纵
a. 宽松的, 松的, 宽的, 不牢固的, 散漫的, 自由的, 不精确的
vt. 释放, 放枪, 开船
vi. 变松, 开火
adv. 松散地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is loose is not firmly held or fixed in place.
Something that is loose is not attached to anything, or held or contained in anything.
gloss_zh: 零散的；不相连的；松脱的

senses.concept_en: If people or animals break loose or are set loose, they are no longer held, tied, or kept somewhere and can move around freely.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Clothes that are loose are rather large and do not fit closely.
If your hair is loose, it hangs freely round your shoulders and is not tied back.
If something is loose in texture, there is space between the different particles or threads it consists of.
gloss_zh: 疏松的；稀松的；结构不紧密的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A loose grouping, arrangement, or organization is flexible rather than strictly controlled or organized.
gloss_zh: （分组、安排、组织等）松散的，随便的，自由的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Loose words or expressions are not exact but rather vague.
gloss_zh: 意义含糊的；不严谨的；不精确的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone describes a woman or someone's behaviour as loose, they disapprove of that person because they think she or he has sexual relationships with too many people.
To loose a shot, arrow, or missile means to fire it.
If you loose something, you hold it less tightly or untie it slightly or completely.

loud.translation:
a. 大声的, 不断的, 喧吵的
adv. 高声地, 大声地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a noise is loud, the level of sound is very high and it can be easily heard. Someone or something that is loud produces a lot of noise.
gloss_zh: （声音）响亮的；（声源）发出响亮声音的；吵闹的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is loud in their support for or criticism of something, they express their opinion very often and in a very strong way.
gloss_zh: （对某事的支持或批评）强烈的，激烈的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe something, especially a piece of clothing, as loud, you dislike it because it has very bright colours or very large, bold patterns which look unpleasant.
gloss_zh: （尤指衣服）大红大绿的，花里胡哨的，俗艳的

machine.translation:
n. 机器, 机械装置, 机构, 自动售货机, 机械般工作的人
vt. 以机器制造

senses.concept_en: A machine is a piece of equipment which uses electricity or an engine in order to do a particular kind of work.
If you machine something, you make it or work on it using a machine.
gloss_zh: 用机器制造;用机器加工

senses.concept_en: You can use machine to refer to a large and well-controlled system or organization.
If you say that someone is a machine, you mean that they are so tired or bored that they do their work without thinking.
gloss_zh: （由于工作过于劳累或乏味）机械般工作的人，做工作不动脑筋的人

mail.translation:
n. 邮件, 邮政, 邮递, 盔甲
vt. 邮寄, 给...穿盔甲
[计] 邮件

senses.concept_en: The mail is the public service or system by which letters and parcels are collected and delivered.
You can refer to letters and parcels that are delivered to you as mail .
If you mail a letter or parcel to someone, you send it to them by putting it in a post box or taking it to a post office.
To mail a message to someone means to send it to them by means of e-mail or a computer network.

make.translation:
vt. 制造, 安排, 创造, 构成, 使得, 产生, 造成, 整理, 布置, 引起, 到达, 进行
vi. 开始, 前进, 增大, 被制造, 被处理
n. 制造, 构造, 性情

senses.concept_en: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.
gloss_zh: （与大量名词连用，表示做动作、说某事等）做出，作出

senses.concept_en: You can use make with certain nouns to indicate that someone does something well or badly. For example, if you make a success of something, you do it successfully, and if you make a mess of something, you do it very badly.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词连用）把…做（好），把…搞（糟）

senses.concept_en: If you make as if to do something or make to do something, you behave in a way that makes it seem that you are just about to do it.
gloss_zh: 摆出…的姿态;做出…的样子

senses.concept_en: In cricket, if a player makes a particular number of runs, they score that number of runs. In baseball or American football, if a player makes a particular score, they achieve that score.
gloss_zh: （在板球、棒球、橄榄球比赛中）得（分）

senses.concept_en: If something makes you do something, it causes you to do it.
If you make someone do something, you force them to do it.

You use make to talk about causing someone or something to be a particular thing or to have a particular quality. For example, to make someone a star means to cause them to become a star, and to make someone angry means to cause them to become angry.
gloss_zh: 使成为（某种人或物）;使具有（某种特性）

senses.concept_en: If you say that one thing or person makes another seem, for example, small, stupid, or good, you mean that they cause them to seem small, stupid, or good in comparison, even though they are not.
If you make yourself understood, heard, or known, you succeed in getting people to understand you, hear you, or know that you are there.
gloss_zh: 使自己（被理解、听见、知晓等）

senses.concept_en: If you make someone something, you appoint them to a particular job, role, or position.
If you make something into something else, you change it in some way so that it becomes that other thing.
To make a total or score a particular amount means to increase it to that amount.
gloss_zh: 使（总数）升为;使（分数）达到

senses.concept_en: When someone makes a friend or an enemy, someone becomes their friend or their enemy, often because of a particular thing they have done.
To make something means to produce, construct, or create it.
If someone makes a film or television programme, they are involved in creating or producing it.
gloss_zh: 拍摄（电影）;制作（电视节目）

senses.concept_en: If you make a meal or a drink, you prepare it.
If you make a note or list, you write something down in that form.
If you make rules or laws, you decide what these should be.
If you make money, you get it by working for it, by selling something, or by winning it.
If something makes something else, it is responsible for the success of that thing.
gloss_zh: （某事物）使（其他事物）变得成功

senses.concept_en: The make of something such as a car or radio is the name of the company that made it

You can use make to say that someone or something has the right qualities for a particular task or role. For example, if you say that someone will make a good politician, you mean that they have the right qualities to be a good politician.
If people make a particular pattern such as a line or a circle, they arrange themselves in this way.
You can use make to say what two numbers add up to.
If someone makes a particular team or makes a particular high position, they do so well that they are put in that team or get that position.
gloss_zh: 成为…的一员;加入;谋得（高级职务）

senses.concept_en: If you make a place in or by a particular time, you get there in or by that time, often with some difficulty.
You use make it when saying what you calculate or guess an amount to be.
You use make it when saying what time your watch says it is.

man.translation:
n. 男人, 人类, 人
vt. 为...配备人手, 操纵, 使振奋
[计] 城域网, 手册

senses.concept_en: A man is an adult male human being.
Man and men are sometimes used to refer to all human beings, including both males and females. Some people dislike this use.
gloss_zh: 人，人类（此用法仍有争议）

senses.concept_en: If you say that a man is, for example, a gambling man or an outdoors man, you mean that he likes gambling or outdoor activities.
If you say that a man is, for example, a London man or an Oxford man, you mean that he comes from London or Oxford, or went to university there.
gloss_zh: （来自某地的）人；（在某地上过学的）人

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a particular company's or organiza-tion's man, you mean a man who works for or represents that company or organization.
gloss_zh: （某公司或组织的男性）职员，代表

senses.concept_en: If you say that a man is someone's man, you mean that he always supports that person or does what they want.
Some people refer to a woman's husband, lover, or boyfriend as her man .
In the armed forces, the men are soldiers, sailors, marines, or airmen of lower rank, as opposed to the officers.
Male workers are sometimes referred to as men, especially if they do physical work or work for a more senior person.
gloss_zh: （尤指从事体力劳动或为上级工作的）男工，男雇员，男下属

senses.concept_en: One man sometimes addresses another as 'man' when he is angry or impatient with him.
gloss_zh: （对男子的称呼，表示生气或不耐烦）老兄，老弟，小伙子

senses.concept_en: In very informal social situations, man is sometimes used as a greeting or form of address to a man.
gloss_zh: （在非正式场合中用以称呼男子）老弟,老兄

senses.concept_en: If you man something such as a place or machine, you operate it or are in charge of it.
gloss_zh: 在…岗位上工作;操作（机器等）

merit.translation:
n. 优点, 功绩, 价值, 功过, 真相
vt. 值得
vi. 应受
merit.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.
The merits of something are its advantages or other good points.
If someone or something merits a particular action or treatment, they deserve it.

message.translation:
n. 消息, 通讯, 讯息, 教训, 预言, 广告词
vt. 通知
vi. 通报, 报告, 报信
[计] 报文; 消息; 信息

senses.concept_en: A message is a piece of information or a request that you send to someone or leave for them when you cannot speak to them directly.
The message that someone is trying to communicate, for example in a book or play, is the idea or point that they are trying to communicate.
gloss_zh: （书、戏剧等的）要旨，主题思想，寓意

senses.concept_en: If you message someone, you send them a message electronically using a computer or another device such as a mobile phone.
gloss_zh: （用电脑、手机等）给…发消息，给…留言

metal.translation:
n. 金属, 金属制品, 合金, 本质, 质料
a. 金属制的
vt. 以金属覆盖
metal.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: See also:base metal; Metal is a hard substance such as iron, steel, gold, or lead.

method.translation:
n. 方法, 办法, 条理, 秩序
[医] [方]法
method.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: A method is a particular way of doing something.

mile.translation:
n. 英里, 很大距离
[机] 英里, 哩

money.translation:
n. 金钱, 一笔款, 财富, 货币, 金额
[经] 货币, 金钱, 财产

senses.concept_en: Money is the coins or bank notes that you use to buy things, or the sum that you have in a bank account.
Monies is used to refer to several separate sums of money that form part of a larger amount that is received or spent.

morning.translation: n. 早晨, 早上, 初期

senses.concept_en: The morning is the part of each day between the time that people usually wake up and 12 o'clock noon or lunchtime.
gloss_zh: 早晨;上午（从人们通常醒来到中午或午餐前的一段时间）

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a particular time in the morning, you mean a time between 12 o'clock midnight and 12 o'clock noon.
gloss_zh: 凌晨，早晨，上午（从子夜到中午的这段时间）

move.translation:
n. 移动, 迁居, 步骤
vt. 移动, 开动, 感动, 搬(家)
vi. 移动, 离开, 运行, 迁移, 摇动, 搬家, 交往, 进展, 脱手
[计] 移动; 传送; DOS外部命令:移动文件, 它可将文件移动到指定的地方

senses.concept_en: When you move something or when it moves, its position changes and it does not remain still.
When you move, you change your position or go to a different place.
If you move, you act or you begin to do something.
A move is an action that you take in order to achieve something.
If a person or company moves, they leave the building where they have been living or working, and they go to live or work in a different place, taking their possessions with them.
If people in authority move someone, they make that person go from one place or job to another one.
If you move from one job or interest to another, you change to it.
If you move to a new topic in a conversation, you start talking about something different.
gloss_zh: 改变（谈话内容）;转到（新的话题）

senses.concept_en: If you move an event or the date of an event, you change the time at which it happens.
If you move towards a particular state, activity, or opinion, you start to be in that state, do that activity, or have that opinion.
If a situation or process is moving, it is developing or progressing, rather than staying still.
If you say that you will not be moved, you mean that you have come to a decision and nothing will change your mind.
If something moves you to do something, it influences you and causes you to do it.
If something moves you, it has an effect on your emotions and causes you to feel sadness or sympathy for another person.
If you say that someone moves in a particular society, circle, or world, you mean that they know people in a particular social class or group and spend most of their time with them.
gloss_zh: 活跃，出入，涉足（于某团体、领域或圈子）

senses.concept_en: At a meeting, if you move a motion, you formally suggest it so that everyone present can vote on it.
A move is an act of putting a chess piece or other counter in a different position on a board when it is your turn to do so in a game.

muddy.translation:
a. 泥泞的, 浑浊的, 模糊的
vt. 使污浊, 使沾上泥污

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is muddy contains mud or is covered in mud.
gloss_zh: 沾满泥的;多泥的;泥泞的

senses.concept_en: If you muddy something, you cause it to be muddy.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Muddy is used to describe a colour which is dull and brownish.
If someone or something muddies a situation or issue, they cause it to seem less clear and less easy to understand.
gloss_zh: 使更为复杂;使难以理解

derivation.breakdown_zh: mud 泥 + -y 形容词后缀：泥泞的

mutter.translation:
n. 喃喃低语
vi. 喃喃自语, 作低沉声
vt. 出怨言, 抱怨地说

senses.concept_en: If you mutter, you speak very quietly so that you cannot easily be heard, often because you are complaining about something.

name.translation:
n. 名字, 名称, 姓名, 名义, 名誉, 文件名
vt. 命名, 称呼, 任命, 提名, 列举
a. 姓名的, 据以取名的
[计] 名称, 文件名, 姓名

senses.concept_en: The name of a person, place, or thing is the word or group of words that is used to identify them.
When you name someone or something, you give them a name, usually at the beginning of their life.
If you name someone or something after another person or thing, you give them the same name as that person or thing.
If you name someone, you identify them by stating their name.
gloss_zh: 叫出…的名称;说出…的名字

senses.concept_en: If you name something such as a price, time, or place, you say what you want it to be.
gloss_zh: 提出，说出，指出（价格、时间、地点等）

senses.concept_en: If you name the person for a particular job, you say who you want to have the job.
You can refer to the reputation of a person or thing as their name .
You can refer to someone as, for example, a famous name or a great name when they are well-known.

nation.translation:
n. 国家, 民族
[法] 民族, 国家

senses.concept_en: A nation is an individual country considered together with its social and political structures
The nation is sometimes used to refer to all the people who live in a particular country.

never.translation:
adv. 从不, 决不, 不曾
[法] 永不, 决不, 从来没有

senses.concept_en: Never means at no time in the past or at no time in the future.
Never means 'not in any circumstances at all'.
Never is used to refer to the past and means 'not'.
You say 'never!' to indicate how surprised or shocked you are by something that someone has just said.
You say 'Well, I never' to indicate that you are very surprised about something that you have just seen or found out.
gloss_zh: （表示惊讶）我真没看到（或发现、想到）过

new.translation:
a. 新的, 陌生的, 最近的, 不熟悉的
[法] 新发现的, 新的, 重新开始的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is new has been recently created, built, or invented or is in the process of being created, built, or invented.
gloss_zh: 新的;刚出现的;新做的;新建的

senses.concept_en: Something that is new has not been used or owned by anyone.
You use new to describe something which has replaced another thing, for example because you no longer have the old one, or it no longer exists, or it is no longer useful.
New is used to describe something that has only recently been discovered or noticed.
A new day or year is the beginning of the next day or year.
gloss_zh: （一天或一年）新开始的，初始的

senses.concept_en: New is used to describe someone or something that has recently acquired a particular status or position.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are new to a situation or place, or if the situation or place is new to you, you have not previously seen it or had any experience of it.
New potatoes, carrots, or peas are produced early in the season for such vegetables and are usually small with a sweet flavour.
gloss_zh: （土豆、胡萝卜、豆子等）时鲜的，早的

noisy.translation:
a. 嘈杂的, 喧闹的
[机] 噪声的, 嘈杂的
noisy.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A noisy person or thing makes a lot of loud or unpleasant noise.
gloss_zh: 喧闹的;嗓门大的;聒噪的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A noisy place is full of a lot of loud or unpleasant noise.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone as noisy, you are critical of them for trying to attract attention to their views by frequently and forcefully discussing them.
gloss_zh: （为引起注意）吵吵嚷嚷的;哗众取宠的

derivation.breakdown_zh: noise 噪音 + -y 形容词：吵闹的

none.translation:
adv. 一点也不, 毫不
pron. 没有人, 无一物, 并无一个
a. 没有的

senses.concept_en: None of something means not even a small amount of it. None of a group of people or things means not even one of them.
gloss_zh: 没有一点儿;全无;没有一个（人或物）

not.translation:
adv. 不, 非, 未
[计] 非

senses.concept_en: You use not with verbs to form negative statements.
gloss_zh: （与动词连用构成否定句）不，非，没有

senses.concept_en: You use not to form questions to which you expect the answer 'yes'.
gloss_zh: （构成期望得到肯定回答的疑问句）

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in questions which imply that someone should have done something, or to express surprise that something is not the case.
gloss_zh: （通常以 n't 的形式出现在问句中，用于推断某人应已做某事或表示惊讶）

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in question tags after a positive statement.
gloss_zh: （通常用 n't 的形式，用于肯定陈述后的附加疑问句）是吗? 不是吗?

senses.concept_en: You use not, usually in the form n't, in polite suggestions.
gloss_zh: （通常以 n't 的形式，表示礼貌的建议）

senses.concept_en: You use not to represent the negative of a word, group, or clause that has just been used.
gloss_zh: （用于表示对刚提及的单词、词组或从句的否定）不，没有

senses.concept_en: You can use not in front of 'all' or 'every' when you want to say something that applies only to some members of the group that you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于 all 或 every 前，表示部分否定）并非，不是

senses.concept_en: If something is not always the case, you mean that sometimes it is the case and sometimes it is not.
You can use not or not even in front of 'a' or 'one' to emphasize that there is none at all of what is being mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于 a 或 one 前加强语气）（一个…）也不，（一个…）也没有

senses.concept_en: You can use not in front of a word referring to a distance, length of time, or other amount to say that the actual distance, time, or amount is less than the one mentioned.
gloss_zh: （用于表示距离、时间或其他数量的词前）不到，少于

senses.concept_en: You use not when you are contrasting something that is true with something that is untrue. You use this especially to indicate that people might think that the untrue statement is true.
gloss_zh: （用于对比真实和不真实的情况，尤用于可能使人产生误解的陈述）不是

senses.concept_en: You use not in expressions such as 'not only', 'not just', and 'not simply' to emphasize that something is true, but it is not the whole truth.
gloss_zh: （用于not only，not just, not simply 等短语中，强调某事物的真实性，但不是全部事实）

objection.translation:
n. 异议, 反对, 不喜欢, 缺点, 缺陷, 妨碍, 拒绝之理由
[法] 异议, 反对, 抗议
objection.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you make or raise an objection to something, you say that you do not like it or agree with it.
If you say that you have no objection to something, you mean that you are not annoyed or bothered by it.

derivation.breakdown_zh: object 反对 + -ion 名词后缀：反对意见

obligation.translation:
n. 义务, 责任, 约束, 契约, 恩惠, 债务
[经] 待付款, 债务, 义务
obligation.tags: cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: If you have an obligation to do something, it is your duty to do that thing.
If you have an obligation to a person, it is your duty to look after them or protect their interests.
gloss_zh: （照顾某人或保护某人利益的）义务，责任

observer.translation:
n. 观察者, 遵守者, 观察员
[法] 观察者, 观察员, 监场员

senses.concept_en: You can refer to someone who sees or notices something as an observer .
An observer is someone who studies current events and situations, especially in order to comment on them and predict what will happen next.
An observer is a person who is sent to observe an important event or situation, especially in order to make sure it happens as it should, or so that they can tell other people about it.
gloss_zh: （监督重大事件或局势的）观察员

senses.concept_en: You use of to combine two nouns when the first noun identifies the feature of the second noun that you want to talk about.
gloss_zh: （用于连接两个名词，其中前者表示后者的特定方面）

senses.concept_en: You use of to combine two nouns, or a noun and a present participle, when the second noun or present participle defines or gives more information about the first noun.
gloss_zh: （用于连接两个名词或名词与现在分词，其中后者对前者进行界定或补充信息）

senses.concept_en: You use of after nouns referring to actions to specify the person or thing that is affected by the action or that performs the action. For example, 'the kidnapping of the child' refers to an action affecting a child; 'the arrival of the next train' refers to an action performed by a train.
gloss_zh: （用于指称动作的名词后说明该动作的对象或主体）

senses.concept_en: You use of after words and phrases referring to quantities or groups of things to indicate the substance or thing that is being measured.
gloss_zh: （用于指称数量或组群的词和短语后表示计量的对象）

senses.concept_en: You use of after the name of someone or something to introduce the institution or place they belong to or are connected with.
gloss_zh: （用于人或事物的名称后引出其所属或相关的机构或地方）

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun referring to a container to form an expression referring to the container and its contents.
gloss_zh: （用于指称容器的名词后，说明容器及其所含物）

senses.concept_en: You use of after a count noun and before an uncount noun when you want to talk about an individual piece or item.
gloss_zh: （用在可数名词后、不可数名词前表示某一单个物品）

senses.concept_en: You use of to indicate the materials or things that form something.
gloss_zh: （表示材料或成分）由…制成（或组成）的

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun which specifies a particular part of something, to introduce the thing that it is a part of.
gloss_zh: （用于名词后表示其为某事物的一部分）

senses.concept_en: You use of after some verbs to indicate someone or something else involved in the action.
gloss_zh: （用于某些动词后表示动作所涉及的人或事物）关于，由于

senses.concept_en: You use of after some adjectives to indicate the thing that a feeling or quality relates to.
gloss_zh: （用于某些形容词后表示与情感或特性相关的事物）对，为

senses.concept_en: You use of before a word referring to the person who performed an action when saying what you think about the action.
gloss_zh: （用于指称施动者的单词前说明对该动作的看法）出自…，在…一方

senses.concept_en: You use of after a noun which describes someone or something, to introduce the person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （用于描述名词后引出所指的人或事物）

senses.concept_en: If something is more of or less of a particular thing, it is that thing to a greater or smaller degree.
gloss_zh: （表示程度）更大/较小程度上的…

senses.concept_en: You use of to indicate a characteristic or quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （表示某人或某事物具有的特点或特性）

senses.concept_en: You use of after the verb 'be' to indicate a characteristic or quality that someone or something has.
gloss_zh: （用于be动词后表示某人或某事物具有的特点或特性）

senses.concept_en: You use of to specify an amount, value, or age.
You use of after a noun such as 'month' or 'year' to indicate the length of time that some state or activity continues.
gloss_zh: （用于年、月等名词后表示状态或活动的持续时间）

senses.concept_en: You can use of to say what time it is by indicating how many minutes there are before the hour mentioned.
gloss_zh: （表示时间离某一钟点差几分）在…之前

office.translation:
n. 办公室, 部, 公职, 职责
[化] 办公室

senses.concept_en: An office is a room or a part of a building where people work sitting at desks.
An office is a department of an organization, especially the government, where people deal with a particular kind of administrative work.
An office is a small building or room where people can go for information, tickets, or a service of some kind.
gloss_zh: （问询、购票或提供服务的）处，所

senses.concept_en: A doctor's or dentist's office is a place where a doctor or dentist sees their patients.
If someone holds office in a government, they have an important job or position of authority.

official.translation:
n. 官员, 公务员, 职员
a. 公务的, 官方的, 正式的

senses.concept_en: Official means approved by the government or by someone in authority.
Official activities are carried out by a person in authority as part of their job.
Official things are used by a person in authority as part of their job.
If you describe someone's explanation or reason for something as the official explanation, you are suggesting that it is probably not true, but is used because the real explanation is embarrassing.
gloss_zh: （解释、理由等）冠冕堂皇的，桌面上的

senses.concept_en: An official is a person who holds a position of authority in an organization.
gloss_zh: 官员；行政人员；高级职员

senses.concept_en: An official at a sports event is a referee, umpire, or other person who checks that the players follow the rules.
gloss_zh: （体育比赛中的）裁判员，执法人

derivation.breakdown_zh: office 办公 + -ial 形容词后缀：官方的

old.translation:
n. 以前, 往昔
a. 老的, 旧的, 古老的, 年长的, 老练的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.
gloss_zh: 年老的；年纪大的；不年轻的

senses.concept_en: You use old to talk about how many days, weeks, months, or years someone or something has lived or existed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is old has existed for a long time.
gloss_zh: 古老的；长久的；历史悠久的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is old is no longer in good condition because of its age or because it has been used a lot.
You use old to refer to something that is no longer used, that no longer exists, or that has been replaced by something else.
gloss_zh: 旧时的；过去的；从前的；过时的

senses.concept_en: You use old to refer to something that used to belong to you, or to a person or thing that used to have a particular role in your life.
gloss_zh: 原来（属于自己）的；原先（生活中）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: An old friend, enemy, or rival is someone who has been your friend, enemy, or rival for a long time.
gloss_zh: （朋友）相识已久的；（敌人）结有宿怨的；（对手）长期竞争的

senses.concept_en: You can use old to express affection when talking to or about someone you know.

on.translation:
prep. 在...之上
adv. ...上去
a. 正起作用的
[计] 打开

senses.concept_en: If someone or something is on a surface or object, the surface or object is immediately below them and is supporting their weight.
If something is on a surface or object, it is stuck to it or attached to it.
If you put, throw, or drop something on a surface, you move it or drop it so that it is then supported by the surface.
You use on to say what part of your body is supporting your weight.
You use on to say that someone or something touches a part of a person's body.
gloss_zh: （表示接触到身体某部位）在…上

senses.concept_en: If someone has a particular expression on their face, their face has that expression.
When you put a piece of clothing on, you place it over part of your body in order to wear it. If you have it on, you are wearing it.
You can say that you have something on you if you are carrying it in your pocket or in a bag.
If someone's eyes are on you, they are looking or staring at you.
If you hurt yourself on something, you accidentally hit a part of your body against it and that thing causes damage to you.
If you are on an area of land, you are there.
If something is situated on a place such as a road or coast, it forms part of it or is by the side of it.
gloss_zh: 是（道路、海岸等）的一部分；在…边上

senses.concept_en: If you get on a bus, train, or plane, you go into it in order to travel somewhere. If you are on it, you are travelling in it.
gloss_zh: 上，乘（公共汽车、火车或飞机）

senses.concept_en: If there is something on a piece of paper, it has been written or printed there.
If something is on a list, it is included in it.
Books, discussions, or ideas on a particular subject are concerned with that subject.
You use on to introduce the method, principle, or system which is used to do something.
gloss_zh: 以，凭，靠（某一方法、原则或系统）

senses.concept_en: If something is done on an instrument or a machine, it is done using that instrument or machine.
gloss_zh: 通过，借助于（某一器械或机器）

senses.concept_en: If information is, for example, on tape or on computer, that is the way that it is stored.
If something is being broadcast, you can say that it is on the radio or television.
When an activity is taking place, you can say that it is on .
You use on in expressions such as 'have a lot on' and 'not have very much on' to indicate how busy someone is.
gloss_zh: （表示某人忙碌程度）忙得很/没什么可忙

senses.concept_en: You use on to introduce an activity that someone is doing, particularly travelling.
gloss_zh: （引出所进行的活动，特别是旅行）处于…情况中，在从事…中

senses.concept_en: When something such as a machine or an electric light is on, it is functioning or in use. When you switch it on, it starts functioning.
gloss_zh: （机器、电灯等）开着，工作着，使用中

senses.concept_en: If you are on a committee or council, you are a member of it.
You can indicate when something happens by saying that it happens on a particular day or date.
gloss_zh: 在（某一日子或日期）（发生）

senses.concept_en: You use on when mentioning an event that was followed by another one.
You use on to say that someone is continuing to do something.
If you say that someone goes on at you, you mean that they continually criticize you, complain to you, or ask you to do something.
You use on in expressions such as from now on and from then on to indicate that something starts to happen at the time mentioned and continues to happen afterwards.
You often use on after the adverbs 'early', 'late', 'far', and their comparative forms, especially at the beginning or end of a sentence, or before a preposition.
gloss_zh: （常用在副词early，late，far及其比较级之后，尤置于句首、句尾或介词之前）

senses.concept_en: Someone who is on a drug takes it regularly.
If you live on a particular kind of food, you eat it. If a machine runs on a particular kind of power or fuel, it uses it in order to function.
gloss_zh: 以…（为食）；（机器）用（某种动力或燃料运转）

senses.concept_en: If you are on a particular income, that is the income that you have.
Taxes or profits that are obtained from something are referred to as taxes or profits on it.
When you buy something or pay for something, you spend money on it.
When you spend time or energy on a particular activity, you spend time or energy doing it.

one.translation:
n. 一(个)
pron. 一, 任何人
num. 一, 一个
a. 一致的, 完整的

senses.concept_en: One is the number 1.
If you say that someone or something is the one person or thing of a particular kind, you are emphasizing that they are the only person or thing of that kind.
One can be used instead of 'a' to emphasize the following noun.
gloss_zh: （用于代替a以强调之后的名词）

senses.concept_en: You can use one instead of 'a' to emphasize the following adjective or expression.
gloss_zh: （用于代替a以强调之后的形容词或短语）

senses.concept_en: You can use one in front of someone's name to indicate that you have not met them or heard of them before.
gloss_zh: （用于人名前，表示未曾相识或听闻的）某一个

senses.concept_en: You can use one to refer to the first of two or more things that you are comparing.
gloss_zh: （表示与其他的作比较）这一个

senses.concept_en: You can use one or ones instead of a noun when it is clear what type of thing or person you are referring to and you are describing them or giving more information about them.
gloss_zh: （用于代替名词，指代某类明确的人或事物）

senses.concept_en: You use ones to refer to people in general.
You can use one instead of a noun group when you have just mentioned something and you want to describe it or give more information about it.
gloss_zh: （用于代替名词词组，表示刚提到过的事物）

senses.concept_en: You can use one when you have been talking or writing about a group of people or things and you want to say something about a particular member of the group.
gloss_zh: （特指一群人或事物中的）一人，一个

senses.concept_en: You use one in expressions such as 'one of the biggest airports' or 'one of the most experienced players' to indicate that something or someone is bigger or more experienced than most other things or people of the same kind.
collocations: one of the most experienced players

senses.concept_en: You can use one when referring to a time in the past or in the future. For example, if you say that you did something one day, you mean that you did it on a day in the past. one day
You can use one to refer to a question, joke, remark, or subject of discussion.
gloss_zh: （指代问题、笑话、评论、讨论的主题等）一个

senses.concept_en: You can use one to refer to an alcoholic drink.
You use one to make statements about people in general which also apply to themselves. One can be used as the subject or object of a sentence.
gloss_zh: （泛指包括自己的人，可作句子的主语或宾语）一个人，任何人

open.translation:
n. 公开, 户外, 空旷
a. 开着的, 开放的, 开阔的, 营业着的, 公开的, 悬而未决的
vt. 打开, 公开, 开放
vi. 展开, 开始, 展现
[计] 打开指令; 打开语句

senses.concept_en: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.
If you open something such as a bottle, box, parcel, or envelope, you move, remove, or cut part of it so you can take out what is inside.
gloss_zh: 将（瓶、盒等）开封；拆开（包裹、信封等）

senses.concept_en: If you open something such as a book, an umbrella, or your hand, or if it opens, the different parts of it move away from each other so that the inside of it can be seen.
If you open a computer file, you give the computer an instruction to display it on the screen.
When you open your eyes or your eyes open, you move your eyelids upwards, for example when you wake up, so that you can see.
If you open your arms, you stretch them wide apart in front of you, usually in order to put them round someone.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you stand or sit in an open way, the front of your body is fully exposed and you are not bending forward or at an angle to someone.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a person or their character as open, you mean they are honest and do not want or try to hide anything or to deceive anyone.
gloss_zh: 坦率的；诚恳的；不作伪的

senses.concept_en: If you describe a situation, attitude, or way of behaving as open, you mean it is not kept hidden or secret.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are open to suggestions or ideas, you are ready and willing to consider or accept them.
gloss_zh: 愿意接受（建议、观点等）的；虚怀若谷的

senses.concept_en: If you say that a system, person, or idea is open to something such as abuse or criticism, you mean they might receive abuse or criticism because of their qualities, effects, or actions.
gloss_zh: 容易招致（滥用、批评等）的；易受（攻击）的

senses.concept_en: If you say that a fact or question is open to debate, interpretation, or discussion, you mean that people are uncertain whether it is true, what it means, or what the answer is.
gloss_zh: 悬而未决的；尚未决定的

senses.concept_en: If people open something such as a blocked road or a border, or if it opens, people can then pass along it or through it.
gloss_zh: 开放（被封的道路、边界等）；开通

senses.concept_en: If a place opens into another, larger place, you can move from one directly into the other.
An open area is a large area that does not have many buildings or trees in it.
An open structure or object is not covered or enclosed.
gloss_zh: 敞开的；无遮盖的；无围挡的

senses.concept_en: An open wound is one from which a liquid such as blood is coming.
If you open your shirt or coat, you undo the buttons or pull down the zip.
gloss_zh: 把（衣服）解开；把…的拉链拉开

senses.concept_en: When a shop, office, or public building opens or is opened, its doors are unlocked and the public can go in.
When a public building, factory, or company opens or when someone opens it, it starts operating for the first time.
gloss_zh: 为（大楼、工厂、公司等）举行揭幕典礼；开设；开办；开张

senses.concept_en: If something such as a meeting or series of talks opens, or if someone opens it, it begins.

If an event such as a meeting or discussion opens with a particular activity or if a particular activity opens an event, that activity is the first thing that happens or is dealt with. You can also say that someone such as a speaker or singer opens by doing a particular thing.
On the stock exchange, the price at which currencies, shares, or commodities open is their value at the start of that day's trading.
When a film, play, or other public event opens, it begins to be shown, be performed, or take place for a limited period of time.
If you open an account with a bank or a commercial organization, you begin to use their services.
If an opportunity or choice is open to you, you are able to do a particular thing if you choose to.
gloss_zh: （机会、选择等）可利用的，可得到的

senses.concept_en: To open opportunities or possibilities means the same as to open them up.
gloss_zh: （使）（机会、可能性等）出现;（使）产生

senses.concept_en: You can use open to describe something that anyone is allowed to take part in or accept.
gloss_zh: 人人可以参加（或接受）的；开放的

senses.concept_en: See also:opening; If something such as an offer or job is open, it is available for someone to accept or apply for.
gloss_zh: （提议等）有效的；（职位等）空缺的，可申请的

or.translation:
conj. 或, 或者
[计] 或

senses.concept_en: You use or to link two or more alternatives.
gloss_zh: （连接两个或两个以上选择的可能性）或，或者，还是

senses.concept_en: You use or to give another alternative, when the first alternative is introduced by 'either' or 'whether'.
gloss_zh: （与 either 或 whether 连用，给出另一个选择项）或，还是，就是

senses.concept_en: You use or between two numbers to indicate that you are giving an approximate amount.
gloss_zh: （用于两个数字之间表示概数）或，大约

senses.concept_en: You use or to introduce a comment which corrects or modifies what you have just said.
gloss_zh: （用于对刚说过的话进行更正或补充）或者说

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone should do something or something unpleasant will happen, you are warning them that if they do not do it, the unpleasant thing will happen.
You use or to introduce something which is evidence for the truth of a statement you have just made.
gloss_zh: （用于证明刚刚所作陈述的真实性）否则，要不然

out.translation:
a. 外面的, 熄灭的, 结束的
adv. 在外, 熄灭, 出现
prep. 出自, 离去, 向

senses.concept_en: When something is in a particular place and you take it out, you remove it from that place.
You can use out to indicate that you are talking about the situation outside, rather than inside buildings.
If you are out, you are not at home or not at your usual place of work.
If you say that someone is out in a particular place, you mean that they are in a different place, usually one far away.
When the sea or tide goes out, the sea moves away from the shore.
If you are out a particular amount of money, you have that amount less than you should or than you did.
gloss_zh: 缺少，不足，损失（某一数量的钱）

senses.concept_en: If a light or fire is out or goes out, it is no longer shining or burning.
If flowers are out, their petals have opened.
If something such as a book or CD is out, it is available for people to buy.
If workers are out, they are on strike.
In a game or sport, if someone is out, they can no longer take part either because they are unable to or because they have been defeated.
In baseball, a player is out if they do not reach a base safely. When three players in a team are out in an inning, then the team is out.
If you say that a proposal or suggestion is out, you mean that it is unacceptable.
gloss_zh: （提议或建议）不能接受的，不值得考虑的

senses.concept_en: If you say that a particular thing is out, you mean that it is no longer fashionable at the present time.
gloss_zh: 不时髦的；不流行的；过时的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that a calculation or measurement is out, you mean that it is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （计算或测量）不准确的，错误的

senses.concept_en: If someone is out to do something, they intend to do it.
If a group of people out a public figure or famous person, they reveal that person's homosexuality against their wishes.
gloss_zh: 公开揭露（公众人物、名人等）的同性恋身份

overnight.translation:
n. 前一天晚上, 一夜的逗留
a. 通宵的, 晚上的, 前夜的
adv. 在前一夜, 整夜, 昨晚一晚上

senses.concept_en: If something happens overnight, it happens throughout the night or at some point during the night.
gloss_zh: 在整个夜间；在夜里的某一时刻

senses.concept_en: You can say that something happens overnight when it happens very quickly and unexpectedly.
Overnight bags or clothes are ones that you take when you go and stay somewhere for one or two nights.
If you overnight somewhere, you spend the night there.

derivation.breakdown_zh: over- 贯穿 + night 夜：整夜

paper.translation:
n. 纸, 文件, 文章, 报纸, 证券, 证件
vt. 用纸糊, 贴壁纸于, 用纸包装
vi. 贴壁纸
a. 纸做的, 纸上的

senses.concept_en: Paper is a material that you write on or wrap things with. The pages of this book are made of paper.
A paper is a newspaper.
You can refer to newspapers in general as the paper or the papers .
Your papers are sheets of paper with writing or information on them, which you might keep in a safe place at home.
Your papers are official documents, for example your passport or identity card, which prove who you are or which give you official permission to do something.
A paper is a long, formal piece of writing about an academic subject.
See also:term paper; A paper is an essay written by a student.
A paper is a part of a written examination in which you answer a number of questions in a particular period of time.
See also:Green Paper;White Paper; A paper prepared by a government or a committee is a report on a question they have been considering or a set of proposals for changes in the law.
gloss_zh: （政府或委员会发表的关于重大问题的）文件，报告

senses.concept_en: Paper agreements, qualifications, or profits are ones that are stated by official documents to exist, although they may not really be effective or useful.
If you paper a wall, you put wallpaper on it.

partially.translation: adv. 部分地, 一部分地, 不公平地

senses.concept_en: If something happens or exists partially, it happens or exists to some extent, but not completely.
gloss_zh: 部分地；在某种程度上；有点儿

pipe.translation:
n. 管, 导管, 输送管, 管状器官, 声带, 尖细的声音, 烟斗, 笛, 管乐器
vt. 以管输送, 吹哨子, 吹奏, 尖声唱
vi. 吹笛, 尖叫, 吹长哨发令
[计] 管道

senses.concept_en: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.
gloss_zh: （通常指金属或塑料制的）管子，管道

senses.concept_en: A pipe is an object which is used for smoking tobacco. You put the tobacco into the cup-shaped part at the end of the pipe, light it, and breathe in the smoke through a narrow tube.
A pipe is a simple musical instrument in the shape of a tube with holes in it. You play a pipe by blowing into it while covering and uncovering the holes with your fingers.
Pipes are the same as bagpipes .
An organ pipe is one of the long hollow tubes in which air vibrates and produces a musical note.
If liquid or gas is piped somewhere, it is transferred from one place to another through a pipe.
gloss_zh: 用管子输送，用管道运输（液体或气体）

senses.concept_en: If someone, especially a child, pipes something, they say it in a high-pitched voice.
In some computer systems, a pipe is a method of passing information from one program to another.
gloss_zh: （一些计算机系统中用来在程序间传送信息的）管道

plan.translation:
n. 计划, 方案, 策略, 方法, 进度表, 程序表, 平面图, 设计图, 轮廓, 示意图
vt. 计划, 设计, 意欲
vi. 订计划

senses.concept_en: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand.
If you plan what you are going to do, you decide in detail what you are going to do, and you intend to do it.
If you have plans, you are intending to do a particular thing.
gloss_zh: （有做某一特定事的）计划，打算，意向

senses.concept_en: When you plan something that you are going to make, build, or create, you decide what the main parts of it will be and do a drawing of how it should be made.
gloss_zh: 设计；绘制…的图样（或图表）

senses.concept_en: A plan of something that is going to be built or made is a detailed diagram or drawing of it.

postal.translation:
a. 邮政的, 邮局的
[经] 邮政的

senses.concept_en: Postal is used to describe things or people connected with the public service of carrying letters and packages from one place to another.
Postal is used to describe activities that involve sending things by post.

derivation.breakdown_zh: post 邮寄 + -al 形容词后缀：邮政的

pressure.translation:
n. 压, 榨, 按, 强制, 压力, 压迫, 压强
vt. 迫使, 使增压, 密封
pressure.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: Pressure is force that you produce when you press hard on something.
The pressure in a place or container is the force produced by the quantity of gas or liquid in that place or container.
If there is pressure on a person, someone is trying to persuade or force them to do something.
If you are experiencing pressure, you feel that you must do a lot of tasks or make a lot of decisions in very little time, or that people expect a lot from you.
If you pressure someone to do something, you try forcefully to persuade them to do it.

prince.translation: n. 王子, 亲王, 国君, 贵族, 诸侯, 有权势的大人物

senses.concept_en: A prince is a male member of a royal family, especially the son of the king or queen of a country.
A prince is the male royal ruler of a small country or state.
If someone describes a man as the prince of a particular type of work, they mean that he is the best man doing that type of work.

problem.translation:
n. 问题, 难题
a. 成问题的, 难处理的

senses.concept_en: A problem is a situation that is unsatisfactory and causes difficulties for people.
A problem is a puzzle that requires logical thought or mathematics to solve it.
gloss_zh: （通过逻辑思考或数学运算解决的）问题，习题，题

senses.concept_en: Problem children or problem families have serious problems or cause serious problems for other people.
gloss_zh: （儿童或家庭）有严重问题的，引起严重问题的

produce.translation:
n. 生产品, 物产, 后代
vt. 产生, 生产, 提出, 出示
vi. 生产, 制造
produce.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl gre

senses.concept_en: To produce something means to cause it to happen.
If you produce something, you make or create it.
When things or people produce something, it comes from them or slowly forms from them, especially as the result of a biological or chemical process.
If you produce evidence or an argument, you show it or explain it to people in order to make them agree with you.
If you produce an object from somewhere, you show it or bring it out so that it can be seen.
If someone produces something such as a film, a magazine, or a CD, they organize it and decide how it should be done.
gloss_zh: 上演（戏剧）；制作（电影、电视节目）；灌制（唱片）

senses.concept_en: Produce is food or other things that are grown in large quantities to be sold.

project.translation:
n. 计划, 设计, 事业
vt. 计划, 设计, 投掷, 发射, 使凸出, 放映
vi. 凸出
project.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A project is a task that requires a lot of time and effort.
A project is a detailed study of a subject by a pupil or student.
If something is projected, it is planned or expected.
If you project someone or something in a particular way, you try to make people see them in that way. If you project a particular feeling or quality, you show it in your behaviour.
If you project feelings or ideas on to other people, you imagine that they have the same ideas or feelings as you.
gloss_zh: 把（情感、想法）投射转移（到他人身上）

senses.concept_en: If you project a film or picture onto a screen or wall, you make it appear there.
If something projects, it sticks out above or beyond a surface or edge.

promise.translation:
n. 诺言, 约定的事情, 有指望
vt. 允诺, 约定, 预示
vi. 允诺, 有前途, 有指望
promise.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you promise that you will do something, you say to someone that you will definitely do it.
If you promise someone something, you tell them that you will definitely give it to them or make sure that they have it.
gloss_zh: 答应给予；承诺给予；保证让…得到

senses.concept_en: A promise is a statement which you make to a person in which you say that you will definitely do something or give them something.
If a situation or event promises to have a particular quality or to be a particular thing, it shows signs that it will have that quality or be that thing.
If someone or something shows promise, they seem likely to be very good or successful.
gloss_zh: （非常好的或成功的）希望，迹象，指望

proposal.translation:
n. 提议, 计划, 求婚
[经] 提案, 申请, 投标

senses.concept_en: A proposal is a plan or an idea, often a formal or written one, which is suggested for people to think about and decide upon.
A proposal is the act of asking someone to marry you.

protect.translation:
vt. 防卫, 保护, 警戒
[法] 庇护, 保护, 警戒

senses.concept_en: To protect someone or something means to prevent them from being harmed or damaged.
If an insurance policy protects you against an event such as death, injury, fire, or theft, the insurance company will give you or your family money if that event happens.

prove.translation:
vt. 证明, 查验, 检验, 勘探, 显示
vi. 证明是

senses.concept_en: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.
If you prove that something is true, you show by means of argument or evidence that it is definitely true.
If you prove yourself to have a certain good quality, you show by your actions that you have it.

public.translation:
n. 公众, 民众
a. 公众的, 公共的, 公立的, 公用的
public.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: You can refer to people in general, or to all the people in a particular country or community, as the public .
You can refer to a set of people in a country who share a common interest, activity, or characteristic as a particular kind of public .
gloss_zh: 志趣相投（或从事同一类活动、具有共同特征）的群体

senses.concept_en: Public means relating to all the people in a country or community.
Public means relating to the government or state, or things that are done for the people by the state.
gloss_zh: 政府的；国家的；公共事务的

senses.concept_en: Public buildings and services are provided for everyone to use.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A public place is one where people can go about freely and where you can easily be seen and heard.
If someone is a public figure or in public life, many people know who they are because they are often mentioned in newspapers and on television.
Public is used to describe statements, actions, and events that are made or done in such a way that any member of the public can see them or be aware of them.
gloss_zh: （声明、事件等）公开的，公之于众的

senses.concept_en: If a fact is made public or becomes public, it becomes known to everyone rather than being kept secret.
gloss_zh: 公之于众的；公开的；人人皆知的

pull.translation:
vt. 拉, 拖, 拔, 牵, 撕开, 吸引
vi. 拉, 拖, 拔, 有吸引力
n. 拉, 拖, 拔, 拉力, 牵引力, 划船, 吸引

senses.concept_en: When you pull something, you hold it firmly and use force in order to move it towards you or away from its previous position.
When you pull an object from a bag, pocket, or cupboard, you put your hand in and bring the object out.
When a vehicle, animal, or person pulls a cart or piece of machinery, they are attached to it or hold it, so that it moves along behind them when they move forward.
If you pull yourself or pull a part of your body in a particular direction, you move your body or a part of your body with effort or force.
When a driver or vehicle pulls to a stop or a halt, the vehicle stops.
In a race or contest, if you pull ahead of or pull away from an opponent, you gradually increase the amount by which you are ahead of them.
If you pull something apart, you break or divide it into small pieces, often in order to put them back together again in a different way.
If someone pulls a gun or a knife on someone else, they take out a gun or knife and threaten the other person with it.
To pull crowds, viewers, or voters means to attract them.
gloss_zh: 吸引，拉拢（人群、观众或选民）

senses.concept_en: If something pulls you or pulls your thoughts or feelings in a particular direction, it strongly attracts you or influences you in a particular way.
A pull is a strong physical force which causes things to move in a particular direction.
If you are pulling for someone, you support and encourage them, especially in a competition.
If you pull a muscle, you injure it by straining it.
If someone pulls on a cigarette, they take a deep breath with the cigarette in their mouth.
To pull a stunt or a trick on someone means to do something dramatic or silly in order to get their attention or trick them.
If someone pulls someone else, they succeed in attracting them sexually and in spending the rest of the evening or night with them.

pump.translation:
n. 抽水机, 打气筒, 泵, 抽吸
vt. 用唧筒抽水, 打气, 盘问, 倾注, 使疲惫
