vi. 抽水, 上下(或往复)运动
pump.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A pump is a machine or device that is used to force a liquid or gas to flow in a particular direction.
To pump a liquid or gas in a particular direction means to force it to flow in that direction using a pump.
A petrol or gas pump is a machine with a tube attached to it that you use to fill a car with petrol.
If someone has their stomach pumped, doctors remove the contents of their stomach, for example because they have swallowed poison or drugs.
If you pump money or other resources into something such as a project or an industry, you invest a lot of money or resources in it.
If you pump someone about something, you keep asking them questions in order to get information.
To pump bullets into someone means to fire a lot of bullets into them very quickly.
Pumps are canvas shoes with flat rubber soles which people wear for sports and leisure.
gloss_zh: （运动或休闲时穿的）橡胶底帆布鞋

senses.concept_en: Pumps are women's shoes that do not cover the top part of the foot and are usually made of plain leather.

push.translation:
n. 推, 推动, 奋斗, 攻击, 进取心
vt. 推, 推动, 使伸出, 推行, 逼迫, 增加
vi. 推, 推进, 增加, 努力争取

senses.concept_en: When you push something, you use force to make it move away from you or away from its previous position.
If you push through things that are blocking your way or push your way through them, you use force in order to move past them.
If an army pushes into a country or area that it is attacking or invading, it moves further into it.
To push a value or amount up or down means to cause it to increase or decrease.
If someone or something pushes an idea or project in a particular direction, they cause it to develop or progress in a particular way.
If you push someone to do something or push them into doing it, you encourage or force them to do it.
If you push for something, you try very hard to achieve it or to persuade someone to do it.
If someone pushes an idea, a point, or a product, they try in a forceful way to convince people to accept it or buy it.
gloss_zh: 力劝接受；极力宣传；推销

senses.concept_en: When someone pushes drugs, they sell them illegally.
If you say that someone is pushing it, you mean that their actions or claims are rather excessive or risky.

radical.translation:
n. 激进分子, 词根, 基础, 根式, 根
a. 激进的, 根本的, 基本的, 根的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Radical changes and differences are very important and great in degree.
gloss_zh: 重大的;根本的;基本的;彻底的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Radical people believe that there should be great changes in society and try to bring about these changes.

raise.translation:
n. 上升, 高地, 增高
vt. 升起, 举起, 唤起, 提高, 使出现, 使复活, 提出, 筹集, 饲养

senses.concept_en: If you raise something, you move it so that it is in a higher position.
If you raise a flag, you display it by moving it up a pole or into a high place where it can be seen.
If you raise yourself, you lift your body so that you are standing up straight, or so that you are no longer lying flat.
If you raise the rate or level of something, you increase it.
To raise the standard of something means to improve it.
If you raise your voice, you speak more loudly, usually because you are angry.
A raise is an increase in your wages or salary.
If you raise money for a charity or an institution, you ask people for money which you collect on its behalf.
gloss_zh: （为慈善组织、机构等）募捐，筹（款）

senses.concept_en: If a person or company raises money that they need, they manage to get it, for example by selling their property or by borrowing.
If an event raises a particular emotion or question, it makes people feel the emotion or consider the question.
If you raise a subject, an objection, or a question, you mention it or bring it to someone's attention.
Someone who raises a child looks after it until it is grown up.
If someone raises a particular type of animal or crop, they breed that type of animal or grow that type of crop.

recognize.translation:
vt. 认出, 认可, 承认, 公认, 识别, 赏识
vi. 承认, 具结

senses.concept_en: If you recognize someone or something, you know who that person is or what that thing is.
If someone says that they recognize something, they acknowledge that it exists or that it is true.
If people or organizations recognize something as valid, they officially accept it or approve of it.
gloss_zh: 正式认可;承认;正式接受;赞成

senses.concept_en: When people recognize the work that someone has done, they show their appreciation of it, often by giving that person an award of some kind.
gloss_zh: 赞赏，认可（某人的所作所为）

reliability.translation:
n. 信度, 可靠性
[计] 可靠性

rely.translation: vi. 信赖, 依赖, 信任
rely.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you rely on someone or something, you need them and depend on them in order to live or work properly.
If you can rely on someone to work well or to behave as you want them to, you can trust them to do this.

reputation.translation:
n. 名誉, 名声, 声望
[法] 名声, 名誉, 公认证据
reputation.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts gre

senses.concept_en: To have a reputation for something means to be known or remembered for it.
Something's or someone's reputation is the opinion that people have about how good they are. If they have a good reputation, people think they are good.

require.translation:
vt. 需要, 命令, 要求
[法] 需要, 要求, 命令

senses.concept_en: If you require something or if something is required, you need it or it is necessary.
If a law or rule requires you to do something, you have to do it.

response.translation:
n. 反应, 回答, 响应
[计] 应答

senses.concept_en: Your response to an event or to something that is said is your reply or reaction to it.

road.translation:
n. 路, 道路, 公路, 途径, 方法
[法] 公路, 道路, 行车道

senses.concept_en: A road is a long piece of hard ground which is built between two places so that people can drive or ride easily from one place to the other.
The road to a particular result is the means of achieving it or the process of achieving it.

roughly.translation: adv. 概略地, 粗糙地, 粗暴地

run.translation:
n. 跑, 赛跑, 奔跑, 奔跑的路程, 趋向, 流出, 运转时间, 连续
vi. 跑, 奔跑, 跑步, 赛跑, 竞赛, 行驶, 运转, 进行, 蔓延
vt. 使跑, 参赛, 追究, 驾驶, 开动, 管理, 经营, 使流出, 运行
a. 熔化的, 融化的, 浇铸的
run的过去式和过去分词
[计] 运行

senses.concept_en: When you run, you move more quickly than when you walk, for example because you are in a hurry to get somewhere, or for exercise.
When someone runs in a race, they run in competition with other people.
When a horse runs in a race or when its owner runs it, it competes in a race.
If you say that something long, such as a road, runs in a particular direction, you are describing its course or position. You can also say that something runs the length or width of something else.
If you run a wire or tube somewhere, you fix it or pull it from, to, or across a particular place.
gloss_zh: 安装（电线、管道等）;布线;使（电线、管道等）通过

senses.concept_en: If you run your hand or an object through something, you move your hand or the object through it.
If you run something through a machine, process, or series of tests, you make it go through the machine, process, or tests.
gloss_zh: 使通过（机器、过程或测试）

senses.concept_en: If someone runs for office in an election, they take part as a candidate.
A run for office is an attempt to be elected to office.
If you run something such as a business or an activity, you are in charge of it or you organize it.
If you talk about how a system, an organization, or someone's life is running, you are saying how well it is operating or progressing.
If you run an experiment, computer program, or other process, or start it running, you start it and let it continue.
When you run a cassette or video tape or when it runs, it moves through the machine as the machine operates.
When a machine is running or when you are running it, it is switched on and is working.
A machine or equipment that runs on or off a particular source of energy functions using that source of energy.
gloss_zh: （机器或设备靠某种能源）运转，开动

senses.concept_en: If you run a car or a piece of equipment, you have it and use it.
When you say that vehicles such as trains and buses run from one place to another, you mean they regularly travel along that route.
gloss_zh: （火车、公交车等沿固定路线）行驶

senses.concept_en: If you run someone somewhere in a car, you drive them there.
If you run over or down to a place that is quite near, you drive there.
A run is a journey somewhere.
If a liquid runs in a particular direction, it flows in that direction.
If you run water, or if you run a tap or a bath, you cause water to flow from a tap.
If a tap or a bath is running, water is coming out of a tap.
If your nose is running, liquid is flowing out of it, usually because you have a cold.
If a surface is running with a liquid, that liquid is flowing down it.
If the dye in some cloth or the ink on some paper runs, it comes off or spreads when the cloth or paper gets wet.
If a feeling runs through your body or a thought runs through your mind, you experience it or think it quickly.
If a feeling or noise runs through a group of people, it spreads among them.
gloss_zh: （感觉或吵闹声）扩散，弥漫，传遍

senses.concept_en: If a theme or feature runs through something such as someone's actions or writing, it is present in all of it.
When newspapers or magazines run a particular item or story or if it runs, it is published or printed.
You can use run to indicate that you are quoting someone else's words or ideas.
If an amount is running at a particular level, it is at that level.
If a play, event, or legal contract runs for a particular period of time, it lasts for that period of time.
If someone or something is running late, they have taken more time than had been planned. If they are running to time or ahead of time, they have taken the time planned or less than the time planned.
gloss_zh: 占用（多于、等于或少于预定的时间）

senses.concept_en: If you are running a temperature or a fever, you have a high temperature because you are ill.
A run of a play or television programme is the period of time during which performances are given or programmes are shown.
gloss_zh: （演出或电视节目的）上映期，放映期

senses.concept_en: A run of successes or failures is a series of successes or failures.
gloss_zh: 一系列，一连串（成功或失败等）

senses.concept_en: A run of a product is the amount that a company or factory decides to produce at one time.
gloss_zh: 额定产量;单次生产数额

senses.concept_en: In cricket or baseball, a run is a score of one, which is made by players running between marked places on the field after hitting the ball.
gloss_zh: （板球或棒球运动中击球后跑动得到的）一分

senses.concept_en: If someone gives you the run of a place, they give you permission to go where you like in it and use it as you wish.
gloss_zh: 自由出入的权力;随意使用的权力

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone or something is different from the average run or common run of people or things, you mean that they are different from ordinary people or things.
If there is a run on something, a lot of people want to buy it or get it at the same time.
A ski run or bobsleigh run is a course or route that has been designed for skiing or for riding in a bobsleigh.

runner.translation:
n. 跑步者, 赛跑者, 送信人, 走私船, 操作者, 滑槽
[化] 碾碎机; 压碎机

senses.concept_en: A runner is a person who runs, especially for sport or pleasure.
The runners in a horse race are the horses taking part.
A drug runner or gun runner is someone who illegally takes drugs or guns into a country.
Someone who is a runner for a particular person or company is employed to take messages, collect money, or do other small tasks for them.
gloss_zh: 送信人;信使;收账员;听差

senses.concept_en: Runners are thin strips of wood or metal underneath something which help it to move smoothly.
gloss_zh: （雪橇的）滑板;（冰鞋的）冰刀;（抽屉的）滑轨

senses.concept_en: On a plant, runners are long shoots that grow from the main stem and put down roots to form a new plant.
A runner is a long narrow mat that is put on a piece of furniture or on the floor.

safety.translation:
n. 安全, 保险, 平安, 保安设备
vt. 保护, 防护
safety.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Safety is the state of being safe from harm or danger.
If you reach safety, you reach a place where you are safe from danger.
If you are concerned about the safety of something, you are concerned that it might be harmful or dangerous.
gloss_zh: 安全程度;安全性;无害;无危险

senses.concept_en: If you are concerned for someone's safety, you are concerned that they might be in danger.
Safety features or measures are intended to make something less dangerous.

scream.translation:
n. 尖叫声
vi. 尖叫, 大笑, 尖啸, 令人震惊
vt. 尖叫着说, 大叫大嚷着要求

senses.concept_en: When someone screams, they make a very loud, high-pitched cry, for example because they are in pain or are very frightened.
If you scream something, you shout it in a loud, high-pitched voice.
When something makes a loud, high-pitched noise, you can say that it screams .
If you say that someone is a scream, you think they are very funny.

sealing.translation:
[化] 封闭; 封闭处理
[医] 封闭, 封口(创伤)

serious.translation:
a. 严肃的, 认真的, 重要的, 严重的
[电] 严重的
serious.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Serious problems or situations are very bad and cause people to be worried or afraid.
gloss_zh: 严重的;危急的;令人担忧的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Serious matters are important and deserve careful and thoughtful consideration.
gloss_zh: 重要的;需要认真考虑的;严肃的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: When important matters are dealt with in a serious way, they are given careful and thoughtful consideration.
Serious music or literature requires concentration to understand or appreciate it.
gloss_zh: （音乐、文学作品）严肃的，非供消遣（或娱乐）的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is serious about something, they are sincere about what they are saying, doing, or intending to do.
gloss_zh: 认真的;当真的;真心的;郑重其事的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Serious people are thoughtful and quiet, and do not laugh very often.
gloss_zh: （人）若有所思的，庄重的，严肃的

senses.concept_en: Serious money is a very large amount of money.

service.translation:
n. 服务, 贡献, 雇佣, 公职, 服役, 功劳, 仪式, 送达, 行政部门
vt. 保养, 维修
a. 武装部队的, 服务性的, 仆人的, 耐用的
[计] 服务, 业务

senses.concept_en: A service is something that the public needs, such as transport, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body.
gloss_zh: 公共服务事业;公共服务系统

senses.concept_en: You can sometimes refer to an organization or private company as a particular service when it provides something for the public or acts on behalf of the government.
If an organization or company provides a particular service, they can do a particular job or a type of work for you.
gloss_zh: （机构或公司提供的某一）服务

senses.concept_en: Services are activities such as tourism, banking, and selling things which are part of a country's economy, but are not concerned with producing or manufacturing goods.
The level or standard of service provided by an organization or company is the amount or quality of the work it can do for you.
gloss_zh: 服务内容;服务（质量）;服务态度

senses.concept_en: A bus or train service is a route or regular journey that is part of a transport system.
gloss_zh: （公共汽车或火车的）路线，行程车次，班车

senses.concept_en: Your services are the things that you do or the skills that you use in your job, which other people find useful and are usually willing to pay you for.
If you refer to someone's service or services to a particular organization or activity, you mean that they have done a lot of work for it or spent a lot of their time on it.
gloss_zh: （为某组织或活动所做的）工作，服务，效劳

senses.concept_en: The Services are the army, the navy, and the air force.
Service is the work done by people or equipment in the army, navy, or air force, for example during a war.
When you receive service in a restaurant, hotel, or shop, an employee asks you what you want or gives you what you have ordered.
A service is a religious ceremony that takes place in a church.
A dinner service or a tea service is a complete set of plates, cups, saucers, and other pieces of china.
A services is a place beside a motorway where you can buy petrol and other things, or have a meal.
gloss_zh: （高速公路边可加油、购物或用餐的）服务站

senses.concept_en: In tennis, badminton, and some other sports, when it is your service, it is your turn to serve.
gloss_zh: （网球、羽毛球等的）发球权，开球局

senses.concept_en: Service is used to describe the parts of a building or structure that are used by the staff who clean, repair, or look after it, and are not usually used by the public.
gloss_zh: （大楼、建筑中的设施）员工专用的，后勤专用的

senses.concept_en: If someone is in service, they are working as a servant.
If you have a vehicle or machine serviced, you arrange for someone to examine, adjust, and clean it so that it will keep working efficiently and safely.
gloss_zh: 维修，检修,维护（机器、车辆）

senses.concept_en: If a country or organization services its debts, it pays the interest on them.
If someone or something services an organization, a project, or a group of people, they provide it with the things that it needs in order to function properly or effectively.
gloss_zh: 为…提供服务;满足…的需求

several.translation:
a. 几个的, 一些的, 各自的
pron. 几个

senses.concept_en: Several is used to refer to an imprecise number of people or things that is not large but is greater than two.

shake.translation:
n. 摇动, 震动
vt. 摇动, 动摇, 使震动, 挥舞
vi. 震动, 发抖, 动摇
shake.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl

senses.concept_en: If you shake something, you hold it and move it quickly backwards and forwards or up and down. You can also shake a person, for example, because you are angry with them or because you want them to wake up.
If you shake yourself or your body, you make a lot of quick, small, repeated movements without moving from the place where you are.
gloss_zh: 摇动，抖动（身体或身体部位）

senses.concept_en: If you shake your head, you turn it from side to side in order to say 'no' or to show disbelief or sadness.
gloss_zh: 摇头（表示拒绝、怀疑或难过）

senses.concept_en: If you are shaking, or a part of your body is shaking, you are making quick, small movements that you cannot control, for example because you are cold or afraid.
gloss_zh: （因为寒冷或害怕而）发抖，颤抖，战栗，哆嗦

senses.concept_en: If you have the shakes, your body is shaking a lot because you are afraid or ill, or because you have drunk too much alcohol.
gloss_zh: （因害怕、生病或喝醉酒而产生的）颤抖，战栗，哆嗦

senses.concept_en: If you shake your fist or an object such as a stick at someone, you wave it in the air in front of them because you are angry with them.
gloss_zh: （因愤怒而）挥动,舞动（拳头、棍子等）

senses.concept_en: If a force shakes something, or if something shakes, it moves from side to side or up and down with quick, small, but sometimes violent movements.
To shake something into a certain place or state means to bring it into that place or state by moving it quickly up and down or from side to side.
If your voice is shaking, you cannot control it properly and it sounds very unsteady, for example because you are nervous or angry.
If an event or a piece of news shakes you, or shakes your confidence, it makes you feel upset and unable to think calmly.
If an event shakes a group of people or their beliefs, it causes great uncertainty and makes them question their beliefs.
If you shake someone out of an attitude or belief that you disapprove of, you cause them to change their attitude or belief to one that is more responsible or sensible.
gloss_zh: 使摒弃，使改变（态度、信念）

senses.concept_en: A shake is the same as a milkshake .

shock.translation:
n. 震动, 冲突, 震惊, 冲击, 突击, 禾束堆, 休克, 长毛狗
vt. 使震动, 使休克, 使受电击, 震惊得
vi. 震动, 吓人
a. 蓬乱浓密的
shock.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you have a shock, something suddenly happens which is unpleasant, upsetting, or very surprising.
gloss_zh: 震惊;惊愕;令人震惊的事

senses.concept_en: Shock is a person's emotional and physical condition when something very frightening or upsetting has happened to them.
If someone is in shock, they are suffering from a serious physical condition in which their blood is not flowing round their body properly, for example because they have had a bad injury.
If something shocks you, it makes you feel very upset, because it involves death or suffering and because you had not expected it.
If someone or something shocks you, it upsets or offends you because you think it is rude or morally wrong.
gloss_zh: （因行为粗鲁或不道德而）使不快，使气愤，使厌恶，使反感

senses.concept_en: A shock announcement or event is one which shocks people because it is unexpected.
gloss_zh: （通告、事件等）令人惊愕的，令人震惊的

senses.concept_en: A shock is something sudden and unexpected that threatens the economy, traditions, or way of life of a group of people.
gloss_zh: （对经济、传统、生活方式的）冲击，撞击

senses.concept_en: A shock is the force of something suddenly hitting or pulling something else.
A shock is the same as an electric shock .
A shock is a shock absorber .
A shock of hair is a very thick mass of hair on a person's head.
You use should when you are saying what would be the right thing to do or the right state for something to be in.
You use should to give someone an order to do something, or to report an official order.
gloss_zh: （表示给出指示或公布官方命令）应该，必须

senses.concept_en: If you say that something should have happened, you mean that it did not happen, but that you wish it had. If you say that something should not have happened, you mean that it did happen, but that you wish it had not.
gloss_zh: （表示与说话者的意愿相反）本应

senses.concept_en: You use should when you are saying that something is probably the case or will probably happen in the way you are describing. If you say that something should have happened by a particular time, you mean that it will probably have happened by that time.
gloss_zh: （表示预期或可能性）应该会，可能

senses.concept_en: You use should in questions when you are asking someone for advice, permission, or information.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句中表示征求意见、同意或咨询情况）可以，应该

senses.concept_en: You say 'I should', usually with the expression 'if I were you', when you are giving someone advice by telling them what you would do if you were in their position.
gloss_zh: （通过假设自己处于对方立场会怎么做来提出建议）应该，可以，会

senses.concept_en: You use should in conditional clauses when you are talking about things that might happen.
gloss_zh: （用在条件从句中表示事件发生的可能性）将要，假定要

senses.concept_en: You use should in 'that' clauses after certain verbs, nouns, and adjectives when you are talking about a future event or situation.
gloss_zh: （用在由 that引导的从句中，放在某些动词、名词和形容词之后，表示将来的事件或情况）应该，能够，竟然会

senses.concept_en: You use should in expressions such as I should think and I should imagine to indicate that you think something is true but you are not sure.
gloss_zh: （与第一人称连用，表示没有把握）会，可能

senses.concept_en: You use should in expressions such as I should like and I should be happy to show politeness when you are saying what you want to do, or when you are requesting, offering, or accepting something.
gloss_zh: （与第一人称连用表示客气的请求等）想要，将会

senses.concept_en: You use should in expressions such as You should have seen us and You should have heard him to emphasize how funny, shocking, or impressive something that you experienced was.
gloss_zh: （强调所经历的事有趣、令人震惊等）实在该，真该，真应当

senses.concept_en: You use should in question structures which begin with words like 'who' and 'what' and are followed by 'but' to emphasize how surprising or shocking a particular event was.
gloss_zh: （用在由who，what等引导的疑问结构中，后接but，强调某件事令人惊讶或震惊）居然

slam.translation:
n. 砰然声, 猛然, 猛烈的抨击
vt. 猛然关上, 砰地关上, 猛烈抨击
vi. 砰地关上, 猛攻

senses.concept_en: If you slam a door or window or if it slams, it shuts noisily and with great force.
If you slam something down, you put it there quickly and with great force.
To slam someone or something means to criticize them very severely.
If one thing slams into or against another, it crashes into it with great force.

slow.translation:
a. 慢的, 缓慢的, 迟缓的, 迟钝的, 冷漠的, 落后的
adv. 慢地, 迟缓地
v. (使)慢下来

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is slow moves, happens, or is done without much speed.
In informal English, slower is used to mean 'at a slower speed' and slowest is used to mean 'at the slowest speed'. In non-standard English, slow is used to mean 'with little speed'.
gloss_zh: （用于非正式英语中）缓慢地，慢吞吞地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is slow takes a long time.
gloss_zh: 费时间的;时间长的;迟缓的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone is slow to do something, they do it after a delay.
If something slows or if you slow it, it starts to move or happen more slowly.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is slow is not very clever and takes a long time to understand things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe a situation, place, or activity as slow, you mean that it is not very exciting.
gloss_zh: 呆滞的;不景气的;沉闷的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a clock or watch is slow, it shows a time that is earlier than the correct time.

small.translation:
a. 小的, 少的, 小型的, 低微的, 小气的, 细微的
adv. 些微地
n. 狭小部分

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A small person, thing, or amount of something is not large in physical size.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A small group or quantity consists of only a few people or things.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A small child is a very young child.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use small to describe something that is not significant or great in degree.
gloss_zh: 不重要的;无足轻重的;程度小的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Small businesses or companies employ a small number of people and do business with a small number of clients.
gloss_zh: （企业或公司）小规模的，小型的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone speaks in a small voice, they speak in a quiet, high voice because they are frightened or ashamed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone makes you look or feel small, they make you look or feel stupid or ashamed.
The small of your back is the bottom part of your back that curves in slightly.

smoke.translation:
n. 烟, 雾气, 烟熏剂, 抽烟, 烟色
vi. 吸烟, 冒烟, 弥漫
vt. 以烟熏, 抽烟而导致...

senses.concept_en: Smoke consists of gas and small bits of solid material that are sent into the air when something burns.
If something is smoking, smoke is coming from it.
When someone smokes a cigarette, cigar, or pipe, they suck the smoke from it into their mouth and blow it out again. If you smoke, you regularly smoke cigarettes, cigars, or a pipe.
If fish or meat is smoked, it is hung over burning wood so that the smoke preserves it and gives it a special flavour.

so.translation:
adv. 如此, 如是, 如...那样
conj. 所以, 因此
pron. 这样

senses.concept_en: You use so to refer back to something that has just been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 如此，这样（指已经提到的事）

senses.concept_en: You use so when you are saying that something which has just been said about one person or thing is also true of another one.
gloss_zh: 同样，也一样（指后者跟前者一样）

senses.concept_en: You use the structures as...so and just as...so when you want to indicate that two events or situations are similar in some way.
gloss_zh: （表示两个事件或情况在某方面相似）正如…，也…

senses.concept_en: If you say that a state of affairs is so, you mean that it is the way it has been described.
gloss_zh: （指某一情况）就是这样，事实如此

senses.concept_en: You can use so with actions and gestures to show a person how to do something, or to indicate the size, height, or length of something.
gloss_zh: （向别人示范）这样，像这样;（用手势比划大小、高度或长度）这么，那么

senses.concept_en: You use so and so that to introduce the result of the situation you have just mentioned.
You use so ,so that, and so as to introduce the reason for doing the thing that you have just mentioned.
You can use so in stories and accounts to introduce the next event in a series of events or to suggest a connection between two events.
gloss_zh: （在叙述过程中引出一系列事件中的下一件或说明两件事情之间的联系）此后，于是

senses.concept_en: You can use so in conversations to introduce a new topic, or to introduce a question or comment about something that has been said.
gloss_zh: （表示开始新话题、引入新问题或对刚说过的问题进行评论）那么，这么

senses.concept_en: You can use so in conversations to show that you are accepting what someone has just said.
gloss_zh: （谈话中表示接受别人的说法）的确，确实

senses.concept_en: You can use so in front of adjectives and adverbs to emphasize the quality that they are describing.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词和副词之前强调所描述的特性）如此，这么，多么，太

senses.concept_en: You can use so...that and so...as to emphasize the degree of something by mentioning the result or consequence of it.
gloss_zh: 如此…（以致…）;到…的程度（以致…）

soon.translation: adv. 不久, 早, 快, 宁可

senses.concept_en: If something is going to happen soon, it will happen after a short time. If something happened soon after a particular time or event, it happened a short time after it.

sort.translation:
n. 种类, 方式, 品质, 态度, 举止
vt. 分类, 排序, 挑选
vi. 交往, 协调
[计] 排序; DOS外部命令:从标准输入设备接收数据, 整个数据输入完后
对它以行为单位进行排序, 然后在标准输出设备上输出
sort.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: If you talk about a particular sort of something, you are talking about a class of things that have particular features in common and that belong to a larger group of related things.
You describe someone as a particular sort when you are describing their character.
gloss_zh: 具有某种性格的人;某种人

senses.concept_en: If you sort things, you separate them into different classes, groups, or places, for example so that you can do different things with them.
If you get a problem or the details of something sorted, you do what is necessary to solve the problem or organize the details.

sound.translation:
n. 声音, 语音, 吵闹, 声调, 听力范围, 探条, 海峡
a. 健全的, 可靠的, 合理的, 健康的, 彻底的, 资金充实的
adv. 彻底地, 充分地
vi. 发出声音, 回响, 测深, 试探, 听起来
vt. 使发声, 宣告, 听诊, 测...深, 试探
[计] 声音

senses.concept_en: A sound is something that you hear.
Sound is energy that travels in waves through air, water, or other substances, and can be heard.
gloss_zh: 声（指通过空气、水或其他物质传播的一种能量）

senses.concept_en: The sound on a television, radio, or CD player is what you hear coming from the machine. Its loudness can be controlled.
gloss_zh: （电视、收音机、CD 机等可调节音量的）声音，音响

senses.concept_en: A singer's or band's sound is the distinctive quality of their music.
gloss_zh: （歌手或乐队的）音乐风格，乐曲特色

senses.concept_en: If something such as a horn or a bell sounds or if you sound it, it makes a noise.
If you sound a warning, you publicly give it. If you sound a note of caution or optimism, you say publicly that you are cautious or optimistic.
gloss_zh: 发出（警告等）;（以…语调）发表

senses.concept_en: When you are describing a noise, you can talk about the way it sounds .
When you talk about the way someone sounds, you are describing the impression you have of them when they speak.
When you are describing your impression or opinion of something you have heard about or read about, you can talk about the way it sounds .
gloss_zh: （用于谈论印象或观点）听起来，似乎

senses.concept_en: You can describe your impression of something you have heard about or read about by talking about the sound of it.
gloss_zh: （对于听说或读到的事情的）印象

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a structure, part of someone's body, or someone's mind is sound, it is in good condition or healthy.
gloss_zh: （身体）健康的;（心智）健全的;（建筑）坚固的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Sound advice, reasoning, or evidence is reliable and sensible.
gloss_zh: （建议、推理或证据）正确的，合理的，可靠的，明智的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe someone's ideas as sound, you mean that you approve of them and think they are correct.
If someone is in a sound sleep, they are sleeping very deeply.

stack.translation:
n. 堆叠, 堆, 大量, 书库, 枪架, 烟囱, 堆积, 存贮栈
vt. 堆积, 堆满, 暗中对...做手脚
vi. 堆起
[计] 堆积, 堆栈

senses.concept_en: A stack of things is a pile of them.
If you stack a number of things, you arrange them in neat piles.
If you say that someone has stacks of something, you mean that they have a lot of it.
If someone in authority stacks an organization or body, they fill it with their own supporters so that the decisions it makes will be the ones they want it to make.
gloss_zh: 在（某组织机构中）安插（对自己有利的人员）

stand.translation:
n. 站立, 站住, 停顿, 讲台, 看台, 立场, 法院证人席
vi. 站, 立, 坐落, 停滞, 位于, 坚持, 维持原状
vt. 忍受, 使站立, 抵挡

senses.concept_en: When you are standing, your body is upright, your legs are straight, and your weight is supported by your feet.
When someone who is sitting stands, they change their position so that they are upright and on their feet.
If you stand aside or stand back, you move a short distance sideways or backwards, so that you are standing in a different place.
If something such as a building or a piece of furniture stands somewhere, it is in that position, and is upright.
You can say that a building is standing when it remains after other buildings around it have fallen down or been destroyed.
gloss_zh: （建筑物在周围其他建筑物倒塌或被毁后）依然存在，矗立

senses.concept_en: If you stand something somewhere, you put it there in an upright position.
If you leave food or a mixture of something to stand, you leave it without disturbing it for some time.
gloss_zh: （将食物或调拌物等）搁置不动

senses.concept_en: If you take or make a stand, you do something or say something in order to make it clear what your attitude to a particular thing is.
If you ask someone where or how they stand on a particular issue, you are asking them what their attitude or view is.
If you do not know where you stand with someone, you do not know exactly what their attitude to you is.
You can use stand instead of 'be' when you are describing the present state or condition of something or someone.
If a decision, law, or offer stands, it still exists and has not been changed or cancelled.
If something that can be measured stands at a particular level, it is at that level.
You can describe how tall or high someone or something is by saying that they stand a particular height.
If something can stand a situation or a test, it is good enough or strong enough to experience it without being damaged, harmed, or shown to be inadequate.
gloss_zh: 经得起，承受得住（困难、考验）

senses.concept_en: If you cannot stand something, you cannot bear it or tolerate it.
If you cannot stand someone or something, you dislike them very strongly.
If you stand to gain something, you are likely to gain it. If you stand to lose something, you are likely to lose it.
gloss_zh: 可能获得/ 可能失去

senses.concept_en: If you stand in an election, you are a candidate in it.
If you stand someone a meal or a drink, you buy it for them.
See also:newsstand; A stand is a small shop or stall, outdoors or in a large public building.
gloss_zh: （设在户外或大型公共建筑物内的）小店，售货摊

senses.concept_en: A stand at a sports ground is a large structure where people sit or stand to watch what is happening.
A stand is an object or piece of furniture that is designed for supporting or holding a particular kind of thing.
A stand is an area where taxis or buses can wait to pick up passengers.
gloss_zh: （出租车、公共汽车的）停车候客处

senses.concept_en: In a law court, the stand is the place where a witness stands to answer questions.

star.translation:
n. 星, 恒星, 星形物, 运气, 明星
vt. 以星状物装饰, 用星号标, 使成为明星
vi. 变成明星

senses.concept_en: See also:morning star;shooting star; A star is a large ball of burning gas in space. Stars appear to us as small points of light in the sky on clear nights.
You can refer to a shape or an object as a star when it has four, five, or more points sticking out of it in a regular pattern.

You can say how many stars something such as a hotel or restaurant has as a way of talking about its quality, which is often indicated by a number of star-shaped symbols. The more stars something has, the better it is.
Famous actors, musicians, and sports players are often referred to as stars .
If an actor or actress stars in a play or film, he or she has one of the most important parts in it.
gloss_zh: （在戏剧或电影中）担任主角，主演

senses.concept_en: If a play or film stars a famous actor or actress, he or she has one of the most important parts in it.
Predictions about people's lives which are based on astrology and appear regularly in a newspaper or magazine are sometimes referred to as the stars .

station.translation:
n. 车站, 站, 局, 驻地, 位置, 身分, 地位
vt. 安置, 配置, 驻扎
[计] 站

senses.concept_en: A station is a building by a railway line where trains stop so that people can get on or off.
A bus station is a building, usually in a town or city, where buses stop, usually for a while, so that people can get on or off.
If you talk about a particular radio or television station, you are referring to the programmes broadcast by a particular radio or television company.
If soldiers or officials are stationed in a place, they are sent there to do a job or to work for a period of time.
gloss_zh: 安置,派驻（士兵或官员）;使驻扎

senses.concept_en: If you station yourself somewhere, you go there and wait, usually for a particular purpose.
gloss_zh: （常指为某一特定目的）在…守候

steam.translation:
n. 蒸汽, 精力
a. 蒸汽的
vi. 蒸发, 行驶, 发怒
vt. 蒸, 煮, 散发
steam.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: Steam is the hot mist that forms when water boils. Steam vehicles and machines are operated using steam as a means of power.
If something steams, it gives off steam.
If you steam food or if it steams, you cook it in steam rather than in water

step.translation:
n. 步骤, 步, 步幅, 脚步声, 踏级, 步伐, 短距离, 步态, 手段, 等级
vt. 踏, 以步测量, 跨步, 使成阶梯状
vi. 跨步, 轻快地走, 跳舞, 踩, 踏上, 行走
[计] 步骤

senses.concept_en: If you take a step, you lift your foot and put it down in a different place, for example when you are walking.
If you step on something or step in a particular direction, you put your foot on the thing or move your foot in that direction.
Steps are a series of surfaces at increasing or decreasing heights, on which you put your feet in order to walk up or down to a different level.
See also:doorstep; A step is a raised flat surface in front of a door.
A step is one of a series of actions that you take in order to achieve something.
A step in a process is one of a series of stages.
The steps of a dance are the sequences of foot movements which make it up.
Someone's step is the way they walk.
Steps are the same as a stepladder .

stone.translation:
n. 石头, 宝石, 果核, 纪念碑, 结石
vt. 投扔石子, 铺石头
a. 石的, 石制的, 完全的
stone.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Stone is a hard solid substance found in the ground and often used for building houses.
A stone is a small piece of rock that is found on the ground.
A stone is a large piece of stone put somewhere in memory of a person or event, or as a religious symbol.
gloss_zh: （作为宗教标志的）石碑;纪念碑

senses.concept_en: Stone is used in expressions such as set in stone and tablets of stone to suggest that an idea or rule is firm and fixed, and cannot be changed.
gloss_zh: （表示观念或规则固定而不可改变）板上钉钉，铁板钉钉

senses.concept_en: You can refer to a jewel as a stone .
A stone is a small hard ball of minerals and other substances which sometimes forms in a person's kidneys or gall bladder.
The stone in a plum, cherry, or other fruit is the large hard seed in the middle of it.
If you stone a fruit, you remove its stone.
If people stone someone or something, they throw stones at them.
A stone is a measurement of weight, especially the weight of a person, equal to 14 pounds or 6.35 kilograms
gloss_zh: 英石（重量单位，相当于 14 磅或6.35公斤）

street.translation:
n. 街道, 马路, 街区
a. 街道的

senses.concept_en: A street is a road in a city, town, or village, usually with houses along it.
You can use street or streets when talking about activities that happen out of doors in a town rather than inside a building.

strong.translation:
a. 强壮的, 坚固的, 坚强的, 强烈的, 有力的, 优良的
adv. 强劲地, 有力地, 猛烈地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is strong is healthy with good muscles and can move or carry heavy things, or do hard physical work.
gloss_zh: 强壮的;健壮的;力气大的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is strong is confident and determined, and is not easily influenced or worried by other people.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Strong objects or materials are not easily broken and can support a lot of weight or resist a lot of strain.
gloss_zh: 不易损坏的;坚固的;结实的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A strong wind, current, or other force has a lot of power or speed, and can cause heavy things to move.
gloss_zh: （风、水流等）强劲的，迅猛的，狂奔的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A strong impression or influence has a great effect on someone.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you have strong opinions on something or express them using strong words, you have extreme or very definite opinions which you are willing to express or defend.
gloss_zh: （观点、措辞）坚定的，强烈的，不动摇的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone in authority takes strong action, they act firmly and severely.
gloss_zh: （当权者的行为）坚定的，强硬的，严厉的，不动摇的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If there is a strong case or argument for something, it is supported by a lot of evidence.
gloss_zh: （理由、论据）有说服力的，强有力的，充分的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If there is a strong possibility or chance that something is true or will happen, it is very likely to be true or to happen.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Your strong points are your best qualities or talents, or the things you are good at.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A strong competitor, candidate, or team is good or likely to succeed.
gloss_zh: （竞争者、候选人、队伍）强大的，有望成功的，有实力的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a relationship or link is strong, it is close and likely to last for a long time.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A strong currency, economy, or industry has a high value or is very successful.
gloss_zh: （货币）坚挺的;（经济）强劲的;（行业）景气的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is a strong element or part of something else, it is an important or large part of it.
gloss_zh: （因素、成分）重要的，占很大比例的

senses.concept_en: You can use strong when you are saying how many people there are in a group. For example, if a group is twenty strong, there are twenty people in it.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A strong drink, chemical, or drug contains a lot of the particular substance which makes it effective.
gloss_zh: （饮品、化学品、药物）含量高的，浓的，酽的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A strong colour, flavour, smell, sound, or light is intense and easily noticed.
gloss_zh: 醒目的;响亮的;浓烈的;强烈的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If someone has a strong accent, they speak in a distinctive way that shows very clearly what country or region they come from.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can say that someone has strong features or a strong face if their face has large, distinctive features.

success.translation: n. 成功, 成就, 胜利

senses.concept_en: Success is the achievement of something that you have been trying to do.
Success is the achievement of a high position in a particular field, for example in business or politics.
The success of something is the fact that it works in a satisfactory way or has the result that is intended.
gloss_zh: （某事所取得的）成功，良好表现

senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is a success achieves a high position, makes a lot of money, or is admired a great deal.

such.translation: a. 如此的, 这样的

senses.concept_en: You use such to refer back to the thing or person that you have just mentioned, or a thing or person like the one that you have just mentioned. You use such as and such...as to introduce a reference to the person or thing that has just been mentioned.
gloss_zh: 这样的;那样的;上述的;诸如此类的

senses.concept_en: You use such...as to link something or someone with a clause in which you give a description of the kind of thing or person that you mean.
You use such...as to introduce one or more examples of the kind of thing or person that you have just mentioned.
You use such before noun groups to emphasize the extent of something or to emphasize that something is remarkable.
gloss_zh: （用于名词词组前强调某事的程度或某事了不起）如此，这样，非常

senses.concept_en: You use such...that in order to emphasize the degree of something by mentioning the result or consequence of it.
gloss_zh: （用于强调程度）如此…，非常…（以至于…）

senses.concept_en: You use such...that or such...as in order to say what the result or consequence of something that you have just mentioned is.

sudden.translation:
n. 突然, 忽然
a. 突然的, 意外的, 快速的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Sudden means happening quickly and unexpectedly.

suddenly.translation: adv. 突然, 意外, 忽然, 迅速, 即席作成, 即刻, 急速

senses.concept_en: If something happens suddenly, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.

suffer.translation:
vt. 遭受, 经历, 忍受
vi. 受痛苦, 受损害

senses.concept_en: If you suffer pain, you feel it in your body or in your mind.
gloss_zh: 遭受，经受（疼痛）;感到（痛苦）

senses.concept_en: If you suffer from an illness or from some other bad condition, you are badly affected by it.
gloss_zh: （因疾病或处于其他不利境地而）受苦，受难，受折磨

senses.concept_en: If you suffer something bad, you are in a situation in which something painful, harmful, or very unpleasant happens to you.
gloss_zh: 遭遇，遭受，蒙受（不好的事）

senses.concept_en: If you suffer, you are badly affected by an event or situation.
If something suffers, it does not succeed because it has not been given enough attention or is in a bad situation.
gloss_zh: （因不够关注或处于不利境况而）失利，失败，不成功

suggest.translation:
vt. 提议, 建议, 促成, 暗示, 启发, 使人想起
[法] 建议, 提出, 提议

senses.concept_en: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.
If you suggest the name of a person or place, you recommend them to someone.
If you suggest that something is the case, you say something which you believe is the case.
If one thing suggests another, it implies it or makes you think that it might be the case.
If one thing suggests another, it brings it to your mind through an association of ideas.

support.translation:
n. 支持, 支撑, 援助, 供养, 支撑物
vt. 支援, 支撑, 帮助, 支持, 忍受, 供养, 证实
[计] 后援; 支持

senses.concept_en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.
If you give support to someone during a difficult or unhappy time, you are kind to them and help them.
Financial support is money provided to enable an organization to continue. This money is usually provided by the government.
If you support someone, you provide them with money or the things that they need.
If a fact supports a statement or a theory, it helps to show that it is true or correct.
If something supports an object, it is underneath the object and holding it up.
A support is a bar or other object that supports something.
If you support yourself, you prevent yourself from falling by holding onto something or by leaning on something.
If you support a sports team, you always want them to win and perhaps go regularly to their games.
At a concert or show, the support or the support act is a less well-known person or band who performs before the main person or band.
gloss_zh: （音乐会、演出的）助演演员，助演乐队

system.translation:
n. 系统, 体系, 制度, 方式, 秩序, 分类原则
[计] 系统; 体制; 体系
system.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A system is a way of working, organizing, or doing something which follows a fixed plan or set of rules. You can use system to refer to an organization or institution that is organized in this way.
A system is a set of devices powered by electricity, for example a computer or an alarm.
A system is a set of equipment or parts such as water pipes or electrical wiring, which is used to supply water, heat, or electricity.
A system is a network of things that are linked together so that people or things can travel from one place to another or communicate.
Your system is your body's organs and other parts that together perform particular functions.
A system is a particular set of rules, especially in mathematics or science, which is used to count or measure things.
gloss_zh: （尤指数学或科学中的）体系,体制

senses.concept_en: People sometimes refer to the government or administration of a country as the system .
gloss_zh: 政府;现行体制;公共行政

table.translation:
n. 桌子, 餐桌, 工作台, 铭文, 表格, 表, 高原, 平地层
vt. 搁置, 嵌合, 制表, 把...列入议事日程
[计] 表格, 模拟运算表

senses.concept_en: A table is a piece of furniture with a flat top that you put things on or sit at.
If you ask for a table in a restaurant, you want to have a meal there.
If someone tables a proposal, they say formally that they want it to be discussed at a meeting.
If someone tables a proposal or plan which has been put forward, they decide to discuss it or deal with it at a later date, rather than straight away.
A table is a written set of facts and figures arranged in columns and rows.
A table is a list of the multiplications of numbers between one and twelve. Children often have to learn tables at school.

take.translation:
vt. 拿, 取, 抓, 带领, 获得, 就座, 接受, 吃, 吸引, 采取, 乘, 需要, 花费
vi. 吃掉对方棋子, 抓住, 起作用, 依法获得财产
n. 拿, 取, 收成, 奏效

senses.concept_en: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say 'she took a shower' instead of 'she showered'.
gloss_zh: （后接名词，用于描述动作或事件）

senses.concept_en: In ordinary spoken or written English, people use take with a range of nouns instead of using a more specific verb. For example people often say 'he took control' or 'she took a positive attitude' instead of 'he assumed control' or 'she adopted a positive attitude'.
gloss_zh: （与一系列名词连用，代替意义更为具体的动词）

senses.concept_en: If you take something, you reach out for it and hold it.
If you take something with you when you go somewhere, you carry it or have it with you.
If a person, vehicle, or path takes someone somewhere, they transport or lead them there.
If something such as a job or interest takes you to a place, it is the reason for you going there.
If you take something such as your problems or your business to someone, you go to that person when you have problems you want to discuss or things you want to buy.
gloss_zh: 请教（问题等）；洽谈（生意等）

senses.concept_en: If one thing takes another to a particular level, condition, or state, it causes it to reach that level or condition.
gloss_zh: 使…达到（一定水平、程度或状态）

senses.concept_en: If you take something from a place, you remove it from there.
If you take something from someone who owns it, you steal it or go away with it without their permission.
If an army or political party takes something or someone, they win them from their enemy or opponent.
gloss_zh: （军队、政党）攻占，夺取，赢得，俘虏

senses.concept_en: If you take one number or amount from another, you subtract it or deduct it.
If you cannot take something difficult, painful, or annoying, you cannot tolerate it without becoming upset, ill, or angry.
If you take something such as damage or loss, you suffer it, especially in war or in a battle.
gloss_zh: （尤指在战争中）蒙受，遭受（损害、损失）

senses.concept_en: If something takes a certain amount of time, that amount of time is needed in order to do it.
If something takes a particular quality or thing, that quality or thing is needed in order to do it.
gloss_zh: 需要，要求（某种素质或某物）

senses.concept_en: If you take something that is given or offered to you, you agree to accept it.
If you take a feeling such as pleasure, pride, or delight in a particular thing or activity, the thing or activity gives you that feeling.
If a shop, restaurant, theatre, or other business takes a certain amount of money, they get that amount from people buying goods or services.
You can use take to refer to the amount of money that a business such as a store or theatre gets from selling its goods or tickets during a particular period.
If you take a prize or medal, you win it.
If you take the blame, responsibility, or credit for something, you agree to accept it.
gloss_zh: 承担，承受，接受（责备、责任或功劳）

senses.concept_en: If you take patients or clients, you accept them as your patients or clients.
If you take a telephone call, you speak to someone who is telephoning you.
If you take something in a particular way, you react in the way mentioned to a situation or to someone's beliefs or behaviour.
You use take when you are discussing or explaining a particular question, in order to introduce an example or to say how the question is being considered.
If you take someone's meaning or point, you understand and accept what they are saying.
If you take someone for something, you believe wrongly that they are that thing.
If you take something from among a number of things, you choose to have or buy it.
If you take a road or route, you choose to travel along it.
If you take a house or flat, you rent it, usually for only a short time.
If you take something such as a newspaper, you buy it or have it delivered to your home on a regular basis.
If you take a car, train, bus, or plane, you use it to go from one place to another.
If you take a subject or course at school or university, you choose to study it.
If you take a test or examination, you do it in order to obtain a qualification.
If you take someone for a subject, you give them lessons in that subject.
If someone takes drugs, pills, or other medicines, they take them into their body, for example by swallowing them.
If you take food or drink, you eat or drink it.
If you take a note or a letter, you write down something you want to remember or the words that someone says.
If you take a particular measurement, you use special equipment to find out what something measures.
If a place or container takes a particular amount or number, there is enough space for that amount or number.
If you take a particular size in shoes or clothes, that size fits you.
gloss_zh: 穿（特定尺码的鞋或衣物）

senses.concept_en: If something such as a drug or a dye takes, it has the effect or result that is intended.
A take is a short piece of action which is filmed in one continuous process for a cinema or television film.
Someone's take on a particular situation or fact is their attitude to it or their interpretation of it.

tall.translation:
a. 高的, 长的, 夸大的
adv. 夸大地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone or something that is tall has a greater height than is normal or average.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use tall to ask or talk about the height of someone or something

task.translation:
n. 工作, 任务, 作业, 困难的工作
vt. 派给...工作, 使辛劳
[计] 任务

senses.concept_en: A task is an activity or piece of work which you have to do, usually as part of a larger project.
If you are tasked with doing a particular activity or piece of work, someone in authority asks you to do it.

technology.translation:
n. 技术, 工业技术, 术语
[医] 技术学, 工艺学
technology.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: Technology refers to methods, systems, and devices which are the result of scientific knowledge being used for practical purposes.

terror.translation:
n. 恐怖, 可怕的人
[医] 惊吓, 惊悸
terror.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: Terror is very great fear.
Terror is violence or the threat of violence, especially when it is used for political reasons.
gloss_zh: （尤指有政治目的的）恐怖活动，恐怖主义

senses.concept_en: A terror is something that makes you very frightened.
If someone describes a child as a terror, they think that he or she is naughty and difficult to control.
gloss_zh: 讨厌的小孩;淘气鬼;小捣蛋

test.translation:
n. 测试, 试验, 化验, 检验, 考验, 甲壳
vt. 测试, 试验, 化验
vi. 接受测验, 进行测试
test.tags: zk gk cet4 cet6 ky ielts

senses.concept_en: When you test something, you try it, for example by touching it or using it for a short time, in order to find out what it is, what condition it is in, or how well it works.
A test is a deliberate action or experiment to find out how well something works.
If you test someone, you ask them questions or tell them to perform certain actions in order to find out how much they know about a subject or how well they are able to do something.
A test is a series of questions that you must answer or actions that you must perform in order to show how much you know about a subject or how well you are able to do something.
If you test someone, you deliberately make things difficult for them in order to see how they react.
If an event or situation is a test of a person or thing, it reveals their qualities or effectiveness.
If you are tested for a particular disease or medical condition, you are examined or go through various procedures in order to find out whether you have that disease or condition.
A medical test is an examination of a part of your body in order to check that you are healthy or to find out what is wrong with you.
A test is a sports match between two international teams, usually in cricket, rugby union, or rugby league.
gloss_zh: （常指板球、橄榄球的）国际锦标赛

than.translation:
conj. 比, 除...外
prep. 比

senses.concept_en: You use than after a comparative adjective or adverb in order to link two parts of a comparison.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词、副词的比较级之后，连接比较对象）比

senses.concept_en: You use than when you are stating a number, quantity, or value approximately by saying that it is above or below another number, quantity, or value.
gloss_zh: （数目、数量、价值等）比…（多、少、重要或次要等）

senses.concept_en: You use than in order to link two parts of a contrast, for example in order to state a preference.
gloss_zh: 与其说，而不是（连接对比的对象，以表示优先考虑等）

that.translation:
a. 那, 那个
conj. 以致, 因为
pron. 那
adv. 那么, 那样

senses.concept_en: You use that to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.
gloss_zh: 那，那个（指代前面句子里提到的）

senses.concept_en: You use that to refer to someone or something already mentioned.
gloss_zh: 那个人,那个（用来指代已经提到的人或物）

senses.concept_en: When you have been talking about a particular period of time, you use that to indicate that you are still referring to the same period. You use expressions such as that morning or that afternoon to indicate that you are referring to an earlier period of the same day.
gloss_zh: 那，那个（指已经谈到过的特定时期）

senses.concept_en: You use that in expressions such as that of and that which to introduce more information about something already mentioned, instead of repeating the noun which refers to it.
gloss_zh: （用于 that of, that which 等短语中引出有关上文提到的某事物的更多信息，而避免重复相关名词）

senses.concept_en: You use that in front of words or expressions which express agreement, responses, or reactions to what has just been said.
gloss_zh: 那个，那（用于对前述内容表示同意或作出应答的词和词组前）

senses.concept_en: You use that to introduce a person or thing that you are going to give details or information about.
gloss_zh: 那一个，那个（引出将要更加详细介绍的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use that when you are referring to someone or something which is a distance away from you in position or time, especially when you indicate or point to them. When there are two or more things near you, that refers to the more distant one.
gloss_zh: 那个（指代在时间、空间上离自己稍远的人或物，尤用于指示;有两个以上的事物时，that 指较远的那个）

senses.concept_en: You use that when you are identifying someone or asking about their identity.
You can use that when you expect the person you are talking to to know what or who you are referring to, without needing to identify the particular person or thing fully.
gloss_zh: （不需明确指出的情况下谈话对方即可能知道所指的人或物）那个

senses.concept_en: If something is not that bad, funny, or expensive for example, it is not as bad, funny, or expensive as it might be or as has been suggested.
gloss_zh: 不太，不那么（坏、滑稽、昂贵等）

senses.concept_en: You can use that to emphasize the degree of a feeling or quality.
gloss_zh: 那么，那样（用于强调感情或品质的程度之深）

senses.concept_en: You can use that after many verbs, adjectives, nouns, and expressions to introduce a clause in which you report what someone has said, or what they think or feel.
gloss_zh: （用于动词、形容词、名词、短语之后，引导间接引语从句）

senses.concept_en: You use that after 'it' and a link verb and an adjective to comment on a situation or fact.
gloss_zh: （用于“it+系动词+形容词”结构之后，表示评论）

senses.concept_en: You use that to introduce a clause which gives more information to help identify the person or thing you are talking about.
gloss_zh: （引导从句，以提供更多有关谈论对象的信息）

senses.concept_en: You use that after expressions with 'so' and 'such' in order to introduce the result or effect of something.
gloss_zh: （用在 so，such 之后，引出结果或影响）

senses.concept_en: You use the at the beginning of noun groups to refer to someone or something that you have already mentioned or identified.
gloss_zh: （用于名词短语之前，指代已经提及或指明的人或物）

senses.concept_en: You use the at the beginning of a noun group when the first noun is followed by an 'of' phrase or a clause which identifies the person or thing.
gloss_zh: （当名词后接 of 短语或表明身份的从句时，该名词前用the）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of some nouns that refer to something in our general experience of the world.
gloss_zh: （用于某些表示人们共有经历的名词前）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of nouns that refer to people, things, services, or institutions that are associated with everyday life.
gloss_zh: （用于和日常生活相关的人、物、服务、机构的名词前）

senses.concept_en: You use the instead of a possessive determiner, especially when you are talking about a part of someone's body or a member of their family.
gloss_zh: （用于代替所有格限定词，尤在谈论身体某一部分或家庭某一成员时）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of a singular noun when you want to make a general statement about things or people of that type.
gloss_zh: （用于单数名词前，表示一类人或事物）

senses.concept_en: You use the with the name of a musical instrument when you are talking about someone's ability to play the instrument.
gloss_zh: （谈论是否会演奏乐器时，用于乐器名称前）

senses.concept_en: You use the with nationality adjectives and nouns to talk about the people who live in a country.
gloss_zh: （用于表示国籍的形容词和名词以谈论一国全体国民）

senses.concept_en: You use the with words such as 'rich', 'poor', 'old', or 'unemployed' to refer to all people of a particular type.
gloss_zh: （与 rich, poor, old, unemployed 等形容词连用，表示某一类人）

senses.concept_en: If you want to refer to a whole family or to a married couple, you can make their surname into a plural and use the in front of it.
gloss_zh: （用于姓氏的复数前，表示一家人或夫妻）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of an adjective when you are referring to a particular thing that is described by that adjective.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词前，表示其修饰的某个事物）

senses.concept_en: You use the to indicate that you have enough of the thing mentioned for a particular purpose.
gloss_zh: （表示拥有为某一特定目的所需的足够的某物）

senses.concept_en: You use the with some titles, place names, and other names.
gloss_zh: （与某些称号、地名和其他名称连用）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of numbers such as first, second, and third.
You use the in front of numbers when they refer to decades.
You use the in front of superlative adjectives and adverbs.
gloss_zh: （用于形容词和副词的最高级前）

senses.concept_en: You use the in front of each of two comparative adjectives or adverbs when you are describing how one amount or quality changes in relation to another.
gloss_zh: 越…越…（用于两个比较级前，表示其中一个随另一个发生量或质的变化）

senses.concept_en: When you express rates, prices, and measurements, you can use the to say how many units apply to each of the items being measured.
gloss_zh: 每，一（表示速度、价格、度量等）

senses.concept_en: You use the to indicate that something or someone is the most famous, important, or best thing of its kind. In spoken English, you put more stress on it, and in written English, you often underline it or write it in capitals or italics.
gloss_zh: （表示某人或某物是同类中最有名、最重要或最好的。口语中 the 要重读；书面语中常加下划线或用大写、斜体）

senses.concept_en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.
You use their instead of 'his or her' to indicate that something belongs or relates to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people think this use is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （代替 his or her，而不指明是男是女;有人认为这种用法不对）

then.translation:
adv. 然后, 当时
conj. 然后, 当时
n. 那时

senses.concept_en: Then means at a particular time in the past or in the future.
Then is used when you refer to something which was true at a particular time in the past but is not true now.
You use then to say that one thing happens after another, or is after another on a list.
You use then in conversation to indicate that what you are about to say follows logically in some way from what has just been said or implied.
You use then at the end of a topic or at the end of a conversation.
You use then with words like 'now', 'well', and 'okay', to introduce a new topic or a new point of view.
gloss_zh: （和 now，well，okay 等连用，引出新话题或新观点）

senses.concept_en: You use then to introduce a summary of what you have said or the conclusions that you are drawing from it.
gloss_zh: 也就是说，总之（引出总结或结论）

senses.concept_en: You use then to introduce the second part of a sentence which begins with 'if'. The first part of the sentence describes a possible situation, and then introduces the result of the situation.
gloss_zh: 那么，则（引导if开头的句子的第二部分，第一部分描述可能的情况，第二部分引入结果）

senses.concept_en: You use then at the beginning of a sentence or after 'and' or 'but' to introduce a comment or an extra piece of information to what you have already said.
gloss_zh: 毕竟，话说回来，而且（用于句首，或用于 and，but 之后引出对之前所说话的评论或补充）

senses.concept_en: You use they to refer to a group of people, animals, or things.
You use they instead of 'he or she' to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people think this use is incorrect.
gloss_zh: （用以代替he or she，而不指明是男是女;有人认为这种用法不对）

senses.concept_en: You use they in expressions such as 'they say' or 'they call it' to refer to people in general when you are making general statements about what people say, think, or do.
gloss_zh: （用于 they say，they call it 等表达中表示泛指）他们

this.translation:
pron. 这, 本
a. 这, 本
adv. 这么

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer back to a particular person or thing that has been mentioned or implied.
gloss_zh: （指代先前提及的人或物）这，这个

senses.concept_en: You use this to introduce someone or something that you are going to talk about.
gloss_zh: （引出将要谈论的人或物）下面（这个），以下

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences.
gloss_zh: 这一点（指前一句或几句话中提到的观点或情况）

senses.concept_en: In spoken English, people use this to introduce a person or thing into a story.
gloss_zh: （叙述时引出新出现的人或物）这个，一个

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer to a person or thing that is near you, especially when you touch them or point to them. When there are two or more people or things near you, this refers to the nearest one.
gloss_zh: 这个，这位（尤指所触碰或指向的离自己较近的人或物，有两个以上时，用于指最近的一个）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you refer to a general situation, activity, or event which is happening or has just happened and which you feel involved in.
gloss_zh: 这个，这（指代正在发生或刚刚发生的与自己有关的一般情况、活动或事件）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you refer to the place you are in now or to the present time.
gloss_zh: 这，该，此（指当前所处地点或时间）

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer to the next occurrence in the future of a particular day, month, season, or festival.
gloss_zh: 本，今，这个，下一个（指接下来将要发生某事的特定时间）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you are indicating the size or shape of something with your hands.
gloss_zh: 这么，这样（用于用手比划大小、形状时）

senses.concept_en: You use this when you are going to specify how much you know or how much you can tell someone.
gloss_zh: 这么，这样（用于说明自己知道或能告知的内容）

senses.concept_en: You use this in order to say who you are or what organization you are representing, when you are speaking on the telephone, radio, or television.
gloss_zh: （用于电话、广播或电视中，表明身份或所代表的机构）我是，这里是

senses.concept_en: You use this to refer to the medium of communication that you are using at the time of speaking or writing.
gloss_zh: 这个（指说话、写作时的媒介）

thousand.translation:
num. 千
a. 成千的, 许多的
n. 许许多多

senses.concept_en: A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000.
If you refer to thousands of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

through.translation:
adv. 穿越, 从头至尾, 到底, 因为
prep. 经过, 穿过
a. 对穿的, 直达的, 完结的

senses.concept_en: To move through something such as a hole, opening, or pipe means to move directly from one side or end of it to the other.
gloss_zh: 穿过,通过（洞、口子、管道等）;从…的一端到另一端

senses.concept_en: To cut through something means to cut it in two pieces or to make a hole in it.
To go through a town, area, or country means to travel across it or in it.
gloss_zh: 穿过，通过（城市、地区、国家）;遍及

senses.concept_en: If you move through a group of things or a mass of something, it is on either side of you or all around you.
To get through a barrier or obstacle means to get from one side of it to the other.
If a driver goes through a red light, they keep driving even though they should stop.
If something goes into an object and comes out of the other side, you can say that it passes through the object.
To go through a system means to move around it or to pass from one end of it to the other.
If you see, hear, or feel something through a particular thing, that thing is between you and the thing you can see, hear, or feel.
If something such as a feeling, attitude, or quality, happens through an area, organization, or a person's body, it happens everywhere in it or affects all of it.
gloss_zh: （感觉、态度、品质）遍布，遍及，贯穿

senses.concept_en: If something happens or exists through a period of time, it happens or exists from the beginning until the end.
If something happens from a particular period of time through another, it starts at the first period and continues until the end of the second period.
If you go through a particular experience or event, you experience it, and if you behave in a particular way through it, you behave in that way while it is happening.
If you are through with something or if it is through, you have finished doing it and will never do it again. If you are through with someone, you do not want to have anything to do with them again.
gloss_zh: 完成的;结束的;（与…）关系了结的

senses.concept_en: You use through in expressions such as half-way through and all the way through to indicate to what extent an action or task is completed.
If something happens because of something else, you can say that it happens through it.
You use through when stating the means by which a particular thing is achieved.
If you do something through someone else, they take the necessary action for you.
If something such as a proposal or idea goes through, it is accepted by people in authority and is made legal or official.
gloss_zh: （提议、观点）获得通过，得到批准

senses.concept_en: If someone gets through an examination or a round of a competition, they succeed or win.
gloss_zh: 通过（考试）;（在比赛中）胜出

senses.concept_en: When you get through while making a telephone call, the call is connected and you can speak to the person you are phoning.
If you look or go through a lot of things, you look at them or deal with them one after the other.
If you read through something, you read it from beginning to end.
A through train goes directly to a particular place, so that the people who want to go there do not have to change trains.
If you say that someone or something is wet through, you are emphasizing how wet they are.

to.translation:
prep. 到, 向, 趋于
adv. 向前

senses.concept_en: You use to when indicating the place that someone or something visits, moves towards, or points at.
If you go to an event, you go where it is taking place.
If something is attached to something larger or fixed to it, the two things are joined together.
You use to when indicating the position of something. For example, if something is to your left, it is nearer your left side than your right side.
When you give something to someone, they receive it.
You use to to indicate who or what an action or a feeling is directed towards.
gloss_zh: （表示动作或情感的对象）对，于

senses.concept_en: You use to with certain nouns and adjectives to show that a following noun is related to them.
gloss_zh: （与某些名词、形容词连用，表示关联）对于，关于

senses.concept_en: If you say something to someone, you want that person to listen and understand what you are saying.

You use to when indicating someone's reaction to something or their feelings about a situation or event. For example, if you say that something happens to someone's surprise you mean that they are surprised when it happens.
You use to when indicating the person whose opinion you are stating.
You use to when indicating what something or someone is becoming, or the state or situation that they are progressing towards.
To can be used as a way of introducing the person or organization you are employed by, when you perform some service for them.
You use to to indicate that something happens until the time or amount mentioned is reached.
You use to when indicating the last thing in a range of things, usually when you are giving two extreme examples of something.
If someone goes from place to place or from job to job, they go to several places, or work in several jobs, and spend only a short time in each one.
You use to when you are stating a time which is less than thirty minutes before an hour. For example, if it is 'five to eight', it is five minutes before eight o'clock.
You use to when giving ratios and rates.
You use to when indicating that two things happen at the same time. For example, if something is done to music, it is done at the same time as music is being played.
If you push or shut a door to, you close it but may not shut it completely.
You use to before the base form of a verb to form the to-infinitive. You use the to-infinitive after certain verbs, nouns, and adjectives, and after words such as 'how', 'which', and 'where'.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前构成不定式;不定式用于某些动词、名词、形容词以及 how，which, where 等词之后）。

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb to indicate the purpose or intention of an action. in order to
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示动作的目的或意图）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb when you are commenting on a statement that you are making, for example when saying that you are being honest or brief, or that you are summing up or giving an example.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示对自己要说的话加以说明）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb in exclamations when you are emphasizing a very strong emotion, such as a desire or wish, or a regret or disappointment.
gloss_zh: （用于感叹句中的动词原形前，强调某一强烈情感）

senses.concept_en: You use to before the base form of a verb when indicating what situation follows a particular action.
gloss_zh: （用于动词原形前，表示某一动作之后的情形）

senses.concept_en: You use to with 'too' and 'enough' in expressions like too much to and old enough to

trap.translation:
n. 圈套, 陷阱, 诡计, 存水弯
vi. 设圈套, 设陷阱
vt. 诱捕, 诱骗, 抓住, 使受限制
[计] 俘获; 陷井
trap.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A trap is a device which is placed somewhere or a hole which is dug somewhere in order to catch animals or birds.
gloss_zh: （捕鸟兽的）陷阱，罗网，夹子，捕捉器

senses.concept_en: If a person traps animals or birds, he or she catches them using traps.
A trap is a trick that is intended to catch or deceive someone.
If you trap someone into doing or saying something, you trick them so that they do or say it, although they did not want to.
To trap someone, especially a criminal, means to capture them.
A trap is an unpleasant situation that you cannot easily escape from.
If you are trapped somewhere, something falls onto you or blocks your way and prevents you from moving or escaping.
When something traps gas, water, or energy, it prevents it from escaping.
A trap is a light carriage with two wheels pulled by horses in which people used to travel.

travel.translation:
n. 旅行, 游历, 行进
vi. 旅行, 行进, 移动, 被传播
vt. 旅行, 通过, 使移动

senses.concept_en: If you travel, you go from one place to another, often to a place that is far away.
Travel is the activity of travelling.
If you travel the world, the country, or the area, you go to many different places in the world or in a particular country or area.
When light or sound from one place reaches another, you say that it travels to the other place.
When news becomes known by people in different places, you can say that it travels to them.
Someone's travels are the journeys that they make to places a long way from their home.

trial.translation:
n. 审判, 试验, 艰苦, 麻烦事, 考验
a. 审讯的, 试验性的
trial.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.
A trial is an experiment in which you test something by using it or doing it for a period of time to see how well it works. If something is on trial, it is being tested in this way.
If someone gives you a trial for a job, or if you are on trial, you do the job for a short period of time to see if you are suitable for it.
If you refer to the trials of a situation, you mean the unpleasant things that you experience in it.
In some sports or outdoor activities, trials are a series of contests that test a competitor's skill and ability.

trouble.translation:
n. 烦恼, 麻烦, 困难, 动乱, 故障
vt. 困扰, 麻烦, 使烦恼, 折磨
vi. 烦恼, 费心

senses.concept_en: You can refer to problems or difficulties as trouble .
If you say that one aspect of a situation is the trouble, you mean that it is the aspect which is causing problems or making the situation unsatisfactory.
gloss_zh: 麻烦;问题;引起麻烦的事

senses.concept_en: Your troubles are the things that you are worried about.
If you have kidney trouble or back trouble, for example, there is something wrong with your kidneys or your back.
If there is trouble somewhere, especially in a public place, there is fighting or rioting there.
If you tell someone that it is no trouble to do something for them, you are saying politely that you can or will do it, because it is easy or convenient for you.
If you say that a person or animal is no trouble, you mean that they are very easy to look after.
gloss_zh: 需劳神费力的人（或动物）

senses.concept_en: If something troubles you, it makes you feel rather worried.
If a part of your body troubles you, it causes you physical pain or discomfort.
If you say that someone does not trouble to do something, you are critical of them because they do not behave in the way that they should do, and you think that this would require very little effort.
You use trouble in expressions such as I'm sorry to trouble you when you are apologizing to someone for disturbing them in order to ask them something.

true.translation:
a. 真实的, 正确的, 忠诚的, 可靠的, 纯粹的, 正式的
n. 真实, 准确
adv. 真实地, 准确地

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something is true, it is based on facts rather than being invented or imagined, and is accurate and reliable.
gloss_zh: 基于事实的;真实的;如实的;可信的

senses.concept_en: You use true to emphasize that a person or thing is sincere or genuine, often in contrast to something that is pretended or hidden.
gloss_zh: （感情）真实的，真挚的；（物品）真的，真正的,正品的

senses.concept_en: If you use true to describe something or someone, you approve of them because they have all the characteristics or qualities that such a person or thing typically has.
gloss_zh: 纯粹的;真正的;名副其实的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you say that a fact is true of a particular person or situation, you mean that it is valid or relevant for them.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You can use true in order to admit that a fact or opinion is real or valid before indicating that you think that it is not important or relevant in the circumstances.
If you are true to someone, you remain committed and loyal to them. If you are true to an idea or promise, you remain committed to it and continue to act according to it.
gloss_zh: 忠实的;忠诚的;恪守（诺言、思想等）的

trust.translation:
n. 信任, 信赖, 相信, 受托, 职责, 信心, 托拉斯
a. 信托的, 托拉斯的
vt. 信赖, 信任, 相信, 盼望, 赊卖给
vi. 相信, 信赖, 依靠
[计] 委托, 信任

senses.concept_en: If you trust someone, you believe that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.
Your trust in someone is your belief that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.
If you trust someone to do something, you believe that they will do it.
If you trust someone with something important or valuable, you allow them to look after it or deal with it.
