If you do not trust something, you feel that it is not safe or reliable.
If you trust someone's judgment or advice, you believe that it is good or right.
If you say you trust that something is true, you mean you hope and expect that it is true.
gloss_zh: 希望…是对的;估计…是对的

senses.concept_en: If you trust in someone or something, you believe strongly in them, and do not doubt their powers or their good intentions.
A trust is a financial arrangement in which a group of people or an organization keeps and invests money for someone.
A trust is a group of people or an organization that has control of an amount of money or property and invests it on behalf of other people or as a charity.
gloss_zh: 信托基金机构;财产托管机构

senses.concept_en: In Britain, a trust or a trust hospital is a public hospital that receives its funding directly from the national government. It has its own board of governors and is not controlled by the local health authority.
gloss_zh: 公立医院（由政府资助、独立经营）

tube.translation:
n. 管, 软管, 隧道
vt. 把...装管, 使通过管子
[计] 管子
tube.tags: gk cet4 cet6 ky toefl ielts

senses.concept_en: A tube is a long hollow object that is usually round, like a pipe.
A tube of something such as paste is a long, thin container which you squeeze in order to force the paste out.
Some long, thin, hollow parts in your body are referred to as tubes .
The tube is the underground railway system in London.
You can refer to the television as the tube .

tumble.translation:
n. 跌倒, 摔跤, 翻斤斗
vi. 翻倒, 摔倒, 倒塌, 滚动, 翻斤斗, 仓促地行动
vt. 使摔倒, 使滚翻, 弄乱

senses.concept_en: If someone or something tumbles somewhere, they fall there with a rolling or bouncing movement.
gloss_zh: 滚下;摔倒;跌落;翻滚而下

senses.concept_en: If prices or levels of something are tumbling, they are decreasing rapidly.
If water tumbles, it flows quickly over an uneven surface.
If you say that someone tumbles into a situation or place, you mean that they get into it without being fully in control of themselves or knowing what they are doing.
gloss_zh: 突然闯入（某地）;陷入，浑然不觉地进入（某种状态）

senses.concept_en: Two is the number 2.

under.translation:
prep. 在...之下, 低于
a. 下面的, 从属的
adv. 在下面

senses.concept_en: If a person or thing is under something, they are at a lower level than that thing, and may be covered or hidden by it.
In a place such as a sea, river, or swimming pool, if someone or something is under the water, they are fully in the water and covered by it.
If you go under something, you move from one side to the other of something that is at a higher level than you.
Something that is under a layer of something, especially clothing, is covered by that layer.
gloss_zh: 在（尤指一层衣服）的里面（或底下）

senses.concept_en: You can use under before a noun to indicate that a person or thing is being affected by something or is going through a particular process.
If something happens under particular circumstances or conditions, it happens when those circumstances or conditions exist.
If something happens under a law, agreement, or system, it happens because that law, agreement, or system says that it should happen.
gloss_zh: 根据，按照，依照（法律、协定、制度等）

senses.concept_en: If something happens under a particular person or government, it happens when that person or government is in power.
gloss_zh: 在（…领导）下；在（…当政）期间；在（…统治）之下

senses.concept_en: If you study or work under a particular person, that person teaches you or tells you what to do.
gloss_zh: 在…指导下（学习）；在…手下（工作）

senses.concept_en: If you do something under a particular name, you use that name instead of your real name.
gloss_zh: 用（…之名）；以（…的名义）；假借（…之名）

senses.concept_en: You use under to say which section of a list, book, or system something is in.
If something or someone is under a particular age or amount, they are less than that age or amount
gloss_zh: （年龄或数量）不足，低于，在…以下

underground.translation:
n. 地下, 地铁, 地道, 秘密活动
a. 地下的, 秘密的
adv. 在地下, 秘密地

senses.concept_en: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground.
The underground in a city is the railway system in which electric trains travel below the ground in tunnels.
In a country which is controlled by an enemy or has a harsh government, the underground is an organized group of people who are involved in illegal activities against the people in power.
gloss_zh: （反抗敌人或暴政的）地下组织，秘密组织

senses.concept_en: Underground groups and activities are secret because their purpose is to oppose the government and they are illegal.
If you go underground, you hide from the authorities or the police because your political ideas or activities are illegal.

unsafe.translation:
a. 不安全的, 不安稳的, 危险的
[经] 不安全

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a building, machine, activity, or area is unsafe, it is dangerous.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you are unsafe, you are in danger of being harmed.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If a criminal conviction is unsafe, it is not based on enough evidence or is based on false evidence.
gloss_zh: 证据不足的;证据不可靠的

use.translation:
n. 使用, 习惯, 使用价值, 用法, 使用权
vt. 使用, 利用, 运用, 耗费
vi. 惯常

senses.concept_en: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.
If you use a supply of something, you finish it so that none of it is left.
If someone uses drugs, they take drugs regularly, especially illegal ones.
You can say that someone uses the toilet or bathroom as a polite way of saying that they go to the toilet.
gloss_zh: 用（洗手间或卫生间）（礼貌说法）

senses.concept_en: If you use a particular word or expression, you say or write it, because it has the meaning that you want to express.
If you use a particular name, you call yourself by that name, especially when it is not the name that you usually call yourself.

If you say that someone uses people, you disapprove of them because they make others do things for them in order to benefit or gain some advantage from it, and not because they care about the other people.
Your use of something is the action or fact of your using it.
If you have a use for something, you need it or can find something to do with it.
If something has a particular use, it is intended for a particular purpose.
If you have the use of something, you have the permission or ability to use it.
A use of a word is a particular meaning that it has or a particular way in which it can be used.
Your use of a particular name is the fact of your calling yourself by it.

vacuum.translation:
n. 真空, 空间, 真空吸尘器
a. 真空的, 产生真空的, 利用真空的
vt. 用吸尘器打扫

senses.concept_en: If someone or something creates a vacuum, they leave a place or position which then needs to be filled by another person or thing.
If you vacuum something, you clean it using a vacuum cleaner.
A vacuum is a space that contains no air or other gas.

visitor.translation:
n. 参观者, 游客, 访客
[法] 视察人, 检视人, 检查员

senses.concept_en: A visitor is someone who is visiting a person or place.

wall.translation:
n. 墙, 墙壁, 垣, 内壁, 分界物, 屏障
a. 墙的
vt. 给...建墙, 禁闭, 用墙围住
[计] 背景墙

senses.concept_en: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room.
A wall is a long narrow vertical structure made of stone or brick that surrounds or divides an area of land.
The wall of something that is hollow is its side.
A wall of something is a large amount of it forming a high vertical barrier.
gloss_zh: 屏障;堆成墙的大量物品

senses.concept_en: You can describe something as a wall of a particular kind when it acts as a barrier and prevents people from understanding something.

want.translation:
n. 需要的东西, 缺乏, 贫困, 需要
vt. 要, 希望, 应该, 缺少
vi. 生活困苦, 需要, 缺少

senses.concept_en: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.
You can say that you want to say something to indicate that you are about to say it.
You use want in questions as a way of making an offer or inviting someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （用于疑问句中表示提议或邀请）想要，需要

senses.concept_en: If you say to someone that you want something, or ask them if they want to do it, you are firmly telling them what you want or what you want them to do.
If you say that something wants doing, you think that it needs to be done.
If you tell someone that they want to do a particular thing, you are advising them to do it.
If someone is wanted by the police, the police are searching for them because they are thought to have committed a crime.
If you want someone, you have a great desire to have sex with them.
If a child is wanted, its mother or another person loves it and is willing to look after it.
If someone wants you in a particular place or role, they desire you to be in that place or role.
A want of something is a lack of it.
Want is the state of being extremely poor.
Your wants are the things that you want.

watch.translation:
n. 观察, 手表, 看守, 守护, 监视, 值班人
vt. 看, 注视, 照顾, 看守, 守护, 监视
vi. 观看, 注视, 守侯

senses.concept_en: If you watch someone or something, you look at them, usually for a period of time, and pay attention to what is happening.
If you watch something on television or an event such as a sports match, you spend time looking at it, especially when you see it from the beginning to the end.
gloss_zh: 看，观看（电视节目、比赛等）

senses.concept_en: If you watch a situation or event, you pay attention to it or you are aware of it, but you do not influence it.
gloss_zh: 对…保持关注;掌握…的情况

senses.concept_en: If you watch people, especially children or animals, you are responsible for them, and make sure that they are not in danger.
gloss_zh: 照看，看护（尤指孩子或动物）

senses.concept_en: If you watch someone, you follow them secretly or spy on them.
If you tell someone to watch a particular person or thing, you are warning them to be careful that the person or thing does not get out of control or do something unpleasant.
A watch is a period of carefully looking and listening, often while other people are asleep and often as a military duty, so that you can warn them of danger or an attack.
A watch is a small clock which you wear on a strap on your wrist, or on a chain.

wave.translation:
n. 波, 波浪, 波动, 起伏, 高潮, 潮涌, 挥手致意, (气压)突变
vi. 波动, 飘动, 挥手示意, 起伏
vt. 使波动, 使飘扬, 挥舞, 使成波浪形

senses.concept_en: If you wave or wave your hand, you move your hand from side to side in the air, usually in order to say hello or goodbye to someone.
If you wave someone away or wave them on, you make a movement with your hand to indicate that they should move in a particular direction.
gloss_zh: 挥手示意（方向）;挥手指引

senses.concept_en: If you wave something, you hold it up and move it rapidly from side to side.
If something waves, it moves gently from side to side or up and down.
A wave is a raised mass of water on the surface of water, especially the sea, which is caused by the wind or by tides making the surface of the water rise and fall.
If someone's hair has waves, it curves slightly instead of being straight.
A wave is a sudden increase in heat or energy that spreads out from an earthquake or explosion.
Waves are the form in which things such as sound, light, and radio signals travel.
If you refer to a wave of a particular feeling, you mean that it increases quickly and becomes very intense, and then often decreases again.
A wave is a sudden increase in a particular activity or type of behaviour, especially an undesirable or unpleasant one.
A wave is a sudden increase in the number of people moving somewhere.

If a crowd of people do the wave, each person in the crowd stands up and puts their arms in the air after the person to one side of them, then sits down again, creating a continuous wave-like motion through the crowd.

way.translation:
n. 路, 路线, 路途, 方法, 道路, 情形, 规模, 习惯, 行业, 方面
adv. 远远地, 非常

senses.concept_en: If you refer to a way of doing something, you are referring to how you can do it, for example the action you can take or the method you can use to achieve it.
If you talk about the way someone does something, you are talking about the qualities their action has.
If a general statement or description is true in a particular way, this is the form of it that is true in a particular case.
You use way in expressions such as in some ways ,in many ways, and in every way to indicate the degree or extent to which a statement is true.
The ways of a particular person or group of people are their customs or their usual behaviour.
If you refer to someone's way, you are referring to their usual or preferred type of behaviour.
You use way to refer to one particular opinion or interpretation of something, when others are possible.
You use way when mentioning one of a number of possible, alternative results or decisions.
gloss_zh: 可能的后果;可能作出的决定

senses.concept_en: The way you feel about something is your attitude to it or your opinion about it.
If you mention the way that something happens, you are mentioning the fact that it happens.

You use way in expressions such as push your way ,work your way, or eat your way, followed by a prepositional phrase or adverb, in order to indicate movement, progress, or force as well as the action described by the verb.
The way somewhere consists of the different places that you go through or the route that you take in order to get there.
If you go or look a particular way, you go or look in that direction.
You can refer to the direction you are travelling in as your way .

If you lose your way, you take a wrong or unfamiliar route, so that you do not know how to get to the place that you want to go to. If you find your way, you manage to get to the place that you want to go to.
You talk about people going their different ways in order to say that their lives develop differently and they have less contact with each other.
If something comes your way, you get it or receive it.
If someone or something is in the way, they prevent you from moving forward or seeing clearly.
Way is used in the names of some roads, and also in the names of some long paths for walkers in the countryside.
You can use way to refer to the area near where someone lives or near a specified place.
gloss_zh: （某人居住地的）周边；特定的地区

senses.concept_en: You use way in expressions such as the right way up and the other way around to refer to one of two or more possible positions or arrangements that something can have.
You can use way to emphasize, for example, that something is a great distance away or is very much below or above a particular level or amount.
If you split something a number of ways, you divide it into a number of different parts or quantities, usually fairly equal in size.
Way is used in expressions such as a long way ,a little way, and quite a way, to say how far away something is or how far you have travelled.
Way is used in expressions such as a long way ,a little way, and quite a way, to say how far away in time something is.
You use way in expressions such as all the way ,most of the way and half the way to refer to the extent to which an action has been completed.
gloss_zh: （表示动作完成的程度）全部/多半/一半

weather.translation:
n. 天气, 气象, 处境
a. 迎风的
vt. 使受风吹雨打, 侵蚀, 使风化, 经受住
vi. 风化, 受侵蚀, 经受风雨

senses.concept_en: The weather is the condition of the atmosphere in one area at a particular time, for example if it is raining, hot, or windy.
If something such as wood or rock weathers or is weathered, it changes colour or shape as a result of the wind, sun, rain, or cold.
If you weather a difficult time or a difficult situation, you survive it and are able to continue normally after it has passed or ended. to weather the storm
A week is a period of seven days. Some people consider that a week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.
A week is a period of about seven days.
gloss_zh: 一周时间;七天左右的时间

senses.concept_en: Your working week is the hours that you spend at work during a week.
gloss_zh: 工作周（指一周的工作时间）

senses.concept_en: The week is the part of the week that does not include Saturday and Sunday.
gloss_zh: （除去星期六和星期日的）星期，周，礼拜

senses.concept_en: You use week in expressions such as 'a week on Monday', 'a week next Tuesday', and 'tomorrow week' to mean exactly one week after the day that you mention.
You use week in expressions such as 'a week last Monday', 'a week ago this Tuesday', and 'a week ago yesterday' to mean exactly one week before the day that you mention.

whereas.translation:
conj. 然而, 鉴于
[法] 考虑到, 鉴于, 就...而论

senses.concept_en: You use whereas to introduce a comment which contrasts with what is said in the main clause.

which.translation: pron. 哪一个, 那一个

senses.concept_en: You use which in questions when there are two or more possible answers or alternatives.
You use which to refer to a choice between two or more possible answers or alternatives.
gloss_zh: （用于指明在两个或多个答案或选项中所作出的选择）哪个，哪些

senses.concept_en: You use which at the beginning of a relative clause when specifying the thing that you are talking about or when giving more information about it.
gloss_zh: （用于关系从句句首，具体说明所谈论的事物或提供关于它的更多信息）

senses.concept_en: You use which to refer back to an idea or situation expressed in a previous sentence or sentences, especially when you want to give your opinion about it.
gloss_zh: （用来回指前面句子表达的观点或状况）这，那

wide.translation:
a. 宽的, 广阔的, 普遍的, 宽阔的, 广泛的, 一般的
adv. 广阔地, 遍及各处地, 广泛地
n. 大千世界

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Something that is wide measures a large distance from one side or edge to the other.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A wide smile is one in which your mouth is stretched because you are very pleased or amused.
If you open or spread something wide, you open or spread it as far as possible or to the fullest extent.
gloss_zh: 张开很大的;完全张开的

senses.concept_en: You use wide to talk or ask about how much something measures from one side or edge to the other.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use wide to describe something that includes a large number of different things or people.
gloss_zh: 范围广的;包容的;广泛的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use wide to say that something is found, believed, known, or supported by many people or throughout a large area.
gloss_zh: 广泛的;广为流传的;广为人知的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A wide difference or gap between two things, ideas, or qualities is a large difference or gap.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Wider is used to describe something which relates to the most important or general parts of a situation, rather than to the smaller parts or to details.
gloss_zh: 更大的;更多的;更广泛的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If something such as a shot or punch is wide, it does not hit its target but lands to the right or left of it.
gloss_zh: 未击中目标的;未打中的

win.translation:
vt. 赢得, 打胜, 成功
vi. 获胜, 达到, 影响
n. 胜利, 赢, 收益

senses.concept_en: If you win something such as a competition, battle, or argument, you defeat those people you are competing or fighting against, or you do better than everyone else involved.

If something wins you something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, it causes you to defeat the people competing with you or fighting you, or to do better than everyone else involved.
If you win something such as a prize or medal, you get it because you have defeated everyone else in something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, or have done very well in it.
If you win something that you want or need, you succeed in getting it.
gloss_zh: 获得，赢得（想要或需要之物）

senses.concept_en: If something wins you a prize or wins you something else that you want, it causes you to get it.

with.translation: prep. 和...在一起, 以, 由于

senses.concept_en: If one person is with another, they are together in one place.
If something is put with or is with something else, they are used at the same time.
If you do something with someone else, you both do it together or are both involved in it.
If you fight, argue, or compete with someone, you oppose them.
gloss_zh: 和，与，同（…打斗、争论或竞争）

senses.concept_en: If you do something with a particular tool, object, or substance, you do it using that tool, object, or substance.
gloss_zh: 用，使用（某种工具、物品或材料）

senses.concept_en: If someone stands or goes somewhere with something, they are carrying it.
Someone or something with a particular feature or possession has that feature or possession.
gloss_zh: 有，拥有（某种特征或所有物）

senses.concept_en: Someone with an illness has that illness.
If something is filled or covered with a substance or with things, it has that substance or those things in it or on it.
If you are, for example, pleased or annoyed with someone or something, you have that feeling towards them.
You use with to indicate what a state, quality, or action relates to, involves, or affects.
You use with when indicating the way that something is done or the feeling that a person has when they do something.
gloss_zh: 用（某种方式）；带着（某种感情）

senses.concept_en: You use with when indicating a sound or gesture that is made when something is done, or an expression that a person has on their face when they do something.
gloss_zh: 伴着（声音或手势）;带着（表情）

senses.concept_en: You use with to indicate the feeling that makes someone have a particular appearance or type of behaviour.
gloss_zh: 由于，因为（某种感情而使某人有某种表现或行为）

senses.concept_en: You use with when mentioning the position or appearance of a person or thing at the time that they do something, or what someone else is doing at that time.
gloss_zh: （表示以某姿势、外表或伴随某事件做某事）与…同时，随着

senses.concept_en: You use with to introduce a current situation that is a factor affecting another situation.
You use with when making a comparison or contrast between the situations of different people or things.
If something increases or decreases with a particular factor, it changes as that factor changes.
gloss_zh: 随着，跟着（…的变化而变化）

senses.concept_en: If something moves with a wind or current, it moves in the same direction as the wind or current.
gloss_zh: 与（风、水流等）方向一致；顺着…

senses.concept_en: If someone says that they are with you, they mean that they understand what you are saying.
If someone says that they are with you, they mean that they support or approve of what you are doing.

without.translation:
prep. 没有, 不, 在...之外
adv. 在外面, 户外
n. 外面, 外部

senses.concept_en: You use without to indicate that someone or something does not have or use the thing mentioned.
If one thing happens without another thing, or if you do something without doing something else, the second thing does not happen or occur.
gloss_zh: 在没有（发生或做某事）的情况下

senses.concept_en: If you do something without a particular feeling, you do not have that feeling when you do it.
If you do something without someone else, they are not in the same place as you are or are not involved in the same action as you.

wooden.translation: a. 木制的, 呆笨的, 木然的

senses.concept_en: Wooden objects are made of wood.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: If you describe an actor as wooden, you are critical of them because their performance is not at all lively or natural.
gloss_zh: （演员）呆板的，死板的，无活力的

work.translation:
n. 工作, 劳动, 职业, 行为, 功, 作品, 成果, 产品, 工程
vi. 工作, 劳动, 做, 运转, 起作用, 被加工
vt. 使工作, 使转动, 开动, 使用, 经营, 使逐渐变得, 造成

senses.concept_en: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
People who have work or who are in work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.
When you work, you do the things that you are paid or required to do in your job.
Your work consists of the things you are paid or required to do in your job.
When you work, you spend time and effort doing a task that needs to be done or trying to achieve something.
Work is the place where you do your job.
Work is something which you produce as a result of an activity or as a result of doing your job.
A work is something such as a painting, book, or piece of music produced by an artist, writer, or composer.
gloss_zh: （艺术家、作家、作曲家等的）作品；著作

senses.concept_en: If someone is working on a particular subject or question, they are studying or researching it.
If you work with a person or a group of people, you spend time and effort trying to help them in some way.
If a machine or piece of equipment works, it operates and performs a particular function.
If an idea, system, or way of doing something works, it is successful, effective, or satisfactory.
If a drug or medicine works, it produces a particular physical effect.
If something works in your favour, it helps you in some way. If something works to your disadvantage, it causes problems for you in some way.
gloss_zh: 产生（有利或不利的）影响

senses.concept_en: If something or someone works their magic or works their charms on a person, they have a powerful positive effect on them.
gloss_zh: 对…产生（神奇的影响）;使…深受（魅力感染）

senses.concept_en: If your mind or brain is working, you are thinking about something or trying to solve a problem.
If you work on an assumption or idea, you act as if it were true or base other ideas on it, until you have more information.
gloss_zh: 以（某种假定或思想）为基础（或前提）

senses.concept_en: If you work a particular area or type of place, you travel around that area or work in those places as part of your job, for example trying to sell something there.
gloss_zh: 在（某地或某类场所）工作;在…奔波

senses.concept_en: If you work someone, you make them spend time and effort doing a particular activity or job.
If someone, often a politician or entertainer, works a crowd, they create a good relationship with the people in the crowd and get their support or interest.
gloss_zh: （常指政客或艺人）博得，赢得（众人的支持或欢心）

senses.concept_en: When people work the land, they do all the tasks involved in growing crops.
When a mine is worked, minerals such as coal or gold are removed from it.
If you work a machine or piece of equipment, you use or control it.
If something works into a particular state or condition, it gradually moves so that it is in that state or condition.
If you work a substance such as dough or clay, you keep pressing it to make it have a particular texture.
If you work a material such as metal, leather, or stone, you cut, sew, or shape it in order to make something or to create a design.
If you work with a particular substance or material, you use it in order to make something or to create a design.
gloss_zh: 使用，采用（某种材料或物质）

senses.concept_en: If you work a part of your body, or if it works, you move it.
A works is a place where something is manufactured or where an industrial process is carried out. Works is used to refer to one or to more than one of these places.
Works are activities such as digging the ground or building on a large scale.
You can say the works after listing things such as someone's possessions or requirements, to emphasize that they possess or require everything you can think of in a particular category.
gloss_zh: （某种类型的）全部物件，全套物品

worker.translation:
n. 工人, 劳动者
[经] 工人, 劳工, 劳动者

senses.concept_en: A particular kind of worker does the kind of work mentioned.
Workers are people who are employed in industry or business and who are not managers.
See also:care worker;caseworker;dock worker;social worker;teleworker;youth worker; You can use worker to say how well or badly someone works.
You use would when you are saying what someone believed, hoped, or expected to happen or be the case.
gloss_zh: （表示曾经相信、希望或期待）将，将会

senses.concept_en: You use would when saying what someone intended to do.
You use would when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible situation.
gloss_zh: （表示可能出现的情况的结果或影响）会，将会

senses.concept_en: You use would, or would have with a past participle, to indicate that you are assuming or guessing that something is true, because you have good reasons for thinking it.
gloss_zh: （would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示有充分理由认为或猜测是某种情况）肯定，一定，应该

senses.concept_en: You use would in the main clause of some 'if' and 'unless' sentences to indicate something you consider to be fairly unlikely to happen.
gloss_zh: （用于if，unless等引导的条件状语从句的主句，表示认为某事不大可能发生）就，该

senses.concept_en: You use would to say that someone was willing to do something. You use would not to indicate that they refused to do something.
You use would not to indicate that something did not happen, often in spite of a lot of effort.
gloss_zh: （表示尽管付出很大努力却没有发生）就（不），偏（不）

senses.concept_en: You use would, especially with 'like', 'love', and 'wish', when saying that someone wants to do or have a particular thing or wants a particular thing to happen. would rather
gloss_zh: （尤与like, love 和 wish 连用，表示想做某事或拥有某物，或希望某事发生）要，会

senses.concept_en: You use would with 'if' clauses in questions when you are asking for permission to do something.
gloss_zh: （用于带if从句的疑问句中，表示请求许可做某事）会

senses.concept_en: You use would, usually in questions with 'like', when you are making a polite offer or invitation.
gloss_zh: （通常在疑问句中与 like 连用，表示礼貌地给予或邀请）

senses.concept_en: You use would, usually in questions, when you are politely asking someone to do something.
gloss_zh: （通常用于疑问句中，表示礼貌地请求某人做某事）请

senses.concept_en: You say that someone would do something when it is typical of them and you are critical of it. You emphasize the word would when you use it in this way.
gloss_zh: （用于批评，表示对某人做某事并不感到意外，此时 would 须重读）

senses.concept_en: You use would, or sometimes would have with a past participle, when you are expressing your opinion about something or seeing if people agree with you, especially when you are uncertain about what you are saying.
gloss_zh: （would 或 would have 与过去分词连用，表示发表看法或了解他人是否赞同自己的看法，尤用于对自己的话没有把握时）

senses.concept_en: You use I would when you are giving someone advice in an informal way.
gloss_zh: （用于以随便的口气向人提出建议）我（就）会

senses.concept_en: You use you would in negative sentences with verbs such as 'guess' and 'know' when you want to say that something is not obvious, especially something surprising.
gloss_zh: （用于否定句，与 guess, know 等动词连用，表示某事不明显，尤用于某事令人吃惊时）

senses.concept_en: You use would to talk about something which happened regularly in the past but which no longer happens.
gloss_zh: （表示某事过去惯常发生, 而现在不再发生了）就，会

senses.concept_en: You use would have with a past participle when you are saying what was likely to have happened by a particular time.
gloss_zh: （would have 与过去分词连用，表示某个时间前可能发生的事情）就，会

senses.concept_en: You use would have with a past participle when you are referring to the result or effect of a possible event in the past.
gloss_zh: （would have 与过去分词连用，表示过去可能发生的事情的结果或影响）就，会

senses.concept_en: If you say that someone would have liked or preferred something, you mean that they wanted to do it or have it but were unable to.
You use would, usually in negative sentences, to criticize something that someone has done and to express your disapproval of it.
gloss_zh: （通常用于否定句，批评某人所为，表示不满）（不）会

young.translation:
a. 年轻的, 无经验的, 朝气蓬勃的
n. 青年们, 幼小动物, 崽

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: A young person, animal, or plant has not lived or existed for very long and is not yet mature.
gloss_zh: 年幼的;幼小的;未成熟的

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: You use young to describe a time when a person or thing was young.

senses.pos_zh: 能被表示程度的副词或介词词组修饰的形容词
senses.concept_en: Someone who is young in appearance or behaviour looks or behaves as if they are young.
gloss_zh: （显得）年轻的;（显得）岁数不大的

senses.concept_en: The young of an animal are its babies.
